title: Reports list not updated when enketo forms submitted or edited
Assign a different schedule based on a form field value
body: We will want to have a different schedule if a pregnancy registration is determined to be high risk. This will be determined by fields within the registration form (eg `danger_signs` is not empty). This may be currently possible with the rules, but we need to confirm.

title: Open form directly from task list
body: In order to streamline the task-to-form process, we should have a task type which opens the associated form directly from the task list. This means that clicking on that task in the left pane shows the Enketo form in the right pane.

title: Show Enketo form in the right pane
body: Part of a larger UX refactor, we want to show the Enketo form in the right pane of the webapp, instead of the modal. This will make more sense with the rest of the UX refactor issues to come.

title: Forward compatibility: Ensure that implementing Enketo localization sometime in the future is pain-free
body: We should pass the users locale in to the enketo form rendering so the forms can be localised.

title: Refactor EditReportCtrl for unit testing and maintainance
body:
The EditReportCtrl has the Enketo rendering code embedded in it. This is bad because it cannot be reused, is outside of the concern of the controller, and controllers are difficult to unit test.

Pull as much of the Enketo code out of the controller and into an Enketo service as possible. Then write unit tests.

title: Generate tasks from any report
body:
The TaskGenerator picks out ANC registrations with or without LMP to generate tasks. This means it only works for the ANC use case. It's also not configurable enough because it only allows up to two registration forms, and there's no option to have non-registration reports generate events (eg: follow ups).

Pass all reports to nools and let the configuration decide which to generate schedules from.

title: [enketo] jr:// media URLs should be processed before form is added to DOM
body:
Currently the media URLs are processed _after_ the form is added to the DOM, which causes error logs such as:

> `GET jr://video.mp4 net::ERR_UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME`

title: Show right pane content full screen in mobile/tablet view
body:
Part of the larger UX refactor mentioned in #1243, in the mobile view all right pane content should be shown "full screen". 

**Mobile/Tablet view:** Hide the top bars when viewing the right pane. 
**Desktop view:** In desktop view the right pane would **remain as is**.

Here are some examples of the right pane in mobile/tablet view:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9688588/1357e694-52fe-11e5-886b-803bf12c2350.png)

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9688480/6d12512a-52fd-11e5-99a7-3238d592f1b3.png)

Followup issues will be posted for content of the right pane given the context.

title: Update to Enketo navigation buttons
body:
From feedback from several testers, we will not be showing the `submit` button until you have reached the end of the form. That means showing only `back` and `next` as such:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9688431/2eb94122-52fd-11e5-8910-c8fe4a70eb68.png)

When the end of the form is reached, instead of a `next` button it would show the `done` button in its place. The `back` button should be disabled when on the first page of the form.

title: Android container: Support screen reorientation
body:
We used the Tecno Y4's "lock orientation" feature for the demo. Currently, turning the device from portrait to landscape mode (apparently) triggers a full page reload, which turns the screen white for a relatively long period of time and makes the application appear (okay, actually-be) unresponsive.

We should be able to switch between portrait and landscape mode on a Tecno Y4 Chromium 30 Webview without major UX disruption.

title: [Tasks] Icons and styling for individual tasks
body:
Here is a mockup of tasks with related icons:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9690078/3e05cc4e-5308-11e5-8603-ca4c7bfec26b.png)
**Primary icons:** On the left, relate to the task type. Ideally it would be possible to upload a new set of icons to choose from for each project.

**Secondary icons:** On the right, may relate to a property of the task's entity e.g. the patient a task relates to has danger signs, so show as a high risk pregnancy.

**Secondary label:** The text next to the alert icon should be configurable separately from the choice of the icon. Ideally it would be possible to set the text and color of that secondary text.

_Note that icons may overlap with the ones show in #1230._

title: Remove logo from Tablet view
body: As done with the mobile view in #1218, remove the Medic logo from the "tablet view" (401-767px wide). Otherwise the logo appears/disappears when rotating between landscape and portrait on phones used by projects (eg Tecno Y4).

title: Larger tab buttons
body:
We have received feedback from many testers that the buttons and text are too small. The ones that seem to be most problematic so far are top level tabs.

@garethbowen's suggestion was to divide the available space for the visible tabs.

title: Remove `+` from top bar
body:
The actions available in the `+` in the top bar should be moved to the "floating action bar" in their proper context.

**Submit report:** 
Practically speaking, most reports will be triggered from a task, or from a patient profile. For generic reports not related to a person, place, or tasks, you can `Create New Report` using the button in the action bar in the Reports tab shown here:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9690431/4f700ec0-530a-11e5-9148-00e89dd1eaae.png)

**Send message:** 
It is currently possible to send new messages via a button in the sub top bar of the Messages tab. Ideally that would be moved to follow the same pattern as with _Reports_. Since the Messages tab is not used in the mobile app yet it is suitable to leave it as is for now.

title: [Contacts] Show search field when tab is loaded
body:
Show the full input field on the Contacts tab in mobile view. 

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/10619625/a015b2a4-7744-11e5-855b-5cc8743b6270.png)

If we do this for all search fields this will have unintended consequences in the Reports tab where the filter bar is already full of filters. We could show the search bar in full only when there is sufficient space, and collapse to the button version if there isn't. Given that this is a requirement only for the Contacts tab, we can take the approach that is most efficient (eg only have the full search bar in the Contacts tab, leave the field as is in the Reports tab).

title: [Contacts] Remove place and type filters based on user role
body: In order to keep the workflow and UX cleaner, we have been asked to remove some filters. By making the visibility of the individual filter role based, we solve this problem and also have the benefit of postponing discussion related to the filters until we have feedback from users using them.

title: [Contacts] Default filters per role
body:
As alluded to in #1257, the default filter for the Contacts tab should be configurable by role. 

For our immediate needs, the mobile CHW user would need the filter to show only the "Families":
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9691645/adac9e8e-5311-11e5-9b8c-b58d938f5bc2.png)

title: [Contacts] Move add place and person buttons
body:
Based on feedback to clean up the UX and workflow for mobile users we should move the add place/person buttons to the floating action bar. 
- **Add Place** is within the left pane, see image below.
- **Add Person** is done in the action bar for the place, when it is being viewed in the right pane. This means that a person must be associated to a place. Issue related to this yet to come.
- Prevent the deletion of a place if there are people associated to it. The delete icon should be disabled, and/or if clicked should show an alert message explaining that the people would need to be deleted first.

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9690654/c834f6c6-530b-11e5-9e05-d5df0a4c655c.png)

title: [Contacts] Improved workflow to create place
body:
Based on feedback from initial testers, we want to streamline the process to create a place to include the creation of the primary contact. This is somewhat possible already if you select the "add new" as the primary contact, but needs the following improvements:
- Automatically set the Place name as `{{person_name}}'s family`
- Split the person name field into `First Name`, `Last Name`
- Additional fields for the person: `National ID Number`, `Alternate phone number`, `Date of Birth`

Given that these fields may change from one deployment to another it seems prudent to have a configurable solution, time permitting. One possibility would be that the whole contact creation process is just an XML form from which we can configure the person and place creation and assignment. 

_This may be related to #842._

title: [Contacts] Place profile updates
body:
The updated UX for the "Place" should include three sections:

The profile contains three sections:
- **Tasks:** All tasks related to the place or any of its people. Clicking on any of these tasks would open the task's form.
- **People:** All the people associated to the place. Clicking on the person would open the person's profile page.
- **Reports History:** a running list of all of the reports related to the place, but not the ones for the people associated to the place. This is shown outside of the viewport, but is available within the same profile page. Clicking on a report would show the same view as if it were selected from the Reports tab.

Here is an example for the place level called "Family":
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9692167/4ede1dfc-5315-11e5-9f8a-b4f9fc43da9c.png)

title: [Contacts] Person profile updates
body:
Three sections for the person profile page:
- **Base info**: Info from the person creation form. Ideally we could select which subset of info is being shown here since we want this to be compact so that the Tasks are not below the fold.
- **Tasks**: All tasks related to this person. Clicks through to the task's form.
- **Reports History**: All reports submitted about this person. Clicking through brings you to the report's view.

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9692359/8588c9fa-5316-11e5-9a62-b75077fb98ca.png)

title: [Contacts] Action bar updates
body:
As seen in #1261 and #1262, the action bar has updated actions:

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9692644/691ac9f6-5318-11e5-90fa-6310f0b52659.png)
- **Call**: In mobile/tablet view this should be a link to call the primary phone number for the contact (eg `href="tel:+16505551234"`) which we need to then handle in medic-android. In desktop view this can be either disabled, or replaced with the SMS action.
- **Add**: Opens a list of all the possible reports that can be submitted for this person/place. This would also include adding more people to a place, send SMS to the contact, and SMS all where appropriate.
- **Edit**: Edit the current person/place's basic info.
- **Delete**: As expected, deletes the person or place, but only if there are no people/places associated to it. If there are those must first be deleted or reassigned.

title: [Reports] Move top level tab to beneath Menu icon
body:
As seen below, the Reports tab should not be accessible as a top level tab. This is to streamline the top level options and avoid confusion with users that rarely need to see the reports tab - which will increasingly be the case for certain types of users.

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/789512/9692952/a39e29f4-531a-11e5-9f2f-95067ed2d5c1.png)

Given that this requirement is likely to change from one project to another, and even for different types of users within a deployment, we likely want the choice of tabs shown under the Menu icon to be configurable by user role.

_Edit: Changed "settings" to "menu" icon for clarity._

title: [android] Test back button functionality
body:
This is a placeholder to retest the back functionality on Android devices. 

We should determine if the use of the back button is working as expected in its current implementation (back in history until no more, then exit app) and if that is suitable for users.

With the refactored UX, an alternative would be to go "up/back" a level until you reach the top level tabs and then exit.

title: Submit reports related to a person or place
body:
We want to submit reports about a person (eg new pregnancy), or about a place (eg household survey). Currently, followup reports are based on `patient_id`, which is created with a registration form but has no connection to our new contacts.

We likely need to assign people and places a unique ID, and given that contact creation can happen offline, this ID probably needs to be a UUID. This ID could then be discreetly passed to any task and report related to the place/person, and submitted reports would then be associated to the contact.

Reports submitted about a person or place would then be shown on their profile, as described in #1261 and #1262.

title: [android] Start call from webapp
[Tasks] Configurable start and end time
body: Tasks are now shown as soon as they pass a rule. We would want the task to be shown only during a particular time window. This way, a task could be configured to only show up 2 days ahead of an event, and disappear when no longer relevant (eg no point doing the 48hr followup 2 weeks later).

title: [android] improve app URL validation
body: https://github.com/medic/medic-android/issues/9

title: Cannot edit non-enketo reports

title: Contacts: Sort left pane by object type
body:
During today's milestone call, we discussed a project-specific request to _never_ show `Person` objects in the Contacts tab's left pane. We realized that a usability issue was driving this request – namely, that users will almost always know whether they're looking for a person or a building, and that keeping all of the people separate from all of the buildings makes this (visual) search faster.

Proposal: an option (or default behavior) that sorts (or visually groups) left-pane Contacts tab objects based on their type and/or hierarchy level.

title: Extensible Person/Place Profiles via Enketo
body:
Allow a special Enketo form type to be paired with each major contact type (e.g. places and people and clinics and CHWs). Call these forms "contact profile forms". If a contact profile form is configured for a particular contact type, prompt users to fill in that form when a contact of that type is created.

When viewing information about a contact, a report submission history will be presented (see #1262). Lift any data pertaining to a contact profile form submission out of this list and to the top level; present the contents of the form submissions (yes, potentially plural) as a human-readable tabular summary. This will almost always a proper subset of the full field set; some ability to mask/hide less-important fields would be required.

title: couch-to-postgres adapter. forms-as-views
body:
Parse form contents out of json docs into one view per form.

Presently this is done by hand using something like this:

``` SQL
SELECT jsonb_object_keys(data) FROM nosql WHERE data->'type' = '"data_record"' AND data->'form' = '"R"';
```

Possibly switch from two `->` to one or to `@>` so that indexing will assist.

Need to automate the process of figuring out field names for any form. pl/SQL is probably the place to implement such a function once the process is determined.

title: map project form names to internal representation names
body:
Calculations are much easier when the source of the data is the same, be it Spreadsheets or Postgres.

So when each project decides to have a different ANC registration form name (e.g. ANCR, R, P, a Nepalese character that I can't reproduce), yet the fields are pretty much the same, then we get into a situation where our calculations should work but won't due to missing pointers/tables/sheets.

One easy solution is to create a view like `formview_ANCR` and simply `SELECT  * FROM formview_$$$$` where `$$$$` is the project's form name.

But then a recent project has started using reserved form names for different reasons, so maybe instead of `formview_ANCR` we might want `useview_ANCR` so that there is no name collisions between what analysis wants to read from and what projects want to write to.

Then we create a mapping between `formview_XXX` and `useview_YYY` in some table config. Some PL/pgSQL function would read the table config and generate a `useview` for each `formview`.

This covers the 75% use case. However there are some instances where `ANCR` is actually a combination of both `P` and `R` as a union, and one instance where `ANCR` is actually a combination of `P` and `R` as a partial union (`P` + `R` where `R` patient is not in `P`). The mapping might need to be able to define custom SQL or PL/pgSQL rather than just one `formview` mapped onto a `useview`.

title: Access person/place profile's fields from within a report
body:
When starting a new form about a person or place we need to access a variety of fields from their profile. This is used for instance to prepopulate an ID field so that the form is attached to the appropriate person. From a Task the prepopulation is possible using the task rule. We need a way to do this for forms initiated from the person/place's profile page. 

Currently the `place_id`/`patient_id` can be passed to a report. We also want to use other fields such as Name, DOB, LMP, EDD, or any field configured for that project's profiles, so it makes sense to consider the work done in #1260 before tackling this.

This is a followup to #1060 and #1185.

This is the usual URL used by middleware downloads all data:
https://intrahealth-senegal.app.medicmobile.org/medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/export/forms/ISSS?startkey=%5Btrue%2C%22ISSS%22%2C%7B%7D%5D%0A&endkey=%5Btrue%2C%22ISSS%22%2C0%5D&include_docs=true&descending=true

Query string decoded for usual method:

```
{'?startkey': ['[true,"ISSS",{}]\n'],

The data appears to download at approximately 200 kbytes/second from the IHS server instance in Senegal.

The first URL, which should download more total data and require more data processing in Google Apps Script, completes before Google Apps Script times out.

The second URL, which should download less total data and require less data processing in Google Apps Script, times out in Google Apps Script.

title: Enketo: Xpath expression evaluation errors
body:
Some xforms that work with Enketo proper produce errors within the webapp.

We should correct or document differences between the two environments. 

Some of the differences I have noticed so far:
1. round() taking 1 vs 2 arguments
2. now() gives epoch time, today() gives string date, but should be string for both as per [spec](http://opendatakit.github.io/odk-xform-spec/), although the differentiation here may be beneficial
3. in medic, some valid conditions are not expanded properly eg `(A or B) and C` style conditions produce errors

The last one is the highest priority right now because long calculations can be expanded to be valid, but are much less readable and maintainable.

title: create ANC calculations in postgres
body:
Take the middleware calculations for `ANCR manip v2` and make sure the most relevant calculations are handled.

Reviewing the fields, these pop out as useful:
- Real Registry [not applicable for HealthRight ANC unfortunately]. generalize to "Valid?"
- Conception date
- weeks since conception [is this used anywhere anymore? is this worth calculating as part of a view?]
- EDD
- MDD
- ADD
- still pregnant / child likely born

It might be worth breaking these into separate views like:
- metadata
- Current state
- Projection/delivery

Metadata would primarily contain whether a ANC registry form is valid. Other views could filter for only valid registries, which will cut down on some of the data parsing in useful ways the current middleware does not.

title: Enketo: now() and today() give different results, specification says they should return identically-formatted results
body:
The Openrosa specification lists `now()` as being "same as `today()`", but currently one of them returns a Unix epoch timestamp and one returns a Gregorian-formatted date/timestamp. These functions should both return strings that are encoded in the same way. If we need a Unix-style timestamp, we should probably extend the API in a way that doesn't conflict with existing functions.

Split off from #1334, which was moved to Ready with to-do list item #2 still remaining.

title: Modem stops responding to messages & reports after 30 mins
body:
When I leave Medic Mobile running with a modem plugged in, it stops responding after about 30 minutes. It doesn't matter whether or not someone is using the computer in that time, I see the same behavior either way. I also noticed that if I leave the modem plugged in to the point that it stops responding, if I turn Medic Mobile OFF then turn it ON then it starts sending and receiving messages again. There was also one time where I left the modem plugged in and computer on for a few days while I was out of the office. When I got back, the messages that were sent in the interim downloaded into Medic Mobile. Another time I left the computer off and messages that were sent did not get downloaded into Medic Mobile when I started the computer up again (both of these cases were over 3-4 days).

I sent my server logs and user feedback to @browndav. Audit logs couldn't be downloaded because there is a message with an emoji somewhere in there that is breaking the download. See #1389 for more on that.

title: Allow client-side caching of static resources

The most suitable approach to this seems to be to serve an `etag` header from either `medic-api` or `nginx` containing the hash of the file's contents.

title: Task generator performance
body:
Every interaction with the TaskGenerator gets all the contacts and reports from the database, compiles the task rules, and generates the tasks. This is now proving a performance bottleneck.

Some ideas to improve performance:
1. cache results in the task generator and expire the cache every x minutes
2. cache results in the task generator and listen for changes to reports or contacts to expire the cache
3. use a changes listener and keep nools running and provide new facts to the engine on change

Currently the user provided configuration has to decide whether tasks are emitted based on the relevant date. It might be better to have the nools configuration emit all tasks and filter in the task generator. That way items to show could change over time without rerunning the rules which would be particularly useful for option 3.

title: Longpoll requests are being cancelled
body:
Logged in to lg.dev as the restricted user.

In my Network all longpoll requests get cancelled at exactly 30 seconds:

![network](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/2064938/10871509/0f33b42a-814e-11e5-8867-44f0c3cbd939.png)

The requests that get cancelled are:

```
https://lg.dev.medicmobile.org/medic/_changes?timeout=25000&heartbeat=10000&filter=_doc_ids&doc_ids=%5B%22_design%2Fmedic%22%5D&since=6993&limit=25&_nonce=1446409895241&feed=longpoll
https://lg.dev.medicmobile.org/medic/_changes?timeout=25000&style=all_docs&heartbeat=10000&filter=medic%2Fdoc_by_place&id=6850E77F-5FFC-9B01-8D5B-3D6E33DFA73E&since=6991&limit=100&_nonce=1446409916623&feed=longpoll
```

But the following one succeeds. Note the absence of "longpoll" which means it's a single request but otherwise identical to the above:

```
https://lg.dev.medicmobile.org/medic/_changes?timeout=25000&style=all_docs&heartbeat=10000&filter=medic%2Fdoc_by_place&id=6850E77F-5FFC-9B01-8D5B-3D6E33DFA73E&since=6991&limit=100&_nonce=1446409916390
```

We also get a lot of recurring errors in the console (spurious CORS errors omitted for clarity):

```
Error watching for changes on the design doc e
Uncaught (in promise) e
Error watching for changes on the design doc e
Error watching for changes on the design doc e
Uncaught (in promise) e
Error watching for changes on the design doc e
```

It looks like pouchdb expects couchdb should timeout cleanly after 25000 but from [the docs](https://couchdb.readthedocs.org/en/1.4.x/changes.html), if a heartbeat is supplied couchdb ignores the timeout.

> heartbeat: Period in milliseconds after which an empty line is sent in the results. Only applicable for longpoll or continuous feeds. Overrides any timeout to keep the feed alive indefinitely.

On my local machine without nginx these requests remain pending forever which is why I suspect it's nginx that's doing the request cancellation.

Initially I thought this might be part of our replication issues ( #1341 ) but replication appears to work as expected so I think it just causes lots of unnecessary connections and confusing error messages.

The fix is to configure nginx to have a longer (infinite?) timeout on any longpoll request. Also consider patching pouchdb so the timeout header is only included when the heartbeat header is not.

title: BACK button from newly-created contact is weird
body:
As per https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/issues/1459#issuecomment-152605054 and report from @joshnesbit, when you create a new contact and then hit the `<` button (or press browser back button), you are returned to the New Contact/New Family form.
# Steps to reproduce
1. log in
2. browse to _Contacts_
3. _Add Family_
4. save family
5. observe that you are now viewing the family's content page
6. click the `<` button, or press **BACK** button
7. observe you are now back at the _New Family_ form (although without content)
# Expected behaviour
## Pressing `<`

Seems intuitive to me that this would take you back to the list of contacts.  **However**, this may be because I am used to the app in desktop mode, so the list view feels like it's to the left of the content view.  This may not be a natural association for mobile users... or it may be, as LEFT and BACK are commonly linked.
## Pressing browser **BACK**

Not sure what should happen there.  Stay consistent with the `<`?  Stay consistent with the literal browsing history?

@abbyad @Lesterng would be interested in your thoughts on this.

title: How does one use medic-data to populate a local couchdb as would be seen in medic-os distro?
body:
I'm trying to run integration testing on TravisCI.

For my own integration testing environment, I was running a medic-os image. Here's how many records it has and what databases are on it:

```
$ curl http://bryan:password@192.168.56.101/_all_dbs
["_replicator","_users","dashboard","medic","medic-reporter"]
$ curl http://192.168.56.101/medic/_all_docs > docs
$ wc -l docs
3655 docs
```

Travis doesn't have access to my medic-os VM, but it does have CouchDB installed. I've been having problems with Travis using medic-data.

I made a chroot with couchdb in it to try this for myself. I use these settings and run `make install settings gardener load` to populate CouchDB.

```
export DEMOS_COUCHDB="http://localhost:5984"
export PRELOAD_APP_DATA="diy"
export PRELOAD_APP_MARKET="release"
```

I assume the make targets for `compact copy archive` are for packaging the couchdb up for distribution, which is not my intention.

When I check the current state of the `medic` database, there are far fewer docs:

```
# curl -X GET http://127.0.0.1:5984/_all_dbs
["_replicator","_users","dashboard","medic","medic-reporter"]
# curl -X GET http://127.0.0.1:5984/medic/_all_docs > docs

If I try the demo dataset, I get an error:

# make install settings gardener load

title: Replace bower with npm
body:
We use both bower and npm in webapp which causes unnecessary complexity at build time. Switch all the bower dependencies to npm dependencies and `require` the modules so browserify compiles them in. This will make getting sourcemaps ( #1169 ) much easier.

Possible issues:
- Bower flattens the dependency tree so you only get one version of each library. Make sure `npm dedupe` is run as part of the build process which attempts to do a similar thing but less aggressively. Ensure that the final minified file size isn't too much larger than the previous inbox.js + dependencies.js.
- This will result in only a single js import (inbox.js) rather than dependencies.js and inbox.js. We initially split the files because of a bug in Chrome storing large files in the appcache. I think this bug only affected private browsing mode which isn't currently supported. If this is still an issue we can make a dependencies.js but having a separate js file that just requires all the libraries we don't call directly, and browserify that.

title: Warn users, or prevent them from using android app, when device date is set incorrectly
body:
A common problem reported by LG is that CHPs will swap SIMs or battery-out restart their phones, so losing the time & date settings.  When the app is restarted with a date far in the past, _Tasks_ will no longer be correctly calculated.

A suggested way to handle this is record the "previous start time" of the app.  When restarting, if the new start time is less than the last start time, show the user a warning, or block them from using the app.  E.g.

> Your phone's date is set in the past.  Reported date:
>   1 January 1970
> Please update the phone date.
> [ _ignore_ ] [ _exit_ ]

Currently if you want to check if app is up-to-date, you need to check both _About_ page, and the android _Applications Info_ screen or appstore.  Would be very helpful if the `medic-android` version number were included on the _About_ page next to the `medic-webapp` version.  Will save a lot of headache and potential for mistake when checking 10s of phones.

Expected app version is the human-readable one (e.g. `0.1.111`), not the `int` that android uses internally.

title: Server side replication performance analysis

title: Tighten up enketo prepopulation tests
body:
Tests in `tests/karma/unit/services/enketo-prepopulation-data.js` could have more specific URL selecters for where they expect to find `inputs` data, e.g.:

``` js
chai.expect(xml.find('data person last_name')[0].innerHTML).to.equal(data.person.last_name);
```

cold actually become:

``` js
chai.expect(xml.find('data > person > last_name')[0].innerHTML).to.equal(data.person.last_name);
```

This should make the tests more reliable, and clearer in where they are putting data.  We've had a few regressions in this area, so feels worthwhile.

title: Forms save unformatted phone numbers
body:
phone-widget.js will check if a number is valid and block submission if not (that's good), but it will not format the number to international format before saving. 
So we are saving '06 77 88 99 00' for instance, as opposed to '+33677889900'.
Which means if the default country code is changed, numbers are messed up.

UX note: within a given country, seeing '06 77 88 99 00' is much more human-readable. If all your project is in France, you don't want to see '+33677889900' everywhere. So we should add a display format.

title: Replication performance: PouchDB may be downloading more docs than it needs to
body:
pouch is generating a query similar to this:

`/medic/_changes?timeout=25000&style=all_docs&heartbeat=10000&filter=medic%2Fdoc_by_place&_nonce=1450453351782`

the problem is in the `style` value:

> `style` _(string)_ – Specifies how many revisions are returned in the changes array. The default, `main_only`, will only return the current “winning” revision; `all_docs` will return all leaf revisions (including conflicts and deleted former conflicts).
> –_http://docs.couchdb.org/en/latest/api/database/changes.html_

Is there an obvious reason why pouch would need `all_docs` (as it does currently) instead of `main_only`?

title: Investigate pouch attachment downloads

> Using the `attachments` parameter to include attachments in the changes feed is not recommended for large attachment sizes. Also note that the Base64-encoding that is used leads to a 33% overhead (i.e. one third) in transfer size for attachments.
> –_http://docs.couchdb.org/en/latest/api/database/changes.html_

title: Improve ng-repeat rendering?
body:
>  If you are working with objects that have an identifier property, you should track by the identifier instead of the whole object. Should you reload your data later, `ngRepeat` will not have to rebuild the DOM elements for items it has already rendered, even if the JavaScript objects in the collection have been substituted for new ones. For large collections, this significantly improves rendering performance. If you don't have a unique identifier, track by `$index` can also provide a performance boost. 
> –_https://docs.angularjs.org/api/ng/directive/ngRepeat_

We should probably be using `track by item._id` in most of our ng-repeats

title: form metadata cannot be parsed on 0.6 systems
body:
Due to the switch from forms defined in JSON to forms defined in XML to support Enketo, the existing code to interpret couch data into one view per form cannot work for 0.6.

Here is the code which currently parses 0.4 JSON form metadata into relevant views:
https://github.com/medic/middleware/blob/master/postgres/formviews.sql#L37-L43

It expects a ddoc to contain `app_settings.forms.<formname>.fields`, which are currently a dictionary/object/hash by field name. The field name (key) is still required, obviously.

It expects `app_settings.form.<formname>.fields.<fieldname>.labels.short.en` to contain the field's English name as text. This is used as the column label for the form field in the form's view.

It expects `app_settings.form.<formname>.fields.<fieldname>.position` to have an integer. This integer sorts the fields so that the form view builder deterministically generates the same columns in the same order every time for any given form view. This is surprisingly important.

title: Detect when pouch has unsynced changes so we can have a simple sync status somewhere
body:
It would be useful, even if just for debug purposes, to be able to tell if everything in a user's pouchdb has been replicated into the cloud.

I was hoping that pouchdb replication would provide useful information. So far I've had a super quick look at the event handlers you can add to the replication call: http://pouchdb.com/api.html#replication

Unfortunately they don't seem massively useful by themselves. You effectively have `active`, `paused` and `change` to play with:
-  `change` fires _when a change has been replicated_.
- `active` and `pause` are switched between fairly regularly when pouch thinks it might have something useful to do but then realises for whatever reason it doesn't. 
- `pause` is the end state (since we are continuously replicating) regardless of whether we have changes that need to be duplicated.

Note that there is no obvious indication that you're offline, just that you're not currently actively replicating.

One possibility would be to make sure we funnel all our pouch db put calls through one wrapping function which keeps a list of all the document ids that pass through, and then remove them as they work their way through the change event handler. We could then bind that list (or a count of that list) to the UI and use it to display our sync indication.

title: Redesign filters / search
body:
There are likely two (or more) issues here, but for the sake of documenting the conversation thus far: 

In discussing bulk delete (issue 1000), we want to improve the way that users can search or filter reports in order to bulk delete / edit them. Most of bulk delete will be done by managers/trainers in the web app, though filtering applies to both the reports tab (primarily: bulk delete) and contacts tabs (primarily: bulk message). Improving these filters is lower priority than the issue 1000 but we wanted to think about them together. 

In the CHW mobile app, filters and search are most relevant to the Contacts tab since CHWs will have less interaction with their history/reports tab in general and less need to filter their reports since they can only view the ones they have submitted. In the contacts tab, filters can help them identify important types of patients, such as "high risk pregnancies." There are important usability considerations that must be met in order for these to be utilized by CHWs. One option is to preset a number of "quick search" filters in our design phase. 

There are a few exploratory mockups for using filters in the mobile app here:
for contacts: https://moqups.com/joshnesbit/1fF4IwJA/p:af597fa84
for reports: https://moqups.com/joshnesbit/1fF4IwJA/p:aa5c8f123

title: fix initial replication bug so all docs are synced. Issue #1695
body:
DBSync was using `live:true` on all replication requests so that will only get new changes.  It does not initiate replication from update_seq 0. This could be the cause of the perceived "app never finishes installing" problem.  Trying to think of bad repercussions of this change but not coming up with much.

I added an extra replication that is `live:false` and only makes the continuous replication after it completes.  There is no `complete` event for `live:true` replication requests becuase it's designed to never complete.

title: Review and merge LiveList to improve rendering performance
body:

title: XForm field with `calculate="today()"` gets wrong date in certain timezones
body:
A XForm field with `calculate="today()"` gets yesterday's date for computers in EST and PST, but the correct date for a computer in GMT.

Working theory is that the date value _in the current timezone_ is obtained for today at midnight GMT, which results in yesterday's date for Western timezones.

If the `today()` is used in a calculation (eg `decimal-date-time(today())`) it appears as expected. Also, today() seems to have different behaviour in Enketo proper, which maintains the time information.
## Sample form

```
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<h:html xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2002/xforms" xmlns:ev="http://www.w3.org/2001/xml-events" xmlns:h="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:jr="http://openrosa.org/javarosa" xmlns:orx="http://openrosa.org/xforms" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema">
  <h:head>
    <h:title>Test: today</h:title>
    <model>
      <instance>
        <test-today id="test-today" version="2016-02-05">
          <value/>
          <verification/>
          <note/>
        </test-today>
      </instance>
      <bind calculate="today()" nodeset="/test-today/value" type="string"/>
      <bind calculate="decimal-date-time(today())-decimal-date-time(../value)" nodeset="/test-today/verification" type="string"/>
      <bind nodeset="/test-today/note" readonly="true()" type="string"/>
    </model>
  </h:head>
  <h:body>
    <input ref="/test-today/note">
      <label>**today() set as ../value**: <output value=" /test-today/value "/>

**verify today() in calculation vs standalone value:**
decimal-date-time(today()) - decimal-date-time(../today/) = <output value=" /test-today/verification "/>
_should be 0_</label>
    </input>
  </h:body>
</h:html>
```

title: Minimise templated HTML
body:
Looks like the following ngTemplate options could be worthwhile:

> ### htmlmin
> 
> > Object containing [htmlmin options](https://github.com/gruntjs/grunt-contrib-htmlmin) that will _significantly_ reduce
> > the filesize of the compiled templates.
> 
> Without this, the HTML (whitespace and all) will be faithfully compiled
> down into the final `.js` file.  Minifying that file will only cut down
> on the _Javascript_ code, not the _HTML_ within the strings.
> 
> I recommend using the following settings for production:
> 
> ``` js
> htmlmin: {
>   collapseBooleanAttributes:      true,
>   collapseWhitespace:             true,
>   removeAttributeQuotes:          true,
>   removeComments:                 true, // Only if you don't use comment directives!
>   removeEmptyAttributes:          true,
>   removeRedundantAttributes:      true,
>   removeScriptTypeAttributes:     true,
>   removeStyleLinkTypeAttributes:  true
> }
> ```
> 
> If you are using SVG, please make sure you set `keepClosingSlash:true`
> 
> – https://github.com/ericclemmons/grunt-angular-templates#htmlmin

title: App doesn't handle authentication invalidating over time gracefully
body:
CouchDB authentication is only valid for a (configurable) small amount of time, which is refreshed on every request. I think the default is 10 minutes. If you leave your phone / browser for awhile and come back you will have lost that, and will need to reauthenticate.

Here for example. I opened the app on mah tecno, and then left it for 30 min or so. I then `grunt dev`'d to force a design doc change:

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/583851/13142900/2877392c-d638-11e5-9077-e953b0f3e175.png)

The most critical upshot of this is that replication can silently fail (in both directions) once you get into this state. For example, if I then try to change a contact on Cptn. Tecno. Everything looks fine on the phone, but in the log I get.

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/583851/13142939/6af750f2-d638-11e5-9eb1-c53d4481f84a.png)

There are two obvious solutions: 
- Have the couchdb authentication timeout as effectively infinite. I believe this may be what is happening with some clients now. It's not ideal.
- Have a log in modal that we pop up and use to refresh credentials
- Tell the user they have been logged out and then force a a page refresh

title: Simplify medic specific XForm notation
body:
The goal of this issue is to simplify the customization needed to make XForms work within the webapp. We currently use some special notation within the XForm to make it work well with the webapp (eg to assign the form to a contact, or to display only certain fields in the Reports/History tab). 

Here is a proposal for some of the changes, which may help increase performance by reducing field duplication, reduce time to build forms, and make the data more easily accessible for exports as well as for calculations in task/target rules.
### `inputs` group

The fields in this group are currently populated automatically when the form is opened from a Contacts tab profile. Similarly, when form is opened from a Task the fields are populated by the task rule. When opening the form from Reports/History tab we cannot use the same inputs group and also hide it when it is prepopulated. The workaround includes having the patient or place info being selected in a separate group if not already populated, then coalescing these in the outputs. Eg:

``` xml
          <inputs>
            <patient>
              <_id/>
              <name/>
              <date_of_birth/>
            </patient>
          </inputs>
          <g_inputs>
            <_id/>
            <name/>
            <date_of_birth/>
          </g_inputs>
          <outputs>
            <patient_id/>
            <patient_name/>
            <patient_dob/>
            ...
          </outputs>
```

The suggestion here would be to use a `inputs/source` field so we can avoid the duplication and simplify the form creation.  `inputs/source` would be one of `contact`, `task`, `user`, with the later as the default if it is not set programmatically by via a profile or task. The resulting data model would be:

``` xml
          <inputs>
            <source>user</source>
            <patient>
              <_id/>
              <name/>
              <date_of_birth/>
            </patient>
          </inputs>
```

Aside from populating the source field we would need to check the `inputs/patient/_id` instead of `outputs/patient_id` when associating the report to the person. 
### Person, not Patient

We could also use this opportunity to use the more generic `person` rather than `patient` since reports are not always about patients (eg a report may be about a CHW as completed by their manager).
### Make all the fields accessible

We should assign all the field to json, not just the outputs section as done [here](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/167a812e2afc6be62d6b3424fe527cf9b9dc9a44/static/js/services/enketo.js#L233)

Right now we need to duplicate fields into the `outputs` section to have it in the `doc.fields`, which determines which elements are shown in the Reports/History tab, which are accessible programmatically from rules, and which are available for export. This can reduce performance due to extra fields, and makes it difficult to access the data that was initially omitted from the `outputs`. 

By default we would show all fields, and hide those that we don't want to show. This is currently possible with `tag="hidden"` in data model (https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/issues/1476). Nested fields are not shown elegantly right now because all the subfields are shown as JSON, but we can chose to hide these fields until we display them better via https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/issues/1473.

title: Make sure users eventually update their app
body:
If a user is presented with the update dialog and they hit cancel, there are no more (obvious) opportunities for them to install that update. Note that "install that update" really just means refresh the page.

This is probably important, since I imagine if we deploy an update we want people to be moved to it as quickly as is convenient.

It is also understandable that users can cancel the update dialog at that specific moment, as they may be in the middle of something.

This may require UX design.

Two options that Alex and I discussed:
- Storing if there is an unapplied update in the `$scope` and folding a refresh into the next action. For example, saving a form would save the form and then trigger a refresh.
- Storing if there is an unapplied update in the `$scope` and adding an idle timeout. For example, if you needed to refresh and were idle for more than 5min trigger a refresh.

Another that Estelle mentioned would be to re-popup the dialogue every N minutes if the update was not applied.

Note that as long as there is no unsaved data refreshes should be safe in any network situation.

title: Potential memory leak with our use of PouchDB
body:
I have created heap snapshots, dumps and CPU profiles of all this. I will upload them to drive once I have the bandwidth to do so, and link them here.

To reproduce:
- (potentially) connect to a remote host like lg-testing
- Clean your android install
- Configure the app to point to and log in as someone who has production-levels of data. I.e. more than demo on lg.dev
- Let the whole thing sync. Feel free to hang out on the about page, which should be doing nothing at all.
- Once the sync is complete, note that:
  -- The CPU is still doing a bunch of stuff. A pull from the profile I took looks like this:
  ![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/583851/13597765/493b1abe-e52b-11e5-85c3-c033295a2237.png)
  ![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/583851/13597788/619030d6-e52b-11e5-9f76-53b87be2287d.png)
  -- Moving around the application is incredibly slow. Various tap indicators (the tab icon changing colour, the highlight on selecting a form element) can take many seconds to appear.
- Force close the app. You can do this by removing it from the task manager or by going into the application settings page and actually force closing it. Interestingly `location.reload()` doesn't seem to be enough, though I should test that more.
  - Open the app again. Note that once it's done initial loading it's lightning (ish) fast.

Here is a screenshot of the samples I took. The only interesting thing to note is the heapdump sizes on disk:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/583851/13597963/4f4c49d6-e52c-11e5-89dd-82ce29913f96.png)
So we're looking at ~100mb after a sync, ~50mb fresh after re-opening, and ~70mb after clicking around and having it cache forms and what-not.

title: Unbranded container, first-run URL input: Once an invalid URL is tested, subsequent valid URLs fail
body:
If I install the unbranded container and get the server address right the first time, I see a request to `/setup/poll` that results in an HTTP 200, and all is well.

If I purposely input a server name that exists but responds to `/setup/poll` with a 404, I'll be told that it's not a valid application URL. Great so far.

If I _then_ try a known-valid server name after the failure immediately above, it too gets flagged as invalid despite the fact that it's a real `medic-webapp` server. On the server side, I see an HTTP 401:

```
127.0.0.1 - - [11/Mar/2016:00:49:49 +0000] "GET /setup/poll HTTP/1.0" - - "-" "Dalvik/2.1.0 (Linux; U; Android 6.0.1; Nexus 6 Build/MMB29Q)"

==> /srv/storage/medic-core/couchdb/logs/couch.log <==
[Fri, 11 Mar 2016 00:49:49 GMT] [info] [<0.5997.0>] 49.xxx.xxx.220 - - GET /setup/poll 401
```

An easy workaround it to just uninstall and reinstall the APK, but we should figure out what credentials are riding along with that `/setup/poll` request, if any, that are leading to the 401.

title: SIMapp file building only works on Windows
body:
To generate the .trb file to push on the SIMapp, you need an old version of gcc (because the whole simapp is not supported any more by Bladox). The official supported tools are on windows.

PMs are on windows. TLs are on linux or macos or windows. 

The workflow right now is to download the tools, and then : 
- on windows, run [cygwin](https://www.cygwin.com/) (basically linux tools for windows), and build.
- on linux, run a windows VM, run cygwin in the windows VM, and build. (linux on windows on linux! True story.)
- on mac, you can try using old versions of gcc, Eugene tried to get that to work and got stuck. Otherwise go the VM way too.

Another option is to run a VM with medic-os in it, because the appropriate tools are all packaged in it. However, we ran it in VirtualBox (because it's free), which doesn't get the USB ports right, so we couldn't push the files to the simapp. Fail.

Note that the simapp is probably going to be discontinued, in favor of medic collect or full android app. We should assess how much work we should be putting into this workflow.

title: Iterative steps can overlap in time causing redundancies
body:
I had the sleep interval set for 1 minute and doc size set to 3000.

The design doc didn't get pulled in until the very last set, so during the last iteration, all the XML data was being parsed and it took longer than 1 minute.

Meanwhile, the 1 minute timer went off to start the next iteration, which amazingly happened in parallel instead of waiting. Then that iteration, too, began parsing all the data.

In the end, this resulted in duplicate copies of all the parsed form data.

I need to block the next iteration timer from going off until the previous one is done. In fact, I didn't think this was possible but apparently it is.

title: Decision about dependency versioning
body:
Our current [`package.json`](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/develop/package.json) has a mix of `~` and `^` semvers in it. It is unclear how intentional or not this is.

We should:
- Pick a dependency strategy that will be obvious when you look at `package.json`, so that everyone easily keeps to the strategy
- Make is clear when we are deviating from the strategy and why, so that people don't think it's a "mistake" and fix it later (ie we're holding back this version for these reasons)
- Change `package.json` to fit this
## Option A: Loose versioning

_(use `^` as a default, if not note why)_

``` js
  "dependencies": {
    "angular": "^1.5.3",
    "jquery": "~2.1.4", // 2.2.x breaks enketo, see #1234
    "enketo-core": "git://github.com/enketo/enketo-core.git#4.5.5", // not yet on npm, see #5678
    "underscore": "1.8.3", // 1.8.4 has security issues, see #9012
  }
```
## Option B: Automatic patches

_(use `~` as a default, if not note why)_

``` js

title: Improve rendering performance for administrators on large data sets
body:
There are a few things that struggle to render quickly on my (beefy) laptop if you log in as an admin on a dataset the size of LG's (which is just forming, and presumably soon will be _much_ larger).

Currently we've disabled nools for administrators (ie they can't see CHP's tasks), as the massive amount of processing required for such a large dataset was causing huge browser freezes.

There are other issues. Search filters are especially noticeable, presumably because they have to load and render all contacts into the filter drop-downs. This is my network tab after doing a refresh, as admin, on the contacts page, on a server running locally using a PROD-sized DB:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/583851/14612066/3dc82cda-058d-11e6-88dd-16d594c6bae8.png)
41 of those mb are getting all the contacts, and about 10 of those seconds were (presumably) the search bar parsing and rendering after it had downloaded all of those contacts. The bandwidth issue (which tbf is made _much_ worse by the fact that when you work locally you don't have gzip enabled) will be dealt with in: _(a soon to be created and linked ticket)_

As I see it there are three ways to solve this problem:
- Optimise slow interactions so they perform much better with large datasets without changing the UI. Note that this might not be possible in some cases, i.e. we actually need to generate the DOM for all of the contacts for filtering
- Change each UI component that is slow to first have a filter for which CHP you wish to be. For example, step 0 of showing tasks would be to select a CHP, and then we would load their tasks. Or the contact filter would be changed to only allow listing high-level contacts (ie branches) or people / families for a specific CHP.
- Remove / change all interactions that are slow for admins (ie remove tasks, only show high level contacts such as branches) and then have a button that allows you to masquerade as a CHP _side wide_. Once you were a CHP you'd see the Tasks page and you'd see their tasks etc.

The third option may be the best, as it might be possible to just change one piece of code somewhere in the auth system, as well as a bit of UI changes (so that you know who you're masquerading to be) as opposed to making specific UI changes for each potentially slow element.

Regardless, I imagine the answer will be heavily dependent on what admins _actually do_, which is not something I'm overly familiar with.

title: Understand admin bandwidth concerns and optimise accordingly
body:
We have generally been of the impression that admins had great internet, and fast computers. This has led to a design where admins don't have a local DB, and everything is pulled over the network. This is potentially looking like it may not really pan out.

For example, in LG PROD (which is a small dataset in the grand scheme of things, they're just getting going) here is what my machine downloads when I refresh the page:

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/583851/14612566/a0416a78-058f-11e6-84ee-6ebba7b690c1.png)

Things you will notice:
- gzip is super important for us
- We download a huge amount of stuff, and there is a reasonable chance that we download the same thing multiple times

It ended up totalling ~12mb or so, which is either OK if you have great internet, or utterly terrible if you are on mobile internet.

This ticket is for us to answer these questions:
- What are the bandwidth expectations of admin users? Will they have unlimited bandwidth or should we be trying to target a rough amount used per day / month?
- What is the expected internet quality, re: fiber vs. broadband vs. 3g?

Which in turn helps us understand how much we care about this. Note: LG's dataset right now is presumably nowhere near as large as it will get when they start deploying to new locations, so these numbers will all go up quite a bit over time.

title: Run e2e tests in new db. Issue: #1825
CouchDB is not authorized to return `_all_docs` listed from POST but can return docs listed from GET
body:
The couch-to-postgres adapter uses `_all_docs` first to fetch all UUIDs in the system using `include_docs=false`.

Once all UUIDs are fetched, only the necessary UUIDs are requested from `_all_docs` by sending a POST with a list of UUIDs and using `include_docs=true`.

With the analytics user, I am able to GET `_all_docs` even with `include_docs=true`, but I cannot get a subset using POST `_all_docs` (regardless of `include_docs`). I guess POST might be used for other purposes so the entire verb is blocked from analytics?

Is there a way we can resolve this so the adapter does not need admin access? It might not be possible without fully rewriting the adapter to use a changes feed or something.

title: Establish a template for creating new databases
body:
Right now we have two schemas. three roles, and a set of default permissions for two of the users.

These can be created inside a template and then `CREATE DATABASE x WITH OWNER y TEMPLATE z` where z is the template containing all that nifty stuff.

This is all stuff that needs to be done by the postgresql superuser. So it can't be done by the adapter, it really needs to go at a level closer to #1801 

It might be nice if we can find a way to version control these settings so that they get deployed reliably.

title: Import full data set
body:
We need to be able to fully set up an instance with realistic data for testing (eg #2121, #1872, #1836, #2152) as well as demos. Right now this could be done manually, but is very time consuming and not practical.

Here are the known components, some of which are already automated and documented, others not:
- **Settings:** can already be loaded via [this script](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/blob/master/scripts/upload_app_settings.sh), or [this script](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/blob/master/scripts/update_tasks.sh) if pulling in rules.
- **Contacts:** can be added manually or by importing via the Contacts tab UI. The later requires careful creation of JSON for the People and Places, which is **not easily done**. This should be replaced with something simpler, perhaps using `Contacts` API endpoint.
- **Messages:** can be loaded using a [script](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/develop/scripts/load_messages.js).
- **Forms:** can be added via [script](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/develop/scripts/upload_xform.sh), as is currently being done for new projects
- **Form Submissions:** could be meticulously crafted and uploaded via couch, but this is **not practical for general use.** We should look at simplifying this step.
- **Users:** being automated with #2046 

Aside from the individual components we should look at the best way to do the entire setup, which can then be used in our e2e testing or for preparing live demos. Having API endpoints for Contacts, Messages, and Forms also makes it easier for integrations with 3rd party systems (eg OpenMRS, DHIS2).

title: Make single Modal service
Make the Search service return more relevant results
body:
Right now the free-text portion of the search service works querying a view that has an `emit` for every "token" of every document (that we care about, i.e. all Contacts). If a token is deemed to be a string it's broken up on space and emitted N times for each of _those_ tokens.

It is done this way because we do not impose a particular schema, so there is no "white list" of fields that we should be searching.

The downside of this is that it often isn't amazing at relevance. It returns _everything_ associated with your particular query.

This is particularly obvious that we now use the Search service in dropdowns:

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/583851/14918627/e51f6d76-0e1c-11e6-8625-2c27d25b5fbd.png)

He's there, just buried:

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/583851/14918643/f2f4363e-0e1c-11e6-8cdc-17c69c9bfedf.png)

**We need to work out how to make Search more relevant.**
# Options
## Weighted tokens

One idea is to make the view "weighted". You would change the view to, for every token, `emit([doc._id, token], 1);`. We would then group by the first key (the document id) and reduce by the value (a 1 for each result).
## Or something else?

However, I'm not convinced that weighted tokens will necessarily work for us in this case. That algorithm gives preference to documents that contain that value _more_, but that isn't necessarily going to lend itself to more relevance. In the above example all of those probably contain the same number of "victor" tokens.

There is currently undocumented sneaky hax in there, so you can do this:

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/583851/14918892/082d08a4-0e1e-11e6-9a8f-83bd2d13683e.png)

I wonder if we need to think more in this direction?

title: Change field names and include a new training field for contacts
body:
`form_metadata` currently has fields called `chw` and `chw_area` which are UUIDs pointing to a specific CHW and CHW Area respectively.

Whereas most UUIDs pointing to other objects are postfixed with `_uuid`, these two are not.

We should rename these to `chw_uuid` and `chw_area_uuid` respectively. Unfortunately these two fields are incredibly critical to a number of existing analytics queries. In order to support field name transition, we probably want to support `chw` _and_ `chw_uuid` containing the same data, and `chw_area` and `chw_area_uuid` containing the same data.

While we're about, it sounds like there could be a training field added to a CHP Area someday in the future. In the meantime we can build a placeholder for this by adding a `training BOOLEAN` which is set to `FALSE` until that piece is implemented in Couch somewhere.

The form_metadata table is built here: https://github.com/medic/medic-analytics/blob/master/libs/xmlforms/pgsql.js#L40-L43

Form data is written to form_metadata here: https://github.com/medic/medic-analytics/blob/master/libs/xmlforms/pgsql.js#L70-L90

title: Non-XML form view support
body:
For 2.6 systems with XML forms, each form gets a table called `formview_{FORMNAME}_{FORMVERSION}`. Although they are tables, the `formview` predates working on 2.6.

For 0.4, each `formview_{FORMNAME}` is actually a view of the table containing all the JSON. As I work on an old 0.4 system, I realized this process of generating formviews automatically from JSON is not build into the adapter, but rather remains as a pl/pgsql function called `build_formviews()` in this file:
https://github.com/medic/middleware/blob/master/postgres/formviews.sql

For the old 0.4 systems, a bit of doing-this-by-hand is going to be required, and such support requests will be finite/limited. I'm not concerned about automating `build_formviews()` for them.

For 2.6 systems which might have forms that are _not_ XML, we should have some solution. If those forms end up looking like the 0.4 forms, then the above `build_formviews()` function should make its way into the adapter itself at some point.

If all forms, regardless of ODK and other considerations, end up being in XML for some reason, then no action is necessary.

title: Bootstrapping postgres tends to have different behavior than keeping postgres updated
body:
In practice, I found out that bootstrapping postgres from couch tend to operate differently than running the adapter on a populated database. So far, these differences have been acted on by the way in which the adapter is called: the adapter does not make any such distinction.

Technically, there doesn't have to be a difference, but practically there probably should be.

Let's use an example of a CouchDB database with between 50,000 and 300,000 docs (both are actual use cases I've dealt with already). Postgres is being freshly applied, so it has 0 docs in it.

node has limited system memory available. The following link talks about some of this, including the `--max-old-space-size` workaround I've had to use for dealing with audit logs. Any large docs, or any large enough set of small docs, can crash node with out of memory error.
https://bugs.chromium.org/p/v8/issues/detail?id=847

There is a balance between fetching enough data from couch in a single call to not run out of memory, but reduce the overall number of HTTP requests sent to the CouchDB server. We probably don't want a separate GET for each of 50,000 to 300,000 docs. There is a related balance in the interval between HTTP requests sent to CouchDB. If we did call a separate GET for each doc, we'd probably not want to do so in a very short interval of time.

Both the maximum number of docs fetched per interval and the interval itself are settings for the adapter. When actually running the adapter, we can get away with 100 docs every 15 minutes pretty safely (both staying on top of new data and not hitting out-of-memory when audit logs or very large docs come in). However, if we used that combination when there are 0 docs in postgres, we're talking about at least 5.2 solid days to get to 50,000 until we're "caught up" (which, by five days later, we probably aren't caught up).

So for bootstrapping, we might want to crank that up to 4000 docs every 3 minutes. We certainly don't expect that kind of throughput in normal use, so we wouldn't want that to be the normal settings after we've bootstrapped.

The problem is that when there are very large docs (audit_logs in 0.4 systems, possibly some kind of doc that might happen in 2.6 sometime in the future), we'll hit an out of memory and the adapter outright crashes when pulling 4000. So for some systems, babysitting the adapter is required while bootstrapping.

Perhaps there is some way to see how large the next batch of X docs is before downloading them, which can help generate a dynamic doc threshold when bootstrapping (or anytime really). Regardless, it might be worthwhile to consider the bootstrapping case and how we can incorporate it into the adapter (rather than babysitting or running with two different sets of settings).

title: Standardize table and column for the adapter
body:
When the adapter was first written, there were very few absolutes. It was meant to be very flexible.

The table and column are extra variables which allow someone to _potentially_ add a new column to an existing table.

So we have two variables which need special handling and a bunch of testing for various cases (is there a table? if there is a table, is there a column?).

The analytics stuff, in many cases, does not have access to those variables.So making them variable _really_ messes with analytics.

In practice we've been using the table `couchdb` and column `doc`.

If the table doesn't exist, then we should add it with the column. No other logic should be required for initialization of `lib/couch2pg`, so that excess can be removed from the code and the unit and integration testing. We can remove the table and column variables entirely and hard code couchdb and doc.

The reduced variables might also ease configuration stuff related to #1800

title: Move initial replication into bootstrap. Issue: #2394
body:
This moves the initial replication into the bootstrap layer which means it runs once per user+device+server, not every page load. The user will now see a spinner while the initial replication is going. This means they won't be querying the database until all the data is up to date which speeds up the overall initial replication time.

One downside is because this is running before Angular has started it's not easy to capture the replication data to show on the About page. I've tried to capture the same data and output it to the console. That combined with the fact the app won't load until the replication completes hopefully gives enough info about the state of replication. I'd welcome feedback here about how to include more information.

With this patch initial startup takes about 3.5 minutes with a real user on a tecno on a real server which includes downloading static resources, doing initial replication, getting the ddoc, starting angular, and waiting for the rules engine to start up. CPU usage is about 2-3% above baseline during the replication phase.

title: Restructure git branches
body:
### Master

Have a `master` branch as the default github branch. Commits are made directly into this branch or via PRs to this branch. Travis builds and publishes an alpha release every time a commit is made.
### Release branches

Have release branches which branch of `master` and are named `<major>.<minor>.x`, for example "2.6.x". This will gradually diverge from `master` so don't plan to merge this back in, but ensure all changes in the release branch are also in master (either by cherry-picking or merging in either direction). Travis builds and publishes a beta release every time a commit is made to a branch with this form.
### Final releases

Tag a release branch when it's ready for production named `<major>.<minor>.<servicepack>`, for example: "2.6.3". Travis builds and publishes a final release every time a tag is made in this form.

title: column "xyz" of relation "abc" does not exist when writing report data to database
body:
e.g.:

```
error: column "patient_dob" of relation "formview_assessment_2015-11-02" does not exist
    at Connection.parseE (/Users/scdf/Code/Medic/medic-analytics/node_modules/pg/lib/connection.js:539:11)
    at Connection.parseMessage (/Users/scdf/Code/Medic/medic-analytics/node_modules/pg/lib/connection.js:366:17)
    at Socket.<anonymous> (/Users/scdf/Code/Medic/medic-analytics/node_modules/pg/lib/connection.js:105:22)
    at emitOne (events.js:90:13)
    at Socket.emit (events.js:182:7)
    at readableAddChunk (_stream_readable.js:153:18)
    at Socket.Readable.push (_stream_readable.js:111:10)
    at TCP.onread (net.js:529:20)
```

This only occurs when you import a database in batches. This does _not_ mean it's not important: unless you delete everything and regenerate you're always importing in different batches over time.

What it _does_ suggest is that it's something to do with forms having different data in them even though the version is the same. This could be for two reasons:
- The data captured has changed but the version hasn't
- The way we're defining a field to be stored is not consistent across documents (for example, if a field is empty it's not presented to us)

Either way, if we're going to keep the xml extraction we need to deal with this somehow.

title: Design needed : admins sending reports for SMS + web instances
body:
Right now if you're a 0.4 instance, you're an SMS project, and admins send SMS reports with medic-reporter:

When we merge SMS and android in 2.x, we'll have both types of reports enabled, so admins will have to pick between SMS and web form. 
It's possible that a system have only SMS, or only web (XML) forms, or both.

Situations like this are already happening in 0.4 with textforms (JSON) + medic collect (XML), and I think the forms have different names, and separate configs. When updating lg.app to 2.7.2 @sglangevin got this error:

![pasted image at 2016_07_11 04_13 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/2064938/16750591/fa241e26-4826-11e6-87be-2ab7c32d1579.png)

This indicates the "Configuring Type" step has failed. Unfortunately this step ignores any errors so we don't have any more information about what went wrong. Because we were experiencing connection issues at the time I suspect the server was just overloaded and rejected the request.

This step updates some of the Dashboard information about the update which means in this case Dashboard is still reporting 2.7.1 is installed and has an active Update button. Clicking that button gives the following error...

![pasted image at 2016_07_11 04_18 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/2064938/16750636/4204c510-4827-11e6-8aac-63e301816491.png)

title: Sort out roles
body:
Our implementation of roles is complicated. In the UI we only allow configurers to pick one role for a user. Then behind the scenes we [map this to an array of roles](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/master/static/js/controllers/edit-user.js#L48) and store that instead. Then, each of these roles maps to a set of permissions.

Instead, store a single role for the user which maps to a set of permissions.

As part of this refactor update the set of available roles with better names.
- "full access"/"national-manager" should be "admin" (or similar) and probably shouldn't be configurable: https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/issues/2079
- "district-manager" should be "regional-manager" (or similar) as they can operate at any level of the hierarchy.
- "facility-manager" should be removed and existing users migrated to "regional-manager"
- all references to "kujua" should be removed.

title: Always use the same pouchdb configuration
body:
The bootstrap code connects to the local db without passing any options. This means during initial replication auto_compaction is off and the db grows larger than needed until the app starts and compaction is turned on. Getting out of sync on other options would be much more significant (eg: `storage` which would replicate to one place, then try to connect to a different one).

A possible exception is the web worker adapter as we may not want to use it during initial replication.

Use the same configuration everywhere PouchDB instances are constructed. Find a way to ensure the configuration remains consistent, maybe a unit test, or publishing the configuration as a constant, or publishing to resultant PouchDB instance so we only ever make one for local and one for remote.

title: Legacy v0.4.x instances: remove socket limit in medic-api
body:
In https://github.com/medic/medic-api/blob/0.4.x/server.js#L31, we limit the maximum number of Express.js server sockets to 100. This proved unnecessarily low in the 2.8.x/master branch and was removed entirely, effectively making the limit infinite, which worked out okay. We never did the same for the older v0.4.x instances.

Symptom: nginx is timing out while attempting to connect to the local `medic-api` on port 5988. This repeats regularly for a while and then dies down:

```
2016/08/12 18:22:03 [error] 30226#0: *404098 upstream timed out
  (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream,
  client: 127.0.0.1, server: _, request: "GET /medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/add HTTP/1.1",
  upstream: "http://127.0.0.1:5988/medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/add", host: "localhost"
```

Theory: under heavy load, the pool of 100 sockets is exhausted and requests start getting dropped on the floor with no response.

Push an update to v0.4.x that removes `http.globalAgent.maxSockets = 100;` from the bundled Medic API, and does nothing else.

Seemingly unreasonable disk space requirements for 2.7.x to 2.8.0 upgrade
body:
Using a 45GiB production-like dataset, updating from `medic-webapp` version `2.7.2` to `2.8.0-b6` fills a 1 terabyte disk and eventually leads to `502 Bad Gateway` errors. CouchDB reports `{error,enospc}`.

Current understanding: when `medic-webapp` is updated via the Garden dashboard, the `medic` design document is modified. This potentially changes view code, which leads CouchDB to assume the worst and perform a full view regeneration procedure in the background. This procedure eventually fills the disk. One of the newly-generated `.view` files is approximately 40GiB; another is 10GiB.

Expected behavior: Naively, it seems like the space requirement for a full view regeneration should be no more than two times the size of the largest pre-rebuild view. At the very least, it seems like the required space should be no more than two times the total size of all pre-rebuild views (15GiB in this case). How we're regenerating more than 60GiB after a simple design document update is currently outside of my understanding.

To do: figure out why we're using so much space after an update to 2.8.0, then make it stop.
