title: Allow translation to nest another translation key
body:
As mentioned in #4598:
> as part of the [Standard Child Health messaging](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/4155) we are setting up 60 months worth of monthly messages. 

We are setting separate translation keys for each to allow independent changes to each month's message. For now there are three different messages that are repeated 8, 20, and 32 times. To avoid bloating the translations we should allow specifying a translation key within a translation.

For instance, we may want to do something like this:
```properties
month_01 = This is a monthly message
month_02 = ${month_01}
```

title: Make family equity score available for family member task generation and within forms about family members
body:
This feature makes the family equity score available within forms about family members or for generating or updating task schedules for family members. Equity scores can be collected either during family registration or via a form filled in at the family/household level. The scores might impact the frequency at which a CHW should visit a particular household or require the CHW to follow a different pregnancy visit schedule for women in households with lower scores.

The equity score is a measure of wealth. By asking questions about housing materials, possessions, and a few other things, the survey determines which wealth quintile a family falls into. Being in a lower quintile might mean you are less likely to deliver at a health facility or less likely to seek treatment when you are sick. Using these scores to help target households is important in making sure that CHWs can provide equitable care.

Equity scores are somewhat static, but they might be re-evaluated every 6 months or so (schedule would vary by project).

Requirements:
- Equity score for the family is available in forms about all family members
- Equity score for the family can be used to determine task schedules for family members

Acceptance criteria:
- Can access equity score in person-level forms
- Can use equity score to trigger a different task schedule if the score is above/below a certain threshold

title: Support reporting of dates as exact date using text forms
body:
So far our users of Text forms have been reporting on dates of events such as birth of last menstrual period in terms of days or weeks since. In the past its been determined as non-critical when weighed against the likelihood of errors and the degree to which we can validate such field (or group of fields, say if DD MM YYYY were to be treated as different fields) especially when the form contains other fields in addition to the ones that define the date (eg. P MedicID Date of LMP)

This question keeps coming up in conversations about projects including standard and MOH Nepal. From what I know so far, it is likely more valuable on the user's end -- given they would not have to do any maths to deduct the value in terms of weeks or days if they know the date-- vs towards getting more accurate dates for generating relevant schedules -- given the insight that the users are likely to not know the exact date of these events and the schedules are served fine within a window of a week or even a month in case of IMM. Perhaps its worth revisiting and investigating whether and how this would be feasible with text forms. 

There would obviously be various things to think about but one I want to flag outright is that we would need to be able to determine that it is a bikram sambat date for MOH Nepal deployments. 

@abbyad @jillrshah @Dushala -- tagging you all as you are ones I've had this discussion most recently.

cc @diannakane @sglangevin

title: Reports page can mistakenly hide fields
body:
A submitted report may be have fields hidden that should be shown.

**Steps to reproduce**:
 - Write a form with a hidden field whose name is the prefix to another field, or use the one included below
 - Submit that report

**What should happen**:
 - Only the specific field that is marked with `tag="hidden"` should be hidden. In this case it is the `name` field.

**What actually happens**:
 - All fields that start with the same name as the intended hidden field are hidden. In the example below `name2` is greedily hidden, and shouldn't be.

Tested on version 2.14.3


## Example XForm
```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<h:html xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2002/xforms" xmlns:ev="http://www.w3.org/2001/xml-events" xmlns:h="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:jr="http://openrosa.org/javarosa" xmlns:orx="http://openrosa.org/xforms" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema">
  <h:head>
    <h:title>Issue: Hidden Fields</h:title>
    <model>
      <instance>
        <hidden_fields delimiter="#" id="hidden_fields" prefix="J1!hidden_fields!" version="2018-06-12 22-55">
          <name tag="hidden"/>
          <name2/>
          <another_name/>
        </hidden_fields>
      </instance>
      <instance id="contact-summary"/>
      <bind nodeset="/hidden_fields/name" type="string"/>
      <bind nodeset="/hidden_fields/name2" type="string"/>
      <bind nodeset="/hidden_fields/another_name" type="string"/>
    </model>
  </h:head>
  <h:body>
    <input ref="/hidden_fields/name">
      <label>name</label>
    </input>
    <input ref="/hidden_fields/name2">
      <label>name2</label>
    </input>
    <input ref="/hidden_fields/another_name">
      <label>another_name</label>
    </input>
  </h:body>
</h:html>
```

**Snippet of doc for a submitted report**
```json
{
  "hidden_fields":["name"],
  "fields":{
    "name":"i",
    "name2":"i2",
    "another_name":"i3"
  }
}
```

title: relativeDays filter only shows days, not months etc (unlike relativeDate)
body:
To replicate, mucking around with the code is probably the easiest to see the change.

We have two relative time filters that we can use to output relative time based on an absolute time: `relativeDay` and `relativeDate`. From current usage and the code it looks like the intention is that one of them shows relative time including times earlier than "today", and the other does not. e.g. `relativeDate` would show "13 minutes ago" while `relativeDay` would just show "today".

However, there is also another difference that I think is unintentional: the largest time period `relativeDay` seems to support is days. That means it will output "55 days ago", as opposed to "2 months ago" like `relativeDate` would.

To me, the only difference between the two should be the minimum sized time period (seconds for `relativeDate`, days for `relativeDay`) and not the maximum.

title: Improve death reporting workflow by allowing the death confirmation form to specify the date of death
body:
Currently, when the `death_reporting` transition runs, it adds a `date_of_death` field to the contact doc that is equal to the `reported_date` of the death confirmation form. However, the death confirmation is likely to happen after the actual date of death. We'd like to provide a way to indicate the date of death in the death confirmation form so that the date of death that is recorded on the contact doc is the actual date of death.

@garethbowen suggested that the death confirmation form can include a field called `date_of_death` that would be saved on the contact doc. If not, the transition could fall back on the death confirmation report's `reported_date`.

title: Enable response body compression
body:
Old medic-os instances had gzip compression enabled in nginx, but Docker instances don't have nginx and compression is no longer happening. This can be enabled in express but [it's better to implement it at a reverse proxy level](https://expressjs.com/en/advanced/best-practice-performance.html#use-gzip-compression).

This is a blocker for using Docker in production.

title: Use asynchronous logging in node apps
body:

Replace all existing console invocations and implement a precommit regex check similar to the ones that exist for the webapp to ensure no new calls are added.

title: Performance issues loading contacts
body:
Querying the `doc_summaries_by_id` view is _really_ slow. On my Tecno with about 300 docs it takes about 4 seconds just to query the db (ignore rendering, setup, etc). PouchDB is making individual allDocs requests for each of the docs rather than one bulk get. 

I modified the GetDataRecords service to replace the view query with an allDocs request and shaved 2 seconds off the fetch time. If this change is also made for the other queries in the stack I expect to shave another 2 seconds or so off the request making it complete almost immediately.

GetDataRecords is used on the Reports tab too (and maybe other places) so performance improvements here could have broad implications.

Work out why PouchDB is doing so badly, and either fix it or implement the above workaround.

title: Translate our startup messages for non-English speakers
body:
People who do not have English as their primary language find our startup messages ("Loading assets", "Fetching Info (100 docs)..." etc) very confusing.

We do not currently translate these because angular has not yet started, and so we do not have the translation service yet. If this is the very first run we would also not have their language, because it wouldn't be the cookie yet, and we wouldn't have their user document yet.

Do we have any ideas on what we could do here to make this less confusing for users? The two most obvious options would be:
 - Add minimal translation support: hard code different languages, also load the user's context document if it doesn't already exist to make sure we get the language
 - Change what is rendered so it works across languages and cultures without requiring people have a firm grasp of english.

I think the former is easier but a bit more hacky (we'd now have translations in two places, but it's pretty contained and isn't that large of a deal IMO), and the latter is probably better, but much harder and would require a large amount of design work

title: Remove blank UI elements in Enketo forms
body:
In `2.16.0-beta.7` we have a lot of unexpected blank lines in Enketo forms for Standard:

## Actual layout
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/789512/42116335-c42d232a-7bc4-11e8-9663-9f652755d2cb.png)

## Desired layout
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/789512/42116292-9ed60a4c-7bc4-11e8-82ea-324fef94b123.png)

## Notes
- The XForm converter tool pyxform requires labels for groups
- We remove the label text in medic-conf if it is `NO_LABEL`
- These labels are still taking vertical space, even if they are blank.
- Sample form is [here](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/1403c371e5a693618817d21ebc73f49814ede26b/config/standard/forms/contact/district_hospital-create.xml).

Seems as though the ideal solution would be to remove the actual label, and avoid having blank definitions. This would likely be best done in `medic-conf`.

## Current XForm
Currently we have one of the following for every language in the model:
```
          <text id="/data/district_hospital:label">
            <value></value>
          </text>
```

The label is actually blank but in the UI body:

```
    <group appearance="field-list" ref="/data/district_hospital">
      <label ref="jr:itext('/data/district_hospital:label')"/>
      <group ref="/data/district_hospital/contact">
```

## Ideal XForm

Same as before but with no blank definitions in the model, and no empty UI element in the body:
```
    <group appearance="field-list" ref="/data/district_hospital">
      <group ref="/data/district_hospital/contact">

```

title: Create a shared library for server startup checks
body: We have a bunch of code in api/server.js and sentinel/server.js which checks certain prerequisites (eg: node version, logging env.NODE_OPTIONS) before starting. This is duplicated but also gets out of sync if new checks are added to one and not the other. Create a shared library with all the checks that both services should run.

title: Make debugging harder to leave on
body:
On the About page we have an option to turn on debugging. This sets a cookie which is checked on startup and if set sets angular and pouchdb to log everything. This is useful for development but should never be left on in a production environment because it slows down the app significantly and blows out feedback docs (related: #4481). I also have trouble turning it off and getting it to stay off suggesting that the cookie deletion code isn't working. We're getting [reports from the field](medic/medic-projects#4343) which indicate some users have this turned on so it's a problem in the wild.

1. Decide whether we want debugging to be sticky - perhaps it should just stay on until refresh, or maybe it should only be sticky in development mode.
2. Consider disabling debugging altogether in a production environment.
3. Work out how to make sure turning debugging off actually disables it after refresh.

title: Don't save docs that are already in the right state
body:
Following on from #4109 where we don't update the message state if it's the same as the current message state to stop the history getting too long, we should also not persist the doc if none of the messages actually got updated. Doing so causes many unnecessary database writes with only a _rev change, which significantly impacts the server.

**Steps to reproduce**:
- File a report for which sentinel generates scheduled tasks.
- Use the `/api/sms` API to POST a status update which sets the state of a message to `received-by-gateway`.
- Verify that the message state in the db is updated and record the _rev of the doc at this point.
- Use the `/api/sms` API to set the state of the same message to `received-by-gateway` again.

**What should happen**:
 - The doc is not updated, which can be verified by the _rev remaining the same.

**What actually happens**:
 - The doc is updated. The _rev is the only field that changes.

title: medic-conf should support pushing postgres
body:
The way we manage our postgres views etc is currently unstructured. There are a collection of files, usually in the `postgres` folder, that are executed arbitrarily, may not actually reproduce prod and are not always up to date.

We should move people to always executing off these files (as opposed to making live changes).

One way to do this is to make the deploy flow for them really nice.

We could change medic-conf to support pushing / executing postgres queries:
 - execute sql in ./postgres/* (not **, i.e. not sub directories) in alphanumeric order
 - allow to pass a starting position, so you don't have to re-execute everything if you don't need to.

title: Discussion: support writing some contact summary stats to docs
body:
A lot of the cool dynamic stats we have in contact summaries are also useful for analytics.

Given that:
 - It's maybe easier to calculate these using arbitrary javascript instead of in SQL (esp for complicated metrics)
 - Some of these values are not going to change very frequently (eg number of pregnancies)
 - If we only calculate it in one place we reduce the chance of getting two different answers, or one answer getting out of date, bugs etc

We should discuss adding support for a write flag to the contact summary config template. This would allow us to indicate that this statistic should be written to the patient contact that it is about.

One complication here is that we would have to periodically run the contact summary code as opposed to just dynamically when the summary is loaded. One option would be adding a transition that runs it whenever a report for a patient comes in. This would allow us to enable or disable this feature (by enabling or disabling the transition), but it still seems a bit heavy. We would also only run the code that has this flag enabled on it.

It would also be helpful for us to get an indication of the importance of this. @sarahollis can you detail some examples (both real and potential future ones) of complicated situations to give us an idea of places where we could make this better?

Regardless (ie even if all of the calculations are simple), it is a worthwhile feature to consider, because we're still calculating the same values in multiple places, which is bad for all the obvious reasons.

title: Sending an SMS to all contacts in a place doesn't work as expected
body:
If you select a facility name (all contacts) in the To field of an unstructured SMS, when you send the message, an SMS is sent to the primary contact of the facility but none of the CHWs whose areas are below that facility in the hierarchy.

**Steps to reproduce**:
 - Go to the messages tab
 - Click the + (send message)
 - Search for a health facility and select the option that says [facility name] - all contacts
 - Type in a message and click send
 - Notice that messages are only sent to people who are direct descendants of the facility

**What should happen**:
 - A message should be sent to the CHW (primary contact) for each of the areas that are below the facility in the hierarchy

**What actually happens**:
 - Messages are sent to the facility primary contact and any people who are direct descendants of the facility

https://beta-old.dev.medicmobile.org/medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/#/messages/phone:+14152319901

**Environment**:

_Fill in as many of these as apply. It's especially useful if some environments work and some don't (ie works in Chrome but not in FF)._

- Instance: beta-old.dev
- Browser: Chrome
- Client platform: MacOS
- App: webapp
- Version: 2.16.0-beta.8

It's possible that this is a misinterpretation of how "message all" should work, but this is how projects would like to use that feature.

Press Go

title: Replace appcache with a service worker cache
body: Appcache has been deprecated so one day it'll just stop working. To prepare for the future we should switch to using service workers. This will also give us the benefit of more reliable updates and if we're careful will reduce the amount of code that has to be downloaded on update.

title: Add SMS loop detection to sentinel
body:
There have been lots of reports from the field about getting into SMS loop hell: getting an automated response (eg from the ISP) and our auto-responder firing, which in turn causes another automated response, etc etc.

We can posthumously solve this with block lists and the like, but it doesn't help when discovering new ones and racking up huge bills until someone shuts it off.

We should add loop detection to sentinel. The algorithm here is debatable, but one option is: when processing an incoming SMS and deciding if we should respond, look to see if we have received more than 3 identical SMS from the same phone number in the last hour. If so, consider this a loop and do not auto-respond, or process the SMS in any way.

This ticket is important, like #4714, because it contributes to a need to over-manage gateway phones. Specifically in this case, because of a fear of SMS loops phones are only ever drip feed small amounts of credit, to reduce the damage if they automatically burn through it.

title: Make gateway balance easier to view
body:
Currently it's not easy to see how much balance a gateway phone has. This is important, more important due to #4714 and #4715, but just in general this is a thing that needs to be managed over many phones.

We should:
 - Add some configuration to webapp that let's TLs specify a number to send to, and a message to send, to determine balance. This may also require dropping our minimum phone number length limit (depending on where it's enforced), as these phone numbers may be less than 5 characters
 - Add some more configuration that gives TLs a regex, or perhaps an expression, that let's them pull a numerical value out of a balance response text
 - Somehow wire these things together so we periodically send a balance request and parse out the value from the response
 - And then store this value somewhere (CouchDB local doc? It doesn't need to be replicated), and expose that value via api, so that TLs can script off it / add it to a dashboard / do whatever they want.

title: Fix horticulturalist timeouts
body:
Horticulturalist requests, both to the build server and to the app server sometimes time out.

We already have [one hack](https://github.com/medic/horticulturalist/blob/master/src/install/index.js#L41-L85) where we fall back from a problematic bulk docs call to individual writes if needed.

However, we don't do that everywhere, and we are also suffering occasional timeouts in other requests, including bulk gets.

We should:
 - Work out how to set the default PouchDB timeout to something longer. At one point I learnt it was this: `new PouchDB(url, { ajax: { timeout: 65536 }})`, but I can no longer find any reference to that on the internet. Maybe it works, maybe it doesn't. If we do this we would also want to then *shorten* the timeout on the [view warmer](https://github.com/medic/horticulturalist/blob/master/src/install/index.js#L175-L190) so that we get UI updates more frequently (the pattern is: request a view; when it times out update progress; re-request).
 - Work out how to set request timeouts per request, and wrap all PouchDB calls
 - Decide that we're OK with Horti dying on timeout, treat it as an opportunity to restart whatever process it was doing (ie deploying). I don't really like this: it works in MedicOS because something is managing horti, but locally there is no management, and it should work in this instance.

title: Configures PouchDB not to batch changes requests
body:
# Description

By default, PouchDB http adapter batches changes requests with a batch size of 25. 
Because we're already creating our own batches by splitting `_doc_ids`, forcing PouchDB not to batch brings a slight performance improvement and also fixes missed changes bug due to CouchDB not calculating sequences reliably. 
Updates `feeds` to use new `req.id` property. 
Adds `statusCode` check in `db-config` service to reject responses with `404` and `412` statuses.
Adds `changes_doc_ids_optimization_threshold` value validation. 

medic/medic-webapp#4185

title: App bootstraps without data when changes returns an error
body:
When replicating, pouchdb-ajax validates a response from `_changes` by it's status (200 <= status < 300 is considered successfull). Because we could be sending heartbeats before receiving results from CouchDB, we might end up sending an error response with a success status. This, in turn, would cause the app to bootstrap without any data - the app displays an /#/error page and  the users would have to refresh the page to attempt the replication again.

Instead, a user should be able to retry initial replication until docs necessary for correct app bootstrapping are replicated.

title: Show pictures in the report view
body:
For the mRDT workflow supervisors will be reviewing the images submitted by CHWs so they need to be able to see them in the reports view of the app. 

## What currently happens
Images are saved and shown as base64 strings:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/789512/42959408-b1e33bb8-8b56-11e8-9b72-f00e9a8a93c8.png)

## What should happen
The images should show in the reports tab, scaling the image to fit within the available width. After user testing we can determine if we need to be able to enlarge the image.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/789512/42959694-a743f4ee-8b57-11e8-9961-6dbf2226ef8b.png)

## Example form
```
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<h:html xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2002/xforms" xmlns:ev="http://www.w3.org/2001/xml-events" xmlns:h="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:jr="http://openrosa.org/javarosa" xmlns:orx="http://openrosa.org/xforms" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema">
  <h:head>
    <h:title>MRDT Demo</h:title>
    <model>
      <instance>
        <data delimiter="#" id="mrdt_demo">
          <name/>
          <mrdt_image_data/>
          <meta>
            <instanceID/>
          </meta>
        </data>
      </instance>
      <bind nodeset="/data/name" type="string"/>
      <bind nodeset="/data/mrdt_image_data" type="string"/>
    </model>
  </h:head>
  <h:body class="pages">
    <group appearance="field-list" ref="/data">
      <label>Submit a photo of an MRDT test result</label>
      <input ref="/data/name">
        <label>Patient name</label>
      </input>
      <input ref="/data/mrdt_image_data" appearance="mrdt-verify">
        <label>MRDT image</label>
      </input>
    </group>
  </h:body>
</h:html>
```

This form requires the mrdt Enketo widget available in the mrdt branch: https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/tree/mrdt

title: Make People page default sort configurable (UHC mode)
body:
Right now the default sort for the People page list is always "Alphabetically'. What we'd like to do is make the default sort configurable. This way, projects that are prioritizing UHC mode can configure the list to sort "By date last visited" by default if they like. 

This has nothing to do with the sort options icon or menu. Users should still be able to toggle between sorting alphabetically or by date at will.

EDIT: Gareth brought up the possibility of simply defaulting all UHC projects to sort "by date last visited". I originally thought that would be fine, but now I think we should try to make it configurable. Here's why: we are now adding in counts of visits per month as well. Although we do not currently have a sort for "By number of visits this month" I can see that coming up anytime. When it does, we probably would want to give partners the choice between setting the default sort to "By date last visited" or "By number of visits this month". Why give them a choice? Because some partners have very specific goals for number of visits per month (like Muso) while others do not.

title: Offline user rev-less invalid attachment requests return a 404
body:
# Description

When replicating an existent `doc`, PouchDB attachment requests would not include `rev` param. When the `doc` had been deleted (or the latest `rev` would not be allowed), they would receive a `403`,  which would abort the replication process. 
As a fix, offline attachment `rev`-less denied requests will now respond with a `404`, which will cause PouchDB to retry retrieving the attachment including the `rev` param.

Omits `latest` param for offline `_bulk_get` requests.

medic/medic-webapp#2734

title: The image upload enketo widget relies on the form name matching the xml instance element
body:
In the Enketo service `xmlToDocs` function we get files such as photos that were uploaded with the form submission and attach them to the report doc. The attachment is named by the xpath to the field with `user-file` as a prefix, eg: `user-file/mrdt/mrdt_image_data`. In this example the `mrdt` bit is the root element of the xform instance, eg:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<h:html xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2002/xforms" xmlns:ev="http://www.w3.org/2001/xml-events" xmlns:h="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xmlns:jr="http://openrosa.org/javarosa" xmlns:orx="http://openrosa.org/xforms" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema">
  <h:head>
    <h:title>MRDT Demo</h:title>
    <model>
      <instance>
        <mrdt delimiter="#" id="mrdt_demo">
          <name/>
          <mrdt_image_data type="binary"/>
          <meta>
            <instanceID/>
          </meta>
        </mrdt>
      </instance>
      <bind nodeset="/mrdt/name" type="string"/>
      <bind nodeset="/mrdt/mrdt_image_data" type="string"/>
    </model>
  </h:head>
  <h:body class="pages">
    <group appearance="field-list" ref="/mrdt">
      <label>Submit a photo of an MRDT test result</label>
      <input ref="/mrdt/name">
        <label>Patient name</label>
      </input>
      <input ref="/mrdt/mrdt_image_data" appearance="mrdt-verify">
        <label>MRDT image</label>
      </input>
    </group>
  </h:body>
</h:html>
```

When rendering the submitted report we call the ReportViewModelGenerator service `getFields` function which checks to see if there's an attachment with a name that matches the field. It builds the expected name by concatenating "user-file", the report's `form` field, and the name of the field it's inspecting. The report's `form` field comes from the `internalId` of the form doc that was used to submit the report. This `internalId` can be different from the instance name used originally.

We should make the code that stores the image consistent with the code that displays the image so there isn't this requirement to have the two variables match. This solution has to be backwards compatible so reports submitted with the old code will still display the image correctly.

Currently medic-conf warns but doesn't block if the two don't match so it's possible this isn't affecting anyone in production, but it did just cost me a few hours of head scratching.

title: Add display of visit counts and conditionally style them (UHC mode)
body:
For UHC mode, we already display "Date last visited". We would like to keep that, and add in a visual display of "Number of visits this month".

**Clarification**
Although they sound similar, “Date last visited” and “Visits this month” are two completely different data points. Date last visited is calculated based upon a _rolling_ count of “how many days ago” and is not tied to the calendar at all. Visits this month is tied directly to the calendar month. Date last visited never resets while visits this month resets back to 0 at the beginning of each month. 

**Visits this month**
We would like to add large visit count numbers to the right side of each family row. The visit count will display a count of the number of times that family has been visited so far within the current month. The exact definition of the calendar month should be left configurable. Some partners may follow the calendar literally, while other partners have different definitions of a month (ex: Muso counts from the 26th of one month until the 25th of the next month). Whatever forms have been configured to calculate "Date last visited" will be the same forms used to calculate "Visits this month".

**Basic layout** 
- The count can be "0", "1", "2", "3", "4" visits etc. Two digits should be allowed (but probably not common). After two digits (highly unlikely) we should display a summary such as "99+".
- The count number is located in the upper right of the row and sits on the same baseline as the contact name text. Noto Sans, bold, 24px (H1).
- The word "visit(s)" is below the count number and sits on the same baseline as the date last visited text. Noto Sans, bold, 14px.
- Both the visit count and the word "visit(s)" are right-aligned (meaning any extra characters push the word to the left). The far right edge of both text boxes is aligned. There is a 10px gap between the far right edge of the text boxes and the right edge of the screen.
- Both the number digit and the word "visit(s)" should be internationalized so various language translations and scripts can be configured

![markup](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/43285186-064ef94a-90d3-11e8-92d5-0812f56f6cd6.png)

**Conditional styling**
- We would like to give partners the ability to conditionally style the counts, or not
- If the partner has no specific goals, just like with Targets, the text is normal black
- If the partner does have specific goals, we use red to indicate "bad", yellow to indicate "ok" and green to indicate "good" or "goal met". Red = # E33030, Yellow = # C38813, Green = # 538E8D.
- Adding to this, we can also, optionally, display an icon next to the count number. This icon is only available as an option if the partner has a goal. If the partner does not have a goal there will never be an icon. The icon is FontAwesome fa-exclamation-triangle [ & # x f 0 7 1 ; ]. Size 16px, color # E33030.
- The icon is positioned to the left of the count number on the same baseline. 
- Note: We would like to remove the red warning icon by the date last visited text that we implemented in 2.16.1. The new functionality and location of the icon as described here replaces what we did in 2.16.1. It used to be tied to date last visited - now it is instead tied to visits this month.

![screen shot 2018-07-26 at 2 18 36 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/43289137-db683028-90de-11e8-9426-b524ccb24af1.png)


**Muso's desired configuration**
- The text of the counts should be red if the count is “0”, yellow if “1” and green if 2 or more. 
- If the count is "0" or "1" it should also be accompanied by a red warning icon. 

Here is what the visit counts will always look like at the very beginning of the month ("0 visits" for every single family):
![beginning of month](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/43285205-136bdf58-90d3-11e8-8c38-7addbb5fd4cb.png)

Here is what the visit counts should look like after three visits have been made:
![after first week copy](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/43285224-1d090d4c-90d3-11e8-85fe-86a3f5d42b58.png)

And here is what the visit counts might look like even later in the month:
![after second week copy](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/43285230-23cbef50-90d3-11e8-9cc0-eba7be8bb7a6.png)

**Another clarification**
You will notice that it is sometimes possible for families with 2 visits to appear above families with 1 visit in the list, due to the sorting based upon “Date last visited”. We are aware of this outcome but think it makes sense in light of the emphasis on _frequency_ of home visits. It is possible we might get a request in down the road to add the ability to sort "By number of visits this month" but that is an issue for another time.

title: Process CouchDB delete-stubs correctly in LiveList and TombstoneUtils
body:
# Description

When a doc is deleted via a `DELETE` call (or from Fauxton UI), CouchDB only saves a stubbed version of the doc (containing just `_id`, `_rev` and `_deleted: true` flag).

When such a change was received by `webapp`'s listeners, it was not filtered as relevant, since the attached `doc` didn't have the required properties, so the `LiveList` was not updated. This modifies the `webapp` changes listeners to filter delete stubs of docs that exist in the `LiveList`.

Updates `tombstone-utils` shared library so it will try to save the previous revision of delete-stubs as the `tombstone`, so offline users will replicate the `DELETE`s. 

medic/medic-webapp#4754

title: Ability to mute people and places
body:
In response to medic/medic-projects#4329

Full details and additional screenshots can be found in the design spec: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1we_Qu1B4x8PuAi9pxiIu4MeXtdH1kY9W29kMidHThsc/edit?usp=sharing

**Summary of muting in general**
- Muting is a form accessible from the normal form menu on profiles (or Reports)
- Muting is not an individual per-user preference. All users of an instance (both CHWs and nurses) stop receiving new tasks and SMS reminders for any muted person/place. 
- The muted people/places are not deleted and all historical data for all muted people/places remains in the app
- Any currently enrolled schedules are not deleted or paused - just muted (quieted)
- Any condition cards should remain on the person/place profile
- All of the forms that would normally appear are still accessible from a muted person/place profile (as usual, forms are configurable per project)
- If a user begins any new form for a muted person/place that is not the "Unmute" form, they will first get a warning modal saying “This person belongs to a family that is currently muted. Are you sure you want to proceed?”
- A user cannot unmute a person/place from within any form, only from within the official “Unmute” form. If they see the above warning message while trying to submit a different form, they can either proceed knowing the person/place is still muted, or they can close that form, open up the “Unmute” form, and unmute first before submitting the other form.
- A project may support both death reporting and muting, they are not mutually exclusive
- Manager approval should not be required for muting, but, like death reporting, it should be made a configurable option for partners that want it
- Muting should work for both web-app and SMS workflows. We aren't managing "families" over SMS yet, though this is likely to be introduced at some point.



![screen shot 2018-08-01 at 1 14 37 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/43546250-ffb255a0-958c-11e8-9b32-ca54132084c2.png)

**Muting households**
- Muting a household mutes schedules attached to household-level workflows as well as all schedules for all people in the household. It serves as a shortcut to muting all individuals in a household.
- To mute a family, you navigate to the family profile, open up the action window, and select the “Mute Family” form
- If you access the “Mute Family” form from the Reports tab, you first need to select the family to mute from a dropdown of active families
- A question on the form asks “What is the reason for muting?” and provides options for the user to select from (exact questions and options to be configurable by partner)
- If the partner does not require a manager verification step, the family will instantly be muted as soon as the user clicks the “Submit” button on the form
- If the partner does require manager verification, a task will be sent to the manager. The family will remain active until the manager confirms the muting.
- All users stop receiving new tasks or SMS for any muted family or family members
- If there was an existing open task for a now muted person/place on the Tasks tab, that open task should disappear from both the Tasks tab and the muted person/place’s profile
- Muted household profiles are styled to reflect their muted status
- Muted households move to a new section at the bottom of the main People page list
- There is no such thing as an unmuted person in a muted household. Whenever muting is set at the household level, it applies to all individuals within that household. 
- We technically can have a muted person in an unmuted household, but that is not the primary focus of this request (see individual muting ticket #4768)
- A user may add a new person to a muted household. If they do, and choose to leave the family muted, the new person will also be automatically muted.



![screen shot 2018-08-01 at 1 16 55 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/43546328-314916a8-958d-11e8-80d1-ddafce9f7583.png)

**UI changes to main People page list**
- A family that has been muted moves into a new “muted families” section at the bottom of the main people page list
- The muted families section only appears if there is at least one muted family
- The number in parenthesis reflects the number of families that are currently muted
- UI matches that of death reporting bar on family profiles: grey background (#E0E0E0), height 45px, black FontAwesome arrow () on the right side, text normal 16px
- Clicking on the “muted families” section will display a list of all the families that are currently muted
- Clicking again on a family name will take you to that family’s profile



![screen shot 2018-08-01 at 1 14 49 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/43546349-3c61fb40-958d-11e8-91ec-374e6389d8b4.png)

**UI changes to profiles**
- Very similar to profile styling for death
- The person/place icon becomes grey (#A7A9AC)
- And we display the text “Muted” on the second line below the person/place name
- Any forms that were previously available on the profile remain available
- Instead of the “Mute person/place” form, the user now sees “Unmute person/place”

title: Update the on/off handling to mark an individual as muted
body:
This request is a continuation of the request in ticket #4767. 

Full details and additional screenshots can be found in the design spec: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1we_Qu1B4x8PuAi9pxiIu4MeXtdH1kY9W29kMidHThsc/edit?usp=sharing

**Summary**
We already partially support individual muting with the On/Off form, however this mutes pre-existing SMS schedules only and does not “mark” or style the person as muted. There is some additional dev required to update our current On/Off functionality. We would like to update and replace on/off with a new full individual muting feature, and this should ideally happen at same time as family/place muting.

**How it currently works**
The individual muting that we have so far can be done via SMS or App forms, BUT mutes pre-existing SMS schedules only. This means that for subsequent pregnancies new messages will be scheduled and sent.

How it currently works with SMS: turns existing notifications for a person on or off. Mutes all outgoing messages in those schedules for that person. If you submit a new pregnancy, you would continue to get those new messages - you only turned off existing schedules, not new schedules.

How it currently works with webapp: turn notifications off, mutes existing SMS schedules, not future. You can also decide to remove/hide tasks, targets (we’re not doing this for any project right now though).

**Desired changes**
- The form should be called “Mute” instead of “On/Off” (believe this is just config)
- We should actually mark the individual as “Muted”
- We should make the UI changes to their profile to reflect the “Muted” status
- All pre-existing and future messages and tasks should be muted, until such time as the person is unmuted
- Unmuting an individual person in a muted place should also unmute the entire place and people in it (because we don’t allow unmuted individuals underneath a muted place). We should be clear about what will happen on the first page of the individual person’s “unmute” action form.


![screen shot 2018-08-01 at 1 55 23 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/43548386-9c7bfc74-9592-11e8-8576-7aaf9cf9ce84.png)

**UI changes to the family profile**
- If an individual is muted from an individual on/off form, then the greater family remains unmuted, and there is no change to that family’s appearance (family icons stays pink, no “Muted” text)
- There _should_ be a change made to the “Family Members” condition card. Any individuals that are muted within an unmuted family should be specially styled in this card so that they stand out from active unmuted family members. 
- Suggestion: The person’s name becomes grey, and instead of (or in addition to) the age on the second line, we also display the word “Muted”. See example above where Jon Bass is muted.



![screen shot 2018-08-01 at 1 55 33 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/43548399-a5a27c24-9592-11e8-8101-ad679c7dc70f.png)

**UI changes to profiles**
- The same as UI changes to muted place profiles
- The person/place icon becomes grey (#A7A9AC)
- We display the text “Muted” on the second line below the person/place name
- Any forms that were previously available on the profile remain available
- Instead of the “Mute” form, the user now sees the “Unmute” form

title: Process CouchDB delete-stubs correctly in LiveList and TombstoneUtils
body:
# Description


Process CouchDB delete-stubs correctly in LiveList and TombstoneUtils  …
When a doc is deleted via a DELETE call (or from Fauxton UI), CouchDB
only saves a stubbed version of the doc (containing just _id, _rev and
_deleted: true flag).

When such a change was received by webapp's listeners, it was not
filtered as relevant, since the attached doc didn't have the required
properties, so the LiveList was not updated. This modifies the webapp
changes listeners to filter delete stubs of docs that exist in the
LiveList.

Updates tombstone-utils shared library so it will try to save the
previous revision of delete-stubs as the tombstone, so offline users
will replicate the DELETEs.

Additionally, support restricted offline users, namely:
Offline users db-doc `GET` and `_bulk_get` requests always allow delete stubs. 

medic/medic-webapp#4754

title: LG Supervisor IN: only replicate exact docs and hierarchy we need
body:
We have been testing LG Supervisors supervising one IN closed loop experiment, which involves 20 CHWs and, using our current system of filtered replication to a second server, approximately 11,000 docs being loaded onto a tablet.

In a couple of months they will also launch another IN experiment, with the same supervisors, against a second set of CHWs. This will raise the CHW count from 20 to 34, which @benkags estimates will raise the doc count to ~20,000. The concern is that **this** number will not scale correctly. It would be very awkward to move from this system to a second one that is faster, as it would require starting again (re-replicating etc).

Instead, we are proposing replacing our current filtered replication solution with the following:
 - A Sentinel transition that, when a referral report comes in (i.e. the doc type is one of N referral documents) we mark both that document, as well as all of its parents and all of its parents contacts with a flag (if they are not marked already)
 - Change the filtered replication code from the main server -> supervisor server to only replicate a  `contact` or `data_record` if it has that flag

NB: this is not covered by #4591 unfortunately, because that ticket only covers reports and not contacts. The refutation here is that _even all contacts are too much_.

title: LHS list doesn't update "out of page" items
body:
Currently, LiveList and Search webapp services don't support sorting items by fields/values that are likely to change (f.e. by last visited date). 

When the list is multiple pages long and it's not entirely loaded, if an existent item receives a change that would push it lower than the current number of loaded items, the Search request will not update it - it will keep it's old sorting value until the user scrolls down and loads the page the updated item should appear on.

title: Change the text that is displayed on LHS of Reports when there are no results
body:
The very bottom of the LHS always has some sort of statement. On the People page, this statement is "No more contacts". On the Reports page, this statement is "No more reports".

The statement changes when you've performed a search or applied filters with 0 results. On the People page, the statement changes to "No contacts found". On the Reports page, this statement says "No reports". 

Some users have found the "No reports" message to be confusing. Sometimes this text is not always accurate, as the reports are still syncing (this was raised by Isaac).

As a quick solution, suggest that we change the message for 0 results to match how we handle it on the People page. So instead of "No reports" we should say "No reports _found_" to highlight the fact that certain search criteria may be limiting the view.

![screen shot 2018-08-17 at 3 40 23 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/44291551-e55e6280-a233-11e8-84f3-2fe40c9e4991.png)

title: Update the medic-gateway target API
body:
The app currently targets API level 24 and will have to target at least API level 26 to ensure it's built on the latest APIs optimized for security and performance. Starting from August 2018, new apps must target at least Android 8.0 (API level 26) and starting from Nov 2018, app updates must target Android 8.0 (API level 26). If this affects projects on the ground using old phones, this needs to be taken care of before Nov 2018.
Here's the entire warning:
```
Target API level requirements from August 2018 Warning:  Your app currently targets API level 24 and must target at least API level 26 to ensure it is built on the latest APIs optimized for security and performance.  From August 2018, new apps must target at least Android 8.0 (API level 26). From November 2018, app updates must target Android 8.0 (API level 26).
```
Upgrading the target API in medic-gateway requires that the testing framework Robolectric also be updated.  That in turn affects the test coverage plugin JacocoEverywhere which needs to be either updated/replaced with something else.

title: Webapp fails to start on Ubuntu VM
body:

cd medic-webapp
grunt install-dependencies build-dev deploy

title: Replace continuous replication with periodic replication
body:
As discussed in [this document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/159qKQwYo02Cxh3T0YidK_2D-KAtWdLEkvq8slnwdMuc/edit) replace continuous replication with periodic one-shot replication to improve server scalability, phone battery usage, network data usage, and reduce code complexity.

- [ ] Implement polling to do a bidirectional replication every 5 minutes. The specific number is up for debate but 5 minutes is a safe place to start.
- [ ] Implement #3976 so users can manually trigger a bidirectional sync.
- [ ] Investigate using [online event handlers](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/NavigatorOnLine/onLine#Specification) to trigger a bidirectional sync when a user comes back online if it's been longer than the 5 minute timer above.
- [ ] Remove continuous replication code from the API changes endpoint.

title: Fix getting registrations via querying `medic-client/registered_patients`
body:
When sentinel data was pulled out into it's own database (https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/issues/3423), `medic-client/registered_patients` view started to yield no results, due to it's dependence of checking `registration` transition execution info to be present within the doc.
This view is used by Sentinel (to generate and mute messages), by API (`create-patient-contacts` migration) and Webapp to format data records ( generating `scheduled_messages` in the UI ).

title: Expose SMS sending capabilities in android wrapper
body:
We need to allow for the web app to send SMS messages. We can achieve this (on phones) by exposing an API endpoint in the JS bridge that lets you pass a phone number and a message, which the android wrapper will then send.

We do not need to read SMS messages or do anything more complicated at this time.

Things to think about:
 - Do we want to just blind-fire this request, or have it call a callback when it succeeds (or fails)?
 - Do we need some kind of queuing on the android wrapper side?

title: Support XForms that "compile" into SMS messages
body:
See this section of this document for discussion specific pertaining to the project that requires this: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Ygpi5JzVKYbfWF-uEIc1RCvAPSGq-ut0N8cHMSn5eXY/edit#heading=h.2vg9c5lgu2ld

The developer should also work with @maremegaye so they have the specific form that is needed to test with and make sure the implementation works for that form. This is important because:
 - We need to make all the information needed later fits inside one SMS (multi-sms is not globally supported by mobile networks and is generally dodgy AFAICT), and this form has the potential to be quite large
 - We need to either have this report *also* possibly contain patient demos if the patient was created offline (you can tell: if they have a patient shortcode they made it to the server) or also configure the new patient form to send SMS

We could also consider hooking into PouchDB and only sending SMS if the form can't be replicated upward immediately. That could be hard though, and for time constraint reasons it's fine to not do this

title: SIH integration
body:
See this doc for details: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Ygpi5JzVKYbfWF-uEIc1RCvAPSGq-ut0N8cHMSn5eXY/edit#

@maremegaye is the design contact, @Fatoufall is the PM contact.

We need to have a closed loop flow between us and SIH. We're going to use Sentinel (my boy!), triggered based on docs coming in via data/sms from the CHW, as well as inbound JSON docs coming from SIH itself, to both trigger api calls to SIH (from the former) and trigger SMS back to the CHW (from the latter).

We should:
 - Work out exactly what we want to send to SIH when a referral happens, come up with an example JSON and provide it to them so they can build their api
 - Work out what we'd like them to send us back for the different actions that can happen and create JSON forms with example JSON, provide it to them and configure those forms into [the shared dev instance](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/4844). SIH can then use [the records api](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/tree/master/api#post-apiv2records) to send us these JSON forms
 - build a sentinel transition that take incoming referral reports from a CHW, convert them into a SIH api request and send them along
 - build a sentinel transition that manages the JSON forms created above, and sends SMS' to CHWs based on rules described in the linked document

Things we need for a referral:
 - An identifier for the referral. Should be unique across the whole instance. This makes it easy for impact to link referrals and loop closing actions (the patient arriving at the facility etc) together. We would send this to SIH allowing them to send it back to us.
 - An identifier for the patient. Could be the patient UUID, or their shortcode[1]. Again, we would send this to SIH allowing them to send it back to us. Also lets them re-use / overwrite existing patient records in their system
 - Demographics for the patient: name, dob, sex
 - The CHW who is responsible for them: name, area maybe (check with SIH folks)
 - The referral data itself: danger signs etc, work with @maremegaye to come up with this (also see #4812)

[1] Remember that the patient may already exist, but this might also be the first time the server is hearing about them, because the CHW could be offline when they are created. If we can fit it maybe we pass the UUID in the referral SMS from the CHW and then send that as well.

title: Replace yarn with npm
body:
A few months ago [we decided to move to yarn](#3032) due to problems we were having with npm, but now I believe yarn to be a worse solution for us.

This will help solve:

- audit only works with npm
- yarn pack is completely broken
- requiring a yarn version doesn't work when working on older code (aka `--ignore-engines` hell)

Todo:

- [x] Change `yarn` to `npm` everywhere in our build scripts.
- [x] Replace the yarn.lock with package-lock.json everywhere.
- [ ] Enforce transitive dependencies either with [npm-force-resolutions](https://www.npmjs.com/package/npm-force-resolutions) or by rolling our own. Hook this into the npm scripts so it happens automatically.
- [ ] Ensure CI respects the package-lock so what is packed and released is exactly what was used in development and tested in CI.
- [ ] Use `npm audit` responsibly so we mitigate vulnerabilities (#3768).
- [ ] Check this fixes #4701

title: README - Some issues during my first-time developer experience
body:
I got a development environment up and running this week on Ubuntu (no horticulturalist and no medic-os). Overall the docs were great and the path forward was clear but sometimes bumpy. Thought I'd share some of the stumbling blocks/learnings.

Happy to chip in and improve things if you agree with any of these issues. I marked the issues I have been unable to resolve - grateful for any tips! 

1. I set my own password when the CouchDB install prompted me to create the admin account. I tried to use the dofferent admin password via env but got stuck by a few hardcoded spots. Gave up after a couple, but maybe either fix that or just mention to use `admin:pass`
1. Setting `require_valid_user` also means Fauxton doesn't work within a browser. This is a super nice tool for getting started and learning about CouchDB! Was helpful for me to set `httpd/WWW-Authenticate = Basic realm="administrator"` maybe just a [link](https://github.com/apache/couchdb/issues/1305).
1. Can remove the details about CouchDB 1.x. Seems unnecessary since 2.x is listed as "required".
1. The reference to `load_messages.js` may be more helpful if it also linked to sample data.
1. [Unresolved] The command to set `max_http_request_size` didn't work for me. The command has an extra `'` in it. I get `{"error":"not_found","reason":"no such node: couchdb@localhost"}` when I execute. So far doesn't seem impactful.
1. [Unresolved] I'm having some problems with `husky` and `prettier-quick` reformatting pages as part of git precommit. Have it disabled for now, but maybe this is familiar to somebody.

title: Adds admin message queue page
body:
# Description

Adds an admin page with an overview of all outgoing SMS messages, split into 4 tabs:
 - a `scheduled` tab which contains all messages which are in the `scheduled` state, displayed in ascending order, sorted by their due date
- a `will not send` tab which contains all messages which will not be sent (statuses: `muted`, `cleared`, `denied`, `duplicate`), which have a due date in the future, displayed in ascending order sorted by due date,
- a `did not send` tab which contains all messages which have not been sent (statuses: `muted`, `cleared`, `denied`, `duplicate`) which have a due date in the past, displayed in descending order sorted by their due date.
- a `due` tab which contains messages which have statuses not included in other tabs, displayed in descending order. sorted by their due date. 

The menu link points to the `due` tab. Results are paginated, each page displaying 25 items. Message text content respects the language and context that it will be/has been sent in.

title: 3327 - Date picker widget is not translated
body:
# Description

The Enketo Datetime-Extended widget isn't translated in the appropriate language.

#3327

# Review checklist

- [ ] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/blob/master/development/style-guide.md), documented if necessary.
- [ ] Documented: Announced in Changes.md in plain English. Configuration and user documentation on [medic-docs](https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/)
- [ ] Tested: Unit and/or e2e where appropriate
- [ ] Internationalised: All user facing text
- [ ] Backwards compatible: Works with existing data and configuration or includes a migration. Any breaking changes documented in Changes.md.

# Comments

There are a few broad approaches one could take to this: 

1. The enketo widget "datetime-extended" uses [bootstrap-datepicker](https://github.com/uxsolutions/bootstrap-datepicker) under the hood which directly supports many languages. Can flick this switch on.
1. We could use a pattern like using moment as the translator as in `webapp/js/enketo/translator`.  
1. I guess we could use the standard angular translation workflow. 
1. Others? 

Here is a solution based on 1 from above. Happy to revisit with another approach if people think it is better. Some background on the Bootstrap-datepicker:

* Bootstrap-datepicker includes locale data for 6/8 of the default medic languages [en, es, fr, sw, id, hi] plus many additional languages if required. [list of languages](https://github.com/uxsolutions/bootstrap-datepicker/tree/master/js/locales). I have little insight into the number of languages you support in practice ... 
* Nipali (ne) is not supported, but is already handled by a special widget bikram-sambat-datepicker. 
* Bamanankan (bm) is missing. 
* enketo-core uses a _two-year old build_ of bootstrap-datepicker@1.6.x. Which seems to be working fine, but doesn't support Hindi (hi). So some considerations there.

Next, I considered three approaches for getting the user's language down into the bootstrap-datepicker control.

1. Update Enketo-Core `Datepicker-Extended` widget to accept language information through the existing `options` widget parameter.
1. Extend the Enketo-Core `Datepicker-Extended` widget into some sort of Medic-specific  DatepickerExtendedLocalized which obtains language data via Angular (similar to `android-datepicker`).
1. Pass language information directly into bootstrap-datepicker.
1. Other?

I went with option 3 above. Option 1 requires a change in Enketo-Core but is possibly a cleaner solution. 2 was very messy and basically requires forking the full Datepicker-Extended widget. 3 seems reasonable, but is probably not the ideal division of responsibility between Medic/Enketo. Happy to revisit if you have suggestions!

title: 3675 - Blacklist outgoing messages to carriers
body:
# Description

The auto-reply functionality in sentinel can get into infinite loops of robots replying to each other. So, we want to not auto-reply to messages from carriers. Although a carrier is flagged in configuration and an additional blacklist exists, additional generic and default configurations would be useful to make initial configuration easier.

medic/medic-webapp#3675

# Approach 

I've implemented the general configuration mechanisms proposed in @alxndrsn solution # 1 in https://github.com/medic/medic-gateway/issues/122.

This consists of configuration

* `outgoing_deny_numbers_shorter_than=6` - to deny replies to messages from shortcodes (e.g. `60396`)
* `outgoing_deny_numbers_with_alphas=true` - to deny replies to non-numeric senders (e.g. `TELKOMSEL`, `one2one`)

Alternatively, I considered making the `outgoing_deny_list` support a list of regex instead of having multiple outgoing_deny configurations. This could achieve the same result while being a more robust and powerful tool. However, it may not be as intuitive to configure so I went with specific scenario-based configurations. As always, happy to revisit this using any other approach. 

If you like this approach, I'll also update relevant documentation. I'm not sold on the names of the configuration variables, suggestions welcome!

I've tested this with unit tests and using the [message test](http://localhost:5988/medic/_design/medic-admin/_rewrite#/message-test).  Code path is also hit by a bunch of transitions [accept_patient_reports, default_responses, registration, update_notifications] which I don't have a lot of context on, so unsure if it could potentially have negative effects worth testing out.

title: Allow supervisors to see CHW targets and support display of aggregate targets widgets
body:
[Product initiative detail ](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1EQHQI11XqI8aQeUsnmlrD3ny83fj5N6MZATrLzsm_-I/edit#heading=h.q31g948sivit)

Read more details and view additional screenshots in the MVP deck: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1AbOxkGgggUoI0QzRmwVqfX0AqC6aG6CByNd-CzdRgaI/edit?usp=sharing

**TECHNICAL STRATEGY**

We do not have the capacity for managers to see all of their CHW’s patients and documents (setting aside current unsupported/experimental workflows), without some kind of 100x performance improvements. The goal of this MVP is to provide a way for supervisors to view CHW performance data without requiring all of the patient reports offline. We hope to enable supervisors to have much smaller data sets and still accomplish what they need to do.

A clearly helpful thing is exposing CHW’s tasks and targets to their supervisors. This gives supervisors insight into what the CHW is doing, needs to do and has done, without requiring that they can see all of the patients and their documents. This MVP focuses on targets first - investigating how we can periodically write a CHW's targets into a document that can be synchronized to the supervisor's device.

Note to QA team: we should proactively test with high-volume instances.


**DESIGN OVERVIEW**

Note: All of the following require supervisor access/visibility to CHW targets in order to work.

**Support new performance condition card on CHW profile**
- Should be just adding another card type to the contact summary
- The data is based directly on CHW targets and is subject to the same limitations as the widgets/calculations on Targets
- The time period of the data will match what we already have, meaning we will only support data from the most recent month/time period
- As usual, the exact metrics displayed on the card and the total number of metrics displayed will be configurable per partner/project

**Ability to display targets last updated date on performance card**
- The “Date targets last updated” gives crucial context as it is the date when the performance data was last updated (i.e. “This information was true as of this date”)
- The targets "report" gets generated every 24 hours regardless of whether there is a new action by the CHW
- Should be styled just like any other condition card field and should appear first in the condition card

**Support display of aggregate targets widgets**
- Display aggregate performance metrics across all of a supervisor’s CHWs
- Calculating averages may need to be a new widget type??
- Some values may be totals, while others may be averages (total / # of values)
- Should support aggregate values on both count widgets and percentage widgets (depends on what gets recorded in the CHW report)
- Should also support goals - if the group of CHWs is performing on average below the goal, the value will be highlighted in red. If the group of CHWs is performing on average above the goal, the value will be highlighted in green. 
- If there is no goal, the value should be the default black
- Stefan says: Targets page is just like it is now, but unlike CHWs where targets are based on reports completed, Supervisor targets are based on CHW target documents. Should fit the current way targets get calculated (ie nools)
- Marc says: Seems like we need to store numerator and denominator so that we can calculate totals. We also need a way to add numbers to the target, as opposed as counting every target instance as a 1.

![screen shot 2018-09-19 at 12 43 09 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/45777081-a09a6280-bc09-11e8-88fc-dcd2a229f632.png)

title: Make targets widgets clickable and support target detail pages for supervisors
body:
[Product initiative detail](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1EQHQI11XqI8aQeUsnmlrD3ny83fj5N6MZATrLzsm_-I/edit#heading=h.q31g948sivit)

Read more details and view additional screenshots in the MVP deck: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1AbOxkGgggUoI0QzRmwVqfX0AqC6aG6CByNd-CzdRgaI/edit?usp=sharing

This new feature builds off of changes made in ticket #4839. The detail pages are considered a nice-to-have but not essential for the Supervisor MVP. Depends on further technical investigation and level of effort.

**New feature: targets detail pages**
- Aggregate widgets are now clickable
- Clicking on a widget takes you to a new detail page view of that widget with a breakdown of data by individual CHW
- The title of the detail page should match the title of the widget
- CHW names on the left are hyperlinked to a CHW’s profile
- The individual performance of each CHW is displayed on the right (could be a count or a percentage)
- The individual performance values are right-aligned 
- If the data is a percentage, we should also display the counts in parenthesis e.g. “90% (9 of 10)” 
- The list should be automatically sorted from lowest to highest performing and/or lowest to highest value. Lowest performing at the top.
- If a particular widget has a goal, it would be nice to support conditional styling based upon goals: If a certain CHW is performing below the goal, their value should be highlighted in red. If a CHW is performing above the goal, their value should be green.

Note from @SCdF : I think this is just visual: we should be able to make a new URL target that has the target in it and then displays all families by target, and ideally ordering is guessable based on the target type.

title: 4331 - Reports incorrectly filtered if filter changes before search returns
body:
# Description

Any change to report filters are ignored while reports are being fetched. The function `debounce()` in `services/search.js` is effectively bouncing everything until the first query finishes. `_currentQuery.filters` is a reference to the underlying filters object (in this case `$scope.filters` from `controllers/reports.js`). Fix is to cache a copy of the objects instead of a reference.

medic/medic-webapp#4331

Good demo of the underlying issue is to comment out [this](https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/master/webapp/src/js/services/search.js#L142) line and the filters will never update.

title: ZScore Charts are not being found
body:
Trying to load a zscore chart and errors are shown in console stating `Requested z-score table not found {t: "str", quote: "'", v: "weight-for-age"}`. Debugging the line below. The tableID isn't an ID it's an object and the prop .v is the actual tableId. This is what the object looks like ```{t: "str", quote: "'", v: "weight-for-age"}```

https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/50005163f2366819499576477fa49140389a1efe/webapp/src/js/services/z-score.js#L92


 https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/50005163f2366819499576477fa49140389a1efe/webapp/src/js/services/z-score.js#L17-L23

When this evaluates. ```tables[i].id === id``` it is evaluating to false because id is an object and not the actual id. 



**Steps to reproduce**:
Using demo form https://github.com/medic/medic-webapp/blob/master/demo-forms/z-score.xml
With zscore chart https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/blob/master/configuration/forms.md#z-score

title: Make webapp header logo image configurable
body:
**Summary**
Our current logo will still be the default on the webapp. The feature we are working on now will allow partners to swap in their own logo/image in place of our logo, should they so desire. We will share some basic guidelines for making the best use of the space and formatting files correctly but we will not actively restrict/police/enforce how the space ends up being used.

Read more and see examples here: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1qv8WkVIDaNNPUntFoB6EnBpkfhXi1Ax61zXVZ8LGjAo/edit?usp=sharing

**Webapp header image**
- In essence, we are creating a blank container box in the upper left corner of our webapp that is configurable - meaning partners can upload their own custom image in place of the default Medic Mobile logo
- The size of the container box in the upper left of the desktop webapp should be 170 x 50 px. This is my recommendation based upon the overall size of the header bar now, the size of the bar after the nav update, the general horizontal shape of most logos, and the needs of responsive page scaling
- The box should be vertically centered within the black header bar
- The far left edge of the box should stay aligned directly on top of the far left edge of the LHS column as the page scales (just as our current Medic logo does)

![blank box](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/45906389-c742cf80-bda8-11e8-9493-b518a081ea16.png)


**File upload**
- Where should this custom image be uploaded from? Assuming it should ideally be a place that all admin users have access to (i.e. the admin console). That way, if a partner decides down the road that they want to swap out the image with something else, they don’t need to come back to Medic in order to make the change.
- My initial suggestion is this: We rename the “Icons” page to “Images” and then we add “Header logo” and “About page logo” sections or tabs
- Next to the “Choose file” button for image upload, it would be nice if we could display a few sentences with reminder text such as “You can upload an SVG, PNG, or JPG file. File must be less than 100 KB… etc” 
- Unsure how easy or hard it is to restrict the types of files being uploaded, but ideally we would restrict the image types allowed and if a user tries to upload an unsupported image type, we should display a warning message indicating such.
- It would also be nice to set some sort of reasonable cap on the file size. Then, if the user tries to upload a very large image (say 10 MB) we can display a warning message indicating that the file is too large.
- We aren’t going to worry too much about whether or not the image matches the recommended dimensions or ratios. Whatever is uploaded, the image should always scale to fit inside whatever bounding container we’ve coded
- If an image is uploaded that does not match the end ratio or is larger than the recommended dimensions, it should automatically be scaled down, keeping proportions intact, to fit within the available space.

title: Allow sentinel transitions to run synchronously against incoming SMS messages
body:
Currently the flow for an SMS with a default response is slower than it could be:
 - CHW sends an SMS to the gateway, which takes it and puts it in it's queue
 - Gateway wakes up every minute and sends the SMS to Medic, gets any existing SMS to send back and closes the connection
 - Sentinel asynchronously updates the SMS report to add a default response
 - 1 minute later Gateway talks to Medic, finds this response and sends it out.

We should look into extracting sentinel into a shared lib that we can run in realtime when receiving new SMS. This means we will any resulting SMS as part of the same request.

Combined with #4858 this could greatly increase the responsiveness of SMS.

title: 4680 - Translate startup messages for non-English speakers
body:
# Description

People who do not have English as their primary language find our startup messages ("Loading assets", "Fetching Info (100 docs)..." etc) very confusing.

medic/medic-webapp#4680

# Comments

Since this translator isn't really a "best practice", I've done my best to encapsulate all required translations into `bootstrapper.js`. Previously, there was logic for updating the startup status in app.js and in controllers/inbox.js (inside Angular).

Message | Current | Proposed
-- | -- | --
Loading assets... | Appears at DOM load | Can't have translated strings prior to assets loading. For now, I just have a spinner with no text. Unsure what to do here?
Loading app… | Appears if/when replication begins | Unchanged
Starting app…| Appears after replication completes and before "Loading Rules" begins | I removed this, since it appears for just a few milliseconds and only when replication is required.
Fetching info (100 docs)… | Updates as initial replication progresses | Unchanged
Loading rules... | Appears mid-way through inbox angular module initialisation. | Appears after successful sync or when sync is not required. We may consider changing this to "Initializing..." since it now captures the whole application initialisation instead of just the rules.
Loading error, please check your connection. Try again | On bootstrapper error | Unchanged but `bootstrapper.js` handles it instead of `app.js`

I have also looked briefly into progress bars - approximating the entire startup progress, or doing one  just for replication. I'd be interested to look into improvements we can make to shorten start-up times if that feels like a priority. For that, it would be very helpful to have access to live or realist simulated long startup times.

title: Adds muting transition
body:
# Description

Adds muting transition that:
- allows muting on any level in the hierarchy 
- all descendants of a muted contact will also be muted
- a muted contact is marked by a `muted = true` flag. The muted flag is present in the target of the mute action and all their descendants
- muting a contact will change the state of all (own and descendants) schedules that are `scheduled` or `pending` to `muted` 
- new schedules for muted contacts will automatically have `muted` state
- unmuting a contact will unmute the target and all it's descendants
- unmuting a contact will change the state of all (own and descendants) schedules that are `muted` to `scheduled`
- all new contacts that have a muted parent will automatically receive the muted flag and have their schedules muted

Deprecates `update_notifications` transition in favor of muting.
Updates `lineage` shared library to hydrate patient by `uuid` as well, not just by `patient_id`.

Webapp:
- muted contacts appear grayed out in the LHS (styled same as deceased)
- profile pages of muted contacts have grayed out icons and the `"Muted"` text displayed under the name
- muted contacts in profile pages lists appear grayed out only if their parent is not muted
- a popup informing that the contact is muted appears when clicking to add an action (that is not an unmute form) from the profile page of a muted contact. If the user "agrees", they are redirected to the form, otherwise the popup closes and they remain on the profile page. 
- When submitting forms from the reports tab, the contact dropdowns mark the muted contacts with `"Muted"` text.

title: Schedules are not cleared for offline contacts/reports
body:
When working offline, a report submitted about a person that is not yet replicated will never be bound to that person by `patient_id` field.
As a consequence, this report will never be considered a `registration` and it's schedule will not be cleared by any clearing mechanism. 

**Steps to reproduce**:
 - Login with an offline user (on `gamma.dev` for example)
 - Go offline
 - Create a new person
 - Submit a pregnancy for this person
 - Go online and allow replication to happen
 - Create a new pregnancy for the same user

**What should happen**:
 - Scheduled tasks from the first report should be `cleared`

**What actually happens**:
 - Scheduled tasks from the first report are `scheduled`

I think we should expand our searching for registrations by checking for the `patient_uuid` field as well. 
I am not aware of what value `medic-client/registered_patients` provides now versus say `medic-client/reports_by_subject` (which indexes by `patient_id`, `patient_uuid` and `place_id`). 
Is there any situation where we'd want to _only_ obtain sms/online reports? If not, maybe we could retire `registered_patients` entirely.

# Description

Removes the audit layer to stop logging/tracking data into the audit db.
Introduces request headers X-Medic-Service and X-Medic-User to be captured
by an haproxy that controls access to couchdb.
The user is identified and logged in haproxy by:
1. the cookie header when available (api's userCtx.name) 
2. the X-Medic-User header that is now included for the common dbpouch put/post/delete.

We do not always capture the user for those cases that include queries, views
and other bulk operations. But we might be able to capture the session (cookie auth session) 
for a more detailed audit.

Also, the audit layer had logic to setup unique ids when saving new documents. 
This pr uses dbpouch.post to save new documents that require a new id 
and dbpouch.put for documents that already have an id.

The initial logs have been formatted as CSVs but we should be able to configure
them in any format. Initial csv format:
| client ip | http status | http method |  uri | service | user | req body | bytes read | response time | response header Content-Length |

We have all these logging options (end of the page table):
[haproxy configuration](https://cbonte.github.io/haproxy-dconv/1.8/configuration.html)

Here are some samples:
