title: RFC: An `_id` scheme for Medic 4.0
body:
**NB:** This is in the 4.0 "some day" project because it's obviously a huge change that would require nearly all documents to be rewritten and all offline users to re-replicate. We have quite a few of these ideas and are slowly collecting them together so we can try to only do this once.

This ticket exists to create discussion and provoke thought on how we could use this incredibly rare opportunity to be allowed to change our schema to our advantage.

# RFC: New `_id` scheme

This new `_id` scheme is an attempt to:
 - Increase data integrity by tying the location of a document to its identity, more fully expressing the complications around moving
 - Increase replication performance and decrease code complexity by allowing filtered replication based entirely around knowing a user's `facility_id` (available from their authentication record) and parsing ids in the changes feed, removing many other moving parts
 - Allow various simplifications based around being able to predict authorization / location based off id or id query ranges alone.
 - Increase native CouchDB performance by following CouchDB's proposed guidelines for id entropy

Currently we have four main different styles of identifier:
 - Static ids known at "compile" time, e.g. `_design/medic`, `settings`
 - Pseudo-static identifiers prepended with their type, e.g., `form:pregnancy`
 - Random uuids that are almost certainly a contact or a report
 - prepended random uuids (e.g. info documents) to provide meta information about the type above

The core idea is to replace the third and fourth item with a prepend-based concept similar but grander than the second type.

## A quick example

Here is an example of the `_id` of a CHW:

```
place/lGERgZdPSFS1wd+jFTlkjg==/fnzexFSYTkiDnJcU0j+CkQ==/Ff0ryVESRDWtgqf3P-er8Q==/contact/USLdS01USYCKGyFZSyDZUA==
```

Scary!

Here is a pregnancy report generated by.. actually we don't care who the author is. Generated *for* a mother, in a family, in the CHW's area / clinic:

```
place/lGERgZdPSFS1wd+jFTlkjg==/fnzexFSYTkiDnJcU0j+CkQ==/Ff0ryVESRDWtgqf3P-er8Q==/OBQeIGqaRbaAEjfccmLcMQ==/contact/VPch4hVNQoy5dRzds8hYUQ==/report/d12isV79RVmk112tlKxLRw==
```

SCARIER!

## Details

If it's not already obvious, the idea here is that ids are a descriptor for where and what something is, in a similar style to REST endpoint routes:

```
DH:     place/lGERgZdPSFS1wd+jFTlkjg==
HC:     place/lGERgZdPSFS1wd+jFTlkjg==/fnzexFSYTkiDnJcU0j+CkQ==
Clinic: place/lGERgZdPSFS1wd+jFTlkjg==/fnzexFSYTkiDnJcU0j+CkQ==/Ff0ryVESRDWtgqf3P-er8Q==
CHW:    place/lGERgZdPSFS1wd+jFTlkjg==/fnzexFSYTkiDnJcU0j+CkQ==/Ff0ryVESRDWtgqf3P-er8Q==/contact/USLdS01USYCKGyFZSyDZUA==
Family: place/lGERgZdPSFS1wd+jFTlkjg==/fnzexFSYTkiDnJcU0j+CkQ==/Ff0ryVESRDWtgqf3P-er8Q==/OBQeIGqaRbaAEjfccmLcMQ==
Mother: place/lGERgZdPSFS1wd+jFTlkjg==/fnzexFSYTkiDnJcU0j+CkQ==/Ff0ryVESRDWtgqf3P-er8Q==/OBQeIGqaRbaAEjfccmLcMQ==/contact/VPch4hVNQoy5dRzds8hYUQ==
Preg:   place/lGERgZdPSFS1wd+jFTlkjg==/fnzexFSYTkiDnJcU0j+CkQ==/Ff0ryVESRDWtgqf3P-er8Q==/OBQeIGqaRbaAEjfccmLcMQ==/contact/VPch4hVNQoy5dRzds8hYUQ==/report/d12isV79RVmk112tlKxLRw==
```

**Note 1:** There is more or less information we could add here, and we need to carefully consider what will and will not be useful, looking forward to hopefully not having to change this format for years to come. For example, we are not encoding the form type in the report url here. Do we want to? I'm not sure!

**Note 2:** The component identifiers are still UUIDs, they are just base64 instead of base16 to compress them a little. Code to achieve this in Node can be seen in the appendix. Code to achieve this in a browser is slightly more of a pain, but certainly not unachievable.

## Features this unlocks

### Increased data integrity

We can trivially extend `validate_doc_update` to ensure that a record's internally expressed hierarchy matches their identifier. This is nice because its codifying a presumption we already work off, that a record's location is immutable.

Currently you can "move" a record by altering its internal hierarchy. This is in the scary land of "undefined behaviours". It will almost certainly not work 100% correctly, and may work unpredictably, giving you different answers between different parts of the code, and different releases (even those where changes like this are not expressed in the semver, such as a patch level refactor).

In this new scheme, if you wish to move a record you have to delete the original and create a new record, forcing it to be deleted off devices and added only to those devices it's allowed to be on, and to be guaranteed to be refered to consistently throughout the applications that reference it.

### Faster scalable replication

_(NB: I realise replication is a very complicated subject. I **think** this is right, but I acknowledge I may be missing something very obvious which either makes the implementation more complicated / less beneficial, or even a non-starter. The purpose of this ticket is to discuss that if it arises.)_

With this id scheme we should be able to perform filtered replication using only:
 - The user's `facility_id`, pulled from their user document
 - The raw `_changes` feed as asked for by the user's request, probably with some limit multiplier for efficiency

CHW execution flow:
 - A restricted user hits the `_changes` endpoint, with e.g. `GET _changes?since=200&limit=100` with no other parameters
 - We simultaneously request the user's facility_id (we may already have this depending on what authication has run) and proxy the `_changes` feed to Couch, possibly muliplying the `limit` by some multiplier (e.g. 2x, or the number of known restricted users) as we presume some filtering will occur
 - Once we get the `_changes` results back we walk through every change `id`, and delete it out of the changes result unless:
     + If it's part of a whitelist known at compile time, e.g. a collection of static ids (`settings`) and partial ids (`/^form:/`)
     + If it `startsWith` their facility id, and does not end in `/purged`
 - Once we've done this, if our change count is less than the provided limit we loop until we've filled our changes feed
 - The final changes feed contains the same outer metadata (such as `last_seq`) as the last changes feed in the loop, but with the filtered list of ids.

Supervisor flow is nearly identical, except that we split over `/` and use that to determine if the record is too "far away" from the supervisor's facility to be replicated, based on their configured replication depth.

This is all you need to do, and all the support structures you need.

This scheme doesn't need:
 - specific views
 - tombstone generation
 - users providing their known documents

It supports both deleted documents and server-side purging.

It should also be very fast, use very little memory, and be embarrassingly parallel, lending itself to being multi-threaded, either inside api/nodejs, or written in an entirely different language which is easier to thread safely.

### Simplicity through predictability

There are probably lots of ways we can use this id scheme to both remove existing views, as well as running mango queries off the base id index.

For example, it is likely we could replace initial replication with three queries:
 - bulk docs for known static files
 - ranged query for `form:` ids (reports)
 - ranged query based on the user's facility id (this one involves updating our auth scanning in api to remove purged documents)

Correct authentication for documents can now be done by looking at ids at all points, probably simplifying various types of auth. E.g., you can reject GET requests before performing them, as well as being able to detect invalid query ranges (against ids).

There are probably more things you can do here.

### Increase native CouchDB performance

CouchDB works best when record id entropy tends towards the end of the id, not the start or evenly spread. This is why when you ask CouchDB to generate ids sequential requests generate very similar identifiers.

Moving to this scheme will correct our entropy distribution to be more CouchDB-friendly, presumably increasing performance in various ways.

## Downsides of this approach

Apart from the obvious re-replicate everything again thing.

 - If we ever want to replicate based on something not in our resulting id scheme we either have to change all ids again, or change replication back, or have some kind of `/more` feature in ids where we know that we have to pull that document out and hand-inspect it to fulfil more rule requirements
 - Purging has to be global. An option to get around this (if it's truely needed) could be to prepend chunks after `/purge/` describing the depths at which this purge is relevant, e.g. the chunk describing the clinic for CHWs, and the chunk describing the HC for supervisors.

# Appendix

## UUID generation

```js
// This is Nodejs code. Browser code is left as an execise for the reader
const uuid = require('uuid');

const uuid64 = () => {
    const buffer = Buffer.alloc(16); // Buffers are 8-bit, 16*8 => 128bits
    uuid(null, buffer)
    return buffer
        .toString('base64')
        .replace(/\//, '-');
}

uuid64();
```

## ID entropy

Presuming a good UUID implementation, a single UUID already has 2^128 bits of entropy, enough to never conflict. The `_id`s described above have absurd amounts of entropy, more than 2^768 depending how you calculate entropy and from whose perspective.

We could consider reducing this. For example, instead of generating an 128bit UUID per node, instead generate something smaller, say 32 bits. We would have to think carefully about how this works, because probability theory is confusing and we don't want to get it wrong.

## Migration

### Server side

The smart thing to do here would literally be to start again: we would write a script that loads all docs from the source db, renames them based on this scheme and writes them to the target db.

### Client side

Client-side migration being a pain is generic to the theoretical 4.0 release, and so ideas discussed here apply to the entire project.

As we're changing the replication scheme, one thing we could do is detect old versions by checking for old style replication requests and only returning a fake static changes feed containing the new code. Ideally we'd also be able to detect old-style upward replication and 404 / otherwise block it from occuring, either by something we're currently doing, or by adding a flag to >=4.0.0 upward replication and detecting the lack of that flag.

This should isolate the user's device in its current <4.0.0 bubble. They can use the app as normal with no disruptions, and will be updated once they restart.

Once they restart and 4.0.0 code is running we can do whatever we want. Specifically:
 - Complete a full, now-unblocked upward replication to make sure that everything left on their phone is pushed upward, using some kind of MitM to change the document identifier:
     + If we MitM client-side (fetch, service workers), change the `_id` to `_old/${_id}` and write a Sentinel transition would works out their real new id and re-writes their contents against the new id (on top of an existing doc or as a new one as needed)
     + If we MitM server-side (api) we don't need sentinel, we can do it in the api write
 - Delete the existing client-side PouchDB, and start a full initial replication from scratch.
 - Start as normal

body:

title: Optimize the `fix-user-db-security` migration for databases with many users
body:
It currently doesn't do any batching, and generates N parallel PUT requests to CouchDB, where N === the user count.

This is almost certainly A Bad Idea™ for larger databases.

We should at least not make those PUTs all concurrent.

This should be backported to 3.2.x.

title: Drop optimise event, move start event
body:
Drop "optimise", the manual compaction step. We don't need to do this
as we are compacting on write as we go.

Move start. This now happens once we decide we are going to purge, as
it's more useful to show this early and have something to show while
we pull in and organise documents that need purging.

medic/medic#5348

title: Adds support for sending messages to specific phone numbers.
body:
# Description

If provided with a valid phone number recipient, message-utils should use that as a `to` field instead of defaulting to the sender (`from`). 
Certain transitions (like `accept_patient_reports`) support including an explicit phone number as message recipient, while `multi_report_alerts` always passes explicit phone numbers when generating messages. 

medic/medic#5369

title: Errors when navigating away from edited forms
body:
We have a feature that shows a popup when navigating away from an edited form: https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/4013 . This is part of 3.3. This is not working as expected in latest code. 

**Steps to reproduce**:
- Open the app (user type is not relevant as long as you can open some sort of Enketo form). I will continue to describe steps as if logged in as admin and submitting contact creation forms, but the same happens when submitting reports. 
- Open a form to create a new contact (type is irrelevant)
- Edit one of the fields, so the app marks the form as `edited`
- Open browser console

**Bug 1:**
- Click on any of the tabs

**What should happen**:
- You should get a popup saying `This form is not finished....` and not navigate away from the form. Clicking on "YES" should perform the navigation, "NO" should keep you on the same page.

**What actually happens**:
 - Chrome and Firefox: Errors in the console 
```
Transition Rejection($id: 13 type: 6, message: The transition errored, detail: TypeError: Cannot read property 'preventDefault' of undefined)
TypeError: Cannot read property 'preventDefault' of undefined
```

This is most likely connected to a recent upgrade of ui-router in webapp, and a switch from `$stateChangeStart` broadcast to `$transitions.onStart`.

**Bug 2:**
- Click on a contact in the LHS list

**What should happen**:
- You should get a popup saying `This form is not finished....` and not navigate away from the form. Clicking on "YES" should perform the navigation, "NO" should keep you on the same page.

**What actually happens**:
- Chrome: You get the popup, but the page underneath also navigates to the contact you clicked, without interacting with the popup.
- Firefox: Same console errors as in Bug 1

**Environment**
 Instance: _localhost_
 Browser: _Firefox 65, Chrome 72, Chromium 71_
 Client platform: _Ubuntu 18_
 App: _webapp_
 Version: _3.4.x, 3.5.x_

title: Registration transition should calculate dates relative to reported_date
body:
Currently, `registration` transition calculates three dates:
a. date of birth
b. last menstrual period
c. expected birth date

https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/3d4f54ec5772fc2bcc4f77c68d0e4ab26ad0ebf8/sentinel/src/transitions/registration.js#L221
https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/3d4f54ec5772fc2bcc4f77c68d0e4ab26ad0ebf8/sentinel/src/transitions/registration.js#L155

All of these dates are calculated in reference to the moment Sentinel processes the doc instead of (what seems logical to me) the doc's `reported_date`.

In an ideal world, Sentinel would never crash, never be misconfigured and should always process all docs in a timely manner. Sadly.... 

@abbyad @garethbowen I'm not sure if this is a bug or working as intended.

title: Fix linking logic to prevent conflicts
body:
# Description

- reverse sequence between silencing registration and adding report uuid: we don't want to link a report to a reminder that has already been cleared. When tasks are cleared, the field `cleared_by` is added which is enough for the analytics team.

- fix linking logic to prevent conflicts: now if the the second put results in a conflict, we update the `_rev` and re-put.

- fix potential bug with finding the messages to clear: changed when the filter component is applied.  Indeed, if we consider 2 tasks belonging to the same group. title: Optimize deletion of read docs for databases with many users
body:
A sister of https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/5395 .

When Sentinel receives a delete, it attempts to delete the `read` docs from every user database. It doesn't batch and executes all requests in parallel. 

If there are enough users, it sometimes crashes CouchDB (I tested with 1000 users, on 3.3.x with Couchdb 2.3), other times just failing the operation.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. login as admin 
2. go to Contacts
3. open a form to add a new contact and edit something

title: Validate target ID uniqueness
body:
When creating Targets in the admin app you have to provide a unique ID but we don't have any validation to ensure the ID isn't a duplicate. This causes bugs [like this one](https://github.com/medic/medic/issues/5438).

Add validation when creating or updating Targets which stops users submitting duplicate IDs.

title: Add explanatory text about permissions to the admin app
body:
Add explanatory text about what the various permissions mean. Some are fairly self explanatory but others aren’t (for example, “can_view_unallocated_data_records”). It is hard for someone not intimately familiar with our app to understand what all of these mean. 

Suggest that a developer make the first pass looking at the code to see what each permission actually does. When the first pass is done, please loop in @jillrshah to help review the language.

A suggestion from Gareth is that we shouldn't even show the key in the UI - just the translated explanation. If we go this route, we might want to still have titles for each, but something that is more user friendly. For instance, "can_bulk_delete_reports" could be titled "Can bulk delete reports" with some explanatory text below describing what that means (i.e. “This feature allows a user to select more than one report at a time and delete the selected group in a single action.”)

title: Server side purge
body:
We recently added document purging on the client side which works really well for periodically deleting docs that are no longer needed. However because of the way it works it has to download the docs before it can determine if they should be purged. This will cause issues for people starting with a large number of docs, for example, if an existing user wipes the app or gets a new phone.

Instead, run the purge function on the server and store which users should purge the doc without deleting the doc itself - it must remain on the server. Existing clients will be told to purge the document from their local pouchdb. Exclude the document from the changes for those users so a new replication will never download it.

title: Angular $exceptionHandler too sensitive
body:
It appears that all UnhandledPromiseRejections are being pushed as feedback to the DB by the new $exceptionHandler, including network connection errors. 

**Steps to reproduce**:
 - Checkout latest master (3.5)
 - Deploy it - you don't need any configuration for this, just start the app 
 - I recommend deploying on an **empty throw-away DB**, as you're going to create thousands of identical feedback documents
 - Login as admin
 - Open the Dev tools network tab
 - Go to Messages tab
 - Keeping the network tab open, go offline (Via the network tab offline checkbox)
 - Click on the "Send message" button
 - Click "Cancel"

**What should happen**:
 - Your popup should go away and no new requests should appear in the network log

**What actually happens**:
 - The network tab quickly fills up with `_bulk_docs` requests that all fail (because we're offline). 
 - The `requests` counter should rise up quite quickly - don't wait too long, couple of seconds is enough
 - Go online again (Via the network tab offline checkbox)
 - It's very possible your browser will become unresponsive at this moment
 - Login to Fauxton and verify that you have **many** docs (depends on how long you stayed offline - my computer generates about 2000 in a couple of seconds), all feedback docs, all identical, all saying `Failed to fetch...`. 
 
**Some explanations**

 - Because our Modals are Promises that resolve when the user clicks "yes" and reject when the user clicks "no", not catching to the "no" qualifies as an unhandled promise rejection. We mostly do not catch "no"s if we don't want to do anything with them, so the above would be triggered on _most_ modals in the app. 
 - Clicking on the "No" button qualifies as an unhandled promise rejection, which the $exceptionHandler will pick up and try to post a feedback doc with it (which is another bug)
 - Because we are offline, the upload will fail, which will log another error which the $exceptionHandler will catch and will try to post a feedback doc with it  
 - Because we are offline, the upload will fail, which will log another error which the $exceptionHandler will catch and will try to post a feedback doc with it  
 - Because we are offline, the upload will fail, which will log another error which the $exceptionHandler will catch and will try to post a feedback doc with it  
 - You get the point

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/53957283-9f40f180-40e6-11e9-9178-d35eacf6e7c8.png)

 
 There are a number of other connection errors exception which are incorrectly reported as feedback, for example replication attempts of offline users when disconnected from the internet.
 
_Sincere apologies if the steps described above have crashed your browser/computer_

**Environment**:

- Instance: _local_
- Browser: _Firefox, Chrome, Chromium, irrelevant_
- Client platform: _Linux_
- App: _webapp_
- Version: _3.5_

title: Muso supervisors can't review mRDT reports while having a replication depth of 1
body:
## Some Background
Muso supervisors with a replication depth of 2 are forced to replication all families (clinics) and forms associated with those families. Many CHVs per supervisor * many familes per CHV yields an estimated 4000 home-visit forms per week for these supervisors. This causes performance problems. Performance of the app can be improved with purging, but replication for some users takes more than three days. To fix https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/5781, Muso is reducing the replication depth of supervisors to 1.

Muso is conducting an mRDT Trial starting April 1st in which supervisors need to review patient forms. These forms would require a replication depth of 3 (impossible), so Muso leverages the `needs_signoff` flag on reports. 

## Requirement
The needs_signoff flag only works for reports which are one level deeper than the user's replication depth. With a replication depth of 1, Muso supervisors cannot review a report at depth 3. 

For the April 1st trial, Muso is setting a replication depth of 2 for the mRDT supervisor (one user only) and configuring purging with aggressively supervisor-specific rules. However, this won't scale well for the mRDT scaleup in August as all supervisors would be hindered by multi-day replication times with the replication depth of 2. 

Muso needs a solution which would allow a replication depth of 1 for a user which can also review reports at depth 3.

title: Support a Muso Target - % of families which have received 2 home visits this month
body:
In Muso-land, a "home visit" can occur up to once per day per family. For any given family on any give day, the home visit has occured if either a) any member of the family has a report created on that day (which also meets some specific criteria that isn't important for this bug); or b) the family (clinic) has a home visit report created on that day.

A primary goal for Muso's CHWs is to visit every family twice per month. Muso has requested that a target be written which tracks this goal for CHWs. This number can't be calculated by inspecting the reports for any single contact, it is an aggregation of information from many contacts or many emitted target instances. Since nools does not preserved any state information from one contact to the next, I'm unsure how to build this target in either declarative config or the older nools.rules system.

I suspect we need a product change to support this requirement from Muso.

[Target code for total number of home visits](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/blob/muso-declarative/muso_declarative/targets.js#L3)

title: 4750 Moves selected to redux store
body:
# Description

Continuing on from [these PRs](https://github.com/medic/medic/pulls?utf8=%E2%9C%93&q=is%3Apr+is%3Aclosed+4750), this PR moves `selected` to the redux store which involves a significant number of changes (ran into a lot of problems with this).

Points to note:
- There some slightly weird logic flows in the code below. For now I think the best approach is to migrate to redux leaving functionality exactly as it is, and then potentially rethink some of the logic once the migration is finished in order to help with a) getting the migration done quickly and b) diagnosing bugs that are inevitably going to be introduced by this migration
- Introduction of **selectors**. Selectors provide an abstracted way of accessing the store which I've found beneficial for two reasons (read more [here](https://github.com/reduxjs/reselect#reselect)):
  1. If you change the organisation of the store significantly, you can update the selectors without having to update all the components that use those bits of store
  2. They're useful for computing derived data. Memoised selectors mean computing derived data only happens when the underlying store data actually changes, nifty.
- I somehow missed that `$scope.selected` was never actually defined in `inbox.js`, only in `contacts.js` etc, meaning that they were all actually separate variables. In redux they have now become one variable which shouldn't be a problem as it's cleared by every "module" (contacts, reports, etc) when initiated, but it's getting to the point with this redux work where reducers should probably be split out into modules so they can be split out again into separate variables.

medic/medic#5546

title: Creating / syncing meta db-s fails when db name is not "medic"
body:
When you deploy medic app and use a db name that is not `medic`, creation and replication of user meta dbs doesn't work, having all sorts of effects on the app.

For online users, which query the DB directly, loading reports fails and the console is riddled with replication failures. 
For offline users, loading reports works as the queryied DB exists locally, but replicating upstream will fail. 

The reason is that webapp builds the meta db name based on the main db name and adds a suffix: `<main-db-name>-user-<username>-meta`, while API hardcodes the meta db names to `medic-user-<username>-meta` both in `routing` and in the `user-db` service. 

Since we're intending to use meta db-s for more than storing read docs (telemetry, feedback, etc) we should make sure this data is uploaded correctly.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/54440080-b1eca380-4742-11e9-946c-19cf716890b8.png)

title: Update config/standard after medic-conf breaking changes
body:
*Please don't merge this until medic-conf v2.0.0 is merged and available*

# Description

Hey @eljhkrr and @derickl! I've proposed a few breaking changes to the declarative configuration system in the medic-conf repository. Instead of making these changes backwards compatible, I'd simply like to update all declarative configuration projects.

You can read about each of the changes I'm making [here](https://github.com/medic/medic-conf/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3Amuso-config). But to summarize the big changes briefly:

* I'm trying to standardize the contracts that we use to pass data from the application code into the webapp. So instead of each file having a custom contract (like "this file should declare one specific variable name x" or "this file should be an array" or "this file should return an object defining three attributes". All files now pass data through the standard `module.exports` pattern. I'm hoping this will crisp up the expected behavior of code, and allow code to be more unit testable since you can now use the file in unit tests directly.
* I'm trying to converge the CHT code onto the JavaScript community's standard patterns for sharing code between files. So code from shared libraries now export the data which can be used in other files. This adds some boilerplate - but hopefully that will be mitigated when we support ES6 in the near future. I'm trying to position us so that in a future change, we can include third-party libraries (underscore or moment) and we can share code between projects more easily through the arbitrary use of `require`. 
* I find it hard to understand (and hard to document) when functions are overloaded with multiple definitions depending on the value of other data in the declarative system. For example, when `events[n].dueDate` sometimes receives `(c, event)` and sometimes receives `(r, event)` and  sometimes receives `(r, event, scheduledTaskIdx)`. I'm doing an interface change so that interfaces remain constant. As such, there are minor parameter changes to `tasks.events[n].dueDate`, `tasks.actions[n].modifyContent`, `targets.emitCustom`, and `targets.date`.

I'm sending this review early, before it is ready to merge. I'd love our feedback and thoughts, as well as Elijah's assistance testing this for regressions ([code](https://github.com/medic/medic-conf/tree/v2)).

title: Investigate memory footprint of instances emitted by Targets
body:
For each target, for each value counted, two identical objects are held in medic's memory and a third is potentially held within Nools. Each object is roughly ~250 bytes in size.  So for example, if you're seeing a target which shows a count of "200" or which shows a percent of 50% ("100 out of 200"), there are 400 objects in memory for this (~100kb). Nools may also be storing a copy of this, because in practice I'm seeing around ~1kb of heap allocated per target per value counted (would be ~400 kb on heap in this example). 

For a Muso user with 700 reports, I see a delta of 5-7MBs of heap allocation when turning off all targets. For users with a large document count or projects with many targets, I suspect this could end up being quite significant and may warrant further investigation and measurement. 

First copy stored is this [emissions](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/webapp/src/js/services/rules-engine.js#L90) object in RulesEngine. The second copy is this [instances](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/webapp/src/js/services/target-generator.js#L66) object in TargetGenerator.

If this is indeed significant, some performance improvements we might consideration:

1. We are duplicating the stored data in both RulesEngine and TargetGenerator, can we share it? Does Nools have a copy we can use instead of storing this ourselves?
1. We store all emitted instances in RulesEngine, even for users who don't have permissions to `can_view_analytics`.
1. RulesEngine stores all emitted instances, even if they don't end up being relevant to the target's count. If we moved the logic in TargetGenerator's `isRelevant` function into medic-conf, we wouldn't have to store so many unused emitted instances.
1. Each time an instance is emitted, we recalculate the state of the target. This makes an O(n^2) operation and may have a noticeable impact on replication and purging.
1. Currently, the data in the instance is limited to just counting a single object. `{ pass: true }`, but we could emit something which contains a count: `{ count: 5, pass: 3 }`. This could significantly reduce the number of instances as well as improving code clarity in the declarative configuration system.

This ticket raises a small UX issue with lazy loading contact RHS sections (ticket #5086).

From @isaacholeman: "It looks like the UX issue that @ngaruko noted in ticket #5086 is a real issue especially for facility-based users, even if it's low priority because it won't affect our most typical low-end-Android-user."

Problem: We've implemented lazy loading on the contact RHS sections so that each section initially loads with a spinner and then renders the content when it is ready. The problem actually arises with faster connections and faster machines: in these cases, the spinner still shows up for a split second and then disappears, which looks a bit glitchy (see Bede's video of this happening on ticket #5086).

What should happen: If you have a fast connection, and the contacts page content loads quickly, you should not see the "loading" spinner at all.

Potential solution: Maybe we should time the spinner and not attempt to show it if the content loads quickly enough (say within half a second or so).

title: Replace all FontAwesome icons with svg icons
body:
Our app currently uses a mix of FontAwesome icons and custom png or svg icons. This request is to conduct a clean sweep of the app and replace ALL instances of FontAwesome icons with svg versions, and replace any random png icons with svg. This relates to any system icons that are embedded in the app (navigational page icons, hamburger menu icons, admin app). It does _not_ include an audit of form icons, since those are configurable by the partner.

Switching to the svg format allows us to use new custom icons that better convey the meaning instead of being limited to FontAwesome's generic library. Svg also ensures greater control and predictability when placing/aligning the icons in the app. The benefit of svg over png is that svgs can be re-colored directly in the app code. All of the icons are now a singular color to enable optional re-coloring in the code. Some of the new icons will appear quite similar to the icons we've always been using while others have been updated to improve clarity and/or consistency. 

![Screen Shot 2019-03-25 at 4 48 20 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/54962115-e1f52d00-4f20-11e9-978b-8d2430c5c7fc.png)

Icons for the primary page tabs should be displayed at a 30 x 30 px size.
- Messages used to be an envelope but is now conversation bubbles, to more accurately reflect the chat-like nature of the experience
- Tasks used to be a flag but is now a person holding a bag walking to conduct a visit.
- Reports used to be an abstract bulleted list but is now an open book to indicate records.
- People used to be a singular person and is now a group of people.
- Analytics used to be a bar chart and is still a chart but with a trend arrow.

![Screen Shot 2019-03-25 at 5 07 03 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/54962048-9b073780-4f20-11e9-9420-59e2d7ba4cc4.png)

All of the icons in the hamburger menu also have new svg replacements, as well as all of the icons that appear on the admin app/configuration pages. Hamburger menu icons should be displayed at a 20 x 20 px size (for now, until nav update). Any other icons that appear anywhere else in the app, such as the admin app, should default to display at 30 x 30 px.

The source svg files can be downloaded at https://drive.google.com/drive/u/1/folders/1PQ3Ydd3CyHToHXYnRx0oMPsTpkT3i3cv.

title: UHC metrics are incongruous between contacts and analytics tab due to month_start_date
body:
Muso has several UHC-specific targets which report metrics which overlap with the data on the UHC-enabled contacts tab. For example, they track "total number of home visits this month" and "% of families which have received >= 2 home visits this month" in the analytics tab.

The UHC data on the contacts tab reports on a monthly period from the 26th to the 25th (eg. Feb 26th to March 25th). This is controlled via a configurable "month_start_date" in app_settings.  At the same time, the same data is reported on the targets tab from the 1st to the last of the month (eg. Feb 1st to March 1st). This is not configurable.

The two metrics aren't aggregating the same information and appear broken.
* On March 1st, the contacts tab reports "10 home visits for Bob's family" and the analytics tab reports "0 home visits this month". 
* On March 26th, the contact's tab tab reports "0 home visits" for everybody and the analytics tab reports "350 home visits this month".

This is two tabs for the same user at the same time:
![Screenshot from 2019-03-27 09-20-59](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9014751/55093478-b0d84200-5071-11e9-899f-fa4e9f1a08c4.png)

title: Work out what we want to do with Enketo XML, and do that thing
body:
When creating reports we store the user-entered data effectively twice:
 - Once as the raw XML that Enketo returns to us, for use by subsequent Enketo invocations (i.e editing docs)
 - Once as extract JSON in `doc.fields.{}`, for use by everything else (on-screen display, configurable logic like rules and schedules, impact and analytics via couch2pg, etc)

Originally we stored the XML in the `doc.xml` property, as a string.

We later realised that this is inefficient / unhelpful, because CouchDB's view generation performance is a function of the size of a JSON document, and nothing refers to it except editing. So, we moved it into an attachment.

However, this has caused other performance problems:
 - Replication is less efficient in general, because the algorithm requests attachments separately
 - Replication is **far** less efficient relevant to CouchDB 2.0, because we can now batch document GETs, but not attachments GETs, so the disparity is far more obvious
 - For a reason yet to be investigated, PouchDB view generation is **far** slower with attachments present (it should be at worst identical).

We need to work out what to do here.

Obvious options include:
 - Prioritise replication speed and PouchDB view generation performance over CouchDB view generation performance and move the XML back into a string against the JSON
 - Delete the XMl altogether, and re-generate the XML from the `doc.fields` object when we want to edit (hat-tip @dianabarsan for that brilliant suggestion)
 - Do any amount of PouchDB investigation and performance improvements to solve any or all of the problems listed above

Diana's suggestion sounds ideal, and IMO should be investigated first, but it can be up for discussion.

Context: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1kXjsF-orndz0-V5UFf_Esx5J-ogeQ6_tALCwE1K0tvA/edit#heading=h.29bkt8nfi7kw

title: Measure and if possible improve CouchDB GET performance via API
body:
While doing some performance benchmarks (see Context below) I noticed that attachment GETs are really slow for what they are.

This may be true for all GETs, and could be due to our new security code making sure you're allowed to GET the thing you're asking for.

We should measure the performance of GET requests (and honestly authenticated interactions with api in general), work out if we're adding overhead and how much, and see if there are ways we can improve the code to remove those overheads.

Obvious things would be caching certain critical pieces of data, though it's unclear what we could easily cache (apart from UserCtx). At the very least we should understand what is going on.

Context: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1kXjsF-orndz0-V5UFf_Esx5J-ogeQ6_tALCwE1K0tvA/edit#heading=h.29bkt8nfi7kw

title: Investigate Geckoview as a replacement for Crosswalk
body:
When doing some performance tests recently (see Context below) I noticed that Firefox seems to have a much more performant implementation of IndexedDB than Chrome does (or PouchDB uses it in a way that Firefox likes more, or something).

Especially with Crosswalk EOL'd, and with us definitely wanting to squeeze as much performance out of the phones we're deployed to as possible, it may be worth checking out [GeckoView](https://wiki.mozilla.org/Mobile/GeckoView) as an alternative.

Things we care about:
 - Does our app work correctly in general
 - While PouchDB generates views faster, are other things faster? Or slower? Or the same? The performance of common actions (esp those picked out so far for Telemetry) should be looked into
 - As noted: Chrome *does* replicate faster than Firefox (and thus potentially Geckoview). We should see if this is true
 - Does it allow us to easily increase / make infinite our quota (the main reason we use Crosswalk today)
 - Does it get updated frequently? Does it allow us to stay closer to modern browsers (right now we're on Chrome 53 until we work out how to build Crosswalk again or move off it)?
 - Is is easy to integrate with and to build and use on Android?

Context: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1kXjsF-orndz0-V5UFf_Esx5J-ogeQ6_tALCwE1K0tvA/edit#heading=h.29bkt8nfi7kw

title: SSL + DNS stack for on-device testing
body:
# Description

This is an unfortunate barrier to on-device testing which comes from service workers. Run `grunt exec:mobile-service-stack` to spin up a DNS server + SSL proxy, then follow the steps to use it on your Android device. This process enables secure testing via https://medic.dev.

title: Expired tasks don't disappear from the Tasks tab when they expire
body:
1. Configure a task which will emit with a dueDate of today, and an expiry date of tomorrow.
1. Set your clock to 11:55pm, refresh the page, navigate to the 'tasks' tab and see the task.
1. Wait 5 minutes, and you should see the dueDate "today" change to "yesterday" and turn red.
1. Set your clock to tomorrow + 11:55pm, refresh the page, and view the task.

Expected: After 5 minutes, this task should disappear because it has expired.
Observed: Wait 5 minutes, and you will see the dueDate "tomorrow" change to "2 days ago". Refresh the tab and the expired task will disappear.

There is some [code in LiveList which is run at midnight](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/webapp/src/js/services/live-list.js#L543) which refreshes the description of the task. There is an expectation that we should maybe also remove expired tasks here.

title: Fix UHC styling when using both UHC and muting at the same time
body:
There is a bug/oversight in our UI styling when using both UHC and muting features at the same time. 

**What it currently looks like:** 
When a contact is muted and is displaying a grey icon in the main contacts list, the UHC date last visited and visits per month text is still styled red. This is confusing as it sends conflicting signals to the user. The red says “look at me, I’m important”, while the grey icon and muted status is meant to say “don’t worry about me, I’m not as important”.

**What it should look like:**
- If a contact is muted, the date last visited text should always be colored black, even if over 30 days.
- If a contact is muted, the number of visits per month (right side) is always grey, no matter if the visit count is 0, 1, 2, or 2+.
- If a contact is muted, the number of visits per month (right side) does not have a warning sign icon associated with it, no matter if the visit count is 0, 1, 2, or 2+.

**Mockups**
On the left is the current problematic styling. On the right is the desired styling.

![Screen Shot 2019-04-19 at 9 12 45 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/56432724-55b9f980-6283-11e9-9761-e359d5816417.png)


IMPORTANT: Another option could be to remove all UHC information from muted contacts entirely (don't display the date last visited or visits this month at all for those who are muted). But this should only be done if we are also able to accomplish #5596. If the muted contacts remain intermingled amongst active contacts then I think it makes sense to keep the UHC information, as it explains the sorting method.

title: Sort muted contacts to the bottom of the contacts list
body:
Right now muted contacts remain on the main contacts list, intermingled amongst active contacts, the only difference being that their icons are styled grey.

Our initial proposal for muting was that we would like to collect all of the muted contacts in a separate folder that lives at the bottom of the list. However this posed some technical challenges and we dropped it from the muting MVP.

@dianabarsan  said theoretically we could re-sort the contacts, but this would require updating the form that lists the people, and all phones would have to re-index their data.

An alternative could be sorting muted contacts to the bottom of the list ONLY when the list is sorted by “date last visited”. In UHC mode the default sorting is configurable by project, and any UHC user can go in at any time and toggle the sorting back and forth between “by date last visited” and “alphabetically”. But if _most_ UHC projects set their default sort to date last visited (Muso does), and if _most_ users typically leave it on the default sort, this solution could help most users in most cases.

Would be nice if devs could explore the potential solution described above (which would only help UHC projects) and/or any other ways to sort the muted contacts to the bottom of the list, which might potentially work across all projects.

title: Integration with Africa's Talking SMS aggregator
body:
A new project EBS wants to use feature phones and SMS instead of smartphones and data. Usually we use medic-gateway running on android to send and receive SMS using medic-api APIs, but it has some issues including being dropped from the play store, the app going to sleep, low throughput, high latency, etc. It would be much better to use a specialized third party cloud hosted aggregator instead. For this project we've chosen [Africa's Talking](https://africastalking.com/sms/twowaysms).

1. Create a new routine to send SMS via Africa's Talking (both immediate messages such as auto replies, and scheduled messages generated periodically).
2. Create a new API (potentially multiple endpoints) that Africa's Talking will call when an SMS is received.
3. Create a new API to update the status of outgoing messages as they are delivered.
4. This integration must be disabled by default, and all the account information must be configurable.

Africa's Talking provides a sandbox mode you can use during development and testing, and have support if required. The also have an [npm SDK package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/africastalking) which exposes a simple API to use, as well as tutorials on how to integrate.

There will likely be more integrations with other providers at a later date so consider refactoring the gateway and Africa's Talking integrations to use shared services where possible to make reuse easier for the next integration.

@newtewt prototyped an integration using expressjs which almost worked and may be useful as a starting point.

title: Add feature to create a place via SMS
body:
You can create a patient using the `add_patient` trigger on the [registration transition](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/sentinel/src/transitions/registration.js#L349) but there's no way to create a place via SMS so if you want to register a new household you need to do that in the webapp before registering the patients.

Example workflow:

1. CHP: `RF Smith family` (where RF is a JSON form for registering families).
2. Response: `Smith family registered with place ID 11111`
3. CHP: `R 11111 John`
4. Response: `John added to the Smith family with patient ID 11112`
5. CHP: `R 11111 Jane`
6. etc...

title: 6042 fix case sensitive issue

# Description
The immunization visit form (form: C_IMM) submitted from collect app has value `Yes` for a immunization received, i.e. `"received_bcg": "Yes"`. With this commit, the report tab will load without the facilities tree filter being built. When the user clicks on the tab, an initial load of the facilities tree takes place. Subsequent load happen as the user is scrolling through the list of facilities hierarchy and reaching the bottom of the list.

medic/medic#4423

# Code review items

- Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/blob/master/development/style-guide.md), documented if necessary.
- Documented: Configuration and user documentation on [medic-docs](https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/)
- Tested: Unit and/or e2e where appropriate
- Internationalised: All user facing text
- Backwards compatible: Works with existing data and configuration or includes a migration. Any breaking changes documented in Changes.md.

title: Offline users are seeing form errors same user online has no errors
body:
**Describe the bug**
When an offline user is offline there is an error being shown when trying to view forms. When that user is online there is no error. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
Using standard config.
Log in as an offline user with the browser online
Navigate to a person
View any form. It displays properly.
Set the browser to offline
View any form
The error `Error loading form. Please try again or check with an administrator.` is displayed. Console logs are below. 

**Expected behavior**
The forms display so the user can report details.

title: JavaScript errors and crash stacks not logged to the console
body:
**Describe the bug**
Not all JavaScript errors and crash stacks are reported to the console.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Open `webapp/webapp/src/js/controllers/inbox.js` in an editor and delete `Auth` from the ngInjection list (line 24).
1. Rebuild app
1. Login to the webapp

**Observed behavior**
The console has no errors.

**Expected behavior**
This is a basic scripting error in which we are using an undefined variable. The app fails to load (expected) but there should be an error in the console explaining why.



I think this bug is important and labelled it Priority 1 because these console errors are often our only way to investigate/understand live-site issues on the client.

title: Xform rendering hides choices when relevance condition and choice filter are applied to a secondary question
body:
**Describe the bug**
Choices for a secondary `select_one/select_multiple` field do not show when both relevance condition and choice filter are applied. Consider the following design xls immunization section:

| Question/Note/Label  | Type | Required | Choices | Condition (Relevance/Show only if + Constraints/Validation) |
| ------------- | ------------- | ------------- | ------------- | ------------- |
| Select the vaccines that were given on {{date}} *Tick every condition/symptom that applies*  | select_multiple  | yes  | BCG, Birth Polio (OPV 0), OPV, PCV, DPT-HepB-Hib, IPV, Rota, Vitamin A, Measles  | Don't show vaccines already reported. Birth Polio(OPV 0) if age <= 2weeks, OPV, PCV, Rota and DPT-HepB-Hib  if age >= 6 weeks, Vit A if age >= 6 months, Measles if age >= 9 months  |
| Select which dose of OPV was given on {{date}}  | select_one  | yes  | OPV 1/2/3  | If OPV is selected. Show OPV 2 if age >= 10 weeks, OPV 3 if age >= 14 weeks. Don't show doses already reported.  |
| Select which dose of PCV was given on {{date}}  | select_one  | yes  | PCV 1/2/3  | If PCV is selected. Show PCV 2 if age >= 10 weeks, PCV 3 if age >= 14 weeks. Don't show doses already reported.  |
| Select which dose of DPT-HepB-Hib was given on {{date}}  | select_one  | yes  | DPT-HepB-Hib 1/2/3  | If DPT-HepB-Hib is selected. Show DPT-HepB-Hib 2 if age >= 10 weeks, DPT-HepB-Hib 3 if age >= 14 weeks. Don't show doses already reported.  |
| Select which dose of Rota was given on {{date}}  | select_one  | yes  | Rota 1/2  | If Rota is selected. Show Rota 2 if age >= 10 weeks. Don't show doses already reported.  |
| Select which dose of Measles was given on {{date}}  | select_one  | yes  | Measles 1/2  | If Rota is selected. Show Measles 2 if age >= 18 months. Don't show doses already reported.  |

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Configure the above, a sample can be found [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1rMD49QfSO-xHSjt3MZ5vBZqy-RggU_deVh6kMZ0fCKc/edit#gid=1042357020)

**Screenshots**
See captures above.

- Browser: _Chrome_
- Client platform: _Linux_
- App: _webapp_
- Version: _3.4.0_

**Additional context**
This was experienced in _3.3.0_ too. The workaround applied is merging vaccines and doses, i.e. instead of asking to select dose say for OPV, have vaccines as OPV 1, OPV 2 and OPV 3 ...

cc @derickl @smbuthia 


**Why Now?**
Partner(s): Internal
Reason(s): A partner will have CHWs/Supervisors with a detrimental experience, thus providing bad care

title: Add Zapier webhook to Travis
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently we have Travis CI notifications in a group Slack channel for all failures, and when the success status changes. These notifications occur for all branches, which becomes overly noisy in Slack.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
From internal discussion the first phase would be to reduce noise by only showing failures and changes of status of the master branch. Optionally, we could notify only the user in question.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Alternatively we could disable Slack notifications altogether, and rely on email notifications to individuals, otherwise have the notifications in another channel altogether, and they could monitor that channel with notifications for their name/handle.

title: Ability to calculate how many tasks are shown and completed by users
body:
To improve our impact we must first measure our impact.

One of our major features is tasks and we make it very difficult to measure how many tasks are being shown to users and how many tasks are being completed. This is due to tasks being ephemeral and generated on the phone so server side analytics queries don't have access to this information. Instead the impact team create custom queries based on the configuration of each project but this is error prone and time consuming.

One solution would be to write tasks to the database and replicate to couchdb but this could have a potentially serious performance impact.

Consider various implementations and analyse the performance impacts of each before implementation.

title: Calculate data for DHIS2 reports
body:
Every month CHPs are expected to submit a DHIS2 report which records information such as "Number of households visited". We have enough information to automate the calculation of much of this data so we can make the reporting much more efficient and less error prone by prepopulating the form. Note that as well as the aggregate data we also need to be able to view the items that contributed to this total (#5660), using the above example we need to show not only the number of households visited, but also the names of the households.

It may be possible to configure nools to generate a task which has collects all the data and passes it to the form using global variables to store data as the families are being processed.

Alternatively we could create a new doc type to store this data and create a new instance each month on the phone.

Analyse the implementations and prove and/or implement the correct approach.

title: Ability to configure forms access based on hierarchy
body:
_*User story*_
As LG scales up and work on many experiment projects, it’s becoming increasing critical to have a way to `dynamically configure which CHVs access certain workflows` and who don’t have access. Sometimes CHVs participating in experiments are not segregated in a clear way like per branch. We can have sample CHVs from multiple branches.

We also need an intuitive way for non technical staff to assign and de-assign workflows/forms to CHVs unlike the current method where we put CHV uuids on the contact summary to indicate CHVs eligible for a certain experiment

_*Suggested solution*_
Adding an array of forms on the place object. These forms should be visible to everyone below the hierarchy. If you don’t want a form visible to everyone, you configure it down the hierarchy on the relevant place object. Check the example below
```
{
    "name":"…..",
    "uuid":"………",
    "forms": ["assessment.xml", "pregnancy.xml", ….],
    …
}
```
We can have a web tool (maybe on the admin panel) where a non-technical user can assign forms to branches or individual CHVs

title: Update how the in-app tour pop-up reminder works
body:
Relates to #5597, #5680, #5681, #5682. Full design spec: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ErZ7eC-Cbrsgwu0uaIfGq9ZeLuhma1h5K0xvYeRv2KU/edit#

Users can access the in-app tour anytime from the secondary hamburger menu by clicking on the “Guided Tour” link. Users may also access the tour from a periodic pop-up window. Right now this window only appears when the app first launches, which means it might not even be seen by CHWs since oftentimes an admin is the one to first launch the app.

Improvement: We would like this tour reminder window to display whenever there is a new “unread” tour topic. This means we will need the ability to track whether or not a tour has been "read". 

**Determining read/unread status**
- Each tour page section/topic is technically a separate tour. We want to start tracking if and when we’ve shown a particular tour. 
- All tours will start off being marked “unread”
- As soon as a user launches a tour, we will mark it as “read” (we are not going to require them to click through to the last tip in the section) 
- Every time we load the app, we will check for tours the user hasn’t read. If we introduce three new topics, those three sections would automatically be marked “unread”, and the user should see the tour pop-up prompt.
- Do we mark a read tour as “unread” again if we’ve made a change? It depends on how big of a change/update we’ve made. If we want the user to see the prompt again, we would “rename” the tour so it looks like a new tour.

**The pop-up window**
- The first time this window displays for brand new users, it should say something like _“Welcome! Before you get started using the app, take our guided tour to learn the basics.”_ It could also say something like _“If you’d like to access this tour again at a later date, open the menu in the upper right and select “Guided Tour”._ There should be a checkbox option for “Remind me later” but there should also be a way to just close out of the window. 
- Current app users will only see the pop-up if the app detects a new “unread” tour topic. The window in this case should say something like _“Your app has been updated - explore new features now"_. Again, there should also be a checkbox option for “Remind me later”. 
- If the "Remind me later" box is selected, the app will pause the reminder about new unread tour topics for some period of time, perhaps for a week. After a week it will once again display, and the user can again choose to close out entirely, check remind me later again, or actually look at the new tour content.

title: Turn the in-app tour table of contents pop-up into a true page
body:
Relates to #5597, #5679, #5681, #5682. Full design spec: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ErZ7eC-Cbrsgwu0uaIfGq9ZeLuhma1h5K0xvYeRv2KU/edit#

Right now when you click on "Guided Tour" you get a pop-up window where you can select from different page topics. Improvement: The table of contents page will now be a real page, not a modal, just like the About page.

**Tour table of contents page**
- The page should have a short text description that says something like _“This tour gives a guided walkthrough of the app. To go through the full tour, select the button below.”_ with a blue “Begin Tour” button (clicking on this button will start the user at the first topic, General)
- Following this there should be a linked table of contents with the text “To jump to a specific section of the tour, select one of the links below”. There will be an order to the tours/topics but users can click on any topic to skip to a certain section.
- For this initial launch, there will be 6 total topics/tours (1. General, 2. Tasks, 3. People, 4. Targets, 5. History, 6. Messages).
- All users will see the “General” tour. Whether or not a user sees a particular page tour depends on whether or not they have access to that page. For example, many CHWs may never see the Messages tour/topic.

![2019 tour - 2 table of contents](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/58039138-b472cd00-7ae6-11e9-98ec-b6196cf661f9.png)

title: Updates to the in-app tour functionality, including linking tours together
body:
Relates to #5597, #5679, #5680, #5682. Full design spec: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ErZ7eC-Cbrsgwu0uaIfGq9ZeLuhma1h5K0xvYeRv2KU/edit#

Currently a user first chooses a page from the main table of contents (like "Tasks"), they complete the Tasks tour, and then they are done. If they would like to continue and view the "People" tour next, they need to go back to the table of contents and choose the "People" topic. Improvement: link together the different in-app tours so that a user can go through the entire app tour without returning to the table of contents.

In essence how we will do this is to insert a new transitional tip between each section that has a "Next" button instead of a "Finish" button. The transitional tip will say something like "_You have completed the “Tasks” section of the tour.  To proceed to the "People" section, select “Next.” To exit the tour, select “Quit.”"_ Note: the linked string of tours may differ from user to user, depending on whether or not a user has access/visibility to a particular tab. For instance, CHWs often don't see the Messages tab, so they won't see the Messages tour, and the sequence will skip over the Messages tour.

![2019 tour - 6 general transition](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/58039838-be95cb00-7ae8-11e9-9af0-61584fd7003b.png)


Just to summarize:

**Functionality we aren’t altering**
- We will continue to use the same bootstrap tour library that we currently have
- The tour will continue to use the real app instance for the walkthrough 
- Technically, each page section/topic will be created as a separate tour. If a user doesn’t have access to a particular tab (for example, Messages) then they will not see any tips relating to Messages, and they will not see Messages in their table of contents. 
- If a user does have visibility to a tab, but doesn’t have the appropriate data, for example if they can see the tasks tab but don’t currently have any open tasks, the tips will still display but on top of an empty page.
- We will attach tips to a certain element (like a button or an icon), so that when the element moves around as the page scales, the tip will move around with it automatically
- Text is translated but nothing else is currently configurable
- The tour is not mandatory - users can close out of it at any time by clicking on the X in the corner.

**Desired changes to functionality**
- The table of contents page will now be a real page, not a modal, just like the About page.
- For this initial launch, the tour will only include general page overviews, but in the future it could also include special feature topics such as “Muting” or “UHC mode”.  
- The page overviews will obviously be contained to a single tab in the app, but a feature tour may jump between different pages to demonstrate the full workflow.
**- The different sections/topics of the tour will now be linked together so that a user can optionally choose to go through the entire tour without going back to the table of contents at the end of each section.** 
- Tour content will be updated as needed (not necessarily with each release) alongside the public release notes process.

**Other notes on linking tours**

- The very first tip of the very first tour topic does not have a Previous button (The first tip on the “General” section, in this case)

![Screen Shot 2019-05-20 at 10 17 41 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/58039771-93ab7700-7ae8-11e9-9262-b29e6d179baf.png)

- At the end of a tour/topic, we will have a transition slide which names the next section and gives the user a choice to continue on or to close out of the tour (with Next and Quit buttons)
![Screen Shot 2019-05-20 at 10 17 48 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/58039785-9c03b200-7ae8-11e9-9daa-6b71ca8b9d67.png)

- The very last tip of the last tour topic has a “Finish” button instead of a “Next” button

title: Cache the path accessed from _rewrite
body:
# Description

Another regression from #5361. The android app navigates the user to `/medic/_design/medic/_rewrite/` and does not use the root url. To support offline mode, we need to ensure that a redirect from that rewrite page to root is cached.

I see a few options here: 

1. Existing service workers - The `appcache-upgrade.html` could register the existing service-worker and redirect once registration completes. During an upgrade this would load all of the app's resources during an empty page and is not ideal.
1. Appcache - Given that we have the appropriate manifest already in place (required for the upgrade process), I think this is the easiest and is the fix I pursued here.
1. New service worker - Could also do this. But it's a new file, a new build step, and a bit of a registration process. If things go wrong on this page, we have no feedback mechanic.
1. I hoped a `301` permanent redirect would work here. But this really complicates how we clear the appcache during the upgrade to service workers.

#3986 

Nasty business in the app since we now navigate to `/rewire`, get an appcached version of that page, redirect to `/`, and get a serviceworker cached version of that page. So I'm coupling this with a build-time flag in the app to avoid this for partners when they migrate to >3.5.
https://github.com/medic/medic-android/pull/70

title: Update the levels displayed in breadcrumbs across the app
body:
We use breadcrumbs to display contextual information about where a person/place belongs in the app hierarchy. Depending on the user, sometimes the breadcrumbs can contain redundant and unnecessary information. In this example, I am Amanda Cilek, and "Amanda Cilek's Area" is the place I belong to. I do not need to see "Amanda Cilek's Area" in the breadcrumbs of every single report that I have submitted.
![Screen Shot 2019-05-28 at 4 52 21 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/58519816-03190a80-816a-11e9-9255-5acbc8f7763d.png)

This request is to update how we handle breadcrumbs so that we show all levels **except for** the level the user themselves belongs to, the top-most level. The data underneath will still have the entire hierarchy, we'll just choose how much to show based on the logged in user. For example, when I look at my reports tab in the above instance, I should no longer see "Amanda Cilek's Area" at the end of every breadcrumb. However if my manager logged in and looked at the same reports, my manager _would_ still see "Amanda Cilek's Area".

This update should apply to wherever breadcrumbs show on the **LEFT HAND SIDE** of the app (currently Messages and Reports, but also Tasks once [#5710](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5710) is done). 

Wherever breadcrumbs are shown on the **RIGHT HAND SIDE**, we should continue to show all breadcrumbs as users often use these as a shortcut to navigate back to the top level.

title: Schedules are not cleared with Unicode form codes
body:
**Describe the bug**
Reported in `medic-projects`: https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/6366

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Load standard config on an instance.
1. Replace "N" form with "क" (do this in the form definition and `registrations` config, alternatively you can duplicate the form and schedule from another form)
3. Submit your new "क" form, wait until your report is processed and patient created. The report should have one scheduled task. 
4. For the new patient, submit a "P" form.

**Expected behavior**
After your "P" report is processed, the previous "क" report scheduled task should be cleared.

**What actually happens**
The scheduled task from your "क" report is still scheduled. 

**Environment**
- Instance: any 3.4, 3.5 instance
- App: api, sentinel
- Version: 3.4, 3.5

**Additional context**
When validating whether a report is a valid registration, we extract the form code from the document `form` property with `/^[^\w-]*([\w-]+)[^\w-]*$/` [here](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/shared-libs/registration-utils/src/index.js#L3).
In javascript, `\w` does not match non-ASCII unicode even when using the `u` flag. 
Using the `\p` metacharacter along with the `u` flag instead works, like:
`/^[^\p{L}\p{N}_-]*([\p{L}\p{N}_-]+)[^\p{L}\p{N}_-]*$/u`

title: Contacts moved by "medic-conf move-contacts" do not disappear from user's device and synchronization of any changes fail silently
body:
**Describe the bug**
Medic-conf 2.0.5 supports moving contacts within the hierarchy via the action "move-contacts".  When an offline user has downloaded the details for some contacts which are then removed from that position of the hierarchy, the contacts do not disappear. The contact remains on the user's device, but any updates made to the contact (or any reports created for that contact) will silently fail to sync. This can result in silent data loss. 

Known fix is for the offline user to clear cache and perform a clean synchronization. However, it is not straightforward to drive all contacts to complete this task. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Given offline user with `facility_id='health_center_1'` which has child `clinic_1`. 
1. Log in as user 
1. Edit contact under `clinic_1` and resync 
1. `medic-conf move-contacts upload-docs parent=health_center_2 clinic_1` 
1. Synchronize as user 
1. Edit contact again under `clinic_1` and resync 

**Expected behavior**
The edits made by this user should sync or an error should appear so the user knows the data did not sync. Ideally, these documents should be removed from the client's device. 

Observed: Documents remain. Synchronization of data fails silently.

title: Webapp doesn't support languages that are not pluralized by `make-plural`
body:
**Describe the bug**
Reports fail to load when the user language isn't pluralized by `make-plural`. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Install 3.5 (or 3.4)
2. Create a new language with a code that is not-existent or is not pluralized by `make-plural`. For example "rn". 
I prefer to copy whole contents of a translation file that already exists and just change the `code` and `_id` fields to match.
3. Login as an online user to the instance and change your language to "rn". Go to reports. **Refresh**
4. Observe that no reports load on the LHS and translations are missing from some of the filters.

**Expected behavior**
Reports LHS should load. 

**Logs**
There are no errors logged in the console.

**Screenshots**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/58900966-dbe1b080-8708-11e9-9318-cf1a82afb049.png)


**Environment**
- Instance: local, [live instance](https://github.com/medic/medic-projects/issues/6310)
- Browser: Chrome
- Client platform: Linux
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.4, 3.5 (possibly earlier)

**Additional context**
There are no errors visible in the console because `angular-translate` [deliberately ignores all translation loading errors](https://github.com/angular-translate/angular-translate/blob/master/src/service/translate.js#L1950):
```
langPromises[key]['finally'](function () {
    clearNextLangAndPromise(key);
})['catch'](angular.noop); // we don't care about errors (clearing)
``` 
If I change the source to actually log the error, replacing `angular.noop` with `console.error`:
```
Error: Localisation function not found for locale "rn"
    at Object.get (plurals.js:31)
    at new MessageFormat (messageformat.js:37)
    at Object.setLocale (angular-translate-interpolation-messageformat:121)
    at eachInterpolator (angular-translate.js:1633)
    at Object.forEach (angular.js:401)
    at useLanguage (angular-translate.js:1638)
    at angular-translate.js:2324
    at processQueue (angular.js:17914)
    at angular.js:17962
    at Scope.$digest (angular.js:19075)
```
We plug in the `message-format` interpolation to handle plurals, which in turn uses `make-plural` library.
We wait for the `$translate` to be `ready` [before we load forms](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/webapp/src/js/controllers/inbox.js#L421), 
and we wait for forms to be loaded [before we load reports in the LHS](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/webapp/src/js/controllers/reports.js#L471).
We also wait for `$translate` to be `ready` to load report filters.

`$translate` throws the error before broadcasting the "ready" event, so forms never load, so reports never load.

`make-plural` covers lots of languages, but not all. "rn" is a valid language code for Kirundi.
[Link to the source of `make-plural` covered languages](https://github.com/eemeli/make-plural/blob/master/packages/plurals/umd/plurals.js)

title: Add "belongs to" breadcrumbs to tasks in the LHS list
body:
#5697 is related and either needs to be completed before, or at the same time as, this request.

**User stories**
- As a CHW, when I look at my tasks list, I would like to know the family or primary contact that an individual person belongs to, so that I can identify patients easier. (For example, tasks about children currently only display the child’s name. But children often have similar names and some parents wait months to give their baby a name. The child’s name is not always enough information.)

- As a CHW, when I look at my tasks list, I would like to know the family or primary contact that an individual person belongs to, so that I can better plan my visits and can complete all tasks for the same family at the same time. (Currently a CHW may have more than one open task for the same family, but because the tasks list is sorted by due date and doesn’t list the family name, they may miss other tasks for the same family.)

- As a CHW, I would like tasks for the same family to be grouped together so that I can be more efficient with my visit time and planning. (This spec/feature doesn’t address grouping, but just noting that displaying the family name is probably a desired prerequisite to sorting by family.)

**Summary**
- After discussing many possibilities, we decided that we would like to add a third line of text to tasks to display the additional contextual information.
- This new line of text should display breadcrumbs showing where the person/place the task is about belongs to. 
- The functionality should match how we display breadcrumbs elsewhere on the app. Note that we are updating breadcrumbs across the app so that they do not list out the level the user themselves belongs to repetitively (i.e. CHW Janet will not see “CHW Janet’s Area” repeated all over the place, ticket #5697).
- The text should be styled just like breadcrumbs elsewhere on the app (Noto Sans 14px).

**Examples**
- For CHWs on the webapp looking at a task about a particular person, the breadcrumbs should most often be just the family name (e.g. “Beatrice Bass Family”). Only a single level is listed because the next level, CHW Janet’s Area, is the CHW’s own level. 
![Screen Shot 2019-05-22 at 12 16 03 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/58914178-b8037800-86d2-11e9-95f9-309408a24c34.png)


- Some tasks are for families instead of individual people, like family surveys or bed net distribution. In these cases, the breadcrumbs may not display at all, since there are no levels between the family and the CHW area.
![Screen Shot 2019-05-22 at 12 13 35 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/58914201-c2be0d00-86d2-11e9-84a6-8811ee497dae.png)


- IF we ever do eventually add in the concept of sub-areas, at that point the breadcrumbs could display both the family name and the sub area name (since there would now be two levels before the CHW area).

- For facility users on Standard, the breadcrumbs will start with the CHW Area (since Standard does not have a concept of families).

- For a CHW supervisor, if the supervisor has a task about a CHW, the breadcrumbs would display the CHW Area (and any other levels between the CHW and the supervisor, if applicable).

- Also, a reminder that we sometimes have high risk task styling. In the cases of high risk, the breadcrumb info should come after the risk message.

title: Investigate the possibility of dropping Crosswalk
body:
Chrome 55 introduced the persistent storage API which means offline storage should not be cleared unless the user manually clears it.

> When storage on the local machine is running tight (“under storage pressure”), user agents automatically clear storage to make more available space. Of course, for offline apps, this may be unfortunate, as they may not have synced their data to the server yet, or they may be apps that the user expects to just work offline (like a music player); so the Storage spec defines two different modes for storage for a given domain - “best effort” and “persistent”. The default mode, of course, is “best effort”. Storage for a domain that is “best effort” (aka “not persistent”) can be cleared automatically, without interrupting or asking the user. However, “persistent” data will not be automatically cleared. (If the system is still under storage pressure after clearing all non-persistent data, the user will need to manually clear any remaining persistent storage.)

https://developers.google.com/web/updates/2016/06/persistent-storage

This is the main reason why we need Crosswalk.

1. Test the feature works as expected allowing us to use 100% of the available disk space without ever deleting data.
2. Investigate replacing Crosswalk with native android webview and ensure there aren't any other Crosswalk features we rely on.
3. Ensure we can increase our minimum Android version to 5.0.0 (required so the webview can be updated separately to Android) and our minimum Chrome version to at least 55 (so we can use the persistent storage feature).
4. Add code to request persistent storage for the domain.

Currently for the Muso mRDT project, we are hiding most of the fields on the Reports detail page so that supervisors can more quickly and easily find the information that they need (mainly, the Results field).

Right now Muso supervisors are seeing two result fields, instead of one, which is confusing:

**Resultat:** 
pos

**Resultat du TDR de l’ASC est:** 
Positive (+)

![Screen Shot 2019-06-24 at 9 10 42 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26235957/60040849-c1975480-966e-11e9-895b-1a39d4348030.png)


As I understand it, both of these fields have to be shown because they are part of the same section/group and right now we can’t hide a single field within a section. This request is to allow us to hide a field within a section (or to experiment with other solutions that only show one result field to the supervisor).
