title: Creating child documents using repeat groups causing android-wraper to crash
body:
**Describe the bug**
Creating linked documents as per the `Creating Additional Docs` sections of [this doc](https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/blob/master/configuration/forms.md) is not working as expected. If we created documents as outlined in `Repeated Docs Example` and the child document is explicitly bound to the repeat, there's an overallocation of memory (300MB) compared to 50 MB when the child document is bound to a group directly wrapped under the repeat. 

On typical CHW phones (1GB) , we consistently run out of memory and crash when using the original form https://medic.slack.com/files/U1ZF01J12/FQS6DJ2BF/pregnancy_outcomes.xlsx

I'm attaching two forms to illustrate when the feature is working and when it's breaking.

**Test files**
[pregnancy_outcomes_buggy.xlsx](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/files/4456881/pregnancy_outcomes_buggy.xlsx)
[pregnancy_outcomes_fixed.xlsx](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/files/4456882/pregnancy_outcomes_fixed.xlsx)


**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Upload one of the attached forms to an instance
2. Launch the form `Pregnancy Outcome`
3. Enter the 10 as the response to the question `How many children`
4. Take a memory snapshot and observe the memory used.

**Expected behavior**
No crashing when running on mobile, especially memory constrained models that we recommend to partners.

**Environment**
- Instance: moh-zanzibar.dev
- Browser: Firefox (v70), Chrome on latest medic-android
- Client platform: MacOS 10.15
- App: (webapp, medic-android)
- Version: (Probably 3.x but has been tested on 3.4-3.7)

**Additional context**
A workaround to what's explicit documented in https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/blob/master/configuration/forms.md is to bind the child document to a group immediately under the repeat. 

Using the original partner form, memory allocation jumps from around 50MB to 3GB.

This has been reported by [D-Tree](https://medic.slack.com/archives/CEQTMKFT8/p1574250502002000) and [PIH](https://github.com/medic/config-pih/issues/19)

title: Users with a lot of large docs to replicate continuously fail
body:
**Describe the bug**

When replicating we use the default PouchDB batch size of 100 so we can efficiently send large numbers of docs in one request. If the docs include images (eg: MRDT photos) then this request can get large. On the server API limits the JSON parser to 32MB after which we respond with an error. This means if the user accumulates more than 32MB of data to replicate the request fails consistently and the user can never recover.

body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We currently do not have a way of providing a fallback value in a JSON form if the user does not provide it when submitting the report. This is a pain in situations where the text form SMS format is just the form. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
For a  field that is optional, allow for the config to set a default value instead of having it as null.
The CDC-MOH-KE project has a candidate use case. Submitting a report (signal) requires that the user sends only one character e.g 1. That will register a patient record but because `patient_name` isn't provided in the report, that contact is created without patient name and as  result, a list of patients without names is displayed as in the screenshot below.

Using the example above, the JSON form config would look like this:

"forms": {

title: Retries forbidden doc replication
body:
# Description

Implements an upwards replication retry mechanism by "touching" failed doc uploads 3 times - so they get pushed to the end of the changes feed.
Based on the fact that PouchDB emits a "denied" event when it receives a "forbidden" error - but doesn't fail replication (which is correct, it's not its business to care about your "validate_doc_update" rules): https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/blob/master/packages/node_modules/pouchdb-replication/src/replicate.js#L100

title: Store responses from outbound push tasks in couch
body:
As a system admin, I want to see the API responses for an outbound push task in couch so I can monitor (and potentially action upon*) the results of certain tasks.

An example use case for this is pushing dataSets to DHIS2. Even when the transmission is successful, the response gives us useful information about things like how many values were overwritten, if values were ignored, etc...

Another use case for this might be creating person and patient records in OpenMRS, whereby the response to the API call will include (amongst other things) the OpenMRS ID of the created person or patient. 

*When I say “action upon”, an example would be to store the returned OpenMRS Patient ID against the user in the CHT.

title: Fix race condition when deleting reports
body:
We have a race condition when deleting reports, where in mobile view, the user could end up seeing an empty ReportsContent page when deleting a report instead of being redirect to the list.
This is caused by the Changes listener in ReportsContent controller, which calls `ctrl.removeSelectedReport` when receiving a delete, regardless of the `selectMode`. This function will call `globalActions.settingSelected(true);` which in turn will call `setShowContent(true);`, thus ending up displaying the empty ReportsContent page. 
In most situations, the ReportsContent controller is reinitialized by the route change when executing the delete. 

I believe fixing the deletion handling in ReportsContent is the way to go, as it will fix another issue where, as an admin, receiving a deletion of the selected report would not redirect to the list, instead keep you on an empty ReportsContent page. 

We could have it do something like this:
```
if (change.deleted) {
  if (ctrl.selectMode) {
    ctrl.removeSelectedReport(change.id);
  } else {
    ctrl.unsetSelected();
  }
}
```

**To Reproduce**
1. Login as an admin in 2 tabs and switch to mobile view
2. Open the same report in both tabs.
3. In one of the tabs, delete the report. Switch to the other tab.
4. Observe that you are seeing an empty ReportsContent page and the URL still contains the ID of the deleted report.
If you refresh, you should see something like:
```
Error selecting report Error: Document not found: <The report uuid>
```
And then be redirected to the reports list. 


**Expected behavior**
When receiving a delete of the selected report, correct deselection should happen, whether in selectMode or not. 

**Screenshots**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/70252443-1dbbe400-178a-11ea-87f9-ce3ad4982271.png)

**Environment**
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.8

title: Submitting almost any form from the mobile app throws and catches a Java error
body:
In 3.5 we introduced the possibility of sending webapp forms to the server vis SMS: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/4812
The code that generates the SMS content is here: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/js/services/form2sms.js
The code that actually attempts sms sending is here: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/js/services/submit-form-by-sms.js

We check for a field `xml2sms` in the form doc and fallback to the default `odk-xform-compact-record-representation-for-sms` - which is documented here: https://opendatakit.github.io/xforms-spec/#compact-record-representation-(for-sms)
In order to have a form be compactable to SMS, root element needs to have a `prefix` attribute. However, all form templates that I've seen used in our configurations have this `prefix` attribute, so all are compactable. 
examples:
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/config/default/forms/app/pregnancy.xml#L671
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/config/default/forms/app/undo_death_report.xml#L47
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/config/default/forms/app/pregnancy_facility_visit_reminder.xml#L68
And every other `default` config form. 

When submitting such a form in the mobile app, an error is thrown and caught by the SubmitFormBySMS service:

```
Execption thrown in JavascriptInterface function: java.lang.SecurityException: Sending SMS message: uid 10272 does not have android.permission.SEND_SMS.;  at android.os.Parcel.createException(Parcel.java:1950);  at android.os.Parcel.readException(Parcel.java:1918);  at android.os.Parcel.readException(Parcel.java:1868);  at com.android.internal.telephony.ISms$Stub$Proxy.sendTextForSubscriber(ISms.java:881);  at android.telephony.SmsManager.sendTextMessageInternal(SmsManager.java:381);  at android.telephony.SmsManager.sendTextMessage(SmsManager.java:364);  at android.telephony.SmsManager.sendMultipartTextMessageInternal(SmsManager.java:697);  at android.telephony.SmsManager.sendMultipartTextMessage(SmsManager.java:663);  at org.medicmobile.webapp.mobile.j.sms_send(MedicAndroidJavascript.java:2063);  at org.chromium.base.SystemMessageHandler.nativeDoRunLoopOnce(Native Method);  at org.chromium.base.SystemMessageHandler.handleMessage(SystemMessageHandler.java:39);  at android.os.Handler.dispatchMessage(Handler.java:107);  at android.os.Looper.loop(Looper.java:198);  at android.os.HandlerThread.run(HandlerThread.java:65); 
```

This ends up polluting the console and nearly every feedback document generated (since it includes the latest n console messages). 
It also contains a typo `Execption`. 
Typo appears to be coming from here: https://github.com/medic/medic-android/blob/master/src/main/java/org/medicmobile/webapp/mobile/MedicAndroidJavascript.java#L407

This also affects live instances - I first saw the error message in a feedback document generated in `muso-mali` instance. The feedback document reported a different error (fixed here: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5863) but it included a couple of previous log entries. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Deploy default configuration.
2. Login as any user in the mobile app and watch the console
3. Submit any form.
4. See that after submission, you get an error in the console.
Optional: open the report a bug interface and submit. Check the document uploaded to the meta database on the server and observe it contains the Java exception log. 

**Expected behavior**
We should not attempt sending SMS when the app does not have permissions. 

**Logs**
```
submitFormBySmsIfApplicable() failed: Error: Java exception was raised during method invocation(anonymous function) @ angular.js:15567(anonymous function) @ submit-form-by-sms.js:12processQueue @ angular.js:17945(anonymous function) @ angular.js:17993$digest @ angular.js:19112(anonymous function) @ angular.js:19432completeTask @ angular.js:21231(anonymous function) @ angular.js:6812
feedback.js:39 Execption thrown in JavascriptInterface function: java.lang.SecurityException: Sending SMS message: uid 10272 does not have android.permission.SEND_SMS.;  at android.os.Parcel.createException(Parcel.java:1950);  at android.os.Parcel.readException(Parcel.java:1918);  at android.os.Parcel.readException(Parcel.java:1868);  at com.android.internal.telephony.ISms$Stub$Proxy.sendTextForSubscriber(ISms.java:881);  at android.telephony.SmsManager.sendTextMessageInternal(SmsManager.java:381);  at android.telephony.SmsManager.sendTextMessage(SmsManager.java:364);  at android.telephony.SmsManager.sendMultipartTextMessageInternal(SmsManager.java:697);  at android.telephony.SmsManager.sendMultipartTextMessage(SmsManager.java:663);  at org.medicmobile.webapp.mobile.j.sms_send(MedicAndroidJavascript.java:2063);  at org.chromium.base.SystemMessageHandler.nativeDoRunLoopOnce(Native Method);  at org.chromium.base.SystemMessageHandler.handleMessage(SystemMessageHandler.java:39);  at android.os.Handler.dispatchMessage(Handler.java:107);  at android.os.Looper.loop(Looper.java:198);  at android.os.HandlerThread.run(HandlerThread.java:65); 
```

**Screenshots**
If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/70254699-2dd5c280-178e-11ea-9788-6fdfc7bb9d95.png)

title: Add implicit configs that were lost when `config.default.json` was removed
body:
In 3.7 we removed `config.default.json` and replaced it with the `default` config. 
However `default` config doesn't contain all settings that are required for app functionality, like the "sms" section or the "replications" section (already dealt with here: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6147).

The "sms" section is now required for every SMS project that upgrades from an older version and uses `medic-gateway`. 
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/services/messaging.js#L303

Along with "sms", there might be more missing implicit configs. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Deploy a 3.5 instance with 3.5 version of `standard` config. 
2. Generate some messages to be sent. 
3. POST to `/api/sms` to see that you get some results. 
4. Generate some more messages (calling 'api/sms' will have changed the status on the previous ones)
5. Upgrade to 3.7 (or 3.8). 
6. POST to `api/sms` again.
7. Observe that the response is an empty array. Check the admin message queue to verify that there are indeed pending SMS messages. 

**Expected behavior**
`/api/sms` should return 25 pending sms messages after an upgrade. 

**Environment**
- Instance: 3.5 (or lower) upgraded to 3.7 (or 3.8).
- App: api and/or sentinel

title: Db-doc access fails when accessing a report about a deleted contact
body:
In an attempt to make db-doc access quicker for offline users, I implemented a reverse authorization mechanism that created a "scoped" version of the authorization context, relevant just to the requested doc. However, I completely overlooked tombstones. 

As such, when requesting a report that is about a deleted contact, an offline user will receive a faulty 403 error. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Login as an offline user. 
2. Create a report about an existent contact.
3. Delete the contact and sync. 
4. Wipe data from the device / browser and login fresh.
5. Notice that you get a 403 error when trying to get the report's attachment. 

**Expected behavior**
Replication should complete without error. All docs that are received via the _changes feed should be valid for download. 

**Environment**
- App: api
- Version: 3.8

**Additional context**
Introduced during the development of 3.8. Related issue: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5550

body:
**Describe the bug**

If we aren't able to solve this quickly we should at least document the workaround in the meantime.

title: Sentinel doesn't restart its follow feed on error
body:
**Describe the bug**
In Sentinel, if the changes feed that we follow to process docs (https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/sentinel/src/lib/feed.js#L10) throws an error, it is never restarted. Not even when new (valid) settings are pushed. 

This puts Sentinel into a blocked state where only a restart OR (hacky) pushing a faulty transition config and then pushing a correct one (which will cause a `detach` and `attach` https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/sentinel/src/transitions.js#L16)

**To Reproduce**
1. Deploy 3.8 (or 3.7). Ensure that you have `generate_patient_id_on_people` enabled. 
2. Stop Sentinel. Edit the sentinel-meta-data document to use an incorrect seq (for example a number):
http://127.0.0.1:5984/medic-sentinel/_local/sentinel-meta-data
```
{
  "_id": "_local/sentinel-meta-data",
  "_rev": "0-2371",
  "processed_seq": 2500
}
```
3. Start Sentinel
4. Notice a single error in the console:
```
ERROR: transitions: error from changes feed: {
  error: 'bad_request',
  reason: "Malformed sequence supplied in 'since' parameter.",
  status: 400,
  name: 'bad_request',
  message: "Malformed sequence supplied in 'since' parameter."
} 
```
5. As an admin, create a new person in the webapp. Wait and observe that it does not receive a `patient_id`. 
6. Checking the Sentinel console, it does not report processing the person doc. 

**N.B.** 
In this example, even restarting Sentinel won't make it function correctly. 
If it attempted to restart the feed every time it received an error, you would see the above error message logged over and over, not just once.

**Environment**
- App: Sentinel
- Version: 3.7

**Additional context**
Discovered when an upgrade from 2.x -> 3.x went wrong: After replicating docs from Couch 1.x to Couch 2.x, the `local/_sentinel_meta_data` was not created to have it's `processed_seq` equal to the `update_seq` of the new db (so docs would not be processed twice). 
Upon starting, Sentinel started feed, with the `since` parameter coming from the legacy metadata document (https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/sentinel/src/lib/metadata.js#L5) that existed in `medic` database, using a the old Couch 1.x seq format (numbers). 
Because API was doing all the heavy lifting with syncronous transitions, it took days to discover that Sentinel was in fact blocked. 
Restarting Sentinel at this point, would make it start processing docs since 0  (because the legacy metadata doc is deleted immediately after being read: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/sentinel/src/lib/metadata.js#L7)

**Discussion** 
In the above scenario, what would have been the correct behavior?

Do we want to avoid Sentinel starting from 0 when upgrading from 2.x and missing the step of creating the metadata doc with the DB'a current `update_seq`?

If Sentinel had logged the error more frequently or more obviously, it would have probably prompted people earlier in the process.

title: Having a doc with a non-numeric `reported_date` breaks everything
body:
We use the default CouchDB reducer `_stats` for two views, `medic/reports_by_form_and_parent` and `medic-client/contacts_by_last_visited`. 
See the documentation for `_stats` here: https://docs.couchdb.org/en/2.3.1/ddocs/ddocs.html#_stats
It requires that we **only emit numeric or numeric array values** and will throw an error while indexing or querying views if any doc does not comply.
In the view map functions, we do not insure that the emitted value is a number. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Deploy 3.8 or 3.7.
2. Login as an admin, make sure you have at least one report in the instance. 
3. Open a report in fauxton - this report has to emit `medic/reports_by_form_and_parent` (https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/ddocs/medic/views/reports_by_form_and_parent/map.js), so make sure it has all the required fields.
4. Edit the report, setting the `reported_date` field to a string. The content doesn't matter, just that it's a non-empty string. Save! 
5. As an admin, refresh the reports list.
6. Error fetching reports.

**Logs**
The `http://localhost:5988/medic/_design/medic/_view/doc_summaries_by_id` request throws a 500 error:
```
{"error":"invalid_value","reason":"The _stats function requires that map values be numbers or arrays of numbers, not '<<\"oh joy\">>'","ref":4089041121}
```

**Screenshots**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/70371977-422ad400-18e2-11ea-8e79-2923af87153d.png)


**Environment**
- App: all
- Version: any version that uses `_stats` reducer for at least one view. 

**Additional context**
We should make sure that we emit numbers when we pass values to a `_stats` reducer. 
As a workaround, we can search for documents that have faulty fields and edit them to unblock instances.

 ``thi``s `i`s `a ````te`s`t

title: Purging for task and target documents
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5657 changed tasks from being in-memory objects to being database documents. Currently, task documents replicate to the user's device and will remain there forever. After time, some users may have thousands of task documents on the their device which will slow things down. Many of these documents have no functional purpose on the device and can be purged.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
* A task document is safe to purge when it is [60](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/6041/files#diff-8f90c28d3acf485f33868b2660a3d697R18) days past the task document's end date and the document is in a terminal state.
* A target document is safe to purge whenever the reporting period is over.

These rules for when task and target documents are safe to purge are hard-coded into the "rules engine" and are not partner-specific. Therefore, server-side purging can handle them for all partners instead of requiring partner-specific logic for purging these documents.

title: Support custom contact types in medic-pyxform
body:
From 3.7 with the introduction of configurable hierarchy, we now support any number of place and person types (beyond the historically supported ones: `person, clinic, health_center, district_hospital`).

Unfortunately the new contact types are not supported in our fork of pyxform as these have to be set question types in pyxform. Given the variability of these contact definitions, we need to have a way of dynamically adding question types in pyxform when converting forms or settle (initially) on a set of contact types that will initially fulfil the needs of projects that need more than 3 levels of hierarch.

The old contact types are currently defined here: https://github.com/medic/pyxform/blob/6f7909d564e104640562241da4cf8393036243ad/pyxform/question_type_dictionary.py#L158-#L189

Given that we've essentially settled on XLSForms as the approach to form definitions, we really do need to figure. 

One dirty workaround is for folks to modify their local copies of `pyxform/question_type_dictionary.py` and add the the new question types.

title: Supervisors download all task documents from CHWs they supervise
body:
**Describe the bug**
As part of Rules-Engine v2, tasks are now stored to disk and replicated up and down.
However, a stored task has this structure:

```
{
    "type": "task",
    "authoredOn": "<timestamp>",
    "state": "<some_task_state>"
    "stateHistory": [{ "state": "<some_task_state>", "timestamp": "<timestamp>" }, ...],
    "user": "<users's contact document id>",
    "requester": "<taskEmission.doc.contact._id>",
    "owner": "<taskEmission.contact._id>",
    "emission": { ... emission data }
}
```

relevant code here: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/rules-engine/src/transform-task-emission-to-doc.js#L26

The `user` field is used for determining replication permissions for the doc and is the value emitted in `medic/docs_by_replication_key`: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/ddocs/medic/views/docs_by_replication_key/map.js#L71 .
Because the field contains the uuid of the user's contact doc, supervisors are most likely allowed to view the people they supervise, hence they will download all the tasks of these users.

**To Reproduce**

Using "legacy" hierarchy:
1. Create a CHW under a `health_center`, add some families and people to the families and add at least one report that would generate a task. Sync!
2. Create a Supervisor above the CHW, in `district_hospital` level and give it `replication_depth` = 2. This means that he will download the `health_center`, the CHW Contact document and the families, but none of the people in the families or their reports.
3. Log in with the Supervisor account and check the tasks tab. Notice that you see the same task as the "CHW".

**Expected behavior**
I believe it is intended for supervisors not to download supervisee tasks, as that could prove severely detrimental for their devices performance.


**Environment**
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.8.x

**Additional context**
It appears that simply switching the `task.user` field to contain the actual user-settings document id (`org:couchdb:user:<username>`) would solve the replication issue, as only the users themselves have access to the user-settings docs. 

If, in the future, we want to have the ability to generate tasks for other users, not based on their username, we could additionally have `medic/docs_by_replication_key` emit an additional value that would send the task to the correct people - for example emit the `owner` and have the task downloaded to everyone who sees the person.

body:
# Description

Adds a new "default" replication subject, in the form of the user's couchdb user id (`org.couchdb.user:<username>`). Documents that must be replicated by a specific user only should emit this value in `medic/docs_by_replication_key`. 
Updates `task` documents to use this value as their `user` property, making uploaded tasks only available to them, and not to their supervisors or anyone who shares their lineage. Task document ids also change to use the user's doc id instead of the contact's doc id. 

Updates `target` to also use this value as their `user` property (for consistency), adds the `owner` property that saves the contact's uuid and updates `medic/docs_by_replication_key` so `targets` emit `owner` - in order to make targets available for supervisors. The target doc id is updated to include the user's doc id, the value being appended, so it's still possible to search for a target document in a certain month and a certain contact, without knowing the user's id.

title: Add support for outbound push to RapidPro
body:
**Describe the solution you'd like**
The ability to integrate workflows initiated in a CHT app with RapidPro. It seems as though the best way to send data from the CHT app is by using the outbound push feature to RapidPro's API. Currently outbound push only support basic auth and a custom auth protocol for a bespoke EMR. To make outbound push work with RapidPro we'd need to support it's token authentication.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
It is possible to push data to RapidPro using outbound push by redirecting via webhooks that have authentication compatible with outbound push (eg basic auth with Zapier). This is an unnecessary and potentially costly redirect.

**Additional context**
The authentication needed is described in the Authentication section of the [RapidPro API](https://rapidpro.io/api/v2/):

> You must authenticate all calls by including an Authorization header with your API token. If you are logged in, your token will be visible at the top of this page. The Authorization header should look like:
>
> Authorization: Token YOUR_API_TOKEN

Workflows in RapidPro can send data back to a CHT via the API, and connect with CouchDB directly for exploratory purposes. Through this exploration we'll be able to better understand the API requirements needed, which can be opened in another issue.

title: Update aggregate target doc after the reporting interval to ensure accuracy
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Webapp v3.8 included a Rules Engine v2 which resulted in documents with type `target` to be written to PouchDB. This document updates a maximum of once per day. An update for the current reporting interval's target document is triggered by the user viewing the tasks/analytics tab, or by a timer which triggers a minute after the app loads. This was a "best-effort" approach to reporting which conservatively prevents writes to the document.

A few scenarios may lead to the target document of a reporting interval to not include a fully accurate summary of the user's target data. For example, if the user navigates to the task/target tab on the day prior to the end of a reporting interval, then creates/edits reports, then views the task/target tab again that day. The document only updates once per day, so it will not recieve the latest updates. The next day is the next reporting period, so the out of date target doc won't be updated. Other scenarios are possible if the user doesn't view the tasks/targets page for several days prior to the end of the reporting period.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
I'd like to update the target document for the `n`th reporting interval once in the `n+1`th reporting interval.

**Additional context**
This is an existing problem in 3.8 that will impact the fidelity of our impact metrics. I'm scheduling this in 3.9, because Target documents will also be used to drive our DHIS2 workflows. #6002

body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
As part of #6002, target documents will be used to drive our workflow for integrating with DHIS2. For some partners, this will result in many new targets being written and added to the UI (eg. `MoH Kenya 515` will result in `75` new targets). 

Many of targets we may never need users to review manually (eg. popullation statistics) and so they should calculate and aggregate in the `target` document, but not display in the UI. Long-term it would be nice to organize the page under headings or sections, but our feedback from projects is that this many new indicators will be too cluttered with the current UI and many will need to be hidden.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Add a `visible` attribute onto the target configuration. When false, the target will calculate and aggregate into target documents, but will not display in the UI. Defaults to true.

title: The `can_edit` permission doesn't stop you from editing documents (only uploading those edits)
body:
The `can_edit` permission is used in two places in our code base: whether or not someone has permission on arbitrary writes (decided in api's routing), and whether or not upward sync should be enabled (in client side db-sync code).

This creates a confusing situation if `can_edit` is disabled for offline users. The user is still completely capable of creating new reports, editing existing reports, etc. However, *upwards replication simply never occurs*, with no indication that anything is wrong.

A `can_edit` permission check should wrap all write attempts (e.g. creating forms, editing forms etc) so disable the ability to perform those actions, and present a proper "read only" view.
 
Or, if that is too hard, we should not allow offline users to be configured without this permission.

Or, if _that_ is too hard, we should warn in the console on boot (ie in the db sync code that checks this permission) very loadly that this user is basically misconfigured, and it's going to look like they are successfully making changes when they are not.

title: Record the order in which a task is displayed
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
As we consider making changes to the order in which tasks are displayed (#5997, #5886), part of what we are interested in is how task sorting and filtering affects task completion. This is especially relevant for #5997, which aims to order tasks by priority based on the hypothesis that high priority tasks are more likely to be completed if they are displayed earlier in the task list. To do analytics on the effects of sorting, we need to know where tasks are in the sorting when they are seen. However, currently, knowing where a task appeared in the task list is very difficult. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would like to see in the task document something like a list of timestamp, position tuples that record where a task was each time the task page is loaded (or each time the order has changed). Ideally, this would be compatible with eventually adding information about what ordering/filtering options were active when the task was seen.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
A backend solution could use the task statuses to attempt to figure out which tasks might have displayed at any given time (had the user used the app at that time) and then sort based on due date. Attempts at simulating this process on the backend are likely to be complex and error-prone and won't truly be accurate for the purpose of knowing how order affected completion unless we know when a user actually looked at the tasks screen.

**Additional context**
Potentially relevant to #6188

title: Adds analytics target aggregates page and targets in contact-summary
body:
# Description

Adds analytics target aggregates pages. Available for all users (online or offline) who have the `can_aggregate_targets` (new) permission 
Targets are aggregated as follows:
- A target is aggregated if it has the `aggregate` (new) attribute set to a truthy value
- The values that are aggregated are extracted from the **current target documents** (latest reporting interval)
- Only target docs that belong to "supervised" people are taken into consideration
- We consider a contact as "supervised" if they are a primary contact of a place directly under the logged in user's home place
- Count values are summed up `sum(values.pass)`
- Percent values are summed up `sum(values.pass) * 100 / sum(values.total)`
- Targets that have goals will display how many supervisees have achieved their goal instead of the aggregate value. 
- Supervisees are sorted alphabetically
- "target_under_goal" color changed to orange

Provides the current target document to the `contact_summary` function, under the name of `targets`, hydrated with the configuration of every target it contains (so it's possible to pass translation keys to labels for eventual cards). This feature is available for all users, regardless of permissions or role.

body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
In 3.8.0 we added a feature to [warn when replicating too many docs](#5362). This warning is shown when creating a new user, when that user logs in for the first time, and then shown in the API logs every hour the user attempts to replicate.

This is useful but unless people are monitoring the logs closely is likely to be missed.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
1. Extend the [new monitoring endpoint](#6133) to include the number of users replicating too many docs.
2. Provide a method of finding which users are replicating too many docs so they can be investigated. This could be a new API or an addition to the monitoring API JSON format response.

The easiest way to implement this is to extend the existing logging code so instead of refreshing the cache each hour it retains the logins for longer (perhaps 7 days). This may require persistence (eg: in a `_local` couch doc) so that it's maintained between restarts, particularly if the heavy user is crashing API.

An alternative implementation would be to query the telemetry docs which include the number of docs locally. This data will always be a little out of date (telemetry is synced monthly) and only works for users who have successfully synced at least once so wouldn't include a user whose replication is constantly failing.

Once the monitoring code is in place it may no longer be necessary to log this information.

Once the endpoint is done consider including a warning in the users page of the admin app, or raising an issue to tackle this in a later release.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could provide a script to query couch and find this information, but it's quite a heavy operation so to run it for all users could be expensive. By recording the information when the user logs in it's essentially free.

title: change icon
Targets with date: 'now' show stale counts for first days of a reporting window
body:
**Describe the bug**
Targets which should be counted "always" (not part of the monthly interval reporting) emit with `date: Date.now()`. We cache that emission for 7 days. If that emission is cached near the end of a reporting window, and then a new reporting interval begins -- we fail to count it since the cached date is outside the current interval. The result is taht targets with date: 'now' can show incorrect counts for the first seven days of a reporting window.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce:

1. On `default` configuration, register a pregnancy
1. Change clock to first few days of reporting window (eg. Feb 5)
1. Navigate to the targets tab. View "active pregnancies = 1"
1. Change clock to last few days of reporting window (eg. Feb 28)
1. Navigate to the targets tab. View "active pregnancies = 1"
1. Change clock to few days of next reporting window (eg. Mar 1)
1. Navigate to the targets tab.

Expected: View "active pregnancies = 1"
Observed: View "active pregnancies = 0"

If you move your clock forward six more days (eg. Mar 7), and refresh the target tab -- the proper values are displayed again.

**Environment**
- Instance: dev machine
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.8.0 and master

**Additional context**
We recognized clearly that the use of Date.now() was going to be a problem with our approach. But we thought this was rare - only mattering for calculations like "age of contact", etc.  We could have used `date: undefined` instead of `date: now` to communicate that the emission should always be counted, but that's very awkward to do now in 3.9.0.

# Description

#6209 

This is my attempt to patch this measurement gap using the method suggested in the issue.

However, this approach is perhaps not viable since it isn't currently safe to aggregate targets for a time interval which is not the current interval. This works fine for target emissions which expicitly set their `date` attribute, but doesn't work with target emissions which leave the `date` undefined or which set it to [now](https://github.com/medic/medic-conf/blob/master/src/nools/target-emitter.js#L30) (which is the default for declarative configuration when `date: 'now'`).

While investigating, I've discovered that this same issue actually presents in a critical scenarios. See #6267. I'm publishing this PR to illustrate the problem clearly (see the failing test) as the two issues may share a common solution.

title: Use http2 to fetch all login resources at the same time
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
The login page takes a long time to complete loading on slow networks in part because we load resources incrementally. First we load the `login.html`, then the `script.js`, then the `service-worker.js`, and finally all the app resources listed in the service worker. This means we wait for network lag a total of four times.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Provide a `Link` header with the `login.html` to instruct the browser to fetch all the other resources. This reduces the wait from four to two server round trips.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
It would be better to send all resources with the `login.html` so we only have one round trip, but that would require SSL to terminate in API which is harder for SRE to manage than using the load balancer as we currently do.

We could inline our resources into the html but that breaks caching and makes the html a single very large request.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to record the performance metrics:
1. Go to the login page. The instance must be hosted on AWS to get http2 enabled.
2. Clear your cache completely
3. Open the network tab
4. CTRL+F5 to refresh completely
5. View when the requests are fired and measure the time to completion

**Measurements**
Currently you can see four distinct bands where requests are initiated. To see the result more clearly you can throttle your connection.

![Screenshot from 2020-03-07 15-14-04](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2064938/76140829-5370b180-6086-11ea-92ad-6afbb24967ff.png)

**Environment**
- Instance: any AWS hosted instance
- Browser: Any
- Client platform: Any
- App: API & webapp
- Version: 3.8.0

**Additional context**
This only affects the first load but it makes a really bad initial impression.

title: Show locale selector on login page
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently on first run we show the login page in the instance default locale because we don't know what user is looking at the page yet. Once they've logged in we show a modal in the webapp to pick a language. If they change the language then we update the user settings doc so it'll be persisted for future sessions. Because the user settings doc is updated it needs to be replicated down which then prompts the user to refresh to get any changes. This is not a nice user experience.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
If we give users a way to set their language before logging in then we can update the user settings doc before they've replicated it and do away with the in app modal _and_ the update app modal.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Alternatively you could leave the modal where it is and attempt to detect when the user settings doc hadn't changed in any important way, but this is more technically complex and only removes one of the two modals.

**Additional context**
Once #5954 is done then it'll be possible to translate the login page dynamically when the user changes their language which will help if they don't understand the default language.

title: Allow app builders to specify disabled languages in config
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Whether or not a language is disabled is stored in generated docs in the database and can only be set via the app management console. This makes it less likely that app builders will define the list of languages that are actually supported and users are confronted with a long list of broken languages to choose from. Most apps probably support only one or two languages fully so this can be simplified significantly.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Instead of defining whether or not the language is enabled in the messages-* doc, it should be in the appsettings doc so it can be hardcoded in the projects configuration. Make sure to update the default configuration to only include fully supported languages to improve the out-of-the box experience. Also include a migration so as not to break existing projects that _have_ configured it correctly.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could leave the enabled flag where it is and provide a medic-conf hook to disable languages but this is technically more complex.

Alternatively we could disable any language not explicitly provided for in the config but that is an unintended consequence of uploading new languages.

**Additional context**
This will make the language selector in #6280 much cleaner.

title: Detect time-traveling phones offline
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Because phones are sometimes offline for extended periods, their internal clocks can become out of sync with the correct time. This causes a number of problems:

- Decision support based on calculated age may be made incorrectly: for example, the number of breaths qualifying as fast breathing differs based on patient age; if the wrong age is used, an incorrect triage decision may be made
- Task schedules become interrupted: for example, if a pregnancy registration happened before a clock became out of sync, the ANC visit tasks associated with that pregnancy may not be prompted at all or may be prompted at the wrong clinical time, depending on the type/severity of time drift
- Analytics become inaccurate/problematic: When task report times are inaccurate, we cannot calculate basic metrics like the time between visits, and these problems are compounded for more complicated metrics and data science applications

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We can probably use some basic diagnostics upon starting the application to detect internal clock "time travel" and prompt the user to turn on data long enough to update the clock or manually update the clock.

To detect phones traveling backwards in time, we could check:

- Is the current time < most recent sync time?
- Is the current time < most recent report time?

Detecting phones traveling forward in time seems a bit harder, but we could try some things like:

- Is the current time more than 30 days greater than the time of last report?

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None, but am open to any!

**Additional context**

title: Link SMS reports to patient associated with the sender phone number
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
When a client registered in the system submits a text form with the phone number in their profile, we are able to associate that report with that person. However, the report does not appear under their reports, in the reports section on their profile which I interpret to mean that we are not able to associate such reports with the contact when fetching a contact's reports. I suspected this had to do with the lack of patient_id in the report and to investigate this hypothesis,  I added it to the report manually and viola! The report now appears among a contact's reports. This affects schedule clearing logic in schedules where bool check expects such reports.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

title: Upgrade to CouchDB v3
body:
CouchDB 3.0 has been released and eventually we'll want to migrate to it.

- Investigate technical compatibility with the CHT and raise issues to fix the bugs, tests, documentation, etc in a backwards compatible way.
- Run performance and scalability tests to determine the extent of any improvements or regressions. Wherever possible raise issues against CouchDB where performance has regressed to give their team plenty of time to investigate before we're ready to upgrade.

This issue can be closed once we have confidence that we have identified and documented all issues that are blocking us from upgrading today.

title: Remove unread notification bubbles
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The Reports and Messages tabs have red bubbles to track how many docs you have access to but haven't yet opened. Initially this was added for facility based users who could follow along in real-time and respond quickly when a new message was received. In reality I think:

- the facility use case isn't commonly deployed,
- the number usually has a number so high as to be useless (eg: "99+"),
- is implementation technically challenging and hurts performance, and
- it's buggy so the number is likely to be inaccurate anyway

As a result I assume the number is completely ignored.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Remove the bubbles altogether. Keep the bold for unread docs.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could ensure the number is accurate by testing and fixing any bugs, and add improvements such as "mark all read" to clear the number if it gets out of date.

Additionally we could investigate whether we should add a permission so it only shows for particular users.

**Additional context**
This is based on my conjecture - it might be essential for some use case, or it may be working better than I think it is.

title: Ability to generate case_id short codes
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We have a really great feature that allows the generation of patient_ids for contacts. It would be even greater if we had a similar feature for reports too. With it, we would be able to generate a unique identifier sharable to a user. This is particularly useful for projects that need us to respond to the user with code that they can use to identify a report they sent to the system, especially with TextForm workflows. 
One of the projects with this need is the Event-Based Surveillance (EBS) project deployed for MOH Kenya where a user reports an event and expects to get back a code for that signal/event they just reported.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Ability go auto-generate shortcodes in reports.  

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
For the EBS mentioned above, the patient_id generation feature was repurposed to meet the requirement where the signal reporting form is configured to `add_person`. When a report is submitted a contact is created, and it's patient_id is attached to the report which we are then able to send back to the user. 

**Additional context**
Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here.

title: Show correct language labels for dynamic elements and non-localized forms
body:
# Description

When switching to server-side form generation, we switched from setting the user's language directly in the xml, pre-conversion, to relying on Enketo's `lang` module.
This module contains a bug where dynamic elements would be generated using the default language instead of the one set with the module: https://github.com/enketo/enketo/issues/261 . 
Additionally, non-localized forms would have translation values under the `default` translation tag. 
When setting the user's language, we inadvertently stopped supporting non-localized forms that had translation labels. 

This PR attempts to detect whether the form is localized or not.
Non-localized forms are unaltered. Localized forms' html gets updated to set the user's language as active before passing them to Enketo.

title: Telemetry and engagement data for the admin console
body:
As the owner of the "App Builder's Backlog" it is very difficult to prioritise features for the admin console without understanding who uses it, how they use it, which tabs they use, how frequently it is used, whether people use it production or only in development, etc..  

The admin console is only supported for online users, so there is no offline-first requirement for telemetry on this page. Can we add an off-the-shelf telemetry system to this page so we can understand who uses it and for what? Some libraries are as simple as a single line of JavaScript. Can I get the ability to run custom partner-specific JavaScript on the admin console page and we can add Google Analytics for medic-run projects only.

The admin console provides a lot of the same functionality that is provided by the medic-conf tool. But they do not work harmoniously together. Manually making config changes through the admin console is tedious, not backed up, there is no easily accessed audit trail, and changes are easily overwritten by medic-conf. I believe we need to evaluate the long-term direction of the admin console and its overall usefulness. It's unclear what issues and improvements to the admin console should be prioritised in the meantime. Getting data on usage is an essential first step!

title: Telemetry around end user actions
body:
As backlog curator for end users it would be helpful to have telemetry around user actions to help prioritize issues effectively. Having data to support when possible (for example, https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6226) is much more compelling than anecdotal issues (ex. https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5886). 

Telemetry and user tracking will also help validate whether these design improvements are effective and demonstrate clearer results.

title: Send outbound push without delay
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Outbound push

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Sentinel currently schedules outbound push every five minutes. For some workflows, like [messaging using RapidPro](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6207), it would be ideal if those pushes happened as soon as possible so that the creation of a report or contact could trigger a messaging workflow immediately for CHWs or patients. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
It is possible to manually reduce the schedule interval from 5 minutes to 2 minutes, but it is unclear what implications that has if a push doesn't complete before the schedule is run again. There could be scenarios when even 2 minutes is a long time to wait for the outbound push to complete, eg phone number verification.

**Additional context**
Setting the interval to 1 minute caused errors and the outbound push didn't work. 
Also, having the push interval to be less than 2 minutes is possibly more important for testing and demo purposes than in real life. We don't have an actual use case or deployment needing it to be more immediate _yet_.

title: Workflow to merge likely duplicates upon submission
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
A common problem across projects is likely duplicate reports. These

- increase documents stored on the phone
- increase documents synced to the server
- make analytics difficult

**Describe the solution you'd like**
For each form type, set some minimum window expected between reports for the same target (household, patient, etc.) and when a report is submitted, check if the most recent report of the same type for that target is within that window. If so, give a pop-up/snackbar/other UI tool that asks if the CHW would like to merge the reports. If there are any disagreeing fields, enter a workflow where the CHW can select the correct/canonical value. Update the initial report with the corrected values and a flag indicating it is a merged report. Purge the duplicate. If the CHW rejects or ignores the merge prompt, add flags to both reports indicating such.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Sending duplicates to supervisors for confirmation/correction with CHWs. This introduces a delay during which CHWs might lose knowledge of what exactly happened or what the correct values are. This also relies on strong supervision and increases task burden for supervisors.
- Deduplicating reports during data cleaning. This is the current solution. Data users do not know when potential duplicate reports are actually separate events that were recorded later (e.g. a CHW who does form completion once per week) nor how to handle conflicting reports except using heuristics (e.g., use the most recent version), so this is prone to errors.

**Additional context**
Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here.

title: Use the browser language as the default language
body:
**Describe the bug**
Going to the login page for the first time always shows in the system default language even if you have a browser/system language set.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Go to App Management > Display > Languages
2. Set the "default application language" to English
3. Set the primary language in your browser to "Hindi". The method for doing this differs by browser so search for how to do it for your particular flavour.
4. Clear all your cookies and data
5. Load the login page and notice how it's translated to English.

**Expected behavior**
The login page should be translated to your browser's primary language, in this case Hindi.

**Environment**
- Instance: localhost
- Browser: Chrome
- Client platform: Linux
- App: api
- Version: 3.8.0

**Additional context**
The locale should be resolved in this order...

1. Use the `locale` cookie. This is set by the user on a previous login, or by the administrator during user setup so most likely to be correct.
2. If no `locale` cookie is set, use the browser default. This is passed in the request's `accept-language` header. This may not match with the two letter code that we use so make a best effort here. Furthermore it may not match one of the supported languages for this project.
3. If the browser default doesn't match any supported language, use the project "default application language" set in configuration.
4. If the "default application language" in the project config isn't set (very unlikely), default to English.

Step 2 is the step that's not happening yet.

title: "grunt test" doesn't work
body:
The `grunt test` target fails, because:
 - It tries to switch a unit testing environment variable on for unit tests, then off for integration tests
 - However, files that read that environment variable only do so on initial load, and so their decision is cached between unit and int tests

You can work around it by running each inner target individually in separate executions, and so separate node vms.

body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Our latest work in Client-Initiated Health Assessment workflows design, has pointed to the need for an API that returns a hydrated payload. In an example use case, in a RapidPro flow initiated by a client, and using the phone number to identify the client in CHT, CHV and CHV area details are needed in the steps following workflow initiation. 

While we can use (for now) CouchDB view calls to retrieve some useful information, we cannot perform hydration easily

**Describe the solution you'd like**
An api where you pass a collection of doc ids and hydrated versions of those documents are returned.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
This can be hacked in RapidPro (by essentially looping upwards and requesting each doc) but it's dodgy and not very efficient.

**Additional context**
#6325, put together for purposes of CIHA prototyping introduces a hydrate-only API endpoint, where when given a list of UUIDs, returns hydrated payloads for those. We really just need to formalise this by pulling it out of this branch, adding tests etc.

It's also worth mentioning that in the future we'd also want to add actual apis to solve these problems (ie a get person by phone api): CouchDB views being exposed as external apis isn't a great long term solution (eg no versioning), but for now we are going to run with it.

As an offline user, if I create a new contact and add their report quickly without letting it sync first, the report does not get the information such as the link to the contact and Patient ID.

Fields 1 and 2 show up as hyperlinks in the report, but they only take you to the contact tab.
Field 3 does not populate if the contact has not been synced yet.

If a report is sent after syncing the contact, Patient ID and name are shown with a hyperlink, but it takes you to the Contacts tab as reported in #6149 and #3414. 


**Expected behavior**

2. Patient/Medic ID should be added to the report after both contact and report get synced

title: Infinite redirect loop on login
Generate service worker at runtime
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The service worker is generated when the app is built wherein we cache pseudo-static assets like branding and translations. The challenge with this approach is that in order to support dynamic element update (#5954) we have to use a network-first cache policy to ensure the correct assets are served to users. This isn't really true to the spirit of offline first and results in a lot of redundant requests when assets haven't changed.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
The ideal scenario would be to generate the service worker at runtime when the dynamic assets are updated.

**Additional context**
This is a good opportunity to explore the capabilities of the workbox library.

title: Provide an API endpoint for fetching a contact by phone number
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
For RapidPro integration when we receive an SMS message we want to use the sender's phone number to get the contact information of their primary contact. Currently this is being done by querying a couchdb view to get the patient and then calling the hydration API to get the hierarchy details. This is chatty and makes integration difficult because it requires two queries to get one piece of information. It's also fragile because it depends on the view which we may change with any release.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A hardcoded API which takes a phone number, normalises it, finds the patient document, and hydrates it.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The current setup.

title: Add user telemetry for replication requests
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
We don't have a good idea of how often phones are trying and failing to sync data.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Every time a sync attempt is made we should record some user telemetry so we can monitor and improve. It could also be useful in setting more useful Service Level Objective based on the impact to the project of stale data rather than raw server uptime which doesn't impact offline users much.

Particularly it would be useful to know...
- How long the request took to complete.
- The status, eg: success, server offline, phone offline, other
- How long it's been since the last successful sync so we can work out how stale the data is

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could calculate this server side based on logs, but that would miss data points when the server or phone are offline.

title: Improved support for EBS workflows on existing hierarchies
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
There is interest from multiple existing partners to deploy EBS workflows to their existing users.  Broadly, our challenge now is to take an EBS workflow like the [EBS Covid Reference App](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/new-app-supporting-event-based-surveillance-for-covid-19/701) and deploy that on an existing hierarchy.

There are two known challenges at this time - I'm unclear if they have partial or full solutions. I was unsure if I should add requirement as a comment on related issues or create a new issue. I'm hoping to get some design assistance scoping out the ongoing challenges - we can close this issue as duplicate if all challenges are known and accounted for.

1. EBS systems have tight constraints on the hierarchy. Any contact recieving escalations from an event need to be the primary contact of a place in the hierarchy above the person reporting the event.  Can we make this more flexible/configurable. Perhaps #5817 can solve this partially? Fully?
1. Current EBS systems use contacts to track events. For some projects, this is fine because nobody sees the hierarchy or uses the webapp. But for existing projects this is more important. #6291

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
For some partners, they may be able to use configurable hierarchy and move the existing hierarchy under a new hierarchy (eg. County > Sub-county > existing hierarch). But this is an intense operational exercise for large deployments (concretely BRAC). All users need to sync updates to all contact/report documents.

title: Do not deselect the report when search results still contain it
body:
In the good old days, whenever you searched for reports (eg: using the freetext filter), then whatever report you had selected would stay selected. This was a bit weird when the new search results didn't contain the report you had selected, particularly if no results were found at all.

To fix this we resolved https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/4825 so now when the search is initiated the report is always deselected. This is a bit better and makes sense, but now if the selected report is still in the results it'll be deselected unnecessarily. This is particularly strange since we added https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6291 which allows for clicking a link to search for related reports - you do not expect the current report to be deselected.

I think the optimal solution would be to deselect the report if and only if it's not contained in the updated search results. One challenge with this approach is you don't know if the result will be returned right away, so you either have to a) deselect the report and possibly reselect it once the search completes, or b) leave the report selected and then possibly deselect it once the search completes. Both of these UXs have drawbacks so work with design on the proper solution.

This only affects the desktop UI as mobile UIs switch to only viewing the search results immediately as the search is invoked.

title: Validate env variables, better handling of CouchDB down when starting API / Sentinel
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Server checks validation that checks you're setup correctly.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We currently check if you have set env vars but not if they are valid for all cases.  This causes confusion and is hard to trace down later. As well, there's uncaught errors when CouchDB can't be reached. We should work out what we can truly validate and do that here, so we error as quickly and cleanly as possible:

* We don't validate that your couch node name environment variable (`COUCH_NODE_NAME`) is set right such that it matches what's in CouchDB itself (eg `localhost:5988/_membership`). 
* If CouchDB isn't reachable we throw an uncaught error (`ERROR: uncaughtException`). We should catch it and show a nice to read error.

**Acceptance Testing**
All tests should be run twice.  The first test is to start the API  and the second is to start sentinel. Both are started in the dev environment by changing into their respective directories (`cd`) and then running  `node server.js`. The tests below have you override your environment variable by prefacing the call with a new, intentionally bad value:
* start both the API and sentinel with an invalid node name using: `COUCH_NODE_NAME=mrjones@is_great node server.js` Confirm you immediately get a fatal error, that neither can start and that there's a helpful error message displayed on the CLI. The last two lines illustrate this:
   ```
   COUCH_NODE_NAME=mrjones@is_really_great node server.js
   2020-09-01 14:20:02 INFO: Running server checks… 
   Node Environment Options: 'undefined'
   Node Version: 12.18.3 in development mode
   COUCH_URL http://localhost:5984/medic
   COUCH_NODE_NAME mrjones@is_really_great
   2020-09-01 14:20:02 ERROR: Fatal error initialising medic-api 
   2020-09-01 14:20:02 ERROR: `Environment variable 'COUCH_NODE_NAME' set to "mrjones@is_really_great" but doesn't match what's on CouchDB Membership endpoint at "http://localhost:5984/_membership". See https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/DEVELOPMENT.md#required-environment-variables`
   ```
* start both the API and sentinel with an invalid URL for Couch using: `COUCH_URL=http://admin:pass@mrjones-is-great:5984/medic node server.js` Confirm you immediately get a fatal error, that neither can start and that there's a helpful error message displayed on the CLI. The last three lines illustrate this:
   ```
   COUCH_URL http://mrjones-is-great:5984/medic
   COUCH_NODE_NAME nonode@nohost
   [SNIP- some-stack-trace-info-here -SNIP]
   2020-08-28 15:57:55 ERROR: Fatal error initialising medic-api
   2020-08-28 15:57:55 ERROR: "CouchDB doesn't seem to be running on http://mrjones-is-great:5984/medic. Tried to connect but got an error:\n" +
     ' Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND mrjones-is-great\n' +
     '    at GetAddrInfoReqWrap.onlookup [as oncomplete] (dns.js:66:26)' 
   ```
* additional tests may be optionally run by stopping CouchDB instance and trying to start both the API and sentinel, but this should result in the same errors.
* Ensure your `COUCH_NODE_NAME` is correct and that CouchDB is running. Then make sure you see the happy path affirmation that starts with "Environment variable" when you start both the API and sentinel:
   ```
   Node Version: 12.18.3 in development mode
   COUCH_URL http://localhost:5984/medic
   COUCH_NODE_NAME nonode@nohost
   Environment variable "COUCH_NODE_NAME" matches server "nonode@nohost"
   CouchDB Version: 2.3.1
   ```
* additional happy path tests may be run, such as setting up outbound messaging and ensuring the CouchDB server can be reached. This was one of the original issues that was caused before this PR - good outbound config broke because of bad CouchDB node name environment variable.

title: JSON API endpoints should always presume you're a machine not a human
body:
If you access an endpoint and aren't correctly authenticated, we use the presence (or lack thereof) of a header to determine if you are a human and so should be redirected to the login page, or are a machine and so should get a 401.

This is not great in a lot of situations because if you forget to use that header on an api call and your code is looking for status code to detect success, a badly authenticated request will return you a 200 with some HTML instead of a 401 (or a 200 with a JSON response).

Instead, we should just presume that if you're requesting a JSON endpoint then you want a machine response.

title: Release 3.8.2
body:
# Planning

- [x] Create an [organisation wide project](https://github.com/orgs/medic/projects?query=is%3Aopen+sort%3Aname-asc) and add this issue to it.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the project.

# Development

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Manager. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [ ] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR to the release branch. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version patch`.
- [ ] Write an update in the weekly Product Team call agenda summarising development and acceptance testing progress and identifying any blockers. The release manager is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` and backported to the release branch release testing can begin.

- [ ] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing.
- [ ] Create a new document in the [release-notes folder](https://github.com/medic/medic/tree/master/release-notes) in `master`. Ensure all issues are in the GH Project, that they're correct labelled, and have human readable descriptions. Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/medic/blob/master/scripts/changelog-generator) to export the issues into our changelog format. Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
- [ ] Until release testing passes, make sure regressions are fixed in `master`, cherry-pick them into the release branch, and release another beta.
- [ ] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/medic/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [ ] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [ ] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/blob/master/installation/supported-software.md#supported-versions) and update the EOL date and status of previous releases.
- [ ] Announce the release in #products and #cht-contributors using this template:
```
@channel *Announcing the release of {{version}}*

This release fixes {{number of bugs}}. Read the release notes for full details: {{url}}
```
- [ ] Mark this issue "done" and close the project.

title: Ability to manage SMS notifications and schedules from app contacts forms.
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
There is no known way AFAIK to generate notifications, create and clear schedules when a contact is created in the app(using the contact forms). We can manage schedules using app form report submissions much as we can with the TextForms. What we are not able to do create SMS notification and schedules when a contact is created in the app.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A way to configure contact forms to trigger SMS schedules & notifications.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
In summary,
- using the app form report to create a contact as a child doc, use it to schedule SMS messages - _doesn't work_
- generate a report child form within the enrollment contact form and use it to generate the schedules - _doesn't work_
- use an app form, don't have it generate child doc, instead configure it to trigger the registration translation so that a patient is registered by the transition. contact details are maintained in the app form report. - _works to some extent_

See details of these in the issue medic/config-itech#5

Option three above works to some extent but it does not provide a mechanism to register patients to specific places in the hierarchy that are below the place the logged-in user is attached to. And this is critical for the project at this point. 

**Additional context**

title: Cancel "duplicate" tasks
body:
# Description

Adds incoming changes feed listener that reacts when receiving `task` documents, by marking their corresponding "subjects" as dirty. 
When recalculating, if multiple tasks exist for a single emission, a single winner is chosen, while the rest are cancelled with a "duplicate" stateReason. The winner is the most recent, but not "future", most ready task. "Future" tasks are ignored to align with previous functionality. 

Fixes error thrown when receiving subject-less report in Rules-Engine changes listener. 

De-flakes unrelated e2e test.

title: Allow you to configure outbound to send the same record multiple times
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Prior to 3.9, every time a document changed (either by a human or programmatically, including by sentinel itself) and it passed a `relevant_to` function, an outbound push was queued, unless one was already queued. Every 5 minutes or so, sentinel's scheduler would pick up these queued outbound tasks and executed them. 

In [3.9.0](#6312) we added an [optimisation so that outbound tasks now send immediately if they can](#6306). This would have changed the logic above from "up to once every 5 minutes or so, with whatever data is the latest" to "every single time the document changes, or if the external service is down up to once every 5 minutes or so, with whatever data is the latest".

Because this was confusing, and because more writes happen than you'd think (because of sentinel for example), we did the easiest thing to simplify this logic. In 3.9.0, a configured outbound push only sends to the external service once.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

There are legitimate use cases where you would want to send the same document multiple times. The most obvious example is using outbound to keep a contact in sync with an external EMR or similar. If the phone number changes in CHT, that change should be pushed to the EMR. However, their may also be other situations and examples, and we need to learn about these to make sure we are supporting the right situations.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
There may be various ways to work around this depending on the deployment, but there are potentially situations where this is not possible.

**Additional context**

I think there are three really obvious solutions here, all which have pros and cons and can be variously combined:
 - Add a `sync: true` flag, which defaults to false, and when set to true will resend whenever it can whenever it thinks anything has changed. The pros is that this will always keep external services up to date, the cons is that this will definitely send pointless updates, and if the semantic meaning of sending a push is important to you (ie it indicates a "thing" happened) this will not work for you.
 - Internally hash the REST output, store it against the info doc and only send if the prior send was different to this one. Pros: no extra configuration to get wrong. Cons: will break in subtle and unsolvable ways if people configure outbound mappings to not be deterministic / idempotent, an obvious example being adding a timestamp onto your external REST request
 - Add a `uniqueness: [...]` property, which lets you somehow define what things constitute uniqueness, and then hash *that* as above. Pros: solves the deterministic issues above, Cons: more configuration to configure

title: Support resolving tasks concerning unknown contacts
body:
**Describe the bug**
We can no longer rely on `action.modifyContent` to inject contact information into reports generated by task actions.
This causes tasks that are about unknown contacts to generate reports that are unattached (are missing their subject).
This workflow is used where supervisors with replication depth receive `needs_signoff` reports about patients they can't see.

**To Reproduce**
1. Create a supervisor with replication_depth low enough that they don't see patients.
2. Create a chw under this supervisor.
3. Configure a form with needs_signoff.
4. Configure a task for the supervisor triggered by the `needs_signoff` form. Configure this to be resolved if the task action is executed.
5. Submit the `needs_signoff` form as the CHW.
6. Sync as the supervisor and check if you have generated the task.
7. Complete the task.
8. Your task does not resolve (it's still in the list) and inspecting the resulting report, it's missing all patient information.

**Expected behavior**
The resulting report should have the same patient information as the generating report.

**Environment**
- Instance: local
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.9

**Additional context**
When written to disk, tasks are minified and they only retain a "forId" property representing `action.contact._id`, while `action.contact` is deleted.
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/rules-engine/src/transform-task-emission-to-doc.js#L77
When rehydrating the task, we rely on the `forId` contact to exist in order to repopulate `action.contact`: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/js/controllers/tasks-content.js#L109

We should either:
a) keep `action.contact` when the contact is unknown - this allows more information besides a uuid to be injected into the resulting report 
b) use a stub when rehydrating and contact is unknown - this means that the resulting report will only have the uuid available and no other information.

title: Streamline infodoc writes to remove potential for conflicts
body:
Over time our use of infodocs has grown. They used to just be written to by the transition handler. Then api started to write to them preemptively on every doc write. Then transitions were split between "sync" and "async" transitions. Then outbound started storing data in them and writing to them from a couple of places.

It's getting complicated.

We should drop all places where we `db.sentinel.put(infodoc)` and instead replace that with a specific way that you write to infodocs (written into the `infodoc` shared lib) that removes the possibility of data loss or conflicts. One way of doing this would be to pass `infodoc => infodoc` functions around instead of actually modifying infodocs and writing them, so that this function can be replayed (and / or composed) if there is a conflict.
