title: Write transitions to the `transition` parameter of the `-info` doc in all cases the transition is run
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
We have a log of transitions that have run on documents, stored at `infoDoc.transitions`.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Currently it only adds a transition to the log if that transitions `onMatch` function returns `true`. Some don't however, because this boolean does double duty: it also indicates that the transition edited the document and so the document should be saved back into CouchDB at the end of the transition run.

We should split these two concepts so that we can independently declare that a transition ran (and so should be logged) and that it changed the doc (and so should have an entry added). We could do this by returning two things, or more likely just by presuming if `onMatch` ran at all then that counts as a run.

title: Sentinel will skip changes entirely in certain conditions
body:
**Describe the bug**
These are, in fact, two bugs.

First bug is: if sentinel receives lots of changes in one tick, it will queue up multiple handlers of these changes in the event loop. They're synchronous and they'll be executed in one tick.
If, while executing, we're passing the imposed (100) sentinel change queue limit, we cancel the changesFeed - over and over - without null checking. This throws an error that prevents the act of enqueueing to happen.

The second bug is: when we pass the imposed queue limit threshold, we store the last_seq in a variable and we use that instead of the DB value (from sentinel-meta-data) when we restart the feed.
We also kill the change-queue (dump all changes we queued up) when we receive a settings change that breaks transitions config!
So all changes in between memory `last_seq` and `sentinel-meta-data.processed_seq` are straight up skipped when the queue is killed.

I haven't been able to replicate bug#1 locally, but it's failed multiple times on Travis. So I assume it's performance related.
Replicating bug#2 might require some scripting and quick reactions.

**To Reproduce Bug2**
1. Enable `generate_shortcode_on_contacts` transition (or `generate_patient_id_on_people`)
2. Create 200 persons in one batch (you can go for more if you want, but about 200 should be enough).
3. Watch the sentinel output to see an entry like: "Transitions: queue size 101 greater than 100, we stop listening"
4. Very quickly after this, you should break the config (simplest is to enable an non-existent transition) - it's helpful to have a script that does this. After this, Sentinel should stop processing docs (because config is broken).
5. Fix the config. No need to hurry for this one :)
6. At this point, Sentinel should start processing docs (because the config is fixed). Wait for it to process all docs. Optionally, you can repeat steps 3-4.
7. Once everything is processed and the queue is clear, check the "person"s you added in step 2) to see if all have a patient_id. Some will not! <- this is the bug.

**Expected behavior**
All person contacts should be processed!

**Logs**
Bug#1 will output something like:
```
>> Error in .on("change", function): TypeError: Cannot read property 'cancel' of null
>>     at Changes.<anonymous> (/home/diana/projects/medic/sentinel/src/lib/feed.js:53:19)
>>     at Changes.emit (events.js:310:20)
>>     at tryCatchInChangeListener (/home/diana/projects/medic/sentinel/node_modules/pouchdb-core/lib/index.js:20:10)
>>     at Object.Changes.opts.onChange (/home/diana/projects/medic/sentinel/node_modules/pouchdb-core/lib/index.js:58:5)
>>     at /home/diana/projects/medic/sentinel/node_modules/pouchdb-adapter-http/lib/index.js:1040:18
>>     at Array.filter (<anonymous>)
>>     at fetched (/home/diana/projects/medic/sentinel/node_modules/pouchdb-adapter-http/lib/index.js:1030:35)

title: Outbound - Support for capturing mappings via javascript modules
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Outbound Push

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
For the MSF-Goma project, one potential architecture under consideration involves many outbound push configurations - possibly ~25 separate outbound push configurations! The resulting system is verbose and stringy. When integrations start to get complex like this, it would be so really helpful to have basics like reusable functions, or the ability to put code on multiple lines, to use comments, and to write unit tests. The JSON-based system has very poor readability, tons of copy-paste, and there is also a lot of redundant JSON (particularly multiple redundant identical "destination" blocks).

It would be great if outbound push also supported the same `module.exports` interface that is used by tasks, targets, purge, contact-summaries, etc.

Maybe something like a JSON blob in app_settings:
```
{
  "name": "my rapidpro integrations",
  "destination": {
      "base_url": "https://textit.in",
      "auth": { "type": "header", "name": "Authorization", "value_key": "textit.in" },
      "path": "/api/v2/contacts.json"
  },
  "script":  "rapidpro_outbound.js"
}
```

`rapidpro_outbound.js`
```
module.exports = [
  {
    path: '/api/v2/contacts.json',
    mapping: doc => ({ foo: 'bar' }),
  },
];
```

Sentinel could just `require('outbound.js')`, so it seems pretty easy. It is also preferrable to provide general extensibility patterns instead of requiring app builders learn nuanced, hard to debug, bespoke, JSON syntax.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Google seemingly tried to work around this same issue by using resolved task documents to trigger outbound push. This allowed them to move business logic into unit-tested script instead of dealing with this mountain of JSON.

title: When re-assigning a report for follow-up to different users, the report remains visible to users who are no longer assigned
body:
**Describe the bug**

Hierarchy
```
    A
  /   \
B1     B2
```

For the MoH-Niger project, we have a user with facility_id at level A responsible for creating a report and "assigning" that report to another user with facility_id at level B.  To "assign" the report to the user B1, the report is created with an appropriate patient_id such that it appears in B1's replication view. This bug occurs when user A attempts to "re-assign" the report from user B1 to another user B2. To "re-assign" the report to user B2, the report is edited and the patient_id is changed to B2.  When this happens, the report appears for both user B1 and B2.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Deploy [Niger MoH configuration](https://github.com/medic/config-msf/tree/master/niger)
1. Create a SAMU, with a riposte, and two case investigators.
1. Login as SAMU user, create a new COVID case via reports tab.
1. Login as Riposte user, find the task created for this COVID case, click on it, assign Investigator 1 to follow-up.
1. Login as Investigator 1, sync, find the follow-up task for this case
1. Login as Ripsote user, find the report created by the task in step 4, edit it, assign Investigator 2 instead of Investigator 1
1. Login as Investigator 2, sync, find the follow-up task for this case
1. Login as Investigator 1, sync

**Expected behavior**
Currently, both Investigator 1 and Investigator 2 both see the report.  Just based on how replication works, investigator 1 sees `rev-1` of the report and investigator 2 sees `rev-2` of the report. 

How can App Builders make the follow-up task for Investigator 1 disappear to enable the re-assigning of cases?

**Environment**

- Browser: Chrome
- Client platform: Ubuntu Bionic

title: Info companion docs can continue to grow in size
body:
Currently `-info` docs are loaded up pretty frequently in api and sentinel, generally whenever the parent document is CRUD'd. For example, every time you write a document via API the `-info` companion document is loaded, some dates updated, and saved again, synchronously.

With the introduction of outbound push and with the additional work happening to allow for the same document to be pushed multiple times, it seems very likely that some documents will slowly gain a very large `completed_tasks` property (one entry for every successful outbound push).

I'm not sure what the impact may be if someone has hundreds or thousands of completed task entries, but we should look into it, as it's the kind of thing that may creep up on us. We may have to limit the amount of old `completed_task` entries we keep, or move it into a different document entirely.

Note that sentinel metadata is also stored on these docs, which can grow every time the doc is worked through sentinel. However, this feature is kind of broken: only transitions that alter the main document get their sentinel metadata written. So in the case of outbound, no extra writes there.

title: Outbound will send multiple requests for the same record
body:
Adds a hash into completed_tasks so we can correctly detect when to
re-send a record.

This changes the sending semantics for outbound to be that we send an
outbound request whenever we have a configuration with a truthy
relevant_to, and where the prior send (if any) for that configuration
sent a different payload.

This is not a perfect system. If your mapping function is not idempotent
outbound may fire requests when you do not intend it to, e.g., if a user
doesn't actually edit the document meaningfully, or if sentinel or
another process writes to the document.

title: Guard against xpath string concatenation regression
body:
**Describe the issue**
We use `medic/openrosa-xpath-evaluator` to evaluate xpath in Enketo forms, and one non-standard feature is that you can concatenate string values with either the `+` operator or the `concat()` function. At some point we're going to upgrade to a version that deprecates use of the `+` operator but because it's a dependency of a dependency it's hard to know when that'll happen. Because the `+` operator is used widely for different values it's difficult to work out if we're using it for concatenation at all.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
1. Write a test which runs against the version of `openrosa-xpath-evaluator` so we will be notified when it fails and can document it correctly in the release notes.
2. Document the deprecation of the `+` operator so app builders don't use it in future.
3. Investigate writing a test in the [configuration test harness](https://github.com/medic/medic-conf-test-harness) to detect configurations that use `+`.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Sticking on an old version of Enketo forever.
- Patching the official version with some bespoke code.

title: Prevent users from opening and filling forms they're not authorized to see/fill
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
We currently filter the report forms we display as available actions in the actionbar to the ones that the user is authorized to see (via the `context.permissions` property in the forms document).
With https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6401, we also filter the create contact forms in a similar manner.
However, if a user accesses the form (be it contact or report form) by typing a valid URL that opens said form, we have no mechanism in place to authorize this action.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We could display an error screen, similar to the ones where the form fails to load, informing the user they're not authorized to complete the action.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Alternatively we could redirect the user to a "valid" page directly, and show a popup.

**Additional context**
We could, potentially, also apply this to edits (both of contacts AND reports).

title: Add entries to .gitignore so it ignores medic-conf files
body:
**Describe the issue**
By definition, you need to run `medic-conf` in the directory where you CHT configs are. This means it puts additional files into this repo in `config/default`.  These files, in turn, get flagged for being added when git runs and notices new, untracked files.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Add entries to `.gitignore` that excludes files from `cht-core` but doesn't prevent key components to a config from being edited or added.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
You can use either `git clean` to remove the untracked files or a [global git ignore](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/7335420/global-git-ignore), but these are kludgy and are likely to miss files we hadn't thought of.

body:
**Describe the issue**
Currently we run our scalability suite against gamma.dev from a QA's local machine. There are so many variables with this and in an attempt to cut down on some. We'd want to start running these on a server(AWS) against a test instance. This will allow us to control the machine executing and the machine running against. Hopefully to have the same set of variables each release.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
A few things are needed for this to happen. My initial thought is this should likely be two machines. One hosting our app and the other executing. That could be an improvement to the process down the road. Thought being running on the same machine is consuming extra resources. I also feel like steps 4-7 could probably be dockerized.

1. Using github actions. I want to spin up an AWS machine.  Will require credentials to do this. Hopefully restricted so they cannot make any changes to any other machines. Likely using the self hosting method.
2. Clone our `cht-core` repo to this machine. 
3. Install our software on this machine and set a branch. @Hareet  mentioned piping the config to the ec2 init scripts
4. Run Medic-conf to apply standard config. 
5. Seed our standard config data using medic-conf.
6. Install Jmeter 
6. Execute Scalability tests with Jmeter.
7. Store the results somewhere. I assume we could use a directory where our UI tests are storing their results in AWS. EX: `      S3_PATH=s3://medic-e2e/BUILD_$TRAVIS_BUILD_NUMBER/JOB_$TRAVIS_JOB_NUMBER` Storing the results is used for comparing previous runs against older versions.
8. Tear it all down. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could use a paid solution like blazemeter to run the tests but we'd still have to setup an instance with our software, data, config. The other option which we have been doing is described in the issue portion.

title: Upgrading doesn't apply replication configuration which means `users-meta` is empty
body:
**Describe the bug**

In #4898 (3.5.0) we moved feedback and telemetry docs to being stored in the users meta database for performance reasons. This also included a new configuration option for replication which allowed users to set up replications from one db to another based on a configured cron ([documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/replication/)). This was set up to be a generic reusable configuration for replicating from any db to any other db.

Later on we realised it wasn't working because the configuration wasn't included by default which was patched in #6147 (3.9.0) so the default config included a replication config.  

We also progressively made the replication code more specific so it's only really useful for replicating `medic-user-{username}-meta` dbs to the `medic-users-meta` db (eg: we added filtering so we only replicate feedback and telemetry docs). This means the generic configurable component isn't actually useful.

Now that you know the history, here's the bug: projects that don't have replications configured don't replicate docs into the `medic-users-meta` db which breaks the expectations of the analytics, monitoring, and exporting code.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Push a configuration without replications configured
2. Log in as a restricted user and generate feedback docs using the hamburger menu item
3. Force your meta db to sync (takes 30 minutes but can be forced on the `/testing` page)
4. Find the doc in your user's meta db on CouchDB
5. Wait 24 hours

**Expected behavior**
The doc should eventually replicate to the `medic-users-meta` db. It's ok if this takes up to 24 hours to go.

**Logs**
None.

**Screenshots**
None.

**Environment**
- Instance: localhost
- Browser: Chrome
- Client platform: Linux
- App: sentinel
- Version: 3.9.0

**Additional context**
The workaround is to configure the replication, as in the `/config/default/app_settings.json`

title: Work out definitively how CouchDB authentication maintains fresh authentication tokens
body:
There has been some confusion recently about exactly how our authentication tokens are maintained, and what users need to do to maintain them.

We use CouchDB authentication. In production systems we set the auth timeout to 1 year. This means that when you call `_session` and authenticate the token you get back is valid for one year (provided you don't invalid it and all tokens for that server by changing CouchDB's secret key).

The confusion lies in how these tokens get refreshed. One partner has come back to us and noted that users are being logged out exactly one year after they were first created, which implies they are never triggering the creation of fresher tokens for some reason.

Specifically, what interaction with CouchDB will result in this timeout being extended? For example, does it happen when users refresh the app? Or when any background synchronisation happens? Or only if they explicitly login again?

We should work this out, document it correctly, and if it's "wrong" (ie the product team would expect it to happen at a certain time and it isn't) fix it.

Tasks:
 - [x] work out how authentication freshness works with CouchDB
 - [x] work out if auth is working correctly inside the CHT ecosystem
 - [ ] add some kind of automated test so we notice in the future if we accidentally erase the headers required for this to work
 - ~~work out the cause of issues our partners are having~~ this should be done in specific partner tickets

title: Sentinel might process changes when it shouldn't
body:
We have a mechanism where Sentinel would stop processing changes if any of the enabled transitions is misconfigured.
Right now, because of how our queue is paused and resumed when it reaches certain length, we might get in a situation where sentinel processing is resumed even if it was stopped due to a misconfigured transition.

**To Reproduce**
A little disclaimer that this a total race condition that I happened to witness in an e2e test. This is what the e2e test did:
1. Edit a doc (doesn't matter which doc, the idea is to have something in your queue)
2. Immediately edit `settings` with a misconfigured transition
3. Immediately after you see that "'Transitions are disabled until the above configuration errors are fixed." Update another doc.
4. Watch the Sentinel log and notice that your second doc is actually getting processed, but no transitions run over it.

**Expected behavior**
The 2nd doc should not have been processed.

**Logs**
When the race condition happens, you would see something like:
```
change event on doc <your 1st doc>
Reloading configuration
Loading transition ....
......
Failed loading transition <your misconfigured transition>
....
Transitions are disabled until the above configuration errors are fixed.
saved changes on doc <your 1st doc>
transitions: queue drained
transitions: processing enabled <- this is the bug.
change event on doc <your 2nd doc>
```

**Environment**
- Instance: local
- Client platform: Linux
- App: Sentinel
- Version: 3.10

**Additional context**
I tried to replicate this outside of my flacky e2e test, but couldn't write a reliable script that always triggers this.
The change I'm making is so, when the queue is drained, only an working (unpaused) queue will resume processing.

title: Adhere to play store privacy policy requirements update
body:
Google recently announced an [update](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9914283) to their Google Play Policies, which takes effect Aug 12, 2020. Adherence is mandatory, else risk de-listing. Included in this update, they require developers to:

> Post a privacy policy in both the designated field in the Play Console and within the app itself. The privacy policy must, together with any in-app disclosures, comprehensively disclose how your app accesses, collects, uses, and shares user data. Your privacy policy must disclose the types of personal and sensitive data your app accesses, collects, uses, and shares and the types of parties with which any personal or sensitive user data is shared.

For the in-app disclosure, UI requirements include:
- Must be displayed in the normal usage of the app and not require the user to navigate into a menu or settings
- Must present the consent dialog clearly and unambiguously;
- Must require affirmative user action (e.g. tap to accept, tick a check-box);
- Must not interpret navigation away from the disclosure (including tapping away or pressing the back or home button) as consent; and
- Must not utilize auto-dismissing or expiring messages.

These Google Play requirements are in addition to any requirements prescribed by applicable local privacy and data protection laws. Since the CHT is deployed in various countries around the world, each with their own data privacy rules, we should make the in-app disclosure configurable.

Additional info on the user data policy can be [found here](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9888076#personal_sensitive). 

**Complete with this ticket**:
- [ ] updated data policy in the Play Console
- [ ] configurable in-app data policy

The `/users/info` api was added as a means to warn configurers and users when replicating too many docs. 
This endpoint is called with specific parameters (`roles` and a `facility_id`) when adding/editing users (via admin console or medic-conf).This configurer-side request completely disregards which user we're editing.

This endpoint is _also_ called when performing an initial replication on the device. The user-side request is different, it uses no parameters and identifies the user by their authorization context (session cookie). 
The big difference is that this request knows who the authorized user is. 

Before 3.8, the configurer-side request and user-side request yielded identical results.
After 3.8 and the task/targets refactor, tasks are now persistent on disk and are replicated. They also have a special replication_key so they're only replicated by the user that created them, so knowing who the user is relevant now.   
After 3.8 the user-side `/users/info` request will count all of the user's tasks towards the replication warning limit. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We should align the configurer-side request and the user-side request, so you don't end up being warned on one side and not warned on the other. 
Warning that the user replicates too many docs because they have too many tasks isn't actionable. The only way the number of tasks is reduced is by purging, which only happens 60 days after a task is in a terminal state. 
I suggest we **exclude counting task documents** towards the replication warning limit. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
As an addendum rather than complete alternative, we could split the warning and warn separately about number of tasks. 
We could also change the endpoint to accept a new parameter, user_id, which can be called by configurers and get the result that counts the user's tasks as well, and change how the endpoint is called when editing users. 

**Additional context**
This was brought forward by a TL that was confused why a user with 300 docs (as the configurer-side request reported) had a warning during initial replication that they were replicating 20.500 docs (yes - the user indeed had 20k tasks). 

We should also consider the API reporting part, and probably split the number of docs between tasks and non-tasks.

title: Research way for developers to test TLS requiring android app against specific cht-core branches
body:
**Describe the issue**
Currently developers who are following our [developer guide](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/DEVELOPMENT.md) are instructed to reverse proxy their dev instance behind ngrok's TLS servers.  This allows the android app to connect with a valid TLS cert but still gives the developer flexibility to run their own, local code which they can easily iterate on.

When we were updating the dev guide in #6551, it came up that ngrok's free tier can rate limit you under heavy use.  As well, serveo ,obviously, no longer works.  We wondered if setting up our own reverse proxy was easy enough that we should research it.  This would have the added benefit that when testing production instances with real customer data, we would not have grant access to this data unencrypted to third parties like [ngrok](https://ngrok.com/), and soon, [pagekite](https://pagekite.net/).

There are two classes of developers that would use this that we should consider when doing research:
* Medic Mobile employees
* External Contributors and Technical Partners (TPs)

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Research the cost in time to initially set up and ongoing hosting fees of a DIY reverse proxy for terminating TLS.  This might include:
* spinning up a simple EC2 instance and manually installing something like ["self-hosted ngrok or serveo alternative?"](https://www.digitalocean.com/community/questions/self-hosted-ngrok-or-serveo-alternative) or ["A self-hosted ngrok"](https://medium.com/@shivanshvij/a-self-hosted-ngrok-45bcec06d0cf)
* spinning up a simple EC2 instance per above, but deploy with a more advanced reverse proxy that would be provisioned with dozens of vhost/Let's Encrypt TLS cert pairs such that it could support many developers.  This would connect existing FQDNs -> EC2 instance w/ externally accessible vhost and TLS on port 443 -> reverse proxy to localhost port on the server (eg 4500) -> developer connects to their instance running on their localhost `5988` port via `ssh -R 5988:localhost:4500 ec2.host.example.com`. Developers public SSH keys, or predefined private keys, would have to be baked in. Deploy via an automated, repeatable, source controlled process.
* Using a more SRE approach with a feature build docker image (something like [docker-letsencrypt](https://github.com/linuxserver/docker-letsencrypt)) coupled with AWS docker hosting and AWS load balancers which can terminate TLS
* Moar?!?!1

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Alternatives are:
* Stay the course and follow the docs we have in place re ngrok and pagekite
* Research other services:
  *  [Lynk.sh](https://lynk.sh/)
  * [Fog Machine](https://fog.fm/)
* Automated ways to provision test instances hosted in AWS that can easily be tied to a specific cht-core branch
* Purchase a wildcard cert on something crazy like  `*.only-testing-no-phishing-possibe-mm.org`, bake this into cht-core repo/dev env including both public and private key for the cert so that devs can just use `grunt` as they do today but it will deploy on android working 443 with TLS.

title: Work out how to support multiple short codes for a single CHT deployment
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
A typical medic-gateway deployment uses a simcard which can send/receive messages across any MNO. With shortcodes, this may not necessarily be the case. In some countries one has to apply to each MNO for a short code and you would very likely end up with different numbers for each of the networks applied to (e.g. Kenya). In other countries, short code issuance is governed by one authority which ensures one short code works across all networks in that country (e.g South Africa)

In our EBS deployment in Kenya, we used Safaricom as the default MNO since they are the largest provider in the country. As we are scaling, we will definitely deploy in areas where Safaricom is not the dominant provider and would be unfair to have users acquire a simcard just to use the service especially given that the model used is BYOD.

CHT currently only supports one gateway number per deployment.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'd like to see us support multiple short codes in a single deployment.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Use of medic-gateway. This however does not scale well in large deployments.

@SMurithi @benkags @PhilipNgari please add any tidbits I may have missed

title: Release 3.11.0
body:
# Planning

- [x] Create an [organisation wide project](https://github.com/orgs/medic/projects?query=is%3Aopen+sort%3Aname-asc) and add this issue to it. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the project. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bugs.

# Development

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Manager. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`.
- [x] Raise a new issue called `Update dependencies for <version>` with a description that links to [the documentation](https://github.com/medic/medic-docs/blob/master/development/update-dependencies.md). This should be done early in the release cycle so find a volunteer to take this on and assign it to them.
- [x] Go through all features and improvements scheduled for this release and raise cht-docs issues for product education to be written where appropriate. If in doubt, check with Max.
- [x] Write an update in the weekly Product Team call agenda summarising development and acceptance testing progress and identifying any blockers. The release manager is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` release testing can begin.

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in medic. Post a message to #development using this template:

@core_devs I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!

title: Have an upper time limit to generating task documents
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently, the rules-engine will consider any emission due in the future as timely. We do, however, consider emissions due more than 60 days in the past as not timely. 
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/rules-engine/src/task-states.js#L125

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
I find no obvious advantage in generating and storing these far-into-the-future tasks. They will, most likely, become "stale" and be canceled by config changes and updates to the dataset. This breeds a rapidly ever-growing task collection for every user, that puts strain on the device and on the server. 

My proposal is to have an upper time limit to timely emissions, maybe (very generously) 6 months or 1 year, but we could probably go with less and have no impact on user's performance. The interval is TBD. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None. 

**Additional context**
It's happened in production that some task configs generated emissions for more than 10 years in the future.

title: Single emissions recalculation thread
body:
# Description

Updates `rules-engine` shared lib to only allow a single `refreshRulesEmissions` call to be executed in parallel. All calls to `fetchTasksFor` and `fetchTargets` are queued and are execute sequentially. 
To support accurate Telemetry readings, calls to `fetchTargets` and `fetchTasksFor` return promisemitters, which resolve when the tasks are done and emit two events: `queued` when placed in the queue and `running` when execution started.
The webapp `RulesEngine` service listens to these events and logs a new Telemetry record, `queued`, that registers the time the request spent in a queue (from `queued` event to `running` event), along with the already existent "execution" record, that only registers execution time (from the `running` event to promise resolution).

title: Improve performance of subject lookups in authorization service
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
When determining whether a document is sensitive, we immediately search for it's submitter in the subjects array. 
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/services/authorization.js#L453

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Don't immediately search for the submitter, do it only per-need basis if the report is validated by the other "isSensitive" checks. 
We could, also, improve lookup times by keeping the subjects array sorted and leveraging binary search. 

We could use [_.sortedIndexOf](https://lodash.com/docs/4.17.15#sortedIndexOf). This would force us to cast all subjects to strings because of inconsistent results when dealing with mixed arrays: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/issues/4885
We could also write our own binary search function that casts before comparing. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Create a rather large offline user. Say 10k contacts and at least 15k reports. 
2. Request `_changes?limit=1` with this offline user and note the request time.

**Measurements**
The `_changes` requests will be most impacted by this improvement, because it loads all ids that the user is allowed to see. For smal users, the difference won't be noticeable. 
`_bulk_docs` and `_all_docs` requests perform subject lookups, but given the limited size of the requests (max 100 docs when replicating from Pouch), the difference will not be noticeable.

title: Scheduled messages with due date of `null` end up being processed over and over without being updated
body:
**Describe the bug**
If a document has a `scheduled_task` with a due date equal to `null` (or other falsy value), it will get processed over and over for 1 week, every time the `due_tasks` Sentinel task runs. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a doc that has at least a `scheduled_task`. 
2. Change the `scheduled_task` due date to be `null`. 
3. Go to App Management -> Message Queue -> Scheduled and notice your message is part of this list
4. Wait for Sentinel to run the "due_tasks" task.
5. Refresh the Message Queue page and notice your message is still scheduled. 

**Expected behavior**
When due_tasks runs, queued `scheduled_tasks` in `scheduled` state should be updated to `pending`. 

**Environment**
- Instance: local
- Client platform: Linux
- App: Sentinel
- Version: 3.10

**Additional context**
Because we only process 1000 `scheduled_tasks` when we run `due_tasks`, the queue can be saturated with 1000 of these messages and block processing of other valid scheduled tasks.

title: Users are forced to login one year after they last logged in
body:
**Describe the bug**
Exactly one year after users last logged in if they refresh the page or start the app they are redirected to the login page and cannot return to the app unless they provide valid credentials. This should not occur if the user has been interacting with the app in that time as their session should be renewed every time a request is made to the server.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Log in as a CHP. If you check the cookies in the browser you should see the `userCtx` cookie is set with an expiry exactly 1 year in the future.
2. Modify your local date to be around 10 months in the future
3. Refresh the page
4. The app reloads correctly. Wait a few minutes for the various requests to complete. Expected behavior: the `userCtx` cookie expiry has been renewed to 1 year from the new date.
5. Modify your local date to be another 6 months in the future
6. Refresh the page
7. You are now redirected to the login page.

**Expected behavior**
You should not be redirected to the login page because you interacted with the server to keep your session alive in step 4.

**Logs**
N/A

**Screenshots**
N/A

**Environment**
- Instance: gamma.dev
- Browser: Chrome
- Client platform: Linux
- App: webapp and api
- Version: 3.5.0

**Additional context**
One workaround is to supply the users with their password so they can login again.
Another option is for the administrator to collect the phones back before the end of the year and logout and login again.

title: Add instance routing for incoming messages
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
1. As a trainer I want to be able to have messages from my trainees be routed to a training instance so they can use the same shortcode and aggregator without adding dummy data to the production instance.
2. As an app builder I want to be able to route messages to one of multiple production instances so I can have different configurations for different districts and still use the same shortcode and aggregator.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A new product/service to receive WT messages and route them to the correct instance. Which route to choose could be based on which instance has the senders phone number configured (user story 2), or which user has a specific flag set (user story 1), or based on a simple phone number lookup table (user story 1), or some combination thereof.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Training could be done on a dev instance but it's difficult to correctly delete the training data afterwards, and it impacts server performance.
- We could use multiple shortcodes but they're not that easy or cheap to get, and could be confusing for users.
- Training could be done with a long code but not all aggregators accept them.

title: Rebranding apps and renaming repos
body:
**Describe the issue**
We have a mix of the legacy `medic` prefix and the new `cht` prefix for our repos and apps. In general we should use the `cht` prefix for everything that is useful to people outside of Medic Mobile, for example, `cht-infrastructure` is public has scripts for hosting that a self-hosting partner could use, while `medic-infrastructure` is private and has scripts for the Medic Mobile hosting stack.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

Change the following repo names

- [x] medic-conf -> cht-conf
- [x] medic-conf-test-harness -> cht-conf-test-harness
- [x] medic-gateway -> cht-gateway
- [x] medic-android -> cht-android
- [x] medic-couch2pg -> cht-couch2pg
- [x] medic-nootils -> cht-nootils

Also

- [x] Change the cht-cli command line name to `cht` to make it easy to type and use. If possible keep `medic-conf` as a deprecated alias so we don't break backwards compatibility. 
- [x] Rename the medic gateway apps but leave the package ID unchanged, ie: Medic Gateway -> CHT Gateway ([here](https://github.com/medic/medic-gateway/blob/master/src/main/res/values/strings.xml#L3))

We could leave the names alone - it's not hurting anyone...

title: In app "What's new" training cards
body:
**Problem statement:**

As we continue to make incremental updates to the CHT core and program managers continue to make updates to workflows we should easily communicate to end users what has changed in their app without needing an in-person training session.

**User stories:**

- As a user I want to be notified when there are new features or workflows in my app so that I am always up to date on the actions I can take, and how
- As a user I want to be notified when there are updates to my forms, tasks or targets so that I can ensure I am doing my work correctly and efficiently
- As a user I want to revisit update announcements if I am unsure of a recent change to my app
- As a program manager I want to facilitate remote training so I can ensure the success of CHT deployments

**Design requirements (WIP):**

- Announcements should include core updates and configuration updates
- Announcements should be configurable so that each user type receives relevant updates to their specific app and workflows
- When a user logs in for the first time we should show the onboarding material (will we need to update the onboarding material per release?)
- When a user logs in and there have been core or configuration updates we should show them the upgrade material
- Announcements should include a brief overview with the option to tap into more details
- Users should be able close the announcement
- Announcements should be categorized by type (feature release, core update, config update, bug fixes, performance improvements, security updates etc.)
- Announcements should be logged somewhere in the app
- Announcements could include videos or helpful visuals to be more information-rich
- MM should provide a default for each release


**Open questions:**

- How may this work with other in-app training?
- How may this work with the current update modal?
- How may we apply this feature to SMS users?

title: test
Detect and report when users are unable to connect to the server
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We recently had an outage where users on an old version of Android were unable to connect due to being incompatible with a modern certificate installed on the server. Our current uptime reporting was compatible so it didn't report the outage, and it wasn't reported to our support channels for a few weeks. There are other problems that may cause users to be unable to connect.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We want to be alerted as soon as possible when there is a significant drop in users connecting to the server. Provide or update an API or integration to existing services so the number of users who have managed to connect to the server can be tracked. Consider carefully how to express this data to reduce the noise, for example, reporting the percentage of users who have managed to connect in the last 7 days would account for lower usage on the weekend.

Configuring the monitoring and alerting is a separate task.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Client side reporting, but if the user cannot connect then they may not be able to report that fact either.
- Monitoring reports created or other existing metric, but there are other reasons why reporting may drop off so this isn't as accurate.

title: Update `admin` to be a standalone app
body:
**Describe the issue**
Currently, the admin app requires a significantly large number of webapp files (services, filters, directives, redux actions/reducers/selectors). 
This becomes a problem with the migration to Angular 10, where the files imported from webapp will, most likely, be unusable by admin. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
"Duplicate" all files that admin app requires from the webapp folder, preserving git line history as much as possible. (this includes their tests)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could postpone this migration under the assumption that we may be able to use post-angular-10-migration webapp files as we do now, but it's a risk.

title: Document update conflicts when clearing schedules
body:
**Describe the bug**
`accept_patient_reports` and `registration` fail with a conflict when clearing schedules. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Load `standard` config
2. Create a pregnancy (app form) for a patient. Wait for Sentinel to process this change.
3. Create a delivery (app form) for the same patient. Wait for Sentinel to process the change. 
4. Check Sentinel logs and see conflict. 
We also have a race condition where, if Sentinel's queue is reset quickly enough, all will seem well in the app - with the delivery doc updated successfully, even if there is a conflict the 1st time. Most of the time, the delivery doc will not be updated correctly. If multiple transitions run over it, you might even see an error on the doc stating that `registration` transition failed with a conflict. 

**Expected behavior**
Neither of these transitions should fail with a conflict. 

**Logs**
You will see something like this:
```
2020-08-31 15:43:17 ERROR: transition registration errored on doc <delivery doc ID> seq <SEQ>: {
  id: '<pregnancy doc ID>',
  error: 'conflict',
  reason: 'Document update conflict.',
  name: 'conflict',
  status: 409,
  message: 'Document update conflict.',
  docId: '<pregnancy doc ID>'
} 
```

Notice that the conflict isn't on the currently processed delivery doc, rather on the old pregnancy doc, whose schedules need clearing.

**Environment**
- Instance: local
- App: api, sentinel
- Version: 3.9, 3.10

**Additional context**
This problem appeared when `medic-client/reports_by_subject` was changed to emit multiple times per doc: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/commit/f31350c1f5e4dd792a71fc414c731807b1d3e2b2#diff-e503e25acb27edd4d19d7f0badcfedbbR9
This made the original `pregancy` show up multiple times in the results list and fail the subsequent "updates". 

The error also happens when processing SMSs, but if checking SMS, look at API logs instead of Sentinel logs.

title: Be able to run unit tests from different apps in the CHT
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Running `grunt test` run all the tests in the repo, and there are a few tasks defined in `Gruntfile.js` to run some test suites separately but there is no easy way to run just the tests from Sentinel, and there is a way to run just the tests from the API but not working.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Define a few tasks in Grunt to be able to run tests just for the app the developer is working on, saving time when waiting the execution to complete.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Although is not impossible to run these tests separately, it's tricky and not documented. Adding tasks in Grunt will make it easier and "auto" documented, because Grunt allows to list all the tasks available executing `grunt --help`, so no need to read the long `Gruntfile.js` script to figure out that there are other ways to run the tests.

Currently you can run just the Sentinel tests from an IDE like IntelliJ / Webstorm but you need to create a configuration manually, and the configuration differ depending of the IDE you are using. You can also run the tests from the root of the project within the command line:

    $ node_modules/mocha/bin/mocha sentinel/tests/**/*.js  sentinel/tests/**/**/*.js

Same for the API replacing the paths, but not ideal and not documented.

**Additional context**
Supposedly you can run tests just from API with `grunt mochaTest:unit`, but many unit tests fail as follow:

```
...
...
    at Context.it (api/tests/mocha/services/purged-docs.js:34:53)                                      
                                                                                                       

  55) Purged Docs service
       listen
         should restart listener on error:

      AssertionError: expected 2 to equal 1
      + expected - actual

      -2
      +1

    at Context.it (api/tests/mocha/services/purged-docs.js:90:53)




Warning: Task "mochaTest:unit" failed. Use --force to continue.

Aborted due to warnings.


Execution Time (2020-09-02 12:42:55 UTC-0)
loading tasks   328ms  ▇▇▇ 3%
mochaTest:unit  10.1s  ▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇ 97%
Total 10.5s
```

In the PR I'll propose I solve the problem creating a new task that execute the same task above but prepending the `env:unit-test` task:

```js
  grunt.registerTask('unit-api', 'API unit tests', [
    'env:unit-test',
    'mochaTest:api',
  ]);
```

So executing `grunt unit-api` tests work and the execution time is the same.

Also not sure if I should propose a PR before the ticket was triaged and accepted, but the reality is that struggling to run the tests I made changes in the Gruntfile.js first with the plan to add the improvements in another ticket/PR I was working on, but then realized that the proposal needs a separated thread, so feel free to reject the whole idea/PR if there is better way to resolve this.

title: Schedules depending on `later` library might not run when expected
body:
**Describe the bug**
We use the [later](https://github.com/bunkat/later) library for scheduling purging. It has a "documented" glitch where it won't create a timer for the immediately next occurrence of a cron schedule, when this occurrence is less than one second away from the present, instead it will schedule the next occurrence. 

https://github.com/bunkat/later/blob/master/src/core/settimeout.js#L36
```
// minimum time to fire is one second, use next occurrence instead
if(diff < 1000) {
  diff = next[1] ? next[1].getTime() - now : 1000;
}
```

**To Reproduce**
This is very hard to reproduce, as it requires having sentinel schedule purging within a second of the schedule being created. 
However it has happened in production. 
What you would observe, if the bug is triggered, is that purge will just be skipped. Just like it would not be scheduled at all. 

**Expected behavior**
Purge should run on schedule.

**Logs**
Logs from the production instance where this happened:
```
Sep 04 04:00:00 medic-sentinel-logs | [2020-09-04 00:59:59] 2020-09-04 00:59:59 WARN: Reminder configuration invalid
Sep 04 04:00:00 medic-sentinel-logs | [2020-09-04 00:59:59] 2020-09-04 01:00:00 INFO: checking schedule again in 5 minutes 
```

The purge scheduler had run in between these two items. 
Purge should have been scheduled to run at `2020-09-04 01:00:00`, so within a second from the present. 

**Environment**
- Instance: production instance
- App: Sentinel
- Version: discovered on 3.9.1, but it's been an issue since forever

**Additional context**
I think the simplest solution is to change from using `later.setTimeout` to using the builtin `setTimeout`.

title: Improve the performance of Enketo repeated sections
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
There are some good examples of signifiant performance issues in the CHT form-filling experience for projects using repeat sections in XForms: https://github.com/medic/config-moh-mali/issues/56 and https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6136. These have lead to an initiative to "quantify the upper bounds of what the cht-core can handle" https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/issues/308. 

End-users are affected because their forms load slowly.

This is also impacting the CHT app building experience. This performance limitation is below what some developers would intuitively consider devices to be capable of (even legacy devices). This irregularity results in increased educational burdens for onboarding new TPs. The guidelines for avoiding these performance traps are not always totally straightforward as seen with https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6136. The end result is a poor app development experience for complex forms, as it is easy for an inexperienced TP to design an app based around a complex form that later needs to broken up. That team may not learn about these performance limits until late in app development, resulting in a need to re-architect the flows. The end result is a disrupted app-building experience and an increased time to deliver the app.

cc @mrjones-plip 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We should investigate this problem at its source. Could we meaningfully improve the performance of our form experiences through contributions to Enketo?  Is this experience in Enketo slow because it is actually computationally hard, or can Enketo be improved? 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
No idea. Maybe we can use a different library than Enketo? Doesn't seem like a great alternative.

title: Add a native GPS field that can be required in the UI
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently when you want to guarantee that a form has GPS coordinates gathered with it, you only have one option: add a enketo `geopoint` widget and make the input required. This is awkward, at best, because there is no good UI to indicate if the GPS is working and you should wait, let alone if the GPS is disabled and will never work. This is a pressing issue for the Covid MoH Mali (CMoHM) deployment where GPS is mandatory for all forms. The specifics of this issue are being worked on in [config-moh-mali#86 ](https://github.com/medic/config-moh-mali/issues/86).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Allow app builders to have a GPS input in the form be required.  Allow them to give  instructions to CHWs on how to use it.  Make the input be intelligent so that when GPS is off it alerts the user, "You must turn on GPS to proceed" as well as give status updates like "Searching for GPS, please wait" and give the option to show a spinner.  Upon success, allow a message to be shown "GPS coordinates found, you may proceed".  Upon error show a message like "GPS coordinates could not be found. Please try again"

All text should be available for translation and extension (eg they may add "Please move to an area where you can see the sky and try again")

While there are some helpful changes in 3.10, they don't allow you to *require* the field.  Here's the relevant description from 3.10 on GPS features for reference:

>  The app will wait up to 30 seconds to get a location lock before it gives up. If a user tries to submit a form before a location lock is obtained and before 30 seconds are up, the submit action will wait until 30 seconds are up. Also: This change also supports the latest updates in medic-android, where the Location permission is requested at runtime, when editing/creating a report, rather than demanded when starting the app for the first time.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Currently the best work around we can do is to make the `geopoint` field required and then give the error message, "GPS coordinates not found, please ensure GPS is enabled and click the cross hairs to try again". This is awkward b/c GPS may be off and will never work no matter how many times the CHW clicks the cross hairs.

**Additional context**
See  [config-moh-mali#86 ](https://github.com/medic/config-moh-mali/issues/86)
**NB** - If this feature is tied to an upgrade to [medic-android](https://github.com/medic/medic-android/) >0.4.39 (currently deployed [version](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.medicmobile.webapp.mobile.covid_moh_mali)) there is very little rush.  The reason is that any medic-android upgrade for CMoHM involves all 600+ CHW's returning their phones to a central location for upgrade.  So, the only reason to consider rushing this feature would be if it can be done independent of medic-android and done entirely in cht-core and subsequently the [CMoHM app](https://github.com/medic/config-moh-mali/).

title: Improve translations workflow to be more open but without losing accountability
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**

Today the translations workflow using POEditor.com is not as open as the CHT source code, I want a more open workflow to allow more people (everybody) be able to translate the CHT, in an accountable manner.

Current workflow: https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/overview/translations/

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

Currently the CHT source code is publicly available at Github, and everybody can propose changes but without modify the original source code, creating a fork and then a PR with the changes. Despite the same workflow can be used to translate the app editing the files [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/ddocs/medic/_attachments/translations), pull requests may not be suitable for non-developers audience, that's way we use POEditor.com.

I sent a question/suggestion to POEditor [here](https://poeditor.uservoice.com/forums/171919-general/suggestions/41509804--pull-requests-like-contributions?tracking_code=f696782b17bfce7a7c6d9cc2ccd8afb5), quote:

> _is it possible to implement a workflow similar to "pull requests" like the ones in Github? what I mean is: we want to let anybody to contribute with our projects, but when a contributor edits an entry, it would not change the original translation but create a "draft", a "proposal", that needs to be approved before saved._

The response (in the same thread) from the POEditor team is:

> _Perhaps adding an extra proofreading step to your workflow could help: https://poeditor.com/kb/proofreading-translations. Instead of exporting all translations to GitHub, you could add export filters on your links with GitHub files, so that only the proofread strings are exported. You can find more info on how to set export filters in the section ‘Importing and exporting string’ of this article: https://poeditor.com/kb/localization-file-management-with-github-bitbucket-and-gitlab-integrations._

But I don't think it would be a good solution, so I don't have a clear proposal now, but I wanted to create the ticket to leave open the discussion here.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

As mentioned above, we can use just Github pull requests, the user don't need an editor and git installed because the Github webapp allows to change the source code of any file clicking a button, with a web editor provided by Github. If we document how to do that it may work, the major problem is that .properties files despite are simple also have specific rules, like white spaces in keys needs to be escaped with `\`, same for line returns and some special characters. Also POEditor.com provide a more appealing interface for non developers users.

**Additional context**

Despite POeditor.com is open in the sense that we can add anybody to our projects to contribute, the need to add the user to the POEditor project first as a user within the organization to just change a few translations adds friction that may discourage people to contribute, while in Github anybody without invitation can do it. Also once a new contributor edit translations, we lost track of what was the original translation the contributor have edited (accountability), although we still have the original translations in Github, there is no automated way to rollback what the contributor edited in POEditor that we don't liked, that is because I would like contributions to be drafted instead of saved overwriting the original one, like pull requests.

title: Handle training app cut over to production app better
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
CHWs are often trained on one app which uses a test cht-core instance and then expected to use another app for live data entry on the production cht-core instance.  This can result in confusion as to which app to use, [most recently 50 CHWs entered 1800 documents in a test instance](https://github.com/medic/config-moh-mali/issues/98) that all should have been in the live instance.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
cht-core should offer a way to explicitly allow for CHW training in a way that both allows using the app that's as close to production as possible while still offering an explicit, and not confusing way to stop using the test instance on the go live data. This might include, but should not be limited to:
* a "test server" setting such that the app and web UI are very clearly branded "THIS IS A TEST INSTANCE", possibly adding a "DO NOT USE AFTER {{SPECIFIC_DATE}}" 
* Offer a routing option that before the go live date, all traffic is pushed to the test server.  After the go live data, with out any changes on the CHW's device, traffic is transparently pushed to the production server (this presents some issues on sessions and users persisting between the two back ends of course)
* Having the test app cease to function after the go live date, even if the CHW is offline
* Have automatic reminders in the test app to not use it after a certain date
* Allow a test app to push it's data to a different server when it's been discovered it's been used to gather live data.
* Alert administrators when CHWs are uploading docs to a test instance after a certain date

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Some solutions we've thought about:
* change all passwords for CHWs on a specific go live date
* installing the [generic app for testing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.medicmobile.webapp.mobile&hl=en_US), then telling CHW to use [the real app](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.medicmobile.webapp.mobile.covid_moh_mali) on a certain date
* manually migrating data, after it's been synced, from the test server -> production server

**Additional context**
A big problem we've faced is accounting for the offline first nature of cht-core.  That is, if a CHW is one of 50 CHWs entering data into the wrong system, preemptively changing their password _before_ they sync up to the server, means data is lost.  Data loss should be avoided at all costs.


FYI - @kennsippell , @binokaryg , @Marina-Kenf , @abbyad & @garethbowen

title: Creating user feedback loops
body:
Problem statement:
As we are no longer conducting design and user research in person, we should consider alternative ways to collect user feedback on initiatives, features and improvements etc. We should explore recurring vs adhoc feedback cycles as part of the product process.

User stories:
- As a PO/PD I want to gather user feedback on new or updated features so I can facilitate rapid iterations
- As a PO/PD I want to regularly monitor user sentiments so I can seek ways to improve the CHT
- As a PO/PD I want to target specific cohorts so I can receive more focused / relevant feedback
- As a backlog curator I want to discover user pain points in order to prioritize issues or initiatives
- As an organization we want to follow up with users who have given feedback so we can foster a greater sense of community and collaboration

Open questions:
- What kind of feedback are we looking for? (ex. sentiments, workflow specific, UI feedback etc)
- Who might these types of surveys target (personas)?

Speaking with a few folks across the org, a few suggestions have been:
- Sending out surveys to end users via forms in the app (cc @kennsippell )
- Using RapidPro for SMS instances (cc @michaelkohn )
- Whatsapp focus groups
- As a CHT feature to opt into (@benkags )

Design requirements:
TK

Sample survey content:
- [Onboarding](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1yutW4Wcpnbhmdq5zbJAz-z6BTwzbsstMFzxncXqBc-A/edit) (to inform https://github.com/medic/cht-roadmap/issues/32)

title: Variable static target goals.
body:
### TL;DR Part of #4771 which is summarized as: > #### The problem > Lack of flexibility in setting variable targets for CHWs based on varying factors like catchment area size, rural vs urban settings and other data available in the app. > #### Why is it important? > Partners would like to set different target goals for different CHWs, groups of CHWs, supervisory areas and branches that are realistic for CHWs operating in the different contexts. This is currently not possible. For this ticket, the proposal is to focus on, **varying _static_ target goals** for community health workers as informed by demographic, population differences as well as data points associated with the community health workers and their population ### User Stories 1. As a program manager, with a deployment spanning several branches, I would like to configure different target goals for the CHWs in the different branches so that they are working towards a realistic goal as informed by branch context. 2. As a program manager, I would like to give each individual CHW a different target goal specific to them as informed by an analysis of the CHW area population data captured in the app so that they can focus care on the right interventions or population sub groups. 3. As a community health worker, I want my target goal to be reflective of my context so that I am able to effectively deliver care to my community members. 4. As a supervisor, I want to tell in a snapshot, how my community health workers are performing against their target goals so that I know where to offer support as needed. 5. As a supervisor, I would like to drill down to the details of how my community health workers are performing against their set target goals so that I can offer required support where necessary. 6. As a program manager, I would like to set different target goals for different groups of community health workers under different supervisors so that those community health workers, with the help of supervisors, are working towards realistic goals. ### Mockups ![variable-targets-percentages](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3006199/96431591-68144b00-120c-11eb-9510-37bca1b158de.png) ![variable-targets-numbers](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3006199/96431593-69de0e80-120c-11eb-8a36-80714d7f7cf9.png) ### Acceptance Criteria 1. Variable targets should integrate well with the targets status quo:- - Hardcoded static target goals should continue working for targets that are not set up as variable targets. - Variable targets should work with both count and percentage targets. - Variable targets should integrate well with monthly vs all time targets options. - Just like it is in with the product right now, the target goal updates when an update is explicitly made either via config or otherwise and takes effect on the user’s phone when they sync, immediately. - The visuals of the target for a user looking at their target does not change with this feature. - The supervisor's aggregate target view should indicate the various target goals for the different CHWs under them and accordingly update the completion indication displayed for each target correctly. 2. The target goal should be available on disk for analysis. In addition, add an indication of whether a target is variable or not in the data saved. 3. Information on when the target goal took effect(i.e when it was updated to a new value) should be available in data, including a way to tell what the value was before the update. In other words, if an update is made to the target goal, the same should reflect in the document saved on disk including the timestamps when that happened. This should work well with both monthly and all-time targets. 4. If a target changes from a static to variable target, it should be possible to tell that from the data saved on disk. 5. The interface for setting a variable target should be fairly easy to interact with and scalable for the different combinations of user setups that are likely. For guidance, here are some examples: - It should be possible to specify a variable target at an individual level. For example, an isolated CHW X gets a target goal that is different from everyone else. - Extending (a) above, it would be possible to specify a target goal value for a number of users. - Ability to group users to get a specific target goal by a hierarchy level, factoring in a configurable hierarchy. For example, users under Branch X get a target goal of YY while the rest of the users get a target goal of ZZ. 6. Variable targets should be distinguishable as having goals and are not to be mixed up with targets without a goal such that it should not be possible to specify the same target as both having a goal for a subsection of users and not having a goal for another group of users. ### User Acceptance Scenarios #### Scenario 1 There are some projects that we know have implemented this by duplicating target object configurations. Re-implement those in a neat and scalable way using this feature. Expected result: One clean target config object that serves the different target goals for the different branches. #### Scenario 2 A hypothetical organization has the following hierarchy set up: ‘branch -> CHW area -> household’. Supervisors are created at the branch level. For purposes for scenarios below, the supervisor and supervisor naming has a ‘branch-role-number’ pattern e.g A-supervisor-1, B-CHW-1. `assessment` and `assessment-follow-up` are among the forms configured. The following is the requirements spec for this organization that we will validate with the scenarios later. _Some specific branches and CHWs are marked for specific target goals. In some situations, the criteria are a little more generic and the program manager will provide criteria to the app builder as we will see below._ For purposes of the scenarios below, below is a set of requirements for the hypothetical organization above. > The organization tracks assessments conducted(count of assessment) for all CHWs. CHWs in Branch D for the same(count of assessments) do not get a goal. assessment follow-up rate(count of assessment-follow-up / count of assessment) has not been rolled to all branches and currently, only CHWs in Branch B is seeing this target with an exception of one CHW in Branch A. Malaria assessment is included in the assessment workflow for branches marked as malaria endemic. A branch or community health unit is marked as malaria endemic using a flag in the place. Branch C among others is marked as malaria endemic i.e {name: Branch C, malaria_endemic: true}. CHWs issue malaria nets(LLIN) for during the assessment workflow in malaria-endemic areas and the number of LLINs issued tracked using the LLINs issued percentage(count of assessment where malaria_net_issued=yes / count of assessment). > Configure the following: > - A global target goal of 2 for assessments conducted should be configured for all CHWs in the organization. > - A-CHW-1, A-CHW-2, and B-CHW-1 are new health workers and they all get an assessment count goal of 4 to encourage them to visit all the households in their catchment area. > - All CHWs in Branch B should have an assessment follow up rate goal of 80%. No other branch is tracking this target. The one exception is CHW A-CHW-4 in Branch A who has a target goal of 50%. > - Give a target goal of 60% for LLINs issued percentage to CHWs in all branches marked as ‘malaria_endemic=true including those that are added in the future’. > See a tabular representation below for more clarity. ##### Desired Scenarios > Target Title | Calculation | Criteria | Goal > -- | -- | -- | -- > Assessments Conducted | Count of Assessments | Default (Every CHW in every branch unless explicitly configured differently) | 2 >   | Count of Assessments | 3 specific CHWs in Branch A (A-CHW-1, A-CHW-2 and B-CHW-1) | 4 >   | Count of Assessments | CHWs in Branch D | No goal > Assessment Follow up rate | count of assessment follow-up / count of assessment | All CHWs in Branch B | 80% >   | count of assessment follow-up / count of assessment | A specific CHW in Branch A (A-CHW-4) | 50% > LLINs issued percentage | count of assessment where malaria_net_issued=yes / count of assessment | All CHWs in Branches where “malaria_endemic = true” (a metadata field stored on the place record) | 60% ##### Setup > Branch | malaria_endemic > -- | -- > A | false > B |   > C | true > D | no ##### Expected Targets Configuration Output > > > > > > > > >   > > > >   > >
Branch CHW Assessments ConductedAssessment Follow-up Rate LLINs issued percentage
VisibleGoalVisibleGoalVisibleGoal
A A-CHW-1 Yes 4 No No  
A A-CHW-2 Yes 4 No   No  
A A-CHW-3 Yes 2 No   No  
A A-CHW-4 Yes 2 Yes 50 No  
B B-CHW-1 Yes 4 Yes 80 No  
B B-CHW-2 Yes 2 Yes 80 No  
B B-CHW-3 Yes 2 Yes 80 No  
C C-CHW-1 Yes 2 No   Yes 60
C C-CHW-2 Yes 2 No   Yes 60
D D-CHW-1 Yes 2 No   No
D D-CHW-2 Yes 2 No   No  
a. Log in as A-CHW-1 - Fill in reports: 1 assessment - Expected result: Go to targets page and observe: - Can only see _assessments conducted_ target - _assessments conducted_ reads 1 and goal: 4 and color coded red b. Log in as A-CHW-3 - Fill in reports: 3 assessment - Expected result: - Can only see _assessments conducted_ target. - _assessments conducted_ reads 3 and goal: 2 and color coded green c. Log in as A-CHW-4 - Fill in reports: 1 assessment - Expected result: - Can see both _assessments conducted_ and _assessment follow up rate_ targets - _assessments conducted_ reads 1, goal 2 and color coded red - _assessment follow up rate_ reads 0%, goal 50% and color coded red d. Log in as B-CHW-1 - Fill in reports: 3 assessment, 1 assessment-follow-up - Expected result: - Can see both _assessments conducted_ and _assessment follow up rate_ targets - _assessment conducted_ reads 3, goal 4 and color coded red - _assessment follow up rate_ reads 30%, goal 80% and color coded red e. Log in as B-CHW-2 - Fill in reports: none - Expected results: - Can see both _assessments conducted_ and _assessment follow up rate_ targets. - _assessments conducted_ reads 0, goal 2 and color coded red - _assessment follow up_ reads 0%, goal: 80% and color coded red f. Log in as B-CHW-3 - Fill in reports: 2 assessment, 2 assessment-follow-up - Expected results: - Can see both _assessments conducted_ and _assessment follow up rate_ targets - _assessments conducted_ reads 2, goal 2 color coded green - _assessment follow up rate_ reads 100%, goal 80% and color coded green g. Log in as C-CHW-1 - Fill in reports: 1 assessment(malaria_net_issued=yes), 1 assessment(malaria_net_issued=no) - Expected results: - Can see _assessment conducted_ and LLINs issued percentage targets. - _assessments conducted_ reads 2, goal 2 and color coded green - _LLINs issued percentage_ reads 50%, goal: 60% and color coded red h. Log in as A-Supervisor-1(supervisor attached to Branch A) - Expected results: - See only the following list aggregate targets in the LFS: _assessments conducted, assessment follow up rate_ - _assessments conducted_ drill down should read: - A-CHW-1(1 of 4, color: red) - A-CHW-2(0 of 4, color: red) - A-CHW-3(2 of 2, color: green) - A-CHW-4(1 of 2, color: red) - D-CHW-1(0) - D-CHW-2(0) - _assessment follow up rate_ drill down should have the following: - A-CHW-4(0% of 50%, color: red) i. Log in as C-Supervisor-1 - Expected results: - See the following list aggregate targets only in the LFS: _assessments conducted, LLINs issued percentage_ - _assessments conducted_ drill down should read: - C-CHW-1(2 of 2, color: green) - _LLINs issued percentage_ drill down should read: - C-CHW-1(50% of 60%, color: red) ### Feature Update Metrics 1. What proportion of all targets are variable? 2. What is the frequency of updating variable targets? 3. How different were the goals? Distribution?? 4. How do variable vs static targets compare with regards to meeting the target? 5. How varying are the variable targets across the CHWs, branches et al? 6. What proportion of users are using variable targets?

title: Allow more granular synchronizing/purging of hierarchical documents

title: Server-side target generation for SMS projects
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
cht-core has, since v3.8, had the ability to generate target documents and store them on disk. This has brought with it numerous advantages including using the same subsystem to help with DHIS2 metric aggregation.  However, one downside still remains with this approach, it is reliant on users accessing the webapp (either and pc or phone) and this making it unsuitable for SMS deployments.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We have SMS projects going for national scale - e.g EBS in Kenya. One key requirement that the government is pushing data to the national DHIS2 to help with analysis and reporting. The government and stakeholders are currently in the process of defining what data needs to be captured at DHIS2 and Medic has been brought to the table to help with that.

The improvement being sought is developing the ability to do target document generation server-side so that this feature works in purely SMS deployments.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Replicating the target logic in SQL to generate CSVs that could be imported into DHIS2. However, this replication is what go us to build the target doc generation feature.

**Additional context**
Having this will be critical for increasing SMS project adoption by governments
