title: Developer mode gives app builders transparency into how their tasks and targets behave
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
App builders can sometimes struggle to debug and diagnose the behaviour of tasks, targets, contact summaries, and form properties. For example, 

1. Today I worked with an app builder who was trying to debug an issue with a context in a form property and didn't understand the data that was being passed.
1. Today I worked with a set of app builders who were debugging the behaviour of a target that wasn't counting the reports they were expected. It turned out that the target didn't have the right idType, so it was de-duplicating. The investigation lasted about 14 days and involved 5 app builders to understand the behaviour of the target.
1. When a task disappears from the UI, was it completed/canceled/failed

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We need some way of bringing greater transparency into:
1. what instances are actually being counted by the target
1. what data is being passed into form properties
1. what task documents are being created by a specific task configuration? what are the states these task documents are in?

**Additional context**
https://medic.slack.com/archives/CEQTMKFT8/p1602496931025000

title: Clicking on the Android back button while creating a new report minifies the app and generates feedback doc
For targets without `idType`, the winning emission is not deterministic
body:
**Describe the bug**
https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/targets/#targetsjs

Targets will, by default, count a single emission per contact, even if they "apply to" reports. The only way to get a target to count multiple reports per contact is to set its `idType` to `report`. This is not the scope of this issue, though. 
When there are multiple emissions for one contact for one target (multiple reports that match the `appliesIf` and `passesIf` for a single contact), the winning emission (whose reported_date will determine which reporting interval the "contact" gets counted towards the target goal) is not deterministic. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Create a simple target that counts reports, this is an example, but you can use any form you desire:
```
{
  id: 'target_forma',
  translation_key: 'target',
  subtitle_translation_key: 'target',
  type: 'count',
  icon: 'no-icon',
  goal: 16,
  appliesTo: 'reports',
  appliesToType: ['forma'],
  appliesIf: function () {
    return true;
  },
  date: 'reported'
}
```
2. Create a bunch of reports that will match this target, all reports about the same patient. 
It's helpful to generate these in a CSV and upload them with medic-conf because you're going to need to change their reported_date and _id fields. 

Create reports in different reporting periods (different months) and make sure their _id fields are out of sort. When I tested, this was my report list:

| _id | form | reported_date | 
| --- | ---- | ------------- |
| a_report | forma | date in February | 
| b_report | forma | date in January | 
| c_report | forma | date in June | 
| d_report | forma | date in April | 
| e_report | forma | date in May | 

So I'm making a very clear alphabetically sorted list of _id with a completely scrambled list of reported_dates. 

3. Login as an offline user that would sync all these reports. Go to the targets page. 
Check if you get a count on your target.
4. Change your OS clock to be in June (`c_report` is the "latest" of its type, so theoretically it should be the one to generate the winning emission). 
Check your targets page and see that you don't have a target count. 
5. Change your OS clock to be in January (`a_report` is the "first" of it's type, so if the first chronological report is selected, this should be the one to generate the winning emission). 
Check your targets page and see that you don't have a target count. 
6. Change your OS clock to Feb / April and see that you don't have a target count. 
7. Change your OS clock to May and see that you DO have a target count. 

**Expected behavior**
I believe, pre 3.8 the last chronological report was generating the winning emission. 
Pre 3.8, we were using the Search service to get a list of reports:
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/3.7.x/webapp/src/js/services/rules-engine.js#L224
Relevant part of the search service is here: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/3.7.x/shared-libs/search/src/search.js#L33 where we sort the results by view value, which is the reported_date: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/3.7.x/ddocs/medic-client/views/reports_by_validity/map.js#L3

Post 3.8 we just query the `reports_by_subject` here https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/rules-engine/src/pouchdb-provider.js#L34 and never sort the results. 
CouchDB/PouchDB view queries will return rows sorted by the emitted key, and if the key is the same, sorted by _id. The emitted value - which is the reported_date in this case - is not taken into account. 
https://docs.couchdb.org/en/stable/api/ddoc/views.html?highlight=view#api-ddoc-view-sorting

**Environment**
- Instance: any 3.8+
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.8+

**Additional context**
This was reported as a regression by a partner after an upgrade to 3.9.1. 
Not sure about labeling and whether we should consider this production-urgent or not.

title: Form submissions hang in desktop browsers when location permission requests are ignored by users
body: **Describe the bug** In certain conditions, the CHT on version 3.10 fails to defend ~~against missing translation~~ location permissions being ignored. When a form is submitted in this scenario, the data is not written to PouchDB, the form controls are disabled (cancel, prev & submit) and a spinner is shown. **To Reproduce** This was recreated in docker but should affect any CHT hosting environment. The docker set up and Covid MoH Mali (CMoHM) app steps are listed here for completeness, but it's assumed we can isolate the behavior of the app. This assumes you have `node`, `npm`, `docker` and `medic-conf` installed: 1. Download [this](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/362-docs-update-docker-compose-to-3.9.0-rc.2/docker-compose.yml) `docker-compose.yml` - the one with medic-os `image: medicmobile/medic-os:cht-3.9.0-rc.2` and haproxy `image: medicmobile/haproxy:rc-1.17`. 1. Ensure you don't have a persistent docker volume that already has data in it by deleting the containers that use it, and then the volume itself: `docker rm medic-os haproxy` and then `docker volume rm medic-data`. 1. launch the two containers with `docker-compose up` . you now have a 3.9 CHT instance on htps://127.0.0.1 1. clone out the [CMoHM](https://github.com/medic/config-moh-mali/) repo (private) and `cd` into the config dir: `cd config-moh-mali/covid-surveillance/`. After you clone out the repo, be sure to switch to `b8e6c4a` branch in case the app config changed: `git checkout b8e6c4a` 1. In your browser Log in as `medic/password` on your local instance htps://127.0.0.1 1. go to htps://127.0.0.1/admin/#/upgrade and "Install" version 3.10.0 1. Back in the CLI, run `medic-conf` to install the CMoHM app: `medic-conf --url=https://medic:password@localhost --accept-self-signed-certs` 1. In your browser, click on 'people' icon on the top 1. click on "new district" on the bottom left 1. under "set the primary contact" choose "create a new person" 1. ensure their age is over 20, sex to femail and role to asc-s 1. accept all defaults on the next page and click "submit" 1. in the upper right click the hamburger menu and click "app management" 1. click the "Users" option, and click "Add user" at the top 1. enter a username you'll remember, for "role" choose "ASC-S", choose the place and associated contact you just created. Enter a password you'll remember and click "Add user" 1. log out as the admin user or open an incognito tab. Log in as the user you just created 1. click on the "Reports" icon at the very top, and then click "submit report" on the lower left, and click the "Formulaire..." pop up 1. For "User" accept the defaults and choose "Next" 1. For 1st "Village" choose "Autre", for 2nd "Village" enter any value 1. click anywhere on the map to choose a location and click "Next" 1. for "select what applies" choose "I am not currently in the household." 1. Choose "Next" 1. On the "Evaluation" page for "obtained the consent" choose "yes" and "next" 1. On the "Household information" page 1. enter any value for chief 1. enter "71234567" for phone 1. for "hand washing" choose "yes" 1. for how many people put 1 1. for children and all other values on the page put "0" 1. for "anyone in the household sick" put "no" 1. choose "Next" 1. On "Formulaire Evaluation" choose "Next" 1. On the final "Formulaire Evaluation" choose "submit" **Expected behavior** Ideally we defend against this and ensure the data is saved. As well, it'd be nice if we fall back to a default translation to show a message as needed about the transaction succeeding. In a worst case scenario, we should alert the user the data was not saved and they should try again. **Logs** Frustratingly, there are no logs in the browser console when the actual form is submitted :( There are prior errors that show up about missing translations (which turned out to be unreleated), as seen in the screenshots below. **Screenshots** [](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8253488/98174967-9059a600-1eaa-11eb-9536-4886cba9e539.png) **Environment** - Instance: local dev instance - Browser: Firefox & Chrome both latest - Client platform: Linux Ubuntu 20 and 18 - App: webapp - Version: 3.10 **Additional context** Note that this works as expected in 3.9, and then breaks in 3.10. This strongly suggests it's a regression in 3.10. If you follow the above steps, but do not upgrade to 3.9, the bug is not encountered. ~~In 3.10 you can fix the bug by uploading the missing translations by being in the `config-moh-mali/covid-surveillance` directory in CMoHM repo and running `medic-conf --url=https://medic:password@localhost upload-app-settings upload-app-forms upload-resources upload-custom-translations --accept-self-signed-certs`~~ This turned out to be wrong and I very likely choose to allow location permission. See below for [specific workarounds](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6711#issuecomment-722241502).

title: Adds translations compiler to support pluralization
body:
# Description

We used to rely on messageformat to provide pluralization. The AngularJS translator allowed you to control how you could interpolate a translation, but ngx-translate does not. 
It does, however, allow you to overwrite the default compiler and use that as the middle man between it and messageformat. 

I found a library that passed **all** translations through messageformat (https://www.npmjs.com/package/ngx-translate-messageformat-compiler) which is bad for use, because of all the caveats. for example, messageformat encloses params in single curly braces, versus double curly braces that we use. 

So I quickly created our own compiler that does a really stupid filter (only passes translations to messageformat if they use single curly braces!) and mostly rushed it to unblock @njogz with display last visited dates in contacts lists. I did add a TODO to investigate whether there are better options.

Enketo ships with a geo picker widget which uses the browser's geolocation service. The webapp also collects geolocation data for every form submitted using our geolocation angular service. title: Default config delivery form saves incorrect baby uuid
body:
**Describe the bug**
When submitting a `delivery` form part of the default config (https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/config/default/forms/app/delivery.xml) and you select to enter multiple babies (either alive or not), the report will have as many entries for every repeat type, but the uuids of each repeat saved in the report will be the same:

For example:

if you add 3 baby deaths, 3 distinct contact docs will be created, but the report doc fields
`report.delivery.baby_death.baby_death_repeat.0.baby_death_profile_doc`
`report.delivery.baby_death.baby_death_repeat.1.baby_death_profile_doc`, 
`report.delivery.baby_death.baby_death_repeat.2.baby_death_profile_doc` will all have the same value. 

If you add 3 babies that are alive, 3 distinct contact docs will be created, but the report doc fields
`report.delivery.babys_condition.baby_repeat.0.baby_details.child_doc`,
`report.delivery.babys_condition.baby_repeat.1.baby_details.child_doc`,
`report.delivery.babys_condition.baby_repeat.2.baby_details.child_doc` will all  have the same value. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Upload the `delivery` form from `default` config.
2. Fill a delivery report, selecting 6 child births, 3 alive, 3 dead. 
4. Save and load the report. Check the above listed fields.

**Expected behavior**
Each repeat should save the uuid of the generated contact doc. 

**Environment**
- Instance: gamma.dev.medicmobile.org (example report https://gamma.dev.medicmobile.org/#/reports/8fc63ed4-277f-4ea9-8e04-22ee614a5420)
- App: webapp

title: Webapp navigates from report list to detail after navigating back on slow devices
body:
**Describe the bug**
On mobile views, users may be redirected back to the report detail page, without user action, if they verify a report and then immediately go back to the list. This also happens when the user hits back while the report is still loading. 
This only happens on slow networks or devices with low performance.

**To Reproduce with verification**
1. Login with a user that can verify reports on a slow device or throttle your desktop browser's performance OR network (or both for overkill). If using a desktop browser, adjust window size to have a mobile view. 
2. Go to reports and open a report. Verify this report (which verification, correct or with errors is irrelevant). 
3. Very quickly, after the report was verified, click the back button up top to return to the list. 
4. Wait a few seconds (this depends on your device and your network).
5. Get redirected back to the report detail without performing any action. 

**To Reproduce without verification**
1. Same as above.
2. Open a report. While seeing the spinner in the detail page, click on the back button up top to return to the list.
3. Wait a few seconds.
4. Get redirected back to the report detail page and see the report or an empty page (like no report is selected).  

**Expected behavior**
Users should be redirected back to the report detail page after quickly navigating back to the list. 

**Environment**
- Instance: gamma.dev
- Browser: Chrome
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.10 and earlier

**Additional context**
This is either a very old bug (pre 3.0) or was caused by the Redux refactor.

title: Improve how Muting is handled on device before syncs
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The [muting feature](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/transitions/#muting) as it works right now requires Sentinel Transitions to update the relevant contact docs following a muting form submitted by the CHW. Because of very slow/unstable connectivity in the field, we notice some weird situations that arise from it. The most frequent one is that the muting form don't get synced for days/weeks, in the mean time the household or place and its descendants remain active and users sometimes continue to submit forms. 
A part from the form submissions, from a UX perspective it is not ideal if the contact is not muted immediately, the users sometimes submit extra muting forms as they don't understand what's happening. Some of our UX features like UHC are affected as well. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We would want ideally a muting feature that can work fully offline and that would be immediately effective after it was triggered. 
Another solution that would only prevent the form submissions after the muting, could be a improvement in configuration that would make it possible to check if the last form submitted for any of the parents of a contact or the contact itself is a muting form. we could add that check to the form properties to prevent it from being submitted in those cases ( this might be already possible and i'm just not aware of that ).

**Additional context**
We have noticed this issue for our partner MUSO, where CHWs continue to submit forms for a place/contact supposed to be muted, this make it confusing and difficult specially from a data analysis perspective, the reasons why those submissions are being done is unclear, is it a mistake ? Was the family not supposed to be muted in the first place ? Would the CHW had unmuted the family first before submitting the visit if the family was muted in time ? Are the chws submitting visits forms without actually visiting the family to not be penalized by the UHC scoring ? 

initial ticket : https://github.com/medic/config-muso/issues/44

I can create the `app.component.spec.ts` and add at least some tests related with the expiration of the session, so later others can add more tests related with the main component, but I'm wondering why we don't have tests from this core peace of the app, is because it has a lot of injected components and it is a nightmare to maintain it later?
- Another approach would be create a a service `SessionExpiredService` and refactor the AppComponent to move the code there, and then the AppComponent only updates a redux variable that the service is subscribed to, or something else, but there is no much to move and we should avoid refactors of things that are working fine, plus possible performance penalties of increase the use of shared states with redux.

title: Support official CHT icons in form headers
body: **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** Currently our docs specify that you should use [cht icons](https://github.com/medic/icon-library) in your form header icons (see [this docs](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/design/best-practices/#page-sections) -> "header icons"). However, when you look at our forms, we always use Font Awesome(FA) (specifically [FA 4.7](https://fontawesome.com/v4.7.0/icons/)). For examples, see any of the `.xlsx` files in our [default app](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/config/default). In these, you will see only instances of `TITLE HERE `. There is no way to easily include our native icons. **Describe the solution you'd like** We should allow the easy including of our CHT icons in these headers. This will allow us to not only stop using FA, but to also for us to stay on design and brand. **Describe alternatives you've considered** Putting the entire SVG XML or a BASE64 encoding of the PNG inline. **Additional context** We should be sure to include icons in the CHT core itself in a web accessible directly similar to how [we deploy FA currently](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/2c74a6e25428f18c7f41bd80880cbe789953f6a9/webapp/src/css/inbox.less#L3). This will allows to have self contained use of our icons with no external web site dependencies and also easy offline use. Further, allowing for easy including of icons which adhere to our style guides would be great: float right , solid white color, transparent background.

title: More accurately represent sex and gender in the default reference app
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently in our default reference app we ship with CHT core (see [`config/default`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/config/default)), we only capture `sex` as a binary field.  This is an antiquated and biased schema that we should extend to encompass current medical best practices which recognize that `sex` is not binary.  Further, we should audit that `gender` is discrete from `sex` and is also not binary.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
The specific improvements should be researched.  One solution would be to change `sex` to have `select-one` values of `male`, `female`, `intersex`. A more generic version might be  `male`, `female`, `other`. For both `gender` and `sex` values, we may review HL7's Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) documents.  Specifically their ["Patient Gender and Sex"](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/patient.html#gender) document, including their nomenclature on [gender identity](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/valueset-gender-identity.html) and [sex assigned at birth](https://loinc.org/76689-9/).

WHO also has [published related material](https://www.who.int/teams/gender-equity-and-human-rights) on their site as well.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Do nothing and leaving this up to partners to change upon implementation.

**Additional context**
There was some [healthy discussion on Slack](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C024ZK678/p1607750293180800) (private link) which was this ticket's inception and gives some background and internal champions including @garethbowen, @ecsalomon , @helizabetholsen , @marialma .

We may opt to couple this effort with the current effort of authoring the [MNCH reference app](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6727) which will live in `config/default`.

FYI @isaacholeman , @katanu , @rmugwanya and @michaelkohn

title: Support additional reporting periods: DHIS2 & Supervisor Targets
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
v3.9 introduced DHIS2 integration capabilities based off of Targets docs.  A [known limitation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/integrations/dhis2-aggregate/#known-limitations) was that it only supported dataSets that are submitted to DHIS2 monthly. We have a project that needs to support a DHIS2 dataSet that is submitted quarterly.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
At a minimum, support quarterly reporting periods. [Here](https://docs.dhis2.org/en/develop/developing-with-the-android-sdk/workflow.html#android_sdk_aggregated_data) is the list of reporting periods that can be configured in DHIS2 for aggregate reports, so technically all of these will be fair game at some point.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Using a [custom function](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/targets/#targetsjs) for the `date` property on target docs.

**Additional context**
The specific DHIS2 data set that needs to be implemented is the 097b in Uganda. Another consideration we should review is countries like Mali and Togo where often reports are run monthly, but not starting on the first of the Gregorian calendar (for example: August = 28-July to 27-August).

NOTE: Additional design work needs to be done, but wanted to get this on the radar.

**Why Now?**
Partner(s): Kiwi Apple
Reason(s): A partner will be blocked by this for a major release or expansion

title: Targets with property "passesIfGroupCount.gte" count intances with "pass: false" when aggregating
body:
**Describe the bug**
The `passesIfGroupCount.gte` was written to support Muso's target for "% of families with 2 household visits/month" https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5493. The result is a [muso target](https://github.com/medic/config-muso/blob/master/targets.js#L73) which emits instances with `pass: true` for instances that should be counted (home visits) and `pass: false` for instances which should not be counted (families). The `pass: false` instances are essential for ensuring a correctly counted denominator - counting families with no reports and no home visits.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Deploy Muso configuration
2. Create three new families A, B, C
3. For Family A - complete one household visit in current month
4. For Family B - complete no household visits in current month
5. For Family C - complete two household visits on different days in current month

**Expected behavior**
1 of 3 families have recieved 2 household visits this month

**Observed behaviour**
1 of 2 families (incorrect denominator, task does not count families with zero reports)

or (if you remove the comments)
2 of 3 families (task counts denominator correctly, but requires only 1 family visit in the month to be counted)

**Context**
You can work around this for Muso's case using `gte: 3` - assuming there is one and exactly one additional instance per family.

**Environment**
- Instance: muso-mali.app
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.8 - 3.10

body: **Describe the issue** When app developers are building forms, they fill the forms out a lot. Likely dozens, if not hundreds of times. To do this quickly, they often fill out the form via the keyboard (tab + up key fills out a series of radio boxes quickly) as using the mouse slows them down. However, we put the browser focus 10 tab key presses away from the first form element, necessitating use of the mouse to put the focus on the first input. Here's a form for reference: [](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8253488/103833623-49b53300-5036-11eb-9127-5a66e2e8c208.png) **Describe the improvement you'd like** Add a mechanism to put the focus on the first input of a form when the page loads to expedite testing. Something like `autofocus` [attribute](https://www.w3schools.com/TAGS/att_input_autofocus.asp) might work. **Describe alternatives you've considered** 10x more tab key presses ;)

title: Race condition in rules engine / task list interaction can result in a stale tasks list
body:
**Describe the bug**
Because of a race condition that can exist between rules engine and the task controller, the user could end up seeing a stale and incorrect task list.
The reproduction steps I'm about to provide (when a completed task does not disappear from the list) may not be the only situation when this race condition can be triggered. 


**To Reproduce**
1. Push default config (form and tasks). 
2. Login as an offline user with a considerable amount of docs on a slow device. I had 2000 docs (out of which 50 were "current tasks" - that I saw in my task list) and was using a Tecno Y4 (device performance is essential to reproduce the behavior). 
3. Submit a "pregnancy danger sign" form for a contact. This will create a task that will be visible immediately at the bottom of your task list. 
4. Complete this task, by selecting that the patient is not showing danger signs any more. Submit.
5. Observe that the task still exists in the task list, and is not disappearing even after many seconds. 

**Expected behavior**
The completed task should disappear from the task list after a few seconds (though we have no indication that we're actually "reloading" or expecting the task list to be updated). 

**Logs**
There are no relevant logs. 

**Environment**
- App: Webapp
- Browser: Chrome
- Version: reproduced on 3.10, but I suspect 3.9 and 3.8 are also affected.

**Additional context**
The race condition is caused by two distinct events that are in a race, both affecting what the user sees on the screen:
1. RulesEngineService listens to changes and, when it receives a contact/report change, it calls the shared library endpoint that updates the emissions for the affected contacts:
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/js/services/rules-engine.js#L146
This is an *async* operation, as the `subject_ids` that we have access to when we receive the change could be shortcodes, that we need to translate to contact uuids. This requires querying the DB before marking the affected contacts as dirty and, consequently, refreshing their emissions during the next calculation cycle. 

2. TasksController also listens to changes and, like the RulesEngineService, reacts to contact/report and task changes: 
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/js/controllers/tasks.js#L104
After waiting for an arbitrary second (the existence of debounce here is not to serve this purpose, but it's what makes this error less obvious by only being triggered in the lowest performing devices), the controller refreshes the tasks list. 

If both entities (the rules engine and the tasks controller) receive the change in the same "tick", but the "marking contacts as dirty" in (1) takes longer than the task controller (2) waits before requesting tasks, the result will be that the reloaded tasks will be stale, because the contact was not dirty at the moment of refreshing.

title: Release 3.10.2
body:
# Planning

- [x] Create an [organisation wide project](https://github.com/orgs/medic/projects?query=is%3Aopen+sort%3Aname-asc) and add this issue to it.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the project.

# Development

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Manager. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR to the release branch. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version patch`.
- [x] Write an update in the weekly Product Team call agenda summarising development and acceptance testing progress and identifying any blockers. The release manager is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` and backported to the release branch release testing can begin.

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing.
- [x] Create a new document in the [release-notes folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/release-notes) in `master`. Ensure all issues are in the GH Project, that they're correct labelled, and have human readable descriptions. Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/changelog-generator) to export the issues into our changelog format. Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
- [x] Until release testing passes, make sure regressions are fixed in `master`, cherry-pick them into the release branch, and release another beta.
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Announce the release in #products using this template:
```
@channel *Announcing the release of {{version}}*

This release fixes {{number of bugs}}. Read the release notes for full details: {{url}}
```
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/), under the "Product - Releases" category. You can use the previous message and omit `@channel`.

title: Update default config to use contact_types that match what is displayed to users
body:
### Problem

There are many inconsistencies in how we refer to or name different hierarchy levels in the default config, default forms, and doc site.

Currently, the hierarchy configuration in the [default config](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/f20cf655da6bf38eea98bb25944619e03cf181ba/config/default/app_settings.json#L289-L344) is:

- `clinic`
- `health_center`
- `district_hospital`

However, these are displayed in the app as

- Household
- Area
- Health Facility

And on the [doc site, for the reference app](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/examples/anc/#forms-hierarchy), as:
- Household
- CHW Area

And in the [generic hierarchy section](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/concepts/hierarchy/#places) as:

- Family
- CHW Area
- Supervisor Area

### Proposal
We should consider updating the contact_types in the default config to be in sync with how users interact with the system. Having different names here is cause for confusion in configuring other areas of the app as well as for analytics. 

### Some background
The reason the contact_types are configured the way they are is due to the legacy way hierarchies were set (they weren't configurable). When the configurable hierarchy feature was added, the default config was updated to use configurable hierarchies, but the names of the contact_types were just copied over from the old config. For mobile app deployments, "households" to the users were stored in the database as "clinics", there was no way around this. Now with configurable hierarchies, it is possible to bring these back into sync and name them the same/more meaningfully.

These files are hardcoded in to the CHT webapp ([here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/3.10.x/webapp/src/js/app.js#L38) and [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/3.10.x/webapp/src/js/enketo/main.js)), and can only be solved by raising an issue ([here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6861) and [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6849)) and releasing a new version of CHT Core. These packages both ship with extensive translation support ([here](https://github.com/moment/moment/tree/develop/locale) and [here](https://github.com/uxsolutions/bootstrap-datepicker/tree/master/js/locales)), but we're only importing a handful of languages we know we need.

We have also had issues in the past with adding a language that these libraries don't support.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Allow app builders to include moment and date-picker (and any other library's) translation files without changes to CHT Core. It should be easy to include the languages maintained by the library developer and possible to provide a completely bespoke file.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
1. Include all translation files. This is very simple, but adds a little bloat and doesn't solve for languages the library doesn't support.
2. Patch the libraries to use our own translation system. This is powerful but likely to be complex and fragile. It also duplicates effort that these libraries already put in to developing their own system and translation values.

title: Improves the overall performance of the app
body:
# Description

Improves the performance of the app by:
1. Updating contacts, reports & tasks lists to render inline templates instead of separate components
2. Switching from ngx-translate directive to ngx-translate pipe (except for situations where we need translate params, where pipes don't accept "inline" objects as params).

8. Refactoring the mobile detection to avoid forced reflows. 
9. Refactoring contacts effect.

Fixes parser logical operator bug where operator precedence was not respected. 
Migrates some telemetry references.

**What feature do you want to improve?**

title: Users might start upwards replication from 0 after upgrade
body:
**Describe the bug**
Due to PouchDB internal algorithms and non-deterministic minification results (either from Uglify-js used pre 3.11 or Terser used post 3.11), users could restart upwards replication from 0 after an upgrade. 


**To Reproduce**
Reproducing is pretty tricky as it involves changing some code in way that will change certain variable names in the minified source. I've been pretty successfull in unwillingly triggering this in the migration branch. I'll add a comment if I find an 100% reliable way, but for now:

1. Generate a production build. 
2. Login as an offline user in a browser. Fully replicate, leave the browser tab open, watching the network. 
3. Make some code changes, but don't touch the filter function. Build again. Hopefully your changes will shuffle variable names in the minified source.
4. Sync with the offline user. Reload. 
5. Watching the network tab, sync. 
6. See `_revs_diff` requests (the batch size is 100, so if your user has 500 docs, you should see 5 `_revs_diff` requests).

**Expected behavior**
Users should not start upwards replication from 0. Seeing one _revs_diff request is normal - and should contain references to the latest docs that the user has downloaded from the server: probably only the service-worker-cache. 

**Environment**
- App: webapp
- Version: since this depends on internal workings of external libraries (PouchDB & Uglify-js/Terser), it's impossible to tell how long this has been going on without inspecting each release's minified JS and see how the filter function looked like. If between two releases there'd be changes (even a single character), then the bug would occur when upgrading.

**Additional context**
PouchDB generates a (hopefully) unique and stable replication ID for each replication, and uses some of the replication config options into compiling it. 
https://github.com/pouchdb/pouchdb/blob/1db1700382604ab0dc3ddb337096d99641ea12d8/packages/node_modules/pouchdb-generate-replication-id/src/index.js#L15
One of the config options that is used to generate a replication id is the provided filter function. PouchDb calls the provided value (be it a function, or a string) `toString` method to get a value to use. 
The result of the `toString` call is not deterministic, because the actual code that runs is minified for production use. 
So, if between two versions, the minified string representation of the filter function changes, even if no changes have been made to the function itself, the newly generated replication ids will be different from the existent and cause a restart in replication. 

Fortunately, upwards replication is relatively cheap, as it involves hitting an unfiltered CouchDB endpoint (`_revs_diff`) with every pair of doc _id + _rev that exists on the user's device. For the overwhelming majority of cases, responses from the server will be empty (because the docs already exist on the server as well).

title: Release 3.12.0
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create a repo milestone and add this issue to it. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [ ] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Manager for this release.
- [ ] Assign product team members to complete end-user documentation improvements for this release.

# Development - Release Manager

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Manager. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`.
- [x] Raise a new issue called `Update dependencies for <version>` with a description that links to [the documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/guides/update-dependencies/). This should be done early in the release cycle so find a volunteer to take this on and assign it to them.
- [x] Go through all features and improvements scheduled for this release and raise cht-docs issues for product education to be written where appropriate. If in doubt, check with the product manager.
- [x] Write an update in the weekly Product Team call agenda summarising development and acceptance testing progress and identifying any blockers. The release manager is to update this every week until the version is released.
- [x] Announce the kickoff of development for the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org), under the "Product - Releases" category.

# Releasing - Release Manager

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` release testing can begin.

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development using this template:
```
@core_devs I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing.
- [x] [Import translations keys](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/overview/translations/#adding-new-keys) into POE and notify the #translations Slack channel translate new and updated values, for example:
```
@channel I've just updated the translations in POE. These keys have been added: "<added-list>", and these keys have been updated: "<updated-list>"
```
- [x] Create a new document in the [release-notes folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/release-notes) in `master`. Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, that they're correctly labelled (in particular: they have the right Type, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate), and have human readable descriptions. Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/index.js) to export the issues into our changelog format. Manually document any known migration steps and known issues. Provide description, screenshots, videos, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: medic-conf,  medic-gateway, medic-android). Assign the PR to a) the Director of Technology, and b) an SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient.
- [x] Until release testing passes, make sure regressions are fixed in `master`, cherry-pick them into the release branch, and release another beta.
- [x] [Export the translations](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/overview/translations/#exporting-changes-from-poeditor-to-github), delete empty translation files and commit to `master`. Cherry-pick the commit into the release branch. 
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Upgrade the `demo-cht.dev` instance to this version.
- [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/overview/supported-software/) and update the EOL date and status of previous releases.

# Communicating - Product Manager

- [ ] Ask the Product Designer to create release artwork
- [ ] Create a DRAFT blog post on medic.org Wordpress site promoting the release using on the release notes and artwork above. Once it's ready ask the Comms Officer to review and publish it.
- [x] Announce the release in #products using this template:
```
@channel *We're excited to announce the release of {{version}}*

New features include {{key_features}}. We've also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

Read the release notes for full details: {{url}}

Following our support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read our software support documentation: https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/overview/supported-software/

See what's scheduled for the next releases: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/milestones
```
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category. You can use the previous message and omit `@channel`.
- [ ] Announce the release of new documentation for features and improvements in the release on the [CHT Forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/documentation/28), under the "Product - Documentation" category.
- [ ] Schedule a Release communication call to educate stakeholders on product and documentation improvements
- [ ] Mark this issue "done" and close the milestone.

title: New users might be prompted to accept the privacy policy twice or shown the tour modal twice
body:
**Describe the bug**
When a new user logs in (one that is not "known") on an instance that has a privacy policy enabled for the user's language, the user could be prompted to accept the privacy policy twice or be shown the tour twice - in the first 2 consecutive loads (this is a half truth, as things change with different network connection qualities, and the user might see the tour multiple times, but that's not necessarily part of the problem here). 

**To Reproduce**
This is pretty tricky to reproduce reliably, as it requires a race condition to trigger and quick user actions / slow network. 
1. Add a privacy policy for your chosen language.
2. Create a new offline user.
3. Login with this offline user, choosing the language with the privacy policy. 
4. Replicate and accept the privacy policy.
5. Immediately close the tour and all other startup modals (being quick to click is hard!)
6. Reload. 

**Expected behavior**
On next reload, you should see neither the privacy policy nor any of the startup modals (including the tour). 
**If you see either, the bug has happened.**

**Environment**
- Browser: Chrome
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.10, 3.11

**Additional context**
This is caused by a race condition where two actions update the same document, causing a conflict: 
1. Accepting the privacy policy. This edits the user-settings document locally, and relies on replication to upload to the server. '
2. Closing the startup modals. This also edits the user-settings document (setting the `known` property as true), but hits the API endpoint directly, editing the doc directly on the server. 

A local doc edit will trigger upwards replication imemdiately, so it depends on whether this completes before the user closes the tours. 

On next load, the user will perform the required action again (either accepting the policy or closing the tour modal, depending on which rev won) and never have this problem again. 

To repeat testing using the same user, after each try, open the user-settings document (`medic/org.couchdb.user:<username>`) and delete `privacy_policy_acceptance_log` and `known` fields, sync and reload.

title: Mark for outbound might create tasks for already sent jobs
body:
**Describe the bug**
A race condition between Sentinel and API, both creating/saving infodocs, can result in mark-for-outbound creating a task for a document that has already been sent successfully. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Get on a fast and idle server (both important). 
2. Create a very simple config for mark-for-outbound, and disable all other transitions. 
3. Make sure that you mock the server that's supposed to receive your outbound request.
4. Submit a doc that should generate an outbound request.
5. Check that that the request has been sent and that no outboud task exists.
6. Sometimes, you'll find an outbound task for this doc, even if the request was successfully sent.


**Expected behavior**
If the outbound request was successful, the outbound task should not be created.

**Environment**
- App: sentinel
- Version: 3.9, 3.10

**Logs / Additional context**

The reproduction steps are identical to the ones in this e2e test: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/e2e/sentinel/transitions/mark_for_outbound.js - so do find inspiration there concerning how the transition is configured or how the pushed doc should look like. 
This test flakes on occasion with:

```
1) mark_for_outbound when external server is up correctly creates and sends an outbound request immediately
  - Failed: expected 1 to equal 0
```

Upon inspecting Sentinel logs, I found this: 
```
change event on doc <docId> 
isRevSame tested false on transition mark_for_outbound for doc <docId>
calling transition.onMatch for doc <docId> and transition mark_for_outbound 
About to send outbound request 
{
  "url": "http://localhost:41591/working-endpoint",
  "body": {
    "id": "<docId>",
    "rev": "<rev>"
  },
  "json": true,
  "timeout": 10000
} 
result from outbound request 
undefined <- this is expected, the endpoint from the e2e test doesn't return anything! 
Pushed <docId> to test <- means that the outbound task has been sent successfully
Creating outbound task task:outbound:<docId> <- yet, the task was still created! 
finished transition mark_for_outbound doc <docId> is unchanged 
transition results: [false] 
```

Looking at the code here https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/mark_for_outbound.js#L39
we catch all errors and consider the push as failed if there are any. 
Since the request was successful, I suspected that saving the infodoc had failed somehow. 

My hunch was confirmed by the couchdb logs, and seeing that the put had errored with a conflict: 
```
localhost:4984 172.17.0.1 admin PUT /medic-test-sentinel/<docId>-info 409 ok 3
```

title: Arch V3: Making Medic API horizontally scalable
body:
# Description

This PR introduces changes required to make Medic API scale horizontally. 

**Vertical Scaling vs Horizontal Scaling:**

Vertical Scaling: Also called scaling-up. When the capacity of the server is increased in order to handle extra load/traffic. E.g. Upgrade the server from a single core machine with 4GB of RAM to a quad core machine with 16GB of RAM. This can only go so far before you hit a saturation point.

Horizontal Scaling: Also called scaling-out. The number of servers or in container lingo, the number of replicas is increased and not the individual capacity of the server. A load balancer routes traffic to the different replicas based on their current load/availability. This is highly fault tolerant. When the load on the system is very low during the night or on the holidays, the system can scale-in, using fewer resources and saving costs, etc. This brings one closer to paying only for actual usage and high utilization for what one's already paying for.

**PR Details**
This PR seeks to introduce the capability for horizontal scalability for api by breaking api into two components: a helper and launcher processes. The helper starts first and runs initializations and taps into the changes feed to listen for config changes and applies required changes. The launcher process runs the rest of api and listens for requests from users and takes care of routing.

The changes were made in such a way as not to break automation scripts when developing locally. Grunt scripts as well as `node server.js` should work without issues.

When scaling api horizontally, the launcher process is the one that gets scaled-out or scaled-in.

title: Prototype integration with CloudWorks' Rapid Diagnostic Toolkit app
body:
As part of our work with CloudWorks we need to build a prototype integration to the [Rapid Diagnostic Toolkit](https://github.com/dimagi/rd-toolkit) Android application.  

The workflow for the prototype will be an assessment form that provisions a test, and then a follow up task which would have a button to check for the status of the test. If the test is still pending, the user could wait in the form to press the button again until the return status is that the test is complete. 


This [integration](https://github.com/dimagi/rd-toolkit/blob/master/docs/usage.md) requires an Enketo widget to provision a test in the RDToolkit app, and another Enketo widget to collect the test result:

> Since tests take a significant amount of time to resolve, the default execution mode is a two phase interaction. The first phase is an activity callout to provision a diagnostic test, and the second phase is request to capture the result of the test.


The result widget would store the return value as a JSON blob for now, with the status being queryable from within the form itself. That way the field could be required, and preventing advancing in the form until a completed/success status is returned.

title: api and webapp can disagree on whether a user has an online or offline role
body:
**Describe the bug**
Because of different ways of determining whether a user has an online or an offline role, api and webapp can sometimes disagree. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Create an offline role. 
2. Create a user for this offline role. Login and check how many docs the user should download.  Log out.
3. Update the config (you can't do this through the UI) and change the role to be online - by simply removing the `"offline": true` flag. 
4. Login with the user again (in a fresh browser).
5. Notice that you're getting the replication screen, no estimate about how many docs you have and and you just download lots of docs very quickly. 

OR:

1. Create an online role. 
2. Create a user for this online role. Login and make sure the user doesn't get the replication screen. Log out. 
3. Update the config (you can't do this through the UI) and change the role to be offline- by simply adding the `"offline": true` flag. 
4. Login with the user again (in a fresh browser). 
5. Notice that you're not getting the replication screen and then none of your lists load (offline users can't request CouchDB views). 

**Expected behavior**
API and Webapp should reach a consensus on whether this user is an online user or an offline user. 

**Logs**
The only suspicious log is that the initial request to `users-info` returns a 403 (because the user doesn't have permission to update users). 

**Screenshots**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/110068248-f5040f00-7d7d-11eb-93fb-7df4f3ebebc5.png)


**Environment**
- Instance: Live instance
- App: Webapp and API
- Version: 3.10

**Additional context**

In webapp, we determine whether a user is online or offline by checking if they have a role called `mm-online`. We don't manage this role when the other user's roles are changed:
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/session.service.ts#L112

In API, we actually check the roles' config, checking if the user has at least one role that has the `offline` flag, and completely ignore `mm-online` (the only mention to `mm-online` in API is in user creation). 
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/8e139e976ff785598bcdaf3edcfb8716766adfe4/api/src/auth.js#L65

The workaround, when a user gets into this situation, is to manually update them and add (or remove) the `mm-online` role.

Initially [raised on the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/updating-default-login-credentials/1178).

1. Log in using the admin credentials (medic/password)
2. Go to the app menu and select User settings
3. Click on ‘Update password’
4. Set a new password

If it's not possible to update the admin password via API then we should detect this and link to the CouchDB docs rather than masquerading as success.

2021-03-08 11:37:57 INFO: REQ 0af761c9-336f-4eb6-ae5b-fe7e4fe3e5ce - Updated user 'admin'. Setting field(s) 'password'. Requested by 'admin'. 
RES 0af761c9-336f-4eb6-ae5b-fe7e4fe3e5ce ::ffff:127.0.0.1 admin POST /api/v1/users/admin HTTP/1.1 200 176 107.495 ms

title: Research ability to report on releases/features based off github ticket labels
body:
**Describe the issue**
Is it feasible to deduce when a feature or upgrade or initial launch went live based off the GH ticket and related labels alone?

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
After a chat in PO and R&L meetings and [slack discussions](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C024ZK678/p1614380372007900), based off @n-orlowski 's attempt to figure when #5776 went live for BRAC, let's try and see if we can add labels to GH tickets so that we can know when something went live. 

This likely looks something like:
* coming up with a label nomenclature we could use that would be tenable: detailed enough but not so overbearing that they're too verbose.  
* get sign off from relevant teams (eg Product & App Services) that adding a bunch of tags won't be too much of an imposition
* retroactively add a bunch of labels to some tickets to see if we can tell by close date when something went live and as well to vet the nomenclature has actually usefull

Lot's more scoping to do on these before this is actionable, but this _is_ a research ticket ;)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Lots and looooooots of guessing, asking around, trawling over old GH tickets.

title: Muting transition and update clinics don't handle contacts that use a hardcoded type and also have a `contact_type` property correctly
body:
**Describe the bug**


**To Reproduce**
For `muting`: 

1. Configure muting transition and set a muting form.
2. Create a place. 
3. Mute this place. Make sure Sentinel processes the report before proceeding. 
4. Create a contact under this place, making sure to add a type = `person` and some string in a `contact_type` property. (it's important you do this when you first create the contact, otherwise the code will work correctly!). 
5. Wait till sentinel processes the contact. 
6. Check the contact in the DB and observe it's not muted. The UI will show them as muted, because they are muted in lineage and they will count as muted if attaching schedules to them, but it's not 100% correct, and could prove problematic in some configurations. 

**Expected behavior**
A contact created under a muted place should be muted (in its json). 

**To Reproduce**
For `update_clinics`: 

1. Enable `update_clinics`. 
2. Create a place that has a hardcoded type and add a `refid` property, save some string in the field, also add a `contact_type` field with some string. 
3. Create a doc that looks like an SMS report with a `refid` property that has the same value as the `refid` on your place. Make sure it doesn't have a `contact` property, so update clinics runs. 
4. Wait until sentinel processes the doc.
5. Observe that your doc is not connected to your clinic. 

**Expected behavior**
The connection through the refid should have been processed. 

**Environment**
- App: api, sentinel
- Version: 3.10

**Additional context**
Muting not being saved on new contacts is mostly important for analytics, but the app should look and function as if these contacts were muted. It's possible some configurations that don't check for muting in a contact's lineage could also be affected. 
I'm not sure how the `refid` for update_clinics interaction works in production or if it even is used in production.

This results in our testing builds database continuously growing, without being cleaned up. Currently we host **1093** testing builds instead of the desired number of 50.

None.

title: Release 3.10.3
body:
# Planning

- [x] Create an [organisation wide project](https://github.com/orgs/medic/projects/79) and add this issue to it.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the project.

# Development

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Manager. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR to the release branch. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version patch`.
- [x] Write an update in the weekly Product Team call agenda summarising development and acceptance testing progress and identifying any blockers. The release manager is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` and backported to the release branch release testing can begin.

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing.
- [x] Create a new document in the [release-notes folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/release-notes) in `master`. Ensure all issues are in the GH Project, that they're correct labelled, and have human readable descriptions. Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/changelog-generator) to export the issues into our changelog format. Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
- [x] Until release testing passes, make sure regressions are fixed in `master`, cherry-pick them into the release branch, and release another beta.
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Announce the release in #products using this template:
```
@channel *Announcing the release of {{version}}*

This release fixes {{number of bugs}}. Read the release notes for full details: {{url}}
```
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/), under the "Product - Releases" category. You can use the previous message and omit `@channel`.
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the project.

title: Pushing standard config with latest medic-conf fails with translation errors
body:
**Describe the bug**
A new feature to [validate custom translations](https://github.com/medic/medic-conf/issues/254) was released in [medic-conf 3.4.1](https://github.com/medic/medic-conf/blob/v3.4.1/release-notes.md#340). However, `standard` config was not updated to pass this new validation, and fails the `upload-custom-translations` job. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Install latest medic-conf. 
2. Deploy an instance. 
3. Checkout latest `master` or `3.10.x`. Try to install `standard` config by running `medic-conf --local` or `medic-conf --url=<your url>`. Alternatively, just run the `upload-custom-translations` job. 
4. See a bunch of errors. 

**Expected behavior**
The config should be updated to run with latest version of medic-conf. 

**Logs**
```
ERROR Cannot compile 'hi' translation with key 'messages.d.validation.days_since_birth' has placeholders that do not match any in the base translation provided
ERROR Cannot compile 'id' translation with key 'messages.schedule.child.month_01' has placeholders that do not match any in the base translation provided 
ERROR Cannot compile 'id' translation with key 'messages.schedule.child.month_02' has placeholders that do not match any in the base translation provided 
ERROR Cannot compile 'id' translation with key 'messages.schedule.child.month_03' has placeholders that do not match any in the base translation provided 
ERROR Cannot compile 'id' translation with key 'messages.schedule.child.month_04' has placeholders that do not match any in the base translation provided 
ERROR Cannot compile 'id' translation with key 'messages.schedule.child.month_05' has placeholders that do not match any in the base translation provided 
```
and much more. 

**Environment**
- Instance: local instance
- Version: 3.10

**Additional context**
The workaround is to run the command using the new parameter `--skip-translation-check` to skip the validations.

title: Outbound push- enable joining related data before pushing
body:
Outbound push is limited to one data point per request. 

It would be great if we were able to join data points i.e a report and a contact, two reports in one request

Data can be manually joined at the moment before pushing but this process is tedious and manual. 

**Additional context**
Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here.

title: Outbound Push- make it possible to push data to different end points from one push
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Requests from outbound can only be pushed to one end point. I one needs to push to different end points, they have to do it one at a time. 
**Describe the improvement you'd like**
It would be great if we can send data to different end points from one request. 

Middleware such as Open HIM have these functionalities that enable one to configure data to be pushed to different end points

title: Outbound Push- expand functions and syntax
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Outbound push has very limited syntax and flexibility around custom functions such as pulling data and using it in the request.
**Describe the improvement you'd like**
It would be helpful if we could make it more flexible and add custom functioning such as injecting information into a payload then pushing it. 
**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Mature middleware that has this functionality can be integrated into the CHT.

title: Form with truthy expression will be displayed despite permissions
body:
**Describe the bug**
A form context can have an `expression` and a `permission`  property. Both should be checked in order to evaluate whether a form can be displayed or not. 
However, if the form has an expression and it evaluates as truthy, the permissions check will be skipped. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Change a form's context to be shown to persons (for simplicity). Remove the `expression` and `permission` properties.
2. Login as a non-admin user and check that the form is displayed as an action for a person contact. 
3. Update the form context and add a `permission` property with `["non existent permission"]`. 
4. As the same user, check that the form is **not** displayed for a person contact.
5. Update the form context and add an `expression` property with the value "true" (quotes included, so string "true", not boolean true in json)
6. As the same user, check that the form **is** displayed for a person contact.

**Expected behavior**
Permissions should still be checked even if the form expression evaluates as truthy. 

**Environment**
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.7, 3.8, 3.9, 3.10, 3.11

title: In the form's `context.expression` the `summary` parameter is always undefined
body:
**Describe the bug**
Forms have a context.expression that gets evaluated to determine whether the form shows or not. The  contact, user, and summary are passed in. Placing a breakpoint on that function. The summary is always undefined. This breaks a lot of the form expressions in default config. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Upload the default config.
2. Log in as an offline user.
3.  Navigate to the people tab but do not open a person just yet.
4. Open chrome devtools and breakpoint on the line that defines the `evaluateExpression = function(` in main.js
5.  Try to open a person. 
6. When the breakpoint hits you can see the param that should include contact  summary is always undefined. 
7.  This causes all forms that have an expression trying to eval the contact summary to return false. 


**Expected behavior**
The contact  summary should be passed in and the forms should show. 

**Logs**
No logs in console

**Screenshots**
If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem.

**Environment**
- Instance: gamma.dev
- Browser: chrome
- Client platform: windows
- App: webapp
- Version: current master

**Additional context**

title: Meta db sync throws an empty message error when offline, which generates a feedback doc
body:
**Describe the bug**
When offline and syncing the meta database, PouchDB throws an error that Zone.js thinks is uncaught.
This error has no name or message and is not "skipped" by our feedback service, so it will generate a feedback doc every time.

**To Reproduce**
1. Login as an offline user on `~3.11` on a desktop. Check your metadata db and see how many feedback docs there are.
2. Turn off your network (from the dev tools) and refresh the page **. Keep your console open.
3. Hit "sync" from the hamburger menu.
4. Observe a bunch of errors in the console - expected, the app is trying to sync and it can't, but among these errors is a weird one:
```
Error: Uncaught (in promise): {"name":"Error","message":""}
```
5. Check your local metadata db again and see a new feedback doc has been created for this error.

** Refreshing is so we insure that the forced sync will include the meta db as well. Meta dbs sync once 10 seconds after the app is loaded and then once every 30 minutes (even if you sync from the hamburger menu, unless 30 minutes have passed since the last sync, the meta db will not sync). 

To make sure that the meta sync - and not the medic db sync - is throwing this error:
1. Turn the network back on. Refresh the page.
2. Sync from hamburger menu and wait for replication label to go green (this will have synced your meta db, so it won't sync next time you hit the button). 
3. Turn off network again and sync from hamburger menu (do this within 30 minutes of step 2). 
4. Notice that the empty message error is not logged and you have no new feedback doc.

**Expected behavior**
Logging errors when offline is fine, as it's an expected state. We should not be creating feedback docs for these errors, though.

**Logs**
```
main.js?_sw-precache=e6e30284bb3fa10e63f769ab4c140a36:1 Error: Uncaught (in promise): {"name":"Error","message":""}
    at E (polyfills.js?_sw-precache=76abd25b3b164a682f388e7a347960ef:1)
    at E (polyfills.js?_sw-precache=76abd25b3b164a682f388e7a347960ef:1)
    at polyfills.js?_sw-precache=76abd25b3b164a682f388e7a347960ef:1
    at e.value (polyfills.js?_sw-precache=76abd25b3b164a682f388e7a347960ef:1)
    at Object.onInvokeTask (main.js?_sw-precache=e6e30284bb3fa10e63f769ab4c140a36:1)
    at e.value (polyfills.js?_sw-precache=76abd25b3b164a682f388e7a347960ef:1)
    at t.value (polyfills.js?_sw-precache=76abd25b3b164a682f388e7a347960ef:1)
    at _ (polyfills.js?_sw-precache=76abd25b3b164a682f388e7a347960ef:1)
```

**Environment**
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.11

**Additional context**
This is happening because all promises PouchDB are wrapped by Zone.js.
See this very relevant Angular issue: https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/31680
This was "fixed" by: https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/35873 - which just adds an additional zone flag to disable the wrapping of promise rejections.
Enabling this flag (`__zone_symbol__DISABLE_WRAPPING_UNCAUGHT_PROMISE_REJECTION = true`) does indeed solve the problem, but affects ALL promises, so I think we should find a way to do without.

title: Handle compiled messageformat translations throwing errors with missing translation params
body:
**Describe the bug**
Translations that match `messageformat`'s format, but are not given expected params, are throwing errors.

**To Reproduce**
1. Login as any user.
2. Update the translation document for the language you're using and change a visible translation (for example the one for Reports in the header) to contain curly braces: fe `Reports {thing}`.
3. Got to the frontend.
4. See an error in the console and no text in your header where the "Reports" link exists.

**Expected behavior**
No error should be thrown. You should see the "Reports {thing}" text in your header.

**Logs**
Something along the lines of
```
TypeError: Cannot read property '<what you had between the curly braces>' of undefined
```

**Environment**
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.11

**Additional context**
When migrating from AngularJS to Angular, we had to change a lot of the supporting ecosystem, including the translations library.
The translation library we chose is `ngx-translate`, mainly because it's one of the few options available and the fact that it's API is very similar to `angular-translate`, the library we used before.
As one of the key differences between `angular-translate` and `ngx-translate`, `ngx-translate` implements a pre-compilation step to determine the final version of translations and does not support passing an external "interpolator" at runtime.
Since we were using `messageformat` for pluralization, we needed to pre-compile the translation with `messageformat` in order to make use of pluralization in the app.
This means we need to better filter which translations we should pass to `messageformat` to be compiled ahead of time, instead of deciding on the spot or come up with a way to support picking `messageformat` as an interpolator at runtime (though this might mean creating our own translations library to wrap over `ngx-translate`).

body:
**Describe the bug**
When a report is about a place, configured messages to be sent when transitions run over the report could get incorrect recipients. 

**To Reproduce**
1. Update your config to something like this:
```
        transitions: {
          generate_shortcode_on_contacts: true,
          accept_patient_reports: true,
          update_clinics: true
        },
        patient_reports: [
          {
            form: 'FORM',
            messages: [
              {
                event_type: 'report_accepted',
                recipient: 'link:clinic',
                message: [{ content: 'to clinic' }],
              },
              {
                event_type: 'report_accepted',
                recipient: 'link:health_center',
                message: [{ content: 'to health_center' }],
              },
              {
                event_type: 'report_accepted',
                recipient: 'link:district_hospital',
                message: [{ content: 'to district' }],
              },
            ]
          }
        ],
        forms: { FORM: { } }
```
2. Create a district_hospital, a health_center and a clinic, each of them with primary contacts with valid phone numbers.
3. Submit a `FORM` report as an SMS message from the district_hospital level contact, and have this report be about the clinic (have a `fields.place_id` property with the shortcode of your clinic). 
4. Wait until sentinel processes your doc and check the tasks on the message. All of them appear to have the sender as the recipient.

**Expected behavior**
The `link:<contact_type>` should connect to the correct contact from the subject's lineage (in this case, the clinic). 

**Environment**
- App: api, sentinel
- Version: 3.11

**Additional context**
I had forgotten to change this in the never ending list of changes to support places in SMS workflows.

body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
When any of the steps of loading a contact in webapp fails, loading the contact is stopped and the selected contact is unset. 
To replicate: 
1. Update default config and break the contact summary function, for example add:
```
console.log(thisContact.field.field.field);
```
somewhere in the `contact-summary.template.js` file. This will generate a TypeError: `TypeError: Cannot read property 'field' of undefined`. 
2. Login as any user, go to contacts and try to load any contact. 
3. Observe that the contact begins loading, children and reports appear, but when loading contact-summary, the contact detail page unloads and displays "No person selected". If in mobile view, you're also shown the list instead of the contact page. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We should display an error page, and inform the user that there were errors while loading the contact. 
Our template even has a check for this and can display this error, so this functionality existed at some point. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Keep it as it is. 

**Additional context**
I'm unsure when this came to be. The likely culprits are:
1. When we added redux in ~3.5.x
2. When we added lazy loading of contacts in ~3.4.x

title: Error thrown when trying to send message to unknown sender
body:
**Describe the bug**
An error is thrown when trying to send a message to an unknown contact.
However the error is not visible to the user (all the user sees is that he presses "Send" and nothing happens). 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

0. Enable `update_clinics` transition. 
1. Create a new contact with a phone number. 
2. Send a message from this contact to the app (from admin app). 
3. Delete the contact.
4. In webapp, go to messages, click on the conversation from the deleted contact (the list should show a uuid).

body: **What feature do you want to improve?** When there's an empty state some tabs will automatically select the first item and show it, but some others don't do this or don't do this after an item deletion. Examples: 1. When a item is deleted: - Messages tab doesn't redirect from **/messages/[id]** to **/messages** and it doesn't select first item in the list - Reports tab redirect from **/reports/[id]** to **/reports** and it doesn't select another report - Contact tab redirect to parent contact and select it and display information. 2. When loading from empty state - Messages tab select first item when loading **/messages** (no id in url) - Reports tab doesn't select first item when loading **/reports** (no id in url) - Contacts tab doesn't select item when loading **/contacs** (no id in url) if it's admin, but it does select an item when login in as offline user. **Describe the improvement you'd like** Implement consistent behaviour in tabs (messages, tasks, contacts, reports) to improve user experience about what to expect during empty state. **Describe alternatives you've considered** We need feedback about what gives more value to the user and that won't increase confusion.
