title: CHT hosting improvements for App Developers
body:
### Describe the issue
CHT app developers, primarily App Services, currently use [CHT-Core Starter](https://github.com/medic/app-services-team/tree/master/cht-core-starter) (private repo) to do development for specific CHT deployments.  Starter's goal is to enable easy "one liner" deployments of CHT instances in a local dev environment.  

It, along with the complimenting [docker compose](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/tutorials/local-setup/) and [development](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/DEVELOPMENT.md) approaches, faces some challenges:
* Current docker-compose option doesn't start reliably - 403 errors, 404 errors, 
* Docker or bare-metal installs have large internet requirements to use ngrok to get around serviceworker limitations. This is slow b/c routes local traffic via internet
* Multiple projects at the same time are hard (either literally concurrent to compare configs side by side, or working on 3 different deployment serially through out a day)
* Starter can be overly aggressive in deleting ~/.horticulturalist/deployments every time :(
* Starter downloads specific version every time (eg downloading 3.10 w/i horti) 

As well, there's a number of problem tickets related to this (some are dupes of above):
* [One-line app developer experience](https://github.com/medic/app-services-team/issues/72) 
* [Local config: Docker failed to create couchDB account - 404 Not Found](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6456)
* [medic-os docker: Research nginx not starting causing 404s ](https://github.com/medic/medic-infrastructure/issues/293)
* [Cannot login on localhost as restricted user ](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6168)
* [Publish a dev version of the docker-compose.yml](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6455)

### Describe the improvement you'd like
We should offer a public facing, docker based solution for App Developers that:
* caches as much as possible to avoid re-downloading CHT versions & docker images.  This will help greatly for developers who might be bandwidth constrained. 
* supporting the trifecta of macOS* / Windows WSL 2 / Linux development environments (_* - watch out for M1_)
* Offer dockerized version of couchdb to avoid having to run in couchdb in bare-metal (in WSL2 for example)
* support CHT back to version 3.5 and up to any posted version in GH (releases, betas & alphas)
* **Added Apr 22 '21** - Work in Architecture V2 so App Developers are developing on near identical configuration as to what is running in product
*  **Added Apr 22 '21** - Permit access to Fauxton (see [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6455#issuecomment-637047221))
*  **Added Apr 22 '21** - Work on which ever ports are open to avoid port collision (see [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/6962#issuecomment-785606008) and [here](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/self-hosting/#port-conflicts))
*  **Added Apr 22 '21** - Offer Valid SSL support out of the box to support android development (see [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6168))

### Describe alternatives you've considered
Continue using starter, docker-compose and bare-metal installs as we do today.

title: Admin upgrade page shows all upgrades as potentially incompatible
body:
**Describe the bug**
The upgrade page shows all releases as potentially incompatible regardless of what the base version is.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Go to App Management > Upgrade instance

**Expected behavior**
- Final releases (version format `x.y.z`) that are less than the currently installed version are hidden.
- Final releases that are greater than the currently installed version are shown *without* a "potentially incompatible" warning.
- Other releases with unknown versions (eg: branch releases) are shown *with* a "potentially incompatible" warning.

For example, in the screenshot below, 3.11.0 should _not_ have the warning icon, because we know 3.11.0 is compatible with the currently installed 3.10.3.

**Logs**
None.

**Screenshots**
![Screenshot from 2021-04-21 14-54-29](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2064938/115623415-44fa5d80-a34d-11eb-983f-73e4ca8b3d4c.png)

**Environment**
- Instance: demo-cht.dev
- Browser: Firefox
- Client platform: Linux
- App: admin
- Version: 3.10.0, 3.11.0

**Additional context**

This warning is based on the `deploy_info` property in the `medic` ddoc. Before upgrading the value for this was...

```json
  "deploy_info": {
    "timestamp": "2021-03-24T15:33:58.070Z",
    "user": "medic",
    "version": "3.10.3"
  }
```

I debugged [this line](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/admin/src/js/controllers/upgrade.js#L121) in the Upgrade controller which checks for the `base_version` which is undefined above. title: Single quotes escaping `'` rendered wrong
body:
**Describe the bug**
We use the library [npmjs.com/.../properties](https://www.npmjs.com/package/properties) in CHT core that is also used in other components like the [POE scripts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/scripts/poe) to import translations from POEditor, and the library [@medic/translation-checker](https://github.com/medic/translation-checker) that is used by medic-conf and the poe scripts mentioned. The "properties" library has a bug: it does not take into account [single quotes escaping](https://www.mscharhag.com/java/resource-bundle-single-quote-escaping) when there are `{{..}}` arguments in the text.

Although there is no clear specification about the .properties file format, most programs interpret the value of the following:

    sys.form_not_found = Fomu ''{{form}}'' haipatikani.

As:

    Fomu '{{form}}' haipatikani.

And POEditor is not the exception, when we write translations in the POE web editor, we don't care how to escape characters, so we write the value of a translation key like this:

![POEditor_translation_with_escaped_quotes](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1608415/115752982-08405d80-a371-11eb-9a79-cfff635568bc.png)

But the final result when we execute the poe script to import the translation from the POE API is:

    sys.form_not_found = Fomu ''{{form}}'' haipatikani.

Which is right, but again, the value rendered by Angular will be `Fomu ''{{form}}'' haipatikani.` instead of `Fomu '{{form}}' haipatikani.` (with the `{{form}}` replaced by the variable value).

**Environment**
- cht-core version: tested in master, v3.11 and bellow
- medic-conf version: tested in master, v3.5.0 and bellow
- translation-checker: v1.0.0 is the version linked in cht-core and medic-conf

**Additional context**
We could just leave in the .properties files the single quotes without escaping, is even more clear to read, but we relay on POEditor for translations that does the export following the format spec, and even if we add some changes in the poe scripts to post-process the content and remove the escapes, we shouldn't use "custom" made formats for any type of content.

A good solution would be to use another library, the one we use does not have new releases the last 7 years, and the project has a lot of bug not solved. Also has other limitations like the API does not provide "meta" info of the content parsed, like the line where each key / value pair was read, which could be useful to better highlight errors in the translations files.

However this is not a big issue, we should use double quote char `"` in our translations instead of the single one `'`.

Finally, it does not cause the CHT to crash, so I wouldn't consider the error important.

CC @garethbowen

title: Adds offline muting
body:
# Description

Muting is now be processed client-side, for offline users. To run transitions on the client, no config changes are required. However, it is possible to disable client-side muting by updating the config like: 
```json
"transitions": {
  "muting": { "client_side": false }
}
```

Also: 
Splits validation into own shared lib to be used from webapp.
Updates validation to be promise based (some QOL but kept changes to a minimum). 
Updates lineage to use all known docs when building subject lineages (so when we can have hydration for new reports + new contacts out of the box). 
Consolidates the get-message logic into message-utils to be used by validation and transitions.
Consolidates getLocale into message-utils.

Offline muting happens on the device, with the transition code running over docs before they are saved into the local database, following a few rules:
1. Only new docs are processed
2. When a batch contains both muting and unmuting forms, only unmuting forms will be processed, while the muting forms will be ignored.
3. The actions performed over docs are: 
 - when a muting / unmuting report is submitted, local relevant contacts are updated. This follows the same rules as server-side muting, where muting cascades downwards and unmuting cascades upwards.
 - when a new contact is added under a muted parent, it also becomes muted
 - reports get an "client_side_transitions" property to log which transitions have run over them
 - validation runs over reports, with invalid reports being ignored by the transition and validation errors saved in their json. Validation errors are generated in the user's selected language and are visible on the report's detail page. 
 - contacts get a "muting_history" property, to log every muting/unmuting event that has been processed on the device, and which "service" updated the muted state last (options are "server_side" or "client_side")
 - the "muted" property on the contact is still the property that determines if the contact is muted or not, so configs and queries don't require changes. 
4. Except the muting/unmuting reports and the relevant contacts (as described above), no other docs are edited directly -  registrations are not silenced and the config is still responsible with handling muted contacts (cancelling tasks, updating targets. contact summary and etc). 
5. It's necessary to process docs before they are saved, otherwise there is a high risk of generating conflicts on every muting event, if the device has a strong internet connection and Sentinel is up to date (and both device and Sentinel process the event at the same time). 


Server-side muting is updated to handle offline muting:
1. When a contact is processed, its "muting_history.last_update" is updated to "server_side" and an entry is added to the infodoc muting_history.
   If the contact is muted, the muted property is updated with the server's current date (for consistency).
   The contact's offline "muting_history" event log is left untouched and is **not** merged into the infodoc muting_history (to avoid adding complex logic around handling doc conflicts and ending up with muting_history events stored in infodocs that happened only for losing revs).
2. Muting/unmuting reports that were processed offline are always processed sever-side, even if their subjects are already in the correct state (because offline muting doesn't silence registrations, and offline devices don't have access to the whole hierarchy to perform correct muting).
   Additionally, for every contact that is updated, the offline "muting_history" event log is inspected and searched for the muting event corresponding to the currently processed report. If a matching event is found, every other following event is collected to be replayed. 
   After processing all contacts, the collected list of muting events to be replayed is sorted chronologically (this sorting is imperfect, as dates from devices are not reliable, but some sorting is necessary and this is the only data that is available). This results in a sorted list of report uuids. Muting is (re)run over every corresponding report, in sequence and in order, even if muting already ran. 
   Replaying events that were processed on the client (ideally in the same order they were submitted) is necessary because there are little chances for Sentinel to process these events in this ideal order (mainly because the changes feed is not ordered and the position of a doc in the feed is not correlated with when it was created, rather with when it was updated/synced/read from a shard).
3. When receiving a contact that was last_updated offline, Sentinel processes it - to solve the problem of the muting/unmuting report being deleted before it was synced. 
   

The code tries to handle most situations that might arise, in an effort to make the muting action idempotent:
- a composite form that creates a new place, + new persons in the place and mutes this new place (which should mute the new place and the new persons in the place)
- a composite form that creates a new place + new persons in the place and mutes the person (which should only mute the new person)
- a composite form that creates a new person under a muted parent and unmutes the person or any other ancestor (which should unmute all contacts under the topmost muted ancestor). 
- multiple muting/unmuting events processed on the client and then synced out of order. 
- deletion of muting/unmuting reports before syncing

However, there could be situations where muting client-side could yield inconsistent results: for example if settings are updated, so a device and Sentinel run muting over the same doc with different settings, could result in contacts being muted but registrations not silenced. Additionally, the behavior might not be consistent when reports are edited before they are synced (and one contact is muted on the client-side and another contact is muted server-side). 

medic/cht-core#6737

title: Store users' selected language in telemetry and feedback docs
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
As a consequence of https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7068, it's no longer possible to know what language users have selected, since it's no longer stored in the `user-settings` document.


**Describe the improvement you'd like**
I think the currently selected language should be stored in all feedback and telemetry documents. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None. 

**Additional context**
Given that plenty of bugs have been isolated when a specific language was used, with some of these critically affecting production instances, it's extremely important that this information is available, accurate and relatively fresh. 

Data analysis might also find it useful to have this information, but maybe could cope with more stale data.

title: Can't submit forms against muted contacts
body:
**Describe the bug**
We show a modal when before opening an action against a muted contact in webapp: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/117460214-f35cf000-af54-11eb-99b9-f556ad80660f.png)

The modal should close and do nothing if user clicks "No", but should redirect to the form if user clicks "Yes". 
Clicking "Yes" does nothing. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Deploy 3.11. 
2. Mute a contact (quick is to just add a `muted` property in the doc's json)
3. Open the contact in webapp and click to open a form against them (make sure this is not an unmuting form). Click yes in the popup. 
4. You're not redirected when you click yes. 

**Expected behavior**
You should be redirected when clicking yes. 

**Logs**
No logs.

**Environment**
- App: Webapp
- Version: 3.11

**Additional context**
This is a regression in 3.11 and is a one liner fix.

title: Send form_not_found Notifications to Known Senders Only
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
In SMS or collect projects, we have users who are registered (known senders) in the system, but submit invalid forms to the system. We want to be able to send them [notifications to guide them in their form submissions](https://github.com/medic/config-cdc-mohke-dsru/issues/3). When the `forms_only_mode` is set to true, all valid and invalid messages are created as reports, with appropriate error codes issued, however, we still cannot send notifications to registered users **ONLY**. The notifications are sent to unregistered users as well, and we don't want that.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Possible solutions:
- Add a form code that represents the infinite set of form inputs that are not configured, so that a user is able to receive notifications through reminders or alerts.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Using `form validations`, `reminders`, `conditional_alerts` and `multi_report_alerts` all require that the forms be known (configured) in the system.

title: 6915  - Telemetry daily frequency
body:
# Description

Change telemetry frequency from monthly to **daily**.

medic/cht-core#6915

### Improvements

- Telemetry frequency changed from monthly to daily.
- The id of a telemetry record now looks like `telemetry-<year>-<month>-<day>-<username>-<uuid>`. Also in the `metadata` section a new field `day` is added with the day of the month the data belongs to.
- More test coverage in the telemetry spec.
- Minor improvements in the script to collect meta data from a terminal (`scripts/get_users_meta_docs.js`):
  - Output errors in the standard error stream to see the errors in the console while piping results to a JSON file.
  - Add Unix exec permission and header to execute the script without the `node ` prefix.

Please also review the documentation changes [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/pull/493).

### Bug fixed

It also fix the following ~bugs~ bug found in the current implementation:

When `record()` is called for the first time in the period (a period was a month, now is a day), the record is added to the telemetry DB and then the aggregation is executed with the data that was stored previously, so the aggregation process aggregates all the records from the previous period + a record that is actually from the current period. The last record shouldn't be taken into account in the aggregation submitted.

This represents a minor issue even for daily reports, and it is fixed in this PR just changing the order of the execution: executing first the aggregation if a new period started, and then add the new record.

### Backward compatibility

Systems that rely on telemetry data will need to adequate to the new frequency, but so far the data collected and the schema is the same, with the only addition of the new field `metadata.day`.

There is no special code to "migrate" existent data collected in the devices where the new version is installed: if a device was collecting telemetry data to send next month and then the new version is installed, the app will aggregate the data collected the same day the device is used, and send the aggregation when connection is available, but the record will look like a "daily" aggregation, not monthly, or more precisely "partially monthly". E.g.:

1. A device is in sync with a CHT v3.11 deployment and has been sending monthly aggregation for a while. Last time it sent an aggregation report was May 2nd with the data collected previous month (April). So the id of that reports is something like `telemetry-2021-4-greg-aaabbb1234`.
2. Now is May 12, so the device was recording telemetry data since May 2. All these records were not aggregated yet.
3. On May 13 CHT v3.12.0 is deployed, and the same day the app is synced. The new frequency algorithm is applied so data collected from May 2 to May 13 is aggregated and sent as it was data collected from the last recorded day May 2, the id of the record will be: `telemetry-2021-4-2-greg-aaabbb1234`.
4. Next day data sent will be truly daily aggregated. On May 14 the device will aggregate the data collected on May 13 and the record id will be: `telemetry-2021-5-13-greg-aaabbb1234`. Next day if there is data collected will be `telemetry-2021-5-14-...` and son on. Days that the devices is not used won't have telemetry recorded therefore no reports to send.

So once a upgrade of the CHT is rolled out, first reports will include data from many days, but should be easy to identify these reports because the month in the id (or the field `metadata.month`) will be from the past month, not the current month. If we want to implement a more smooth transition, like send one report for each day the telemetry data has not been aggregated, will require more changes, specially in the device webapp, and not sure if it worth the effort.

CC @helizabetholsen and @dianabarsan on this, let me know if is not clear enough.

### ~To-do~ in another app / issue

medic-couch2pg has a PG view [useview_telemetry](https://github.com/medic/medic-couch2pg/blob/master/libs/medic-users-meta/migrations/202102191153.do.54-create-couchdb-users-meta-table.sql#L20-L31) with the telemetry data, and there is a field field `period_start` that we need to adapt to support these changes. I've created a ticket to keep track of it: [medic-couch2pg#85](https://github.com/medic/medic-couch2pg/issues/85)  →  released in 3.3.0

title: Adds telemetry for replication requests

# Description

The following telemetry records are added: 

| key | value | recorded | 
| --- | ------- | -------- | 
| `replication:user-initiated`  | 1 | when the user clicks "Sync now" | 
| `replication:<database>:<direction>:success` | number representing how long in took to replicate, in ms | when replication is successful | 
| `replication:<database>:<direction>:failure` | number representing how long in took to replicate, in ms | when replication is failed | 
| `replication:<database>:<direction>:failure:reason:offline:client` | 1 | replication fails because of connection error and the app detects the client is offline | 
|  `replication:<database>:<direction>:failure:reason:offline:server` | 1 | replication fails because of connection error and the app detects the client is online | 
| `replication:<database>:<direction>:failure:reason:error` | 1 | replication fails because of other errors |
| `replication:<database>:<direction>:docs` | number of replicated docs | For one-directional, stores number of "read" docs, for sync, stores sum of read docs for every direction. | 
| `replication:medic:<direction>:ms-since-last-replicated-date` |  number in ms representing the difference between now and when the client last replicated successfully | only recorded for medic database, every time replication is attempted | 
| `replication:medic:<direction>:denied` | 1 | when replication is denied | 

Unless otherwise specified, <database> and <direction> placeholders stand for any combination of:
| database | direction | 
| --- | --- | 
| `medic` | `from` or `to`  | 
| `meta` | `sync` |

title: Monitoring sentinel backlog values are wrong
body:
**Describe the bug**
The monitoring `sentinel.backlog` value is incorrect, as it counts changes depending on the value from the deprecated `_local/sentinel-meta-data` doc. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Load a 3.11 or 3.10 instance. Make sure you added some docs and Sentinel cleared the queue. The update a contact. Wait for Sentinel to clear the queue again. 
2. Request `api/v1/monitoring` and check the `sentinel.backlog`
3. Value is above 0. - the actual value can differ, if you just installed, it will be equal to the number of docs in the database, if you upgraded or you have an old `_local/sentinel-meta-data` doc, it will count changes depending on values stored in this doc. 

**Expected behavior**
The value should be correct.
Even if sentinel is "up to date", this value doesn't have to be 0. Sentinel skips from processing some docs and when a doc is skipped, the update_seq doesn't advance. 
To make sure that the value gets to 0, update a doc that will be processed, for example a contact or a report. 

**Environment**
- App: api
- Version: 3.10, 3.11, 3.12

**Additional context**
In `3.10` we [changed](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/6408) the doc where Sentinel keeps its transition update_seq from  `_local/sentinel-meta-data` to `_local/transitions-seq` but the monitoring service code was not updated with this change.

title: "Sync Now" should synchronize "meta" database when pressed
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
When users press **"Sync Now"** , only the device's main database is synchronized (the database with the reports, tasks, messages..). The "meta" database that contains feedback and telemetry documents is only synchronized by a _cron_ job each 30 min, and if there is no connection by the time, another 30 min of waiting are needed to successfully synchronize.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
When user clicks "Sync Now", the meta DB should also be synchronized. One synchronization shouldn't affect the sync of the another.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
This was not requested by any particular partner or user, but would be a nice to have now that we are increasing the quality and sync frequency of "meta" data. Also is a one line patch, that going to attach to the issue.


**Additional context**
The size of the request needed to do the synchronization is still little data, it won't affect data caps if the data is synchronized with a mobile data plan instead of WiFi, because taking into account compression used by the devices and that only new data is syncronized, only a few kilobytes are consumed. Moreover, because we put the user in control of when to synchronize, we avoid waste of data spend by requests made automatically by the app because the user can choose to do the sync when is connected to a WiFi connection.

title: Tasks fail to load when priority labels are empty
body:
**Describe the bug**
ngx-translate (which is the tool we use to internationalize webapp) throws an error when it gets passed an empty string as a translation key. 
When using a nools-based config (non-declarative) there are no constraints on tasks priority labels. 
For declarative config, need to be undefined or be at least one character long: https://github.com/medic/medic-conf/blob/master/src/lib/validate-declarative-schema.js#L128
Having an empty string as a task priority label will stop the tasks list from loading. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Deploy 3.11 with a nools based config
2. Update a task and set its priority label to an empty string. 
3. Login as an offline user and trigger the task to generate. 
4. See error when loading tasks

**Expected behavior**
Tasks should load correctly. 

**Logs**
```
Error: Parameter "key" required
        at TranslateService.instant (projects/ngx-translate/core/src/lib/translate.service.ts:439:13)
        at RulesEngineService.translateProperty (_karma_webpack_/src/ts/services/rules-engine.service.ts:344:4)
        at http://localhost:9876/_karma_webpack_/src/ts/services/rules-engine.service.ts:390:4
        at Array.forEach (<anonymous>)
        at RulesEngineService.translateTaskDocs (_karma_webpack_/src/ts/services/rules-engine.service.ts:369:3)
        at apply (_karma_webpack_/main.js:298517:20)
        at ZoneDelegate.invoke (_karma_webpack_/node_modules/zone.js/dist/zone.js:400:30)
        at ProxyZoneSpec.onInvoke (_karma_webpack_/node_modules/zone.js/dist/zone-testing.js:301:43)
        at ZoneDelegate.invoke (_karma_webpack_/node_modules/zone.js/dist/zone.js:399:56)
        at Zone.run (_karma_webpack_/node_modules/zone.js/dist/zone.js:160:47)
```

**Environment**
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.11

**Additional context**
The workaround (thanks to @derickl ) is to set the task labels to be undefined. 
This bug might affect other areas of the app where we accept translation keys from configuration.

**What feature do you want to improve?**
At the moment, any user with "can_configure" permission can initiate an upgrade. The "can_configure" is a very broad permission with makes a user akin to an admin, and is required to enable users to make any config/app/users changes. However, more granularity would be desirable to reduce risk of accidental/unplanned upgrades. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

Leave everything unchanged.

We've recently had an incident where an unscheduled upgrade was initiated by a user who had "can_configure" permission to help with user management. This untested upgrade caused a significant disruption.

title: Add more granularity to permissions scheme for the admin app
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently, the admin app access is not granular. 
There are three permissions that are used to access the admin app:
- `can_configure` enables the user to do everything
- `can_view_outgoing_messages` enables the outgoing messages tab only
- `can_export_all` enables the export tab only

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We should consider defining personas for users who access the admin app and add roles for each persona. For example: 
- a user that updates translations
- a user that can update the branding / partners / privacy policies / header tabs
- a user that creates/updates other users
- etc

Each persona should have their own permission(s) that are required to access various parts of the app. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
An alternative to personas would be to define a permission for each page, but that could be overkill.

title: Fix missed jobs from schedules ahead of time less than 1 second
body:
# Description

Fix missed jobs from schedules ahead of time less than 1 second.

medic/cht-core#6634

- The issue was fixed replacing the use of `later.setTimeout` by the native `setTimeout` and the milliseconds ahead that is calculated before hand, taking into account the difference between "now" and the schedule to not be less than 1 second.
- Add regression tests.
- Minor refactor: method `getSchedule` was repeated in the code twice.

## About the error and how to test it

Doing some tests I found a bit different scenario of why this happen. Contrary to what we think, timers are likely to be executed in less than 1 seconds, here is a small test that can be executed under the `sentinel` folder (because it has the `later` dependency in the `node_modules`):

```js
$ sudo date --set="2021-06-09T14:59:59.900Z" && node -e "
  var later = require('later');
  console.log('Date from Node:', new Date());
  var cron = later.parse.cron('00 * * * *');
  var schedule = later.schedule(cron);
  console.log('Next 3 schedules:', schedule.next(3));
  later.setTimeout(()=> console.log('Schedule executed at', new Date()), cron);
"
```

The output:

```
Wed 09 Jun 2021 11:59:59 AM -03
Date from Node: 2021-06-09T14:59:59.923Z
Next 3 schedules: [
  2021-06-09T15:00:00.928Z,
  2021-06-09T16:00:00.928Z,
  2021-06-09T17:00:00.928Z
]
Schedule executed at 2021-06-09T15:00:00.932Z
```

Basically it crates a cron to be executed at 00 minutes of any hour, the process is launched 100 millis before 12:00 UTC, and it works (tried dozens of times, all them worked, and you have to have disable automatic Date & Time sync in your system).

Then if you try to do the same but milliseconds AFTER, despite an entry is created to be executed, the scheduling for that first entry is not executed (`2021-06-09T15:00:00.117Z`):

```
$ sudo date --set="2021-06-09T15:00:00.090Z" && node -e "
  var later = require('later');
  console.log('Date from Node:', new Date());
  var cron = later.parse.cron('00 * * * *');
  var schedule = later.schedule(cron);
  console.log('Next 3 schedules:', schedule.next(3));
  later.setTimeout(()=> console.log('Schedule executed at', new Date()), cron);
"
Wed 09 Jun 2021 12:00:00 PM -03
Date from Node: 2021-06-09T15:00:00.112Z
Next 3 schedules: [
  2021-06-09T15:00:00.117Z,
  2021-06-09T16:00:00.117Z,
  2021-06-09T17:00:00.117Z
]
```

However testing the bug with the application is almost impossible, because even configuring the system clock to a fixed time like the tests above don't warranty at what time the main loops starts, and how much it takes to reach the purging timer. The only way I could reproduce the error consistently was adding 2 regressions tests to this PR, both uses real timers instead of fake ones because was not possible to test it properly with the ones provided by the sinon mocking library.

I tried the following that only failed in master as expected one time, and at this point I'm not even sure whether the failure was because I did configure the cron wrong in the DB or was the perfect timing to reach the bug.

First setup the purge scheduling as described [here](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/performance/purging/) in Couch at http://localhost:5984/_utils/#database/medic/settings with something like:


```js
{
  ...
  "settings": {
    ...
    "purge": {
      "fn": "function(userCtx, contact, reports, messages) { const old = Date.now() - (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 365); return reports.filter(r => r.reported_date < old).map(r => r._id);}",
      "cron": "*/5 * * * *"
    },

  }

```

The purging is configured to run each 5 minutes on each minute that is multiple of 5: 0, 5, 10, ...

Then execute:


```
sudo date --set="2021-06-14T19:50:00.010Z" && node server.js
```

In `master` you won't see the purging process being executed, and after 5 minutes, it may not be executed either. But switching to this branch, you will see in the logs that the purging is executed both at the beginning and after 5 min:

```
2021-06-14 16:50:01 INFO: Running server side purge 
...
2021-06-14 16:50:01 INFO: Server Side Purge completed successfully in 0.0009530372333402435 minutes

```

title: Update the webapp upgrade process to avoid partial upgrades
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently, an upgrade of the webapp on a client consists of two events: 
1. syncing `_design/medic-client`
2. updating the service worker (which is triggered by syncing `service-worker-meta`)

A partial upgrade is a state where only one of these events have happened, with the second event happening in the (hopefully) near future. 
Being in a partially upgraded state can pose problems, for example, if the code (event 2) is updated and running before the ddoc, the code could be accessing new views, or generating data (tasks for example) using old view code. 
Theoretically, a plethora of issues could happen when the client is in this state. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Figure out a way to package the upgrade in a single step. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Leave it as it is. 

**Additional context**
We've recently received reports from production servers where there is proof (telemetry and feedback docs) that clients had downloaded the code, and ran this code, before downloading the ddoc. 
Example: https://github.com/medic/config-vhw/issues/48#issuecomment-854704181

title: API can return 401 status codes for valid sessions under load, forcing users to be logged out

**Describe the bug**
Requests that reach API and are forwarded (proxied) to CouchDB could result in 401 status codes even if the user has an active session. 
Any 401 response status will trigger a logout in webapp based on: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/3919 where the solution was to hook into all Pouch<->Couch fetch requests and navigate to login whenever a 401 is received. This was introduced in 3.6.0.

**To Reproduce**
No reproduction steps yet, this appears to have been a one-off (?) event on a production server (very high load). 

**Expected behavior**
Given the logistical difficulties of users being logged out, we should make sure that the we mean it for sure before logging them out. 

**Logs**
Logs are extensive, but I extracted some relevant logs for a single user. The logs are redacted to obfuscate the instance, the user's IP and the username:

Some ideas: 
1. API should never respond with a 401 if the user has an active session. 
2. When API receives a 401 from a proxied CouchDB request, checks should be made to make sure that the 401 is actually accurate and Couch really means it. 
3. Webapp should poll `/_session` when a 401 is received, before deciding to definitively log a user out (deleting the userCtx cookie). Alternatively, the login script could also poll session before doing anything. The session endpoint will also populate the userCtx cookie if a valid session is found. 

**Environment**
- Instance: production instance
- App: API & Webapp
- Version: 3.10.x

**Additional context**
Over a period of a day, numerous users from a production instance were logged out.

title: #6989 - Resolve race condition when verifying and selecting reports
body:
# Description

As mentioned in the discussion on the linked issue, there are two interconnected race conditions that need to be addressed. Both of these race conditions contribute to the behavior where a user sometimes cannot navigate to a different report while the initial report is still being verified. Additionally, these race conditions also result in the user sometimes failing to be able to quickly navigate between multiple different reports.  

Closes medic/cht-core#6989

## Race Condition 1

To resolve the race condition between calls to the [change subscription](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/fd417e571c728b571a29381b6a4fd38a52b5921d/webapp/src/ts/modules/reports/reports-content.component.ts#L88) (triggered by the report verification process) and the [route subscription](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/fd417e571c728b571a29381b6a4fd38a52b5921d/webapp/src/ts/modules/reports/reports-content.component.ts#L96) (triggered by the user navigating to a new report), this PR introduces a check in the change subscription to validate that, if there is a report id in the route params, then it must match the id of the changed report or the changed report will not be selected. This should continue to allow changed reports to continue to be re-selected both in "select mode" (when there are no report ids in the route) and when the changed report matches the route id. But, it should prevent re-selected a changed report when user has navigated to a different report (and the route id has been updated).

## Race Condition 2

To resolve the race condition so that the latest [selectReport action that is emitted](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/fd417e571c728b571a29381b6a4fd38a52b5921d/webapp/src/ts/effects/reports.effects.ts#L55) is always the report that actually gets selected and displayed, this PR updates the observable mapping logic in the report effects to use [`switchMap`](https://rxjs.dev/api/operators/switchMap) instead of `exhaustMap`.  With `switchMap`, when a second action is emitted before the first is completed, the first is canceled and the second "wins". This means that the latest emitted selectReport action will always be the one that is actually displayed.

title: Client requests receive a 502 statuscode after 2 minutes of idle time
body:
**Describe the bug** Long-running requests that idle for more than 2 minutes will receive a 502 status from the AWS load-balancer. (longpolls to _changes are excluded, these requests send a heartbeat every 10 seconds and are not considered idle). Such requests should not occur, but they may happen when the server is under heavy load. On the client, these 502s will be recorded as feedback docs. See https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7147 **To Reproduce** Three options: one is time consuming, and two are not. Time consuming option: 1. Get an instance with a sizeable amount of docs and users. I worked on a production clone. 2. Find a few users (10-20) that have most docs (including purged ones). 3. Write a script that hits the instance, requesting `/medic/_changes` for these users concurrently and continuously. (no params added to the changes request, so it's not a longpoll). 4. Notice that when requests exceed 2 minutes, the response is a 502. One caveat is that it might take either a long time to load the server to this point or you'll need misconfigured users that have tens of thousands of documents. Less time consuming option 1: 1. Write a script that generates a large amount of uuids (the number necessary depends on the system you're running this against). 2. Through API, as an admin, request changes with a doc_ids filter with these uuids. It doesn't matter the docs don't exist in the database you're requesting them from. 3. Time the request. 4. Catch the 502 you'll eventually get. Less time consuming option 2 that requires adding an endpoint: 1. Add a new endpoint to api that responds after two minutes and 10 seconds (add it somewhere close to the top of the /api/src/routing.js file, for example here: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/routing.js#L192) ``` app.get('/two-minute-timeout', (req, res) => { const timeoutMs = 60 * 2 * 1000 + 10 * 1000; setTimeout(() => { res.send(`This request responds after ${timeoutMs / 1000} seconds`); }, timeoutMs); }); ``` 2. curl this endoint like: ``` time curl http(s):///two-minute-timeout ``` 3. Wait for 2 minutes to observe this result: ``` 502 Bad Gateway

502 Bad Gateway

real 2m0.247s user 0m0.016s sys 0m0.000s ``` If running this against a local install that doesn't sit behind an AWS load-balancer, you'll see: ``` curl: (52) Empty reply from server real 2m0.012s user 0m0.006s sys 0m0.000s ``` **Expected behavior** We should not send 502s unless the API service is down. For example, CouchDB timeouts with a 500 error. We should also timeout with an error, and overwrite the default node http timeout: https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v8.x/api/http.html#http_server_settimeout_msecs_callback **Environment** - Instance: production, clone, local - App: api - Version: any? **Additional context** The default node http server timeout is 2 minutes in v.8 (https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v8.x/api/http.html#http_server_settimeout_msecs_callback), v.10 (https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v10.x/api/http.html#http_server_settimeout_msecs_callback), v.12 (https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v12.x/api/http.html#http_server_settimeout_msecs_callback). The default timeout is 0 in v.14 - equivalent to setting no timeout at all.

title: Login page redirect loop when password is changed
body:
**Describe the bug**
Our app handles getting 401s correctly while the app is open, but if you launch the app into a 401, you'll see a loading screen and a modal with no text. If you ignore the modal and just type the link to login, your login page will be in a redirect loop. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Login as an online user in a fresh browser. This user can even be an admin. 
2. Close all CHT-Core tabs in this browser. 
3. In another browser, as an admin, change the user's password. You can even use the same password the user had before. CouchDb encription involves a random salt, so the session will be invalidated either way. 
4. Back in the browser from step1, open the previously opened tab - basically open an app link like: /messages or something.  
5. See blank screen with modal that has not text. 
6. If you do nothing, the page will refresh after 1 minute and get you to login. 
7. If you manually go to `/medic/login`, the login page will go in a loop. 

**Expected behavior**
We should definitely never get into a redirect loop ever. Anything is better than a redirect loop. 

**Screenshots**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/125154274-e67d9800-e161-11eb-8ec6-1415d069068c.png)

**Video**
https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/125154128-242df100-e161-11eb-86c0-e365063365f1.mp4


**Environment**
- Browser: any
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.12 but I think this was happening for a while

**Additional context**
For the empty modal, I think the best way is to use the "bootstrap" translations for it, which are cached in the service worker. That way, it will have text even when the user can't access the server to get the translations docs. 
For the login loop, The solution I recommended in https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7186, which is to actually check _session in the login script, should fix this.

title: Scalability Workflow needs updated to use spot fleet instead of spot request.
body:
**Describe the issue**
When the Scalability workflow was first introduced I used spot requests instead of spot fleet requests to setup. This is causing capacity(AWS) issues with running in an automated fashion. Meaning the environments won't spin up because AWS cannot fulfill the request. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Convert the request to a spot fleet request. Will need to determine which instance types are ok to use and then update the scripts in `tests/scalability` to generate the spot fleet requests. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
There are other ways to setup environments on AWS but this is the cost effective solution.

title: Can't re-select message thread after deselecting it
body:
**Describe the bug**
In mobile view, you can't select the same message thread twice in a row. Clicking on the previously selected item does nothing. Clicking on another thread works as expected. 
The URL also doesn't change when going back. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Switch your browser to mobile view, or use a phone - behavior should be the same.
2. Go to messages tab and select a conversation thread. 
3. Click on the "<" button in the header: 
4. When the list loads again, click to open the same thread. 
5. Observe that clicking the same thread does nothing. 

**Expected behavior**
The user should be routed to the selected thread.

**Logs**
No errors in the logs

**Environment**
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.11

**Additional context**
This appears to be a regression in 3.11 Angular migration, and is probably related to renaming the parameter for the messages route, and it not matching the navigation check for `id`.

title: GitHub Action failing because of change to docker-compose location/contents
body:
**Describe the issue**
A [commit back in April](https://github.com/medic/cht-infrastructure/commit/fbe1da566d2af664cf1e23588e2840655420fd50#diff-38219779f5fcc301ef54b6a95ad7287532c7f0d20619c83aebc6c6034b5e7b72R24-R25) moved the location of the `docker-compose.yml` file used in the `medic-infrastracture` repo, specifically the `self-hosting/prepare-system/ubuntu/prepare.sh` script.  The new `docker-compose.yml` file does not allow for `DOCKER_COUCHDB_ADMIN_PASSWORD` to be set in an environment variable.   As such, CI scripts now fail because they can not login to complete testing.  

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We should likely enable the new `docker-compose.yml` to support the old functionality. The [original file is here](https://github.com/medic/cht-infrastructure/commit/883761e36a3b989c6c0711c0622fa413823a010b#diff-0fd6a68424d0e206753100aebe402f451f0026a3b8c28b9598127046fd70d8be) with this as stanza for `medic-os` container:

```yml
services:
  medic-os:
    container_name: medic-os
    image: medicmobile/medic-os:cht-3.9.0-rc.2
    volumes:
      - medic-data:/srv
    ports:
     - 80:80
     - 443:443
    working_dir: /srv
    depends_on:
      - haproxy
    networks:
      - medic-net
    environment:
      - DOCKER_NETWORK_NAME=haproxy
      - DOCKER_COUCHDB_ADMIN_PASSWORD=$DOCKER_COUCHDB_ADMIN_PASSWORD
```

Where as the one in `cht-core`, now being used by CI, looks like this: 

```yml
services:
  medic-os:
    container_name: medic-os
    image: medicmobile/medic-os:cht-3.9.0-rc.2
    volumes:
      - medic-data:/srv
    ports:
     - 80:80
     - 443:443
    working_dir: /srv
    depends_on:
      - haproxy
    networks:
      - medic-net
    environment:
      - DOCKER_NETWORK_NAME=haproxy
      - DOCKER_COUCHDB_ADMIN_PASSWORD=password
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Change the CI script to use the hard coded password in the new `docker-compose.yml` file.

title: Extend docker-compose.yml to allow for ports to be overridden to support developing for concurrent deployments
body:
App Services needs a way to use `docker-compose` to easily run multiple deployments with in a day.  As well, they may need to run two or three deployments simultaneously.  the current `docker-compose.yml` should be extended to:
* allow for external  ports on the host to easily be remapped on per deployment (aka per docker-compose override file)
* offer a prototype of how to override with at least two example files (eg deployment A and deployment B)
* in a private repo, we should publish docker compose documents for all of App Services deployments. This will avoid the issue of port conflicts with multiple deployments.  As well, it will standardize the ports that different folks use on the same team.

See [parent issue](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7061#issuecomment-832190318) for more info/context.

title: Add new docker compose file for App Devs, update existing compose file with env vars
body:
# Description

This PR does two things:
* Updates the existing `docker-compose.yml` to use default ports and passwords that can be easily overridden. 
* Adds two new docker compose files for use with app developers per #7211 .  These will be the basis of either being able to run N concurrent instances or lots of separate instances who's data persists and is discrete. 

## Testing

### Existing `docker-compose.yml`

This file should continue to work the same as it has before: `docker-compose up` in the `cht-core` repo.  However, you now easily override the default https and http ports like so:

* `CHT_HTTP=8082 CHT_HTTPS=8443 docker-compose up`

So that you would then access the instance here:

* https://localhost:8443

### Developer files

Formal documentation will follow on [another pending docs PR](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/pull/532), but for now, here's how to use the two new files:

```shell
docker-compose -f docker-compose-developer.yml up
```

And then if you want to run another instance at the same time on a different port, this should work:

```
CHT_HTTP=8081 CHT_HTTPS=8443 docker-compose -p another -f docker-compose-developer.yml up
```

If you ran both of these at the same time, you should have no conflicts with ports and volumes.  Your `docker ps` should look like this:

```
CONTAINER ID   IMAGE                                 COMMAND                  CREATED         STATUS              PORTS                                                                            NAMES
c078800c9025   medicmobile/medic-os:cht-3.9.0-rc.2   "/bin/bash -l /boot/…"   2 minutes ago   Up 2 minutes        0.0.0.0:80->80/tcp, :::80->80/tcp, 0.0.0.0:443->443/tcp, :::443->443/tcp         cht-core_medic-os_1
328b09c9b9e1   medicmobile/haproxy:rc-1.17           "/entrypoint.sh -f /…"   2 minutes ago   Up 2 minutes                                                                                         cht-core_haproxy_1
7acbc072b1b1   medicmobile/medic-os:cht-3.9.0-rc.2   "/bin/bash -l /boot/…"   4 minutes ago   Up About a minute   0.0.0.0:8081->80/tcp, :::8081->80/tcp, 0.0.0.0:8443->443/tcp, :::8443->443/tcp   another_medic-os_1
efd2e493e7f2   medicmobile/haproxy:rc-1.17           "/entrypoint.sh -f /…"   4 minutes ago   Up About a minute                                                                                    another_haproxy_1
```

And you should have two instances concurrently running on ports `443` and `8443`:

* https://localhost
* https://localhost:8443

Note: you'll have a cookie namespace collision b/c they're on the same `localhost` domain.  The work around is to user `127.0.0.1` on one instance and `127.0.1.1` on the other. Another solution is to use  incognito/site containers/different browsers.

See [parent issue](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7061#issuecomment-832190318) for more info/context.

There have been [some](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6456) [issues](https://github.com/medic/medic-infrastructure/issues/293)  where `docker-compose` has failed and it's unclear how to fix it.  

We should publish a bash script that can be run to check the health of a `docker-compose up` call.  Specifically it should:
* make sure the two containers are up: `haproxy`, `medic-os`
* make sure all services in `medic-os` are running: API, CouchDB, nginx
* offer helpful  tips on how to troubleshoot any of the services that may have gotten stuck
* be aware that there may be more than one instance of [medic-os running](https://github.com/medic/medic-os/issues/55) both in running `exec` calls the specify container name and that there may be port conflicts
* Be sure the admin password to CHT is easy to find.  It can some times be set to something unknown (alternately - just set forcefully to the same thing every time) 
*  publish documentation on [docs site](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org) on how to use this helper script and it's output.

It'd be great to have the script give a fixed output that users can get used to and easily find the information they're looking for.  Just brainstorming here, but this might look something like this:

```
-------------------------------------------------------------
                CHT Instance: Foo Bar Smang

     CHT Version: 3.9.1
     URL:  https://192-168-1-1.my.local-ip.co
     Fauxton: http://172.18.0.2:5984/_utils/
     Admin Login: Medic
     Admin Password: Medic321

     + Medic OS
           - horticulturalist - RUNNING ('horticulturalist/horticulturalist' started successfully)
           - medic-api - RUNNING ('medic-api/medic-api' started successfully)
           - couchdb - RUNNING ('medic-core/couchdb' started successfully)
           - nginx - RUNNING ('medic-core/nginx' started successfully)
           - openssh - RUNNING ('medic-core/openssh' started successfully)
           - medic-couch2pg - RUNNING ('medic-couch2pg/medic-couch2pg' started successfully)
           - postgresql - RUNNING ('medic-rdbms/postgresql' started successfully)
           - medic-sentinel - RUNNING ('medic-sentinel/medic-sentinel' started successfully)
           - cron - RUNNING ('system-services/cron' started successfully)
           - syslog - RUNNING ('system-services/syslog' started successfully)
     + HA Proxy
           - haproxy - RUNNING (May 11 21:32:59 0df0af7b7c90 haproxy[1]: Proxy couch-backend2 started.)
-------------------------------------------------------------
```

This is likely TMI and could skip a lot of the granular statuses.  However the top part I've had to go looking for a lot and would massively helpful to have easily accessible.

title: Empty integer values in Enketo forms evaluate to 0
body:
**Describe the bug**

The [ODK Documentation](https://docs.getodk.org/form-logic/#empty-values) specifies:

> Unanswered number questions are nil...  The empty value will not be converted to zero. The result of a calculation including NaN will also be NaN.

When a form in cht-core is saved with an unanswered number question, the value for that question is properly recorded as `''`.  However, if a calculation is performed in the form that references the unanswered number question, the value for the question will be treated as `0` instead of `NaN`.  So, if you have some other form element that is based on a calculation involving the number question, it will behave unexpectedly. 

**To Reproduce**

type | name | label | relevant
-- | -- | -- | --
integer | my_number | My Number |   
note | my_note | This is shown if number < 10  | ${my_number} < 10


Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Deploy the [test_form.xlsx](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/files/6901588/test_form.xlsx) to a CHT instance
2. Open the form
3. The label `This is shown if number < 10` is displayed even though there is no value for My Number.

**Expected behavior**

The calculation behavior should match what is documented for ODK (unanswered number questions are nil).  Notably, if I upload that same test_form to https://getodk.org/xlsform/ it behaves as expected and the note is not shown unless a value < 10 is actually entered for My Number.

**Additional context**

Originally posted to the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/odk-calculations-empty-integer-evaluate-to-0/1382).

It seems possible that this is caused by cht-core using an older version of `enketo-core` and this issue may be fixed by https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6345.  However, I was not able to find any issues/documentation in the Enketo project around this issue to indicate it was something that they fixed.

title: add docker compose helper script, update add-local-ip-certs-to-docker script
body:
# Description

See #7218 and parent #7061

This PR adds a `cht-docker-compose.sh` script to aid CHT app developers in easily starting up one or many local CHT instances with both a valid TLS certificate and are reachable on the LAN for mobile testing.

This code is entirely in Bash and leverages the wonderful [bashsimplecurses library](https://github.com/metal3d/bashsimplecurses/).  The files included are in the `scripts` directory:
*  `add-local-ip-certs-to-docker.sh` - This has been slightly modified so that it can now update any a container of any name instead of one just called `medic-os`.  Backwards compatible with existing functionality [and docs](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/tutorials/local-setup/#5-optional-install-valid-tls-certificate )such that it defaults to `medic-os` when no container is passed. 
*  `docker-helper/cht-docker-compose.sh` - The bulk of the new code is here.  There is [documentation in the readme.md](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/7218-docker-compose-helper-script/scripts/docker-helper/readme.md) which should be the basis of a testing guide.
* `scripts/docker-helper/docker-status.sh` - A simple script to show the status of all docker containers, even those non-medic ones.  Also (briefly) [covered in the docs](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/7218-docker-compose-helper-script/scripts/docker-helper/readme.md#too-many-containers).
* `scripts/docker-helper/docker.status.png` - screenshot of `docker-status.sh` for docs
* `scripts/docker-helper/helper.png` - screenshot of `cht-docker-compose.sh` for docs
* `scripts/docker-helper/readme.md` - the read me ;)
* `scripts/docker-helper/simple_curses.sh` - external library included locally for eas of deployment. Do not do code review or QA of this. That said, if you do, and you see anything bad, we should submit [upstream PRs](https://github.com/metal3d/bashsimplecurses/)!

### In scope testing
* Most importantly Just Works™ on Ubuntu >=16, Docker >=20 & Docker Compose >=1.27
* Primary actions of `up`, `down` and `destroy`  works as expected.
* works with N instances (I [tested with three no problem](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8253488/129422217-3d3f1f4e-e684-4cee-9310-045a7f248203.png)) - be sure to use [different ports in the env files](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/7218-docker-compose-helper-script/scripts/docker-helper/readme.md#port-conflicts) - bad things will happen if not!
* Can install a config with `medic-conf` (eg `cd cht-core/config/default&&medic-conf --url=https://medic:password@192-168-68-40.my.local-ip.co:8443` - oh oop - should be `cht` not `medic-conf` ; )
* Can use `horti` to upgrade/downgrade (eg `COUCH_NODE_NAME=couchdb@localhost COUCH_URL=https://medic:password@192-168-68-40.my.local-ip.co:8441/medic horti --local --install=medic:medic:3.5.0`)
* works with and with out `jq` 

### Extra fancy in scope testing
* Testing online for initial launch, but then using `/etc/hosts` [workarounds for offline compatibility ](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/7218-docker-compose-helper-script/scripts/docker-helper/readme.md#booting-with-no-connectivity)
* deleting cached images from docker hub and ensuring that `Medic Images` gets incremented and it waits to download the images (eg `docker image rm medicmobile/haproxy:rc-1.17 medicmobile/medic-os:cht-3.9.0-rc.2`)
* fails on projects with capitals (eg `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=MyFirstProject` in env file)

### Out of scope testing:
* Testing on WSL2 on Windows 10 (though Binod got it working)
* Testing on MacOS (though Michael got it working)

We'll do the out of scope stuffs [in the next ticket](https://github.com/medic/medic-os/issues/52) as needed.

title: Release 3.13.0
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [ ] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`.
- [x] Raise a new issue called `Update dependencies for <version>` with a description that links to [the documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/guides/update-dependencies/). This should be done early in the release cycle so find a volunteer to take this on and assign it to them.
- [x] Write an update in the weekly Product Team call agenda summarising development and acceptance testing progress and identifying any blockers. The release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` release testing can begin.

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development using this template:
```
@core_devs I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing.
- [x] Create a new document in the [release-notes folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/release-notes) in `master`. Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, that they're correctly labelled (in particular: they have the right Type, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate), and have human readable descriptions. Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes) to export the issues into our release note format. Manually document any known migration steps and known issues. Provide description, screenshots, videos, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: medic-conf,  medic-gateway, medic-android). Assign the PR to a) the Director of Technology, and b) an SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient.
- [x] Until release testing passes, make sure regressions are fixed in `master`, cherry-pick them into the release branch, and release another beta.
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Upgrade the `demo-cht.dev` instance to this version.
- [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/overview/supported-software/) and update the EOL date and status of previous releases.
- [ ] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
@channel *We're excited to announce the release of {{version}} of {{product}}*

New features include {{key_features}}. We've also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

Read the release notes for full details: {{url}}

Following our support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read our software support documentation: https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/overview/supported-software/

See what's scheduled for the next releases: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/milestones
```
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Task completion landing page
body:
# Description

Adds task completion landing page, which: 
- is only displayed to users that have "can_view_tasks_group" permission. If users are missing the permission, the page is not displayed. Default config is updated to grant this permission to the "chw" role. 
- is only displayed after submitted a task. Routing to the URL manually or using browser history won't re-display the page. 
- depending on the last submitted task, displays tasks that are "Ready" that belong to the same leaf type place. If no tasks are found or a leaf type place was not found in contact lineage, the page is not displayed. 
For example (with default hierarchy), completing a task about a: 
a) person that belongs to a clinic, will display all ready tasks for that clinic
b) clinic, will display all ready tasks for that clinic
c) person that belongs to a health_center, will not display the page
d) health_center, will not display the page
- if the page should be displayed (user has permission, contact belongs to or is leaf type place), but all tasks are completed, the page is not displayed and the snackbar should say "All household tasks completed". 
- when the page is displayed, navigating away from the page to: 
a) another random page (like contacts or reports)
b) a task that is NOT from the same leaf type place
the user should see a modal to confirm navigation, similar to the form edited popup but with different text. The modal should work the same as the form modal, with cancel keeping the user on the page and confirmation navigating away. 
If the user navigates to a task that is from the same leaf type place - whether the click is in the LHS or RHS list, the page should redirect to the task directly, without a modal. 
- the tasks displayed on the page should be identical to the ones displayed on the contact page of the place, including the styling
- For performance reasons (so the user isn't stuck in a loading screen for many seconds while waiting to display tasks), the page uses the tasks that are stored for the tasks list (main component), and cherry picks which tasks to display based on the previous task's contact. This list can become stale between recalculations - this behavior already exists in the tasks list. Also, the list will exclude the last submitted task. The tasks are re-cherry picked every time the main task list is updated. 
- Also for performance reasons, the associated leaf type place is "preloaded" into the store by the task content component, after the form has been rendered (while the database has downtime). 

Recorded telemetry when loading the page: 
- `tasks:group:all-tasks` - total number of tasks for the place, all statuses
- `tasks:group:cancelled` - number of cancelled tasks for the place
- `tasks:group:ready` - number of tasks in "Ready" state 
- `tasks:group:ready:<task_title>` - breakdown of "Ready" tasks by task task_title
- `tasks:group:modal:confirm` - when the user confirms the navigation modal 
- `tasks:group:modal:reject` - when the user rejects the navigation modal 
- `rules-engine:tasks-breakdown:some-contacts` - when fetching tasks counts in the tasks group page

title: Broken functions for xForm repeat_groups
body:
**Describe the bug**
Currently there are several functions (at least [count()](https://docs.getodk.org/form-operators-functions/#count) and [position()](https://docs.getodk.org/form-operators-functions/#position)) that are required when doing any kind of advanced logic in a repeat_group which do not seem to function at all within the CHT.  When any of these functions are included in a form they cause errors to be thrown when the CHT tries to display the form.  

<details>
  <summary>Example Error Log</summary>

```
inbox.js?_sw-precache=5ec5cb99da4ab03e3fd1d06910e2f057:3 Error loading form Error: ["FormLogicError: Could not evaluate: count( /model/instance[1]/test_form/plant ), message: Failed to execute 'evaluate' on 'Document': Type conversion failed while evaluating the expression."]
    at inbox.js?_sw-precache=5ec5cb99da4ab03e3fd1d06910e2f057:3
    at inbox.js?_sw-precache=5ec5cb99da4ab03e3fd1d06910e2f057:3
    at inbox.js?_sw-precache=5ec5cb99da4ab03e3fd1d06910e2f057:3
    at c.$digest (inbox.js?_sw-precache=5ec5cb99da4ab03e3fd1d06910e2f057:3)
    at inbox.js?_sw-precache=5ec5cb99da4ab03e3fd1d06910e2f057:3
    at Object.completeTask (inbox.js?_sw-precache=5ec5cb99da4ab03e3fd1d06910e2f057:3)
    at inbox.js?_sw-precache=5ec5cb99da4ab03e3fd1d06910e2f057:3
```

</details>

Not having this functionality prevents CHT forms from being able to do things like [repeating as long as a condition is met](https://docs.getodk.org/form-logic/#repeating-as-long-as-a-condition-is-met). 

**To Reproduce**

I have created a test form that illustrates the desired behaviors: [test_form.xlsx](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/files/6946288/test_form.xlsx)

This form works fine when previewed in https://getodk.org/xlsform/ but does not function when loaded in the CHT.  

**Additional context**

These issues might be (at least partially) related to the older version of `enketo-core` that is currently used by the CHT.  This issue should be revisited after the enketo-core upgrade is completed for #6345.

title: Simprints integration disabled
body:
**Describe the bug**
Simprints integration was disabled (or I'm missing something), apparently when we did the migration to Angular 10. I tried to use it with a demo app and I cound't make it work, and after digging into the code, looks like it was disabled with the intention to enable it again once related code were also migrated to Angular 10, but we forgot to re-enable it again, or finish the migration of the widget.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Install a Simprints app, eg. the [demo](https://github.com/medic/mocksimprints) app. To build the app locally, try the version in the branch from this [PR](https://github.com/medic/mocksimprints/pull/1).
2. Install the following [demo form](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/demo-forms/simprints-demo.xml)  in a CHT instance from _App Management > App forms_.
3. Try to fill a form from the mobile app, installed in the same device where the Simprints demo app is installed. Go to _Reports > Submit report > Simprints Registration Demo_
4. See the message _"Simprints isn't available on this device. ..."_.

**Expected behavior**
The Simprints widget should be visible instead of the message above, and should allows to trigger the Simprints demo app.

**Additional context**
The widget is disabled with a hardcoded implementation of a class instead of use the simprints service.

Code that disable the widget: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/6485177d7e71771165482e6dd725c7da791c6613/webapp/src/js/enketo/widgets/simprints.js#L32-L37

Code with the actual service class: [webapp/src/ts/services/simprints.service.ts](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/simprints.service.ts)

I think that just replacing the hardcoded implementation with the class in the Angular service should works.

CC @dianabarsan and @latin-panda that may know better how this work.

title: Race condition occurs when logging in as offline user with slow connection
body:
**Describe the issue**
When running a test for an offline user the service worker gets installed and registers. There is a race condition where `onupdatefound` is not triggered. This causes the app to log in and then sit on the "Downloading App..." screen.  

This can be recreated by checking out [this ](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/7236/files)branch and running `npm run wdio-local` on your local machine. 

This can be recreated in chrome using a local docker setup. 

I setup my instance using the `scripts/docker-helper/cht-docker-compose.sh`
Created an offline user. 
Cleared cache and unregistered all service workers. 
Opened a new blank tab. Set my network throttling to slow 3g
Navigate to my local instance https://192-168-1-215.my.local-ip.co/
Quickly log in as the offline user as soon as the login fields show. 
The app sits on Downloading App... page


**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Resolve the race condition or potentially find another event to wait on in the test. 


**Describe alternatives you've considered**
@dianabarsan  has put together a [change ](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/login_offline_user_sw_fix) that possibly fixes this issue but needs to be vetted more thoroughly.

title: 6981 launching external apps
body: # Description This PR adds: - An Enketo widget to launch an Android app. - An Enketo widget to display base64 images (images from apps are passed as Base64) This is a separate widget to give flexibility of using this feature in different places of the form. - A XPath function to parse from timestamp to date and be able to use XForm functions to format date & time. (RDToolkit returns timestamp, and kinda surprised that openrossa doesn't support timestamps) [Ticket](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6981) [PR CHT-Android](https://github.com/medic/cht-android/pull/199) [PR CHT-Docs](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/pull/540) # Code review checklist - [ ] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/style-guide/), documented if necessary. - [ ] Documented: Configuration and user documentation on [cht-docs](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/) - [ ] Tested: Unit and/or e2e where appropriate - [ ] Internationalised: All user facing text - [ ] Backwards compatible: Works with existing data and configuration or includes a migration. Any breaking changes documented in the release notes. # License The software is provided under AGPL-3.0. Contributions to this project are accepted under the same license. # Android app Launcher quick overview: a. Here is [a video](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Zua78y8Sxct0UyD7FLiXflZFWrmnJjHK/view?usp=sharing) of a couple of forms launching an Android app to give an idea of the experience. The Forms I used in the video are here: [form 1](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/10jkXm202Rzog7Ze2FPz09XyQTZr7mRaP/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=102537905337937373446&rtpof=true&sd=true), [form 2](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1L14yKSRX-JCgmQWSkmiT7hvLhPNO6Vn8/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=102537905337937373446&rtpof=true&sd=true), these are not final forms, they are test forms. b. More test forms can be found [here](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xd5RUVw15LCQFszrs1UlGrZs_rxQFGjd?usp=sharing), these aren't perfect, just for testing the launching of forms. c. One form can have multiple Android app launchers, the widget is attached with the appearance `android-app-launcher`. d. The widget can define the Android app's intent (action, category, type, packageName, uri, flags), just after it's appearance definition `android-app-launcher`: e. The widget can send extras to the the Android app's intent, by defining an inputs sections with the appearance: `android-app-inputs`. f. The widget can store data that the Android app returns by defining an outputs section with the appearance: `android-app-outputs`. Note that output fields will have the value only when the Android app returns a response (some apps don't return responses, so it'll be response null) because our current version of Enketo and because these fields will have a value after the response is resolved, the fields marked as readonly will be initially empty and Enketo will convert them to a `note` and will hide the input. A solution is to have a section for [previewing the data](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/10jkXm202Rzog7Ze2FPz09XyQTZr7mRaP/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=102537905337937373446&rtpof=true&sd=true) and copy the values from the output fields. g. Forms rule the game. We send data defined in the form to the Android app and we take the form fields to find the outputs in the Android app response, this way we process what we need only. h. Fields type text are supported. No selects, no radios, no checkboxes. i. Groups represent objects, uses the appearance `android-app-object`. So to have nested objects we make nested groups. Objects cannot be assigned to a field, that's why it should be a group with fields inside to map the properties. j. Data coming from the Android app and assigned to the widget output fields can be: text, numbers, booleans, objects and arrays (of text, numbers, booleans, objects). k. To assign arrays to the form we use repeats with a fix size, the array of string is a group with just 1 field and have the appearance: `android-app-value-list`, while the array of objects is a group with multiple fields or/and nested objects and have the appearance: `android-app-object-list` l. At the end of this widget we automatically append a button to launch the app. m. The data is being passed transparently between the app and the form to avoid extra complexity and keep the widget simple.
