title: Race condition in loading contacts can cause previously selected contact to load
body:
**Describe the bug**
Contacts page could end up loading the previously loaded contact if a contact change is received just prior to the contact being de-selected. 

**To Reproduce**
This is very hard to reproduce with actual usage, but it has been causing a wdio e2e test to fail intermittently. 
Example of failure is: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/runs/3297387483?check_suite_focus=true#step:18:282
This failure is quite common (once every 10 suites?). 

**Expected behavior**
The selected contact shouldn't be changed the the previously selected contact.

**Environment**
- Instance: GHA Virtual machine
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.12

**Additional context**
I added helper logs in the code, so I better understand what's going on, and reran the test locally until I got a failure. This is what is happening: 

```
routing to contact "health_center_uuid"
selecting contact "health_center_uuid"
set selected contact "health_center_uuid"
contact receives external change "health_center_uuid"
selecting contact "health_center_uuid"
set selected contact null <- navigating away from the contact content page, in the case of the test, we route to contact-edit to add a new contact
set selected contact "health_center_uuid" <- the callback from the external change contact load updates the state with the old contact, so the next time we load the contacts content component, the state is actually dirty!
routing to contact "clinic_uuid" <- loading another contact 
selecting contact "clinic_uuid"
contact receives external change "health_center_uuid" <- because the state is dirty when we load the component, the code reacts to a change of the previously selected contact
selecting contact "health_center_uuid"
set selected contact "clinic_uuid"
set selected contact "health_center_uuid"
```

title: Upgrade webapp to Angular 12
body:
# Description

- upgraded Angular and its dependencies to v12.2
- replaced the deprecated `karma-coverage-istanbul-reporter` for its successor `karma-coverage`
- `node-sass` is deprecated in favor of `sass` but we can't make the move because enketo's scss files rely on unsupported behavior https://sass-lang.com/documentation/breaking-changes/extend-compound
- added a CSP rule to allow an inline event handler required by Angular styles optimization
- added `cht-conf` as a `cht-core` dev dependency to be used in tests through https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/7083-upgrade-webapp-to-angular-12/tests/cht-conf-utils.js
  - `medic-conf` usage in `cht-core` is being replaced with `cht-conf`, you can follow the progress here: #7340
- bumped Node.js requirement to >=12.14.x for the webapp

With Node 8, deploying the webapp works but building it fails with the following error message
```sh
Running "exec:build-webapp" (exec) task
Node.js version v8.17.0 detected.
The Angular CLI requires a minimum Node.js version of either v12.14 or v14.15.

Please update your Node.js version or visit https://nodejs.org/ for additional instructions.

>> Exited with code: 3.
```
Are we okay with this requirement or do we want to hold off merging the upgrade until CHT 4.x?

n.b. `tasks-group.wdio-spec.js` and `db-sync.wdio-spec.js` might fail locally. They need `swRegister.js` from #7322 to work.

medic/cht-core#7083

# Code review checklist
<!-- Remove or comment out any items that do not apply to this PR; in the remaining boxes, replace the [ ] with [x]. -->
- [ ] Readable: Concise, well named, follows the [style guide](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/style-guide/), documented if necessary.
- [ ] Documented: Configuration and user documentation on [cht-docs](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/)
- [ ] Tested: Unit and/or e2e where appropriate
- [ ] Internationalised: All user facing text
- [ ] Backwards compatible: Works with existing data and configuration or includes a migration. Any breaking changes documented in the release notes.

title: WDIO node support is not inline with our requirements
body:
**Describe the issue**
Webdriver IO supports v12.16.1 as it is the latest LTS. We require min 8. This means that our tests are running in a version of node and may not catch an issue in the older version. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Determine a way to run our app in a node version that meets our requirements. My first thought is to run horti in a docker container and install the versions of node required in that container. That way the tests will still execute in a more current node and our app runs in a node we require. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

title: Add more granularity to startup telemetry
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently, the granularity of startup telemetry is limited to: 
- `to_first_code_execution` - which tracks how long it took for the browser to parse application JS code
- `to_bootstrap` - which tracks how long it took to bootstrap
- `to_angular_bootstrap` - which tracks how long it took for Angular to load
- `boot_time` - all of the above, summed

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
I'm particularly interested into breaking down `to_bootstrap`. 
Currently, bootstrap executes the following operations: 
- initial replication, only if required
- purging, only if required
- meta db purging, every startup deletes 1000 old feedback docs (if they exist) 
However more operations could be added in the future. 

At the moment, we don't know how long these operations take and how frequent they are (purging frequency depends on configuration, but also requires the user to be online). 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Don't track additional telemetry metrics. 

**Additional context**
Projects report that startup times are long, and when analyzing telemetry data, there are large differences between the minimum startup time and the maximum startup time within one reporting period. However it's impossible to determine which operation is time consuming and whether it should be signaled differently for the user.

title: Phone field invalid when editing a contact with a valid phone number
body: **Describe the bug** Phone field is highlighted as invalid when editing a contact with a valid phone number, because it already exists and can't save unless the phone field gets a new value. It should not highlight the field because the contact is the phone number owner. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behaviour: 1. Create a new contact with a unique valid phone number. 2. Save contact. 3. Click edit contact and modify another field that is not phone number. 4. Click save and observe how the phone field is hight lighted as wrong. **Expected behavior** Should not high light the field as wrong if the phone is correct and the contact is the only one assigned to that phone. **Screenshots** **Environment** - Instance: local (master) and https://gamma.dev.medicmobile.org/ - Browser: Chrome - Client platform: MacOS - App: webapp - Version: 3.11 - 3.12

title: Can't navigate to "new district" form when contact "person" edit is open.

title: FIND COVID-19 RDT Grant Deliverables - Due October 3rd
body:
## Intro

FIND has awarded Medic a grant to "accelerate the development and deployment [...] of COVID rapid diagnostic test (RDT) [...] into existing digital tools".

This issue is a catch-all issue that links to sub issues so we can track deliverables for this grant.  All of the Slack and Google Doc links will require Medic login. 

Here's the current flow showing two CHT forms: a provision form on the left and a capture form on the on the right:

![COVID19 form hierarchy_flow-CHT](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8253488/132567413-6efae9b2-484a-4ab6-bfc2-654349308644.png)

## Overview

Medic will:
* Extend the CHT Core and CHT Android to have a generic integrate with 3rd party solutions, but specifically  the [RD-Toolkit](https://github.com/dimagi/rd-toolkit/) to support a COVID19 configuration within the CHT
* Create a fully functional COVID19 configuration for the CHT which is a ready to use example on how to integrate with the RD-Toolkit based off the data model specified in the grant
* Provide documentation on how to implement this integration to an existing CHT deployment
* Announce and continue to engage with our constituents via blog and forum posts about this new features and configuration

## Specific Grant deliverables:

See [original work order](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1SVRqHhtFiMVJzbx6D2oBU3uT2yGV_IUEhEe3sFpk1N0/edit), but here's the specific items grouped into logical work chunks:

- [x] Update cht-core and cht-android to support generic 3rd Party integrations
    * [Parent ticket #6981](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6981)
    * [CHT-CORE PR](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/7248)
    * [CHT-Android PR](https://github.com/medic/cht-android/pull/199)
    * [CHT-Docs PR documenting generic integrations per above](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/pull/540)
- [x] COVID19 CHT App/Config -  see [cht-core branch](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/6981-covid19-config/config/covid-19) & [google docs with xlsx files
](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1eYdPMVMc43Dx2UBI3PVM3H9fy4fvPuaY)
   * Design and build Data Capture Form: Design and build a form that captures a minimum set of data  points and includes the necessary interoperability attributes. 
   *  Build a data model in the form of a common data exchange format for COVID-19, as specified by  FIND, into a module or form within Medic existing application [CHT] for use by existing customers and  new customers, specifically those in LMIC counties. 
   * Ensure the data capture form is available and operational on the application platform for at least two  years, or preferably longer. 
- [x] Data Export & aggregation Documentation - See [PR](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/pull/548) and [markdown preview](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/blob/6981-covid-config-reference-app/content/en/apps/examples/covid-rdt-reference-app.md)
   *  Design and build Data export: Design and build data export via a REST API in CSV or JSON, or  other suitable formats that will integrate with other commonly used platforms. 
   *  Provide a way to view aggregate data which will aid programmatic improvement in existing  dashboards 
   * Provide a method to export the data to other well-used data aggregation platforms in line with  industry standards, e.g. API. 
   * Create a reporting method within the existing reporting platform of the existing application, allowing  the review of aggregate data which will aid programmatic improvement.
- [X] Blog post and forum post - announcing new integration features and encouraging long term engagement - [Ticket ](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7329) and [internal draft](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1pbjkNnkJ9MIkgP-dGB3pCqkcgVUV1qz6AcBgRikhB4o/edit?usp=sharing) and [external draft](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1I_PXxEj9iDoQI5W8ACmYbvy9btqHDFTZvqGVIGsSCc4/edit) (both private gdocs link) - [Forum post](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/covid-19-testing-with-rapid-diagnostic-tests/1494)
   *  Deliver a communications plan and publicize the launch of the application to existing and new users  through user community and regular social channels 
   *  Governance: Provide guidance on how to build governance and communities of practice around  those forms to ensure continued maintenance and thoughtful evolution. 
- [x] Training material - See [PR](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/pull/548) and [markdown preview](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/blob/6981-covid-config-reference-app/content/en/apps/examples/covid-rdt-reference-app.md)
   * Provide training for users of the application that requires less than two hours of in person time. 
   * Provide training material in line with the proposal, with training being embedded in existing training  material as well 
- [x] Update 2 demo movies to final version - See #medic/cht-docs/issues/554
- [X] Final Report - [See final copy](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1K4V0zXMXcgvTat6qBTrDu7iGin2p8bnTf-jTEsBHF6o/edit)
   * Provide final report and demonstration of the data capture form being used end to end  including the export of data to another system. 


## Related Links

* All documents, including the grant signed statement of work, data model and more, [are here](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/12dsDzIrtrDXr1muBqOO3RShtT3WptwFw).

title: Uplift to use transform functionality from enketo-transformer
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**

Currently [we are using `xsltproc`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/e35c8c70ad880f96ddf0d9888c6f1e38f73ff62c/api/src/services/generate-xform.js#L22) to transform our XML forms into the HTML that Enketo uses. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

We could remove our dependency on `xsltproc` (and other custom transformation code (e.g. markdown conversion)) by switching to use the [enketo-transformer module `transform` function](https://github.com/enketo/enketo-transformer#use-as-module).

**Additional context**

Currently there is not a version of enketo-transformer that supports both Node 8 and 12. Version `1.39.0` [removed support for Node 8](https://github.com/enketo/enketo-transformer/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#1390---2020-03-26), but version `1.38.1` depends on at least one package (https://github.com/libxmljs/libxmljs) that will  not build with Node 12. So, this uplift cannot really happen until we no longer need to support Node 8/10.

Some (unreviewed) code for performing the uplift can be found in the [jkuester_uplift_enketo-transformer](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/jkuester_uplift_enketo-transformer) branch.   (This was started as part of the enketo-core uplift for #6345).

title: Investigate removing view queries from API startup code
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
Some of the API bootstrapping steps make view queries which means if there are a bunch of new changes then API blocks on startup waiting for view building to complete. In fact, the queries end up timing out which crashes API. While it does eventually complete the app is completely unavailable during this time which makes it difficult to work out what's going on. All requests get a 502 response because API is down.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Rewrite these bootstrap steps to use the magic [allDocs](https://pouchdb.com/api.html#batch_fetch) view if possible so that API startup doesn't block. As soon as requests come in the view rebuild will be triggered but API will be handling requests correctly. This is only possible if the docs needed all have a predictable ID prefix.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could add view building as a separate step in the bootstrapping process so it's clear what's going on, but that would still mean all requests would get a 502 response.
We could implement something like a [status page](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/2967) which could report on view warming progress so at least people would know what the issue is but it's better to remove the issue than to just notify about it.

**Environment**
- Instance: all
- Browser: N/A
- Client platform: N/A
- App: api
- Version: 3.6, but also detected on latest.

**Additional context**
This was detected in a call with LG where they split their db into two instances using replication.

Examples of the steps that need to be patched:

- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/services/generate-xform.js where it queries existing forms
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/translations.js where it queries for translation docs
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/config.js where it queries for translation docs
- Anything else you can find...

title: "field required" not shown when field is read_only, required, and has calculation
body: **Describe the bug** I have a form that has a field that is both `read_only` and `required` and **has a `calculation` value**. When the required field is not filled out, it turns red as it's required, but it does not show the "This field is required" message. Further, if you add a custom `required_message`, it does not use this either. The use case is, in the original discovery of the issue, when the field will be populated by a 3rd party integration (e.g. RD-Toolkit via app launcher [see docs PR](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/pull/540)). **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. make an app form with this contents (or use [attached sample form](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/files/7132068/test.zip)): type | name | label::en | required | required_message | read_only | relevant | calculation -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- string | the_status | The Status | yes | None Shall Pass  | yes |   | null 1. Upload the form to a CHT instance and try and submit it, but leave the `Status` empty (which , you know, it's read only, you have no choice ; ) **Expected behavior** The CHT turns the field background red and shows the error message: "None Shall Pass" **Actual behavior** The CHT turns the field background red and shows no error message. Further, it doesn't show the `required_message` if specified. **Logs** NA **Screenshots** Here's the field as `required` and `read_only`: ![required_read_only](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8253488/132592385-82386579-5b9c-465d-a8cc-7b043d51aa3d.png) Here's the field `required` but NOT `read_only`. title: Generate service worker in API
body:
# Description

Removes service-worker grunt task. 
Ddoc extraction no longer bumps the `service-worker-meta` doc. 

Service worker is now generated in API: 
 - once on startup, after migrations 
 - every time the main ddoc is updated
 - every time translations are changed (or added or removed)
 - every time the branding doc is changed
If the call to `sw-precache` fails, the process crashes. Other errors are caught. 

Config that we pass to `sw-precache` is unchanged, excepting: 
 - `ignoreUrlParametersMatching` now also includes `username` to fix the login page cache. 
 - `dynamicUrlToDependencies` for the login page receives the generated html of login page (that includes branding and translations), to make sure cache is busted at the correct times. As a consequence, the `login` controller now exports a `renderLogin` method that returns the generated login page. 
 
After the service-worker file is generated (and saved in the same location as before), the service worker meta doc is updated. Updating the meta doc is skipped if no changes are made to the service-worker script (if the sha1 hash of the former file matches the sha1 hash of the new file). 

This conditional upgrading of the meta doc was not entirely necessary, as the browser-side (native) service-worker code already skips updating if contents are identical. 

Migrates service-worker e2e test to wdio. 
Fixes race condition in bootstrap service-woker installation code, where registration promises only resolved when the service worker was already installed. On slow connections, where installation had not yet succeeded on the login page, the page would be left hanging.

medic/cht-core#7307
medic/cht-core#7242

title: Support xForm `digest` function
body:
Now that we are uplifting to a version of enketo-core/openrosa-xpath-evaluator that supports the xForm [digest](https://docs.getodk.org/form-operators-functions/#digest) function, it would be nice to support this function in the CHT.  

Unfortunately, the [node-forge](https://www.npmjs.com/package/node-forge) library that openrosa-xpath-evaluator [uses to implement that function](https://github.com/enketo/openrosa-xpath-evaluator/blob/f0b86d05f7082b907496d6e165aa39cc1e349281/src/digest.js#L11) is relatively large (Gzipped size is `72.51KB`). Because of this, we are excluding the node-forge dependency from our packed webapp (which, in effect, removes support for the `digest` function in the CHT).

If there is a need in the future for this `digest` function, we can revisit this decision.

title: Enketo Time Picker does not work on Desktop
body:
**Describe the bug**

The Enketo [timepicker-extended widget](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/18eb601f14be415600a9a69319b568485d819122/webapp/src/js/enketo/widgets.js#L12) should activate a time selection pop-over (similar to the year/month/date pop-overs) when activated, but it does not. Instead, when running in a normal desktop (not Android) browser, nothing pops up, but the time can be entered into the text box via the keyboard (and no errors are logged to the console). 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Open a form that contains a time widget:

| type | name | label |
| --- | --- | --- |
| time | time_select | Time widget |

2. Click on the "Time widget" box
3. Nothing happens...

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8441903/134071066-56689084-09e3-485c-ae1c-23ac4f4ce510.png)

**Expected behavior**

The Time Picker in the [Enketo Widgets Demo](https://enke.to/x/widgets) activates a time selection pop-over when selected.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8441903/134071195-9129d239-7079-4e89-bf9b-5cf2944e1d8e.png)

**Environment**
- Instance: Running locally
- Browser: Firefox, Chrome
- Client platform: Linux
- App: webapp
- Version: `master` branch

**Additional context**

When running on Android, the expected Android-native time picker is properly activated when a time question is selected.

Also, for the record the in-progress Enketo uplift for #6345 does not seem to fix this issue since the behavior is reproducible even with the new version of Enekto.

I have not been able to determine a cause for this issue, but I do wonder if perhaps it is related to the [bootstrap hacking that we do](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/18eb601f14be415600a9a69319b568485d819122/webapp/custom-webpack.config.js#L16)....

title: Autocomplete Selector question does not work on Android
body:
**Describe the bug**

Select widgets with the [`autocomplete` appearance](https://docs.getodk.org/form-question-types/?highlight=autocomplete#select-widget-with-autocomplete) do not seem to work at all when running on Android.

**To Reproduce**

2. Click on the question box and begin typing
3. See that no drop-down appears with filtered answers

**Expected behavior**

When using a browser in a normal desktop environment, a drop-down containing a filtered list of choices appears when you start typing.

However, when selecting the same question on Android, no drop-down appears. You can type in the box, but you are never able to actually select an entry from a list.

**Environment**

Also, for the record the in-progress Enketo uplift for #6345 does not seem to fix this issue since the behavior is reproducible even with the new version of Enekto.

title: Enketo form Month and Year Pickers are broken on Android
body:
**Describe the bug**

The Enketo date selection widget supports both `month-year` and `year` appearances which trigger pickers for just the month or the year, respectively.  These pickers function as expected in a normal desktop browser, but on Android they get overridden by our [custom android-datepicker](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/js/enketo/widgets/android-datepicker.js).  So, instead of displaying a picker for a year/month, the normal month-date-year picker is displayed on Android.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. On an Android device, open a form with a `month-year` or `year` question:

| type | name | label | appearance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| date | date_month_year | Month-year widget | month-year |
| date | date_year | Year widget | year |

2. Click on the question box
3. See that the normal month-date-year picker is triggered and not just a month/year picker like there is on the desktop.

**Expected behavior**

On the desktop there are specific pop-overs for choosing a month or a year.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8441903/134251264-dcd354c4-f2e6-46d8-a925-d1e8a87149ad.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8441903/134251304-dc39d55a-bf25-4abb-8e62-a7277f3e5d27.png)

But on Android, all you ever see is the month-date-year picker:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8441903/134251415-c6710a42-09de-4afa-b8dd-aa8f13b8e328.png)

**Environment**
- Instance: Running locally
- Browser: Chrome/WebView
- Client platform: Linux/Android
- App: webapp
- Version: `master` branch

**Additional context**

The in-progress Enketo uplift for #6345 does not seem to fix this issue since the behavior is reproducible even with the new version of Enekto.  There is an Enketo [date-mobile/datepicker-mobile](https://github.com/enketo/enketo-core/blob/master/src/widget/date-mobile/datepicker-mobile.js) that seems to have the purpose of enabling this functionality on mobile, but I think it gets overridden by our custom `android-datepicker`.

I think that we need to investigate whether or not we still need our custom `android-datepicker` (conversation about its origins in the issues linked below):
- https://github.com/enketo/enketo/issues/405
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/1691
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/1693

If we keep our custom `android-datepicker` we should consider enhancing it to support the `month-year` and `year` appearances.

title: Release 3.14.0
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [x] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`.
- [x] Raise a new issue called `Update dependencies for <version>` with a description that links to [the documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/guides/update-dependencies/). This should be done early in the release cycle so find a volunteer to take this on and assign it to them.
- [x] Write an update in the weekly Product Team call agenda summarising development and acceptance testing progress and identifying any blockers. The release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` release testing can begin.

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development using this template:
```
@core_devs I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing.
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases). 
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, that they're correctly labelled (in particular: they have the right Type, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate), and have human readable descriptions. 
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes) to export the issues into our release note format. 
  - [x] Manually document any known migration steps and known issues. 
  - [x] Provide description, screenshots, videos, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. 
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: medic-conf,  medic-gateway, medic-android). 
  - [x] Assign the PR to:
    - The Director of Technology
    - An SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient
- [x] Until release testing passes, make sure regressions are fixed in `master`, cherry-pick them into the release branch, and release another beta.
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Download the scalability results for the final build from S3 at medic-e2e/scalability/$TAG_NAME. Add the release `.jtl` file to `cht-core/tests/scalability/previous_results`. More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [x] Upgrade the `demo-cht.dev` instance to this version.
- [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/overview/supported-software/) and update the EOL date and status of previous releases.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
@channel *We're excited to announce the release of {{version}} of {{product}}*

New features include {{key_features}}. We've also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

Read the release notes for full details: {{url}}

Following our support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read our software support documentation: https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/overview/supported-software/

See what's scheduled for the next releases: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/milestones
```
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Gradually reduce purging batch size.
body:
# Description

Updates `docs_by_replication_key` emitted value to include two new properties for reports:
 - `subject` which is the determined report subject
 - `needs_signoff` whether the report has needs_signoff field
 
Updates purging library:

Changes affecting purging contacts + reports:
 - request `docs_by_replication_key` with `include_docs=false` in batches of 100.000 
 - for every `docs_by_replication_key` batch, filter out lineage emissions for needs_signoff (so one report is only ever purged once). All filtered emissions are pushed to an array. 
 - If the array of filtered emissions exceeds 20.000 entries, contact batch size is halved and current contact batch is dropped. 
 - If the contact batch size is 1 and the array of filtered emissions exceeds 20.000 entries, the current batch is skipped and the contact's uuid is added to a list of skipped contacts. This list is persisted in the `purgelog` file.
 - If the array of filtered emissions has less than 5000 entries, contact batch size is doubled (but never to exceed the maximum of 1000). Current batch continues, the increase will only affect next batch. 
 - The array of filtered emissions is shallowly hydrated with an `all_docs` request. 
 
Changes affecting purging unassigned reports, tasks or targets: 
 - Increased batch size to 20.000 to match the maximum report batch size that can be handled
 
Changes affecting all purges: 
 - using async-await + do ... while to break recursive promise chains and collect garbage earlier. 
 - existent `debug` logs are changed to `info`
 - added a bunch more logging to make purging status clearer
 - when purging fails, a new document `purgelog:error:<timestamp>` is created that contains the error, additionally to the already existent `purgelog` fields. 
 
Updates to `purging-utils` shared lib:
 - adds online-only roles array to exclude from purging

title: Upgrade google-libphonenumber from 3.2.22 to 3.2.23+
body:
**Describe the issue**
[Version 3.2.23 of google-libphonenumber](https://github.com/ruimarinho/google-libphonenumber/compare/v3.2.22...v3.2.23) introduced some change into the `isNumberMatch` logic that breaks the [describe isMessageFromGateway unit test](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/0e4c653890ce020064f7f0a07fa83c89ae7d06cf/shared-libs/transitions/test/unit/messages.js#L384).  I do not know what exactly caused the behavior change.

The `['+774455558888', '77-44-5555-8888', true]` test case fails because `false` is returned from `isMessageFromGateway` and that is because the [`phone-number.same`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/2c1db1618bdafc5ec14c3a27aa4a37249fcc1b4a/shared-libs/phone-number/src/phone-number.js#L109) function does not consider the phone numbers as matching.  This is because the `PhoneNumberUtil.isNumberMatch` function returns `2` (`SHORT_NSN_MATCH`) for the given phone numbers instead of the expected `3` (`NSN_MATCH`).  

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

It seems like we need to consider if the new behavior is desired and if we should update the `phone-number.same` function to account for the functionality (or update the the test case to reflect the new output).

title: Update mocha to latest
body:
**Describe the issue**
Upgrading from our current version of mocha (`7.2.0`) to `8.0.0` or anything higher causes the webapp unit tests to fail with an error similar to what is described here https://github.com/mochajs/mocha/issues/4660 and here https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/42834. It seems like there is some bad interaction between mocha and karma.

```
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
```

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
It will probably be worth revisiting this issue after #7083 has been addressed and we have a new version of Angular (however, the issues linked above indicate that the issue still persists with Angular 12, to this is unlikely to be the fix).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I tried several versions of mocha (`8.0.0`, `8.4.0`. `9.1.2`) and they all failed for the same issue.

title: Updates to COVID-19 RDT reference app
body:
**Describe the issue**
FIND has requested we make the following changes the [COVID-19 RDT app](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/config/covid-19) to better match [the data model](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1uAwoD1WRuFtF4zhXctS2QP9ygzBrgpJ4/edit#gid=1354426745).

### "other" RDT types

When provisioning a test, a CHW can select 2 "Other" options in RD-Toolkit resulting in a the `rdt_session_test_profile` field having a value of either `generic_c19_fifteen` or `generic_c19_twenty`.  We should account for this and conditionally ask the CHW which test they used.

### Expired RDTs

When provisioning a test, a CHW can enter a date in the past for "When does the lot or batch expire?".  When they do enter a date in the past, we should show an inline warning (but allow them to proceed):

> Warning: please use caution when using expired RDTs.  Test results may not be accurate.

### Handle symptoms differently

When provisioning a test, a CHW can enter "symptoms" of both "symptomatic" and "asymptomatic" which should not be allowed.  While this combination should not be allowed, we should be sure to allow  both “asymptomatic” and “history of close contact” for example.

As well, only show the long list of "What symptoms does the patient have?" when they have selected "symptomatic"

title: Webapp relative dates are not localized after Angular 12 upgrade
body:
**Describe the bug**
We officially support the following languages: English, French, Spanish, Bambara, Hindi, Indonesian, Nepali, Swahili, and 3 dialects from the Philippines (ceb, hil, tl).
We use `moment` locales for displaying relative dates for each of these languages. We use locales that come bundled with the moment library, except for the Philippines dialects, which we add ourselves. 
After the upgrade to Angular 12 https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7083 , the default moment locales are no longer bundled and all relative dates are displayed in English. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Checkout `master`. 
2. Make sure you have some older reports. 
3. Change your language to French. 
4. Go to the reports page and look at the date that is displayed in the list. Notice that it's not localized and is displayed in English. 

**Expected behavior**
Relative dates should be localized. 

**Screenshots**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/137667789-7ec3e2d7-683c-4720-aebb-8b14a27fccb8.png)


**Environment**
- Instance: local

title: Add Lighthouse job to CI run
body:
**Describe the issue**
We recently noticed we'd regressed and are no longer officially installable as a PWA. We want to be able to automatically detect when this happens in future. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Google Chrome includes a dev tool call Lighthouse which can detect this, and it's also [available as a CI tool](https://web.dev/lighthouse-ci/). Add a GH Actions job for running this with the `pwa` configuration. Consider if we should also use Lighthouse to check for performance regressions and other options.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Add a manual testing step, but this detects the issue late, and isn't as efficient for QA Engineers.

title: Stopping and resuming initial replication could start local purging
body:
**Describe the bug**
The way that we determine whether initial replication is needed is by checking whether the `settings` document and the `_design/medic-client` document exist on the device. If both of these docs exist in the local PouchDb database, we consider initial replication as _not needed_ and we start business as usual, including purging. 

After all startup steps are completed and the Angular app boots, replication will continue in the background, and while that is happening, the user has just partial access to their docs - which could cause generating tasks unnecessarily when reports that complete those tasks are not yet replicated. Will add another issue to cover improving how we detect if we should do initial replication or not. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Setup your CHT installation. Version must be 3.7+. Configure server-side purging. 
2. Create your user and upload all of their documents (make sure you have at least a couple of thousand, also make sure some of them should be purged). DO NOT update settings AFTER pushing user documents. 
3. Run purging on the server. 
4. Log in as this user. 
5. Immediately after you see the "Fetching...." counter goes over a couple of 100, refresh the page. 
6. See "Cleaned 0" for a while. (purging is running)
7. App boots - you don't have all of your documents so you may see errors, but this is beyond the scope of this issue. 

**Expected behavior**
Purging shouldn't run if the device has not been setup completely yet. 

**Logs**
No errors. 

**Environment**
- Instance: production
- Browser: any
- Client platform: any
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.7+

**Additional context**
We create a purging checkpoint _after_ initial replication is completed. If initial replication is interrupted, we don't create this checkpoint. 
The easy fix for this would be to create the purging checkpoint _before_ initial replication, which would ensure that purging is up to date in the event of an interruption. 
This was brought forward after one partner did a hierarchy change, and when doing the resync, many of their devices started purging instead of doing initial replication (purging from 0 is very time consuming if the user has many _total_ documents and the server is under load).
One workaround would be to push a _rev for the `settings` document, insuring that it's close to the end of the changes feed and not available early on the device.

title: Horti v2
body:
# Horti v2

Every ddoc stores a version, this is:
- the tag name for tags and releases
- the branch name + a timestamp for branch builds
- dev placeholder + a timestamp for local builds
Besides being saved as attachments to the staging document, built ddocs are stored in the API package (same format as the staging ddoc, a json file with a `docs` array property).

## On every API startup

The installation is checked: the ddocs present in every database (both staged and not staged) are compared to the bundled ddocs where:
- all bundled ddocs should exist in the database and
- they should have the same version

Scenarios:
- no differences found -> API just starts
- differences found in the uploaded ddocs, but the bundled ddocs are staged (same comparison as above, staged ddocs exist and have the correct version) -> API complete step (described below)
- differences found in the uploaded ddocs, and at least some bundled ddocs are not staged -> fresh install (described below)

## Fresh install or upgrade steps

### Prep
The previous incomplete installation attempt, if found, is aborted. (in-memory stored upgrade_log id or latest non-final upgrade log). 

Each installation or upgrade should have its own upgrade_log - this is a document that is saved in the medic-logs DB (???) and has a structure like:

```json
{
  "_id": "upgrade_log:<start_timestamp>:<upgrade_to_version>",
  "user": "<initiating user name, for upgrades>",
  "action": "<install, stage or upgrade>",
  "from_version": "<current version, empty when doing fresh install>",
  "to_version": "<future version, bundled version when doing fresh install>",
  "start_date": "<timestamp>",
  "state": "<one of: initiated, staged, indexing, indexed, completing, complete, aborted, errored>",
  "updated_date": "<timestamp>",
  "state_history": [{ "state": "<state>", "date": "<timestamp>" }]
}
```

The _id of the upgrade log is saved in memory. If API restarts, it will search for the latest created upgrade log, that is not in a final state (finalized, errored or aborted). <- this part might need more work. 
The upgrade_log document (has state of "initiated").

Prep stage is not executed for partial installs (when api starts and some ddocs exist and some do not). 

### Stage
Existent uploaded staged ddocs are deleted. (view cleanup is NOT called)
For upgrades, the definitions of the ddocs are downloaded from the staging server. For fresh installs, the bundled definitions are used in the next steps.

The ddocs (bundled or downloaded) are renamed to add the ":staged:" prefix (_design/design_doc_name -> _design/:staged:design_doc_name), assigned partial `build_info` and uploaded to their corresponding databases. At this stage, the `build_info` consists of:
```json
{
  "_id": "_design/something",
  "build_info": {
    "user": "<initiating user from upgrade_log>",
    "upgrade_log_id": "<the _id of the upgrade_log>"
  }
}
```
The upgrade_log state is set to "staged". 

### View indexing

The upgrade_log state is set to "indexing".

Iterates over all uploaded staged ddocs, for every known database, making a list of requests that start view indexing. These requests have a retry mechanism when the failure is a timeout. 
Starts querying `active_tasks` on a timeout (5 seconds) and calls the view indexing requests. The "summary" of `active_tasks` is logged to api logs (identical to the indexer progress in horti). 
Compared to `horti`, the results of the indexing progress summary are _not_ saved in the upgrade_log document. (big spam, think about it?)
View indexing resolves when all view indexing requests get 2xx statuses. Querying `active_tasks` is stopped.

The upgrade_log state is set to "indexed".

### Completing the upgrade (rename this to something else? finalizing? executing?)

This is not part of this PR. This will consist on calling the "upgrader" service upgrade endpoint that is supposed to replace the source code for API and Sentinel.
Big TODO

### Completing by API startup 

As part of the "installation check" mentioned above, we will find that either: 
- (1) all ddocs (for all dbs) are staged 
- (2) some dbs lack staged ddocs

#### For (2)

When not all ddocs are staged, we re-start with "Stage", "View indexing" and then finally "Completing".
Because we initiate the installation code in the old API, which is not aware of the new database existing, those ddocs are ignored.
Because we do not do view_cleanup at any of these stages, the old staged ddocs indexes are preserved, and we only end up indexing view for "new" databases (which should be empty). 

#### For (1), actual completing

TODO: get the upgrade_log _id from any of the staged ddocs. 
The upgrade_log state is set to "completing".
All staged ddocs are renamed, to remove the :staging: prefix, the current timestamp is saved in their `deploy_info`, and then are saved, thus overwriting old ddocs. 
TODO: instead of renaming ALL staged ddocs, match them against the ddocs in the bundle, and only rename the matching ones, delete the others.
The upgrade_log state is set to "complete".
Run compaction and view_cleanup on all databases. 

If any of the steps fails, the upgrade_log doc gets the status of "errored". 

## API upgrade endpoint

### GET /api/v2/upgrade (new endpoint)
- returns "current" upgrade_log contents and indexer progress
- will be queried by the admin app?
```json
{
  "upgradeDoc": { ... },
  "indexers": [{ "database", "ddoc", "progress" }],
}
```

### POST /api/v2/upgrade 
- needs version in payload
- starts an upgrade:
  - prep sync (request is resolved after prep is finished) 
  - stage async
  - view indexing async
  - complete async 

### POST /api/v2/upgrade/stage
- needs version in payload
- stages an upgrade:
    - prep sync (request is resolved after prep is finished)
    - stage async
    - view indexing async     

### POST /api/v2/upgrade/complete
- calls the complete step, which is TODO

### DELETE /api/v2/upgrade (new endpoint)
- aborts the current upgrade 
  - deletes staged ddocs
  - sets the upgrade_log state to "aborted"
  - deletes the upgrade_folder

This PR does not make changes to the Admin app (in the next PR), and does not add e2e tests for the upgrade process. 
Given that, with horti, we always end up with one ddoc (_design/medic), we're always in a "partial" upgrade state. Any e2e tests added at this point would need to work around that by adding some temporary code. I'd prefer to add final e2e tests, that would also cover partial upgrades, once we dockerize the services.

I think more "safety" measures, or edge case handling can be added throughout, also some things might need to get reworked as development progresses and we add the upgrade service.

title: Report export fields can be skipped if forms are edited over time
body:
**Describe the bug**
`/api/v1/export/reports` can export incorrect fields for forms that have changed over time. 

**To Reproduce**
Replicating is inconsistent, because the endpoint uses the "first" report for each form that would exported to generate the map of fields. However the "first" report is chosen based on it's uuid ("string" sorted first uuid) rather than a logical choice of "last reported" or similar. 

Steps to reproduce the behavior consistently: 
1. Choose one form and submit a bunch of reports. 
2. Export your reports by calling: `http://<host>/api/v2/export/reports?filters[search]=&filters[forms][selected][0][code]=<form_id>`
3. Get the "first" report's id by using this query: `http://<host>/medic/_design/medic-client/_view/reports_by_form?key=["<form_id>"]&group=false&reduce=false&limit=1` 
4. Edit this report in fauxton and delete one (or all) of its fields
5. Export reports again and compare the two csvs. The second export should miss all the fields that you deleted. 

Steps to reproduce the behavior inconsistently: 
1. Choose a form and submit a bunch of reports
2. Export the reports
3. Edit the form to add additional fields
4. Create a bunch of more reports
5. Export the reports
6. If one of the old reports is first, you should not see the new fields in the export.

**Expected behavior**
We should see at least all fields from the current version of the form, if it still exists on the server. 

**Logs**
No logs, no errors, just missing fields. 

**Environment**
- App: api
- Version: since this endpoint was added. 

**Additional context**
I believe we should have all of the "current" form's fields (if it still exists on the server) as column headers instead of picking a report "at random". 
This was not an easy option to include when this feature was first implemented, because we did not do any XML processing server-side. Now, with the generated model.xml, it's easy to get a mapping of "current" report fields. 

All possible fields is not an option, because we have no schema and everything is streamed, including reading from the database, but column headers are sent first and need to be compiled beforehand.

title: Users can view reports in contacts detail page despite lacking permissions
body:

We control showing reports on contact detail pages using `can_view_reports` permission. 
As of 3.11, lacking this permission does not hide reports on contact detail pages.

2. Create reports and make sure they are visible on the contact detail page. 
3. Remove `can_view_reports` permission from the user's role. Sync. 
4. Load the same contact page and observe reports are still visible.

title: Detect unsupported browser
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
With the switch to using webviews we no longer control the version of the browser, however we still have a minimum version the app will work with. If the app is used with an unsupported browser it will fail in unpredictable and hard to detect ways.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We need to work out which version we want to set as the minimum and provide a clear message to the user about how to fix it. I envisage this as a splash screen on load with a brief message on how to upgrade, or "contact IT support". A significant challenge is how to detect the unsupported browser. Ideally we would use feature detection for just the features we need, but between cht-core and all the libraries we use that's simply too many features. Browser version detection is difficult to do reliably, and the consequence of getting it wrong is significant. I think the right solution is to find a singular feature which was introduced around the right version of the browsers we support and test for that.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I've raised this in cht-core but it could be implemented in cht-android, but it's better to be tied to the cht-core version I think.

title: Extend add-local-ip-certs-to-docker.sh to install expired and self signed certs
body:
# Description

In working on some debug stuff for [this PR](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/7374), I really wanted an easy way to install self signed and expired certs.  I realized maybe some other people might too!

Better than some other [rando repo](https://github.com/mrjones-plip/mrjones-medic-scratch/blob/main/add-expired-local-ip-certs-to-docker.sh) ;)

Maybe not the right location for this after our efforts in #7413 - happy to move elsewhere if so!

## Testing

I had some issues getting this to work and found this simple test harness really helpful:
1. create a 1 line bash script `checkcert.sh`:
   ```bash
   echo|openssl s_client -servername 127.0.0.1 -connect 127.0.0.1:443 | openssl x509 -noout -dates
   ```
1. make it executable `chmod +x checkcert.sh`
2. run it every half second: `watch -n 0.5 ./checkcert.sh`

This way `openssl` will tell which cert is installed and when it expires.  

Another simple check (because I thought I was going crazy) which I'll add, is a simple way to check the hash of the `crt` and `key` files:
1. create a 1 line bash script `get-hash.sh`:
   ```bash
   docker exec -it medic-os bash -c "md5sum /srv/settings/medic-core/nginx/private/default.*"
   ```
1. make it executable `chmod +x get-hash.sh`
2. run it every half second: `watch -n 0.5 ./get-hash.sh`

The beauty of both solutions is that you can run `docker-compose down&&docker volume rm medic-data&&docker-compose up` and both `watch` commands will happily fail and then succeed across these very destructive docker commands.  `watch` for the win!

title: Allow CHWs to drill down through >1 levels of hierarchy in People Tab
body: **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** I'm planning a large deployment. Instead of having a more [traditional CHT area with all the CHT's families they care for under it](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/features/contacts/), our hierarchy is deeper like this: [](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8253488/148297032-f1dc29da-72e8-4f24-ad11-bbb87cb96585.png) If there's dozens of people in each household, and I'm responsible for 10s families, when I click a section in the people tab, the CHT will flatten all items beneath my area. This means the CHT will show me potentially 100s of profiles in the detail view. The problem is that we're lacking visibility into our hierarchy and the detail view in the CHT will likely take a long time to show 100s of contacts on screen at once. **Describe the solution you'd like** It would be great if a CHT could drill down in the people tab through as many layers as you'd like, with a default that can be overridden with a configuration. Only when, in our case, that you got to the household would you see contacts in the profiles detail view. **Describe alternatives you've considered** Likely we'll have test by mocking up a data set on a CHT test instance with our hierarchy and number of families, households and individuals. Using identical or comparable hardware as will be used in the field, we'll test to see how slow and awkward it is for CHWs to use the CHT as is today. **Additional context** None currently, will add as needed! **Why Now?** Partner(s): Guava Pineapple Reason(s): The CHT was originally limited to a fixed number of hierarchy levels so the need to drill down wasn't important. With configurable hierarchies available, more and more projects are using deeper hierarchies where users need to navigate through several levels.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
It is currently a manual process to get DHIS2 integration to work on a regular basis. It looks something like this:

1. Log into DHIS2 in your browser.
1. Upload the data from step 1 into DHIS2 via an import screen.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Automate the above steps so no humans need to be involved for reliable import into DHIS2.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The is a "no dev" solution that exists [using Apache NiFi](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1lyTNIR2KfnVXIY60bBweABCP5R67Fay1/view), but a CHT native solution would be much better.

**Additional context**
A number of partners have requested DHIS2 integration and if it's not automated it will slow or prevent adoption.

title: Release 3.13.1
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create an GH Milestone and add this issue to it.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR to the release branch. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version patch`.
- [ ] Write an update in the weekly Product Team call agenda summarising development and acceptance testing progress and identifying any blockers. The Release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` and backported to the release branch release testing can begin.

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing.
- [ ] Create a new document in the [release-notes folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/release-notes) in `master`. Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, that they're correct labelled, and have human readable descriptions. Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes/) to export the issues into our release note format. Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
- [ ] Until release testing passes, make sure regressions are fixed in `master`, cherry-pick them into the release branch, and release another beta.
- [ ] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [ ] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [ ] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
@channel *Announcing the release of {{version}}*

This release fixes {{number of bugs}}. Read the release notes for full details: {{url}}
```
- [ ] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

1. Use the default config to create a new place (district_hospital, health_center, or clinic)

3. Then on the "Would you like to name the place after the primary contact:" question, select `No, I want to name it manually`
4. See that a text box appears to enter the name, but there is no label

**Expected behavior**
The text box for entering the place's custom name should have a translated label (that in English just says "Name").

---

## Label issue for `patient_name` on `nutrition_screening` report

First reported by @tatilepizs here: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6345#issuecomment-1017767672

The patient's information is not properly shown for `nutrition_screening` reports when the patient does not have a `patient_id`.

1. Using an offline user, create a new patient and do not sync it with the server (so that it does not get a `patient_id` value)

3. See that the patient information is not properly shown for the report as in the above screenshots

**Expected behavior**

The report should show properly show the patient's name instead of their uuid or the CHW's name.

title: Add service user-creation shared library
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
To be used in CHT 4.0. Each service (api, sentinel, others that may come) should use their own users when interacting with the database. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add a shared library or update an existing one that will create a user for the service that calls it. Have this service only use that user when interacting with the database from that point on. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
User creation could also be in bash scripts that run in the container entry points but there are several disadvantages to that: 
1. Bash scripts are not easily testable
2. Since devs should own this feature, JavaScript is more familiar
3. With a shared library, there is less code duplication. 

**Additional context**
See discussion here: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/7452

title: Updates admin app upgrade page

# Description

API: 
- updates the `upgrade_log` to store the whole "build" definition instead of just the version. 
- adds new `upgrade_log` state `interrupted`. On startup, API will set the previous upgrade log state to interrupted. Exceptions are "staged" upgrades that are already fully indexed.

- updates confirmation modals to wait until triggered action succeeds or fails, and display error inline if failure happens
- in case of API failure during upgrade, the "progress" page will inform the user of the error and keep retrying to get progress form the server (every 2 seconds). When API restarts, the previous upgrade is no longer "active" and the page will reload with the versions list. It's a pending `TODO` to improve this, but didn't want to proceed with any changes without consulting design. 
- minor refactors to the upgrade controller
- adds unit tests for both admin upgrade and admin upgrade confirm. 
- when `upgrade_log` state is interrupted, displays a message and shows additional button to restart the upgrade. This action effectively restarts the upgrade with the same parameters as before.

title: Release 3.15.0
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining. - _[Milestone](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/milestone/98)_
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [x] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release. - _@mrjones-plip_ 

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`.
- [x] Raise a new issue called `Update dependencies for <version>` with a description that links to [the documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/guides/update-dependencies/). This should be done early in the release cycle so find a volunteer to take this on and assign it to them.
- [x] Write an update in the weekly Product Team call agenda summarising development and acceptance testing progress and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` release testing can begin.

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development using this template:
```
@core_devs I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing.
- [x] Announce the start of release testing on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*Release testing has started for {{version}} of {{product}}*
To get a sneak peak at this upcoming release, you can install `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` on your testing environment. We suggest you test your forms and workflows with this release candidate version and raise any issues that you experience. This helps to to discover any potential regressions that wouldn't otherwise be caught during release testing.
Keep an eye on the forum for the release announcement in the next couple of weeks!
```
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases). 
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, that they're correctly labelled (in particular: they have the right Type, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate), and have human readable descriptions. 
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes) to export the issues into our release note format. 
  - [x] Manually document any known migration steps and known issues. 
  - [x] Provide description, screenshots, videos, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes. 
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) and update the EOL date and status of previous releases. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.
  - [x] Assign the PR to:
    - The Director of Technology
    - An SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient
- [x] Until release testing passes, make sure regressions are fixed in `master`, cherry-pick them into the release branch, and release another beta.
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [ ] Execute the scalability testing suite on the final build and download the scalability results on S3 at medic-e2e/scalability/$TAG_NAME. Add the release `.jtl` file to `cht-core/tests/scalability/previous_results`. More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [x] Upgrade the `demo-cht.dev` instance to this version.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*We're excited to announce the release of {{version}} of {{product}}*

New features include {{key_features}}. We've also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

Read the [release notes]({{url}}) for full details.

Following our support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read our [software support documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/overview/supported-software/).

Check out our [roadmap](https://github.com/orgs/medic/projects/112) to see what we're working on next.
```
- [x] Add one last update to the [Medic Product Team call agenda](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AuJ7SerLuOPESBjQlJqpBtzwSAoVf5ykTT7fjyJBT0/edit) and use this meeting to lead an internal release retrospective covering what went well and areas to improve for next time.
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Add API to create many users
body:
**Describe the issue**
Currently it is a laborious process to create many users via the API/cht-conf. In some cases we require UUIDs to match up and in others it can [be a convoluted process](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/cht-conf-create-users-error-wrong-type-object-is-not-a-place/1647) (or both!)

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
An API that can be used directly to create many uses that is easy to use, well documented, and returns helpful errors when creation fails. Ideally it should create the contact, the contact's place and a user with correct role, place, contact and password.  Extra ideal would be if it could be tied into [magic link](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/concepts/access/#magic-links-for-logging-in) delivery to easy login.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Existing methods [as documented](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/data/csv-to-docs/#creating-new-users-with-new-contacts).

title: User stuck on spinner on app load on a poor connection
body:
**Describe the bug**
Reported on the forum: https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/spinner-loading-forever-without-text-core-v3-11-0/1680
We suspect the cause to be a poor connection to the server, but this was not confirmed. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create an offline user. 
2. Login with this offline user in a Chrome browser (desktop). 
3. Create a custom network throttling profile so you simulate fantastically high latencies. Enable this throttling profile.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/151487119-d063d233-37b8-41e3-957e-484d0cd724fb.png)
4. Refresh the offline user app. 
5. You're just seeing a spinner for as long as your throttling latency dictates (there are a couple of bootstrap requests). 

**Expected behavior**
A couple of options: 
1. Add a timeout to all "blocking" network requests
2. Always inform the user about what is going on (needs design?). 

**Logs**
No errors. 

**Environment**
- Browser: any
- App: webapp
- Version: *

**Additional context**
I wasn't sure what tag to set, so I'm tagging it as a bug for now, in case someone investigates and finds something that is bugged, outside of connection issues. 
Feel free to adjust as this progresses.

**Why Now?**
Reason(s): Users are unable to access the app during this time and do not know what is going on. This causes a loss in confidence in the app, unnecessary support calls, people are uninstalling the app and unable to reinstall, and consider themselves locked out of the app.

title: Update API users service to run and return results from all validation checks when creating users
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently, when creating a user, there are a few validations that the payload needs to pass: 
1. Checks for required fields
2. If token_login is enabled, phone number validation
3. Password validation

The checks are performed in a sequence, and return a human readable message when one of the fails. 
Should the payload fail multiple checks : for example missing contact and weak password, the UX would be like: 
-> call API
-> get error that payload is missing contact
-> add contact and call API again
-> get error that payload has an weak password

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Run all validations over one payload and return all failures to the user, so they can all be corrected at once.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Leave it as it is.

title: User Creation: Allow user, contact & place in one step for multiple users
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Using the [UI today](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/tutorials/contact-and-users-1/#implementation-steps), to add a CHW, you first have to create their place and their contact in the CHT app, and then go over Admin app and create their user, selecting the contact and place you just created.  There is the additional overhead of delivering the credentials after the account has been created. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
It would be great if admins could have a way to do this in fewer steps to streamline the account creation. To make this really amazing, if the CHT could [automatically send a magic link](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/concepts/access/#magic-links-for-logging-in) to the user.

Some features we should accommodate in the UX:
* error handling in tabular input (missing fields, unique phone numbers)
* allowing use to skip rows (fill out 2nd and 4th rows only) and still save data
* explanatory labels in admin form should be configurable, thus taken from translations

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Use the existing manual process.

**Additional context**
A number of partners have expressed interested in having the ability of the respective Ministries of Health being able to do this with out the use of a command line in an efficient manner for a small number of users at a time. 

Per the continuous discover process: 
* [story map](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1XufQZEShpWXPel9azisVQlPPaoPpufpKijkRMhAw8K8/edit#slide=id.gfbfc44f19a_0_0) 
* [solution selection](https://docs.google.com/document/d/18MN-e2z-OwcHBE2EvfH5yIKHnVCL7hWvvncYtNeF81I/edit#heading=h.g1sek8njjyb7)
* [Interviews](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1x0ef7bXn2wytCCLFAmFw3tKovx2ZPoEi)

**Why Now?**
Partner(s): Guava Pineapple
Reason(s): A partner will be blocked by this for a major release or expansion

title: Translations not working when using repeat groups with dynamic repeat count
body:
**Describe the bug**
When using a repeat group with the repeat count set to a dynamic field, the text inside the repeat group appears in English even though the language is set to Nepali.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Deploy 3.14
2. Upload this form: https://gist.github.com/dianabarsan/144fd2a781dd989648d21c2f8ad5954c
3. Switch your language to Nepali
4. Open the form and increase the number of repeats. 
5. See that subsequently added repeats are not translated

**Expected behavior**
Repeats should pick correct translations for fields. 

**Screenshots**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/153863642-995ffca2-4b55-4c5d-b2c6-c68817bbb238.png)


**Environment**
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.14 (introduced in 3.14, working in 3.13)

**Additional context**
Originally reported on the forum: https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/translations-not-working-when-using-repeat-groups-with-dynamic-repeat-count/1713

This appears to be cause by [this change](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/commit/d6c83f92168a80b5ebdb7409f8ac61909a54928c#diff-35f326c2c6a97b7394203d191a6128becef8e55244826f4126d53ebcc4494267R295) where we only apply the language to new fields when a certain button is clicked. In the case of this form, repeats are added by increasing the number in an input field.

title: Check Free Disk Space Before Running Upgrades or Corresponding View Warming
body:
Couchdb view warming is a part of the upgrade process. This process doubles the size of views and tends to fill up disk space if there isn't enough of it.  Upgrades get stuck midway if the disk fills up.

The solution would be to check for available disk space before launching upgrades and warn the user if the disk is likely to fill up mid-upgrade. If we are confident about the disk space calculations, it might even make sense to not continue upgrades before disk space has been increased. A rough calculation would be to prepare for a doubling of all the view indexes.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR to the release branch. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version patch`.

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` and backported to the release branch release testing can begin.

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing.
