title: Register feedback doc when forms fail to load
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
We catch all errors that happen when forms fail to load ([an example](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/e8406d3e384cdbc48faa87e7134162b94a0bca33/webapp/src/ts/modules/contacts/contacts-edit.component.ts#L172)). However we don't register feedback docs when these crashes happen. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Create a feedback doc when a form fails to load. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Find some way to trickle down the error further so it gets in the automatic feedback doc capturing mechanism. 

**Additional context**
https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/help-understand-and-fix-error-loading-form-please-try-again-or-check-with-an-administrator/1681/9

title: Improve UX in initial and subsequent loads
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
During loading, there are stages that doesn't provide any information to the user about what's happening. The experience is a white screen with a loading spinner, no additional information, lasting for minutes in slow internet connections, the user might think the app is broken. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Display information, loading spinner is never displayed alone. 

**Additional context**
[See discussion in this other ticket. ](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7492)

title: Improve initial replication
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The user can experience slow initial load of the app. Quoting from [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7492#issuecomment-1038607050):

> I have particular concerns about the initial replication stage which I suspect could be causing significant issues in production when the connection is dropped before the first batch of docs is returned. If that happens I think the initial replication will start again from 0 because the replication API for Pouch and Couch doesn't store checkpointers for partial batches - you need to fill up the entire batch of 100 docs before Pouch will record progress. Particularly with new users to servers with a lot of historical changes this may take some time.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Find a way to not start replication from zero if it already has replicated some. 

**Additional context**
[See discussion in this other ticket. ](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7492)

title: Increase Enketo's size limit for uploading files
body: **What feature do you want to improve?** Increase Enketo's size limit for uploading files in forms. **Describe the improvement you'd like** Currently CHT-Core's Webapp has [a limit of 32Kb](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/43a94fc4813c7ee2e989f34e75346924107fff36/webapp/src/js/enketo/widgets.js#L4), it's quite small for today's media and it's unlikely that CHWs will know how to compress files or change their recording settings. Also, some projects have upgraded the CHW's phones having more capacity to record and store media, however, some other projects might still use low-end phones. Probably the Enketo's limit was added back in 2017 because of [phones with little storage capacity](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/3096#issuecomment-337528667). This [other issue](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6699) relates to the limitation of having forms with big attachments and when using low-end phones. **Additional context** CHT-Core's API has a limit of [32MB for request's bodies](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/routing.js#L60), it was added back in 2015 and it's not clear why setting 32MB ([ExpressJS's default is 100KB](http://expressjs.com/en/resources/middleware/body-parser.html)). CHT-Core's PouchDB had been configured to match up this number and [prevent sending requests](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/e8406d3e384cdbc48faa87e7134162b94a0bca33/webapp/src/ts/constants.ts#L19) that exceed this limit. This means that it won't sync forms to the server, if the body length exceed 32 million. **Describe alternatives you've considered** - Increase [Enketo's limit](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/43a94fc4813c7ee2e989f34e75346924107fff36/webapp/src/js/enketo/widgets.js#L4) to 30MB and see if we can validate the total form size before saving and present an error to the user so they can take actions accordingly, and not let it failing until the user syncs. - Initially we considered adding a new configuration option in app-settings to specify Enketo's size limit for uploading files. But this idea was dropped because of the request's body limit in PouchDB and API. - A more complicated purging system, like, what if we just purged attachments. There are plans of [stopping saving raw XML](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5549) that would help saving some space.

title: Clarify support for file uploads and accepted media types
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently, we impose no limitation on what file uploads we support in Enketo forms. 
For example file form: https://gist.github.com/dianabarsan/f325fe0070c690df634822a0525556b1
This form has a photo, video, audio and "*/*" mediatype upload inputs. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Clarify whether or not we support non-image media type uploads. 
If we do, add support to actually handle these uploads in webapp, and show either previews or download links. 
If we don't, change the way we handle the form to inform configurers that these uploads are not supported (ideally before the form is uploaded). 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Hide fields we don't support? 
Change the form transform so upload fields are removed? 

**Additional context**
Ran into this while reviewing new work on cht-android to support file uploads.

title: Release 3.14.2
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [X] Create an GH Milestone and add this issue to it.
- [X] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR to the release branch. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version patch`.
- [x] Write an update in the weekly Product Team call agenda summarising development and acceptance testing progress and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The Release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` and backported to the release branch release testing can begin.

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing.
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
    - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
    - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, that they're correctly labelled (in particular: they have the right Type, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate), and have human readable descriptions.
    - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes) to export the issues into our release note format.
    - [x] Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
    - [x] Add a link to the new release page in the [Release Notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) section.
    - [x] Assign the PR to:
        - The Director of Technology
        - An SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient
- [x] Until release testing passes, make sure regressions are fixed in `master`, cherry-pick them into the release branch, and release another beta.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Before #7068, we used to collect the user's language in the app forms inputs such as bellow

title: Refactor Enketo service code to allow for reuse by test harness
body:
Refactors code for Enketo forms to allow for reuse by https://github.com/medic/cht-conf-test-harness.  The goal of these changes is to minimize the amount of duplicate code required in the test harness for working with Enketo forms. This should make it easier to maintain the test harness going forwards (simplifying the process of uplifting to new versions of Enketo/cht-core).

@kennsippell has been working on integrating the test harness with this refactored code in https://github.com/medic/cht-conf-test-harness/tree/enketo-uplift.

Changelist:

- api/
  - The `generate-xform` service contained logic both for generating the xForm html files and for updating the forms stored on the client when one changed. This update logic was discrete from the generation logic and had some dependencies that caused issues for the test harness code when trying to consume the generation logic. So, I have refactored the update logic into a new `update-xform` service. 
- webapp/
  - The logic in the `enketo` Angular service is the main bit that we want to be able to reuse in the test harness. To do this, I had to decouple it from all the Angular-specific code and services.  I created the `enketo-form-manager.js` which contains the refactored logic and can be pulled in by both the test harness and the `enketo` service.
  - The `enketo-prepopulation-data` service was only used by the `enketo` service, so I have refactored it into the `enketo-data-prepopulator.js` that is consumed directly by `enketo-form-manager`.
  - The `xpath-element-path` provider was only used by the `enketo` service, so I have refactored it into `xpath-element-path.js` that is consumed directly by `enketo-form-manager`.
  - The logic in the `contact-save` service is also needed by the test harness (to save their contact forms). So, I have refactored this logic into `contact-saver.js`.
    - The `EnketoFormManager` exposes the `contact-saver` functionality via the `saveContactForm` method to give a single point of reference for rendering and saving all Enketo forms.
    - I have updated the `enketo` service to have a `saveContactForm` method that can be used by the `contacts-edit` component to save the contact form (instead of using the (now removed) `contact-save` service).
  - The logic in the `enketo-translation` service was only being used by code that is now centralized in the `enketo-form-manager`. I have refactored that logic into a `enketo-data-translator.js` which is referenced directly by enketo logic.

#7462

title: Make facility lineage available for reading to offline users
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Offline users don't have access to their facility's lineage. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We could grant **read-only** access to the whole facility lineage for an offline user. 
Blocking edits would be best done at device level, blocking at server level would cause conflicts at device level, and thus unforeseeable inconsistencies. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Embed facility lineage information in a document that the user already has access to. 
- Don't do anything

**Additional context**
Historically, there were discussions where storing workflow-related data in place docs, and allowing CHWs access to their whole facility lineage was an option (one I can remember was this: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/4771). 
Another request came in [through the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/lineage-filter-in-summary-contact/1790/3)

title: API startup status page
body:
# Description

Starts API server immediately, but with a different router that: 
- sends a 503 and error message if the request wants JSON 
- resolves with an html page otherwise
- the html page periodically queries an endpoint `/progress`, and updates the startup progress: 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/175941224-7031b9be-21f8-47d6-b0a5-5fc1ef666746.png)

The router replaced with the previous router at runtime, after all startup steps have been completed. 

**optionally** 
I've also added a warm views startup step that runs even when the installation is valid. This is so the startup page shows up even when, for example, a full install has been replicated to a new database and none of the views are warmed. 
This has a significant drawback, because any potential and insignificant API restart could mean downtime if certain views are not used. We could select a handful of "required" views that should always be up to date, or not warm views at startup at all. 

medic/cht-core#2967

# Description

Instead of relying on xml attachments, uses report fields to populate form model on report edits. 
Some changes have been required: 
1. db-doc fields will be saved in the main report fields. To maintain old report content display, these fields will become "hidden".

title: Release 3.15.0-FR-bulk-user-upload
body:
When development is ready to begin on a [Feature Release](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/feature_releases/#release-names), an engineer on the appropriate Care Team or Allies should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are followed, though not necessarily doing the work themselves.

# Planning

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.
- [X] Have an actual named deployment and specific end user that will be testing this Feature Release. They need to test in production, on the latest version. No speculative Feature Releases.
- [X] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release. - @latin-panda  \o/

# Development

- [x] Create a new release branch in `cht-core` from the most recent release and call it  `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-FR-<FEATURE-NAME>`. If latest is `3.15.0` and the feature is to "allow movies to be uploaded", call it `3.15.0-FR-movie-upload`. Done before the release so all PRs can be set to merge to this branch, and not to `master`.
- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <feature-release>`.
- [x] Ensure QA is briefed and is partnering with the Trio to ensure early and often checks of the feature are on track to be of production quality from the start.

# Releasing

This is an iterative process and it's assumed there will be multiple numbered releases throughout development of the Feature Release.

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-FR-<FEATURE-NAME>-1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing. If an updated Feature Release is needed, increment the last `1` by calling it `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-FR-<FEATURE-NAME>-2` etc.

# Close-out

- [x] Validate with the actual end user that this Feature Release delivers a quantifiable improvement.  If yes, plan on adding the feature to the next minor release by creating a new ticket to merge the code to `master`.  If no, we leave the code dead in this branch, never to be merged to `master`, but still loved all the same.
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Investigate webapp behavior and performance after running in background for days
body:
**Describe the issue**
It was recently discovered that, when running webapp in cht-android (webview build), without closing the app entirely, it can stay running in the background for days (I believe this depends on Android version, device battery settings and maybe other things). 

What we were seeing before was that, every time we re-opened the cht-android app, webapp would go through bootstrapping. 
What we're seeing now, and has been confirmed by both telemetry docs and @tatilepizs , is that the app can stay in the background for days and resume operations directly after being opened. 

We have also had reports that, after the app was in the background for a few days, initial loading of tabs was very slow: 
https://github.com/medic/config-nssd/issues/74#issuecomment-1116993284 

> Data did not load quickly in various application tabs (reports, tasks, people) after the tab stayed dormant for a few days. It did load after 10-20 mins

(thanks @PrjShrestha for the summary)

A few startup tasks (purging) require the application to go through bootstrapping on a regular basis. 

**Describe the investigation you'd like**
We should investigate application performance after it was been in the android background for a few days. 
We should also determine whether we want to forcefully reload the app at certain intervals to make sure that the startup tasks are performed, OR change the startup tasks to execute at other times as well. 

**Measurements**
We should check for:
- memory usage
- memory leaks
- CPU usage
- general application speed when online (open the app again after some days and be online)
- general application speed when offline (open the app again after some days and be offline)

One thing to note is that, for offline users, tasks emissions get recalculated every 7 days. So we should check how quick the app is when it's reopened and task emissions are still fresh (less than 7 days), and when task emissions are stale (older than 7 days). 

**Additional context**
Some information in the slack chat: https://medic.slack.com/archives/C024KTGRW/p1651125477412039
We were seeing telemetry docs that were lacking `boot_time_x` fields. It was confirmed by @tatilepizs that, on certain devices, the app stays in the background and never re-boots, and in these cases, telemetry docs were lacking `boot_time_x` (this is expected).

title: Update the release notes generation script to pull together list of fixed vulnerabilities in npm modules
body:
**Describe the issue**
When we make a release we update our dependencies at the same time to keep our code healthy and make sure known vulnerabilities, bugs, and other issues are resolved. However, none of this info is communicated to our partners.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Automate a script which collects the list of known vulnerabilities that have been fixed in this release. This could be added to the existing release notes generation script to append a new section at the bottom. This section needs some verbage to explain what these vulnerabilities actually are, and that we haven't verified that they were actually exploitable in the CHT, etc.

The low cost solution is to run something like `npm audit --json --package-lock-only --omit=dev` which finds vulnerabilities in the current package lock file. This should be done everywhere there's a package.json file (webapp, admin, api, sentinel, shared-libs, etc), merged together, and uniqued, and sorted by severity. Then check out the previous version and do the same, then compare the two lists to only include the disclosures that have gone away.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could just leave it.

body:
**Describe the issue**
In #7609 we added a process for releasing versions of Feature Releases as beta releases.  However, they do not show up under beta releases when giving them a `-beta.N` tag (EG `3.15.0-FR-bulk-user-upload-beta.3`, see [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases/tag/3.15.0-FR-bulk-user-upload-beta.3)): 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8253488/170333762-8cdeac84-584b-485e-9852-d439505443c5.png)

Further, in the top of the admin you can't tell which date/version you're on.  This one is running `beta.3`:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8253488/170360974-f34d5218-8e29-4c7e-a9c4-df888b1bea5a.png)

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
I would like the CD process to show these under a new "Feature Release Beta" section and show the version (eg `-beta.1`, `-beta.2` etc). As well, after installing it should show which version you have installed instead of just the un-versioned branch name.

I suspect this will have to do with how the [Medic Builds repo works](https://github.com/medic/medic-builds-repo/blob/master/ddocs/builds/views/lib/version.js#L32)?

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Have users of the FRs check the dates of the releases listed in the "Branches" section.  However, they'll get weird warnings like this:

> You are about to upgrade from 3.15.0-FR-bulk-user-upload to 3.15.0-FR-bulk-user-upload.

title: Fix `npm ci` hanging
body:
# Description

`npm ci` hangs when installing `grunt-contrib-watch` because it's trying to fetch the remote heads and tags of the project's github repository
```
npm sill pacote Retrying git command: ls-remote -h -t git://github.com/scdf/grunt-contrib-watch.git attempt # 2
```

For an unknown reason, `git ls-remote -h -t git://github.com/scdf/grunt-contrib-watch.git` times out whereas `git ls-remote -h -t https://github.com/scdf/grunt-contrib-watch.git` works normally.

This change makes npm install `grunt-contrib-watch` and `openrosa-formlist` from github over https to avoid running into that timeout error.  
We should maybe raise an issue to @github

title: Add ability to sort hierarchy places in webapp by custom field
body: Currently hierarchy types are sorted in webapp alphabetically as [documented here](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/hierarchy/#app_settingsjson-contact_types). We have a deployment where there are hundreds of households registered in webapp and CHNs (FCHVs) are having hard time navigating to particular household. Currently when registering households, we're capturing house number as well and CHNs had a request to sort those places by household numbers. However, with current option it looks like we can either sort by name or by `dob` by setting `sort_by_dob` to true. This is a request to allow sort by custom key in webapp, so that we can address this request for example household_id, or any configurable key.

**Additional context**

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/41e6582b4c2ce9831428bcc30d05b422ad45cf1c/scripts/conflicts/diff.js#L25

title: Tasks content page sometimes throws ExpressionChangedAfterItHasBeenCheckedError
body:
**Describe the bug**
When running a webapp development build, and running the wdio e2e tests, the [task-group](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/e2e/tasks/tasks-group.wdio-spec.js) suite sometimes fails with 
```
Error: Feedback docs were generated during the test.
```

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Run a webapp dev build locally. (the error is only thrown in dev builds!)
2. Run the wdio e2e tests suite or manually replicate the task group test actions.
3. Check the console for errors.

title: Report's filter redesign
body:
We are working on incremental updates to the UI/UX of the CHT to be more scalable, intuitive, mobile-first and consistent with other Android experiences. The first step of these incremental updates relates to how Filters are handled on the Reports tab.  

### Updated Filter Design
The new design decouples the search and filter functionalities. The user is able to view filters by tapping on the filter icon. This opens a drawer with a list of filter types. By tapping on the dropdown arrows, the user is able to view detailed filter options and tap on the appropriate checkboxes.  This helps simplify the filtering experience by providing a cleaner interface and clearer labels that allows for better scalability.

<details>
<summary> The old version can be seen here </summary>
The old design allowed users to select the type of filter from a row of drop downs with icons. Each filter type expands and users are able to filter content by selecting the appropriate checkboxes. The search icon expands to show a search bar.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/66472237/174545990-39d95647-5aa9-46fe-9357-fee14277602f.png)
</details>

![Untitled drawing](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10096985/185024221-6130c9b1-4801-4d42-a644-e39a59120df9.png)



### Implementation

The Old _and_ New version of the filters interface will be available for a period of time. By default, users will see the new version.  You can have users continue to see the old version by giving them the `can_view_old_reports_filter` [permission](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/user-permissions/) but... _**the old version will be removed in a future release so it is important to have a plan to get users onto the new version ASAP.**_

### Additional context
[CHT Documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/features/reports/#filters--search)
[Forum Post](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/feature-testing-filters/1917)

title: Ignore invisible characters in Unicode for certain SMS fields
body:
_[Already reported in the CHT Forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/hidden-characters-in-unicode-ruining-sms-reports/1942)_

**Describe the issue**
Hidden characters in Unicode are causing some SMS reports to be considered invalid.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Ignore the hidden characters for fields such as form codes, numeric fields, dates, etc.
We might need to research the Unicode subset ranges to filter out control characters, formatting characters etc. The most commonly encountered such characters in the Nepali (Devanagari) script so far are:

- U+200C: [Zero-width non-joiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero-width_non-joiner)
- U+200D: [Zero-width joiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero-width_joiner)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We had considered reaching out to the users and asking them not to type the hidden characters but the challenges were:
- We are getting these messages (with invisible characters) from many users across multiple deployments.
- Different users use different phone models. We are not sure how the hidden characters are typed.
- Users themselves might not be aware that their message contains the invisible characters because they are invisible.
- The message looks fine in the web app and it is not immediately clear that it contains invisible characters

title: Allow android back button to navigate back in CHT
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
FCHVs and CHNs using CHT Android App frequently epxlain their frustration when clicking the back button on Android phones/tablets that an app returns to home page of an app instead of going back to the previous page. 
 
**Describe the solution you'd like**
When user clicks hardware or software back button on android tablets, allow app to go one step back instead of making it return to home page.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Though we have back button in app at the top, most of the android users are used to with hardware/software button that comes with android. 

**Additional context**
I think this feature will make user feel more comfortable with an app as it complies with user's general android UX.

body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
When a contact is deleted from CHT, it appears that tasks that were generated for that particular contacts are not deleted. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

title: Release 3.16.0
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [X] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [x] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [ ] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`.
- [x] (**NB** - skipping for 3.16) Raise a new issue called `Update dependencies for <version>` with a description that links to [the documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/guides/update-dependencies/). This should be done early in the release cycle so find a volunteer to take this on and assign it to them.
- [ ] Write an update in the weekly [Medic Product Team call agenda](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AuJ7SerLuOPESBjQlJqpBtzwSAoVf5ykTT7fjyJBT0/edit) summarising development and acceptance testing progress and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` release testing can begin.

- [x] (**NB** - for `3.16.x` we should branch off `3.15.x` and cherry pick in relevant commits b/c `master` has breaking changes slated for `4.0.0`. **_ALL commits to `master` FIRST then pick back to `3.16.x`!!_**) Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development using this template:
```
@core_devs I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing.
- [x] Announce the start of release testing on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*Release testing has started for {{version}} of {{product}}*

To get a sneak peak at this upcoming release, you can install `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` on your testing environment. We suggest you test your forms and workflows with this release candidate version and raise any issues that you experience. This helps to to discover any potential regressions that wouldn't otherwise be caught during release testing.

Keep an eye on the forum for the release announcement in the next couple of weeks!
```
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, that they're correctly labelled (in particular: they have the right Type, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate), and have human readable descriptions.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
  - [x] Provide description, screenshots, videos, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions) and update the EOL date and status of previous releases. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.
  - [x] Assign the PR to:
    - The Director of Technology
    - An SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient
- [x] Until release testing passes, make sure regressions are fixed in `master`, cherry-pick them into the release branch, and release another beta.
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [ ] Execute the scalability testing suite on the final build and download the scalability results on S3 at medic-e2e/scalability/$TAG_NAME. Add the release `.jtl` file to `cht-core/tests/scalability/previous_results`. More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [x] Upgrade the `demo-cht.dev` instance to this version.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*We're excited to announce the release of {{version}} of {{product}}*

New features include {{key_features}}. We've also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

Read the [release notes]({{url}}) for full details.

Following our support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read our [software support documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions).

Check out our [roadmap](https://github.com/orgs/medic/projects/112) to see what we're working on next.
```
- [x] Add one last update to the [Medic Product Team call agenda](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AuJ7SerLuOPESBjQlJqpBtzwSAoVf5ykTT7fjyJBT0/edit) and use this meeting to lead an internal release retrospective covering what went well and areas to improve for next time.
- [ ] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We've seen some occurances where we don't need GPS information, but CHT App is waiting for up to 30 seconds to get the GPS location resulting unnecessary delay in form submission. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Allow an option to have GPS tracking enabled or disabled through configuratioin. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Not sure if this could be applicable for other partners, but an option to enable/disable location tracking per form would be ideal. 

If form is not configured, it'd take app wide setting for location and if configured it would overwrite application level setting for that particular form.

title: Add xPath function for easily adding years, months, days, etc to date value
body:
Currently there is not an easy way [in an ODK form](https://docs.getodk.org/form-operators-functions/#date-and-time) to add/subtract a specific number of years/months/days/ etc from a date value in a calculation.  Often I have seen `decimal-date-time` + `date` functions used to adjust a date value by a set number of days (convert the date to a number of days since epoch, then use arithmetic to adjust the day count, then convert the days back into a date value). However, this process is inconvenient and is particularly difficult when trying to adjust a date with a dynamic offset.  

It would be very useful to have a custom xPath function that forms could use to perform this operation.

I am not sure about the naming yet, but I am thinking we could either add one function:
```
shift-date(date, years, months, days, hours, minutes)
// Or
offset-date(date, years, months, days, hours, minutes)
```

Or multiple separate functions:
```
add-years(date, years), 
add-months(date, years), 
add-days(date, years)
```

title: Release 3.16.0-FR-offline-user-replace
body:
When development is ready to begin on a [Feature Release](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/feature_releases/#release-names), an engineer on the appropriate Care Team or Allies should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are followed, though not necessarily doing the work themselves.

# Planning

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.
- [x] Have an actual named deployment and specific end user that will be testing this Feature Release. They need to test in production, on the latest version. No speculative Feature Releases.
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development

- [ ] Create a new release branch in `cht-core` from the most recent release and call it  `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-FR-<FEATURE-NAME>`. If latest is `3.16.0` and the feature is to "allow movies to be uploaded", call it `3.16.0-FR-movie-upload`. Done before the release so all PRs can be set to merge to this branch, and not to `master`.
- [ ] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <feature-release>`.
- [ ] Ensure QA is briefed and is partnering with the Trio to ensure early and often checks of the feature are on track to be of production quality from the start.

# Releasing

This is an iterative process and it's assumed there will be multiple numbered releases throughout development of the Feature Release.

- [ ] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-FR-<FEATURE-NAME>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing. If an updated Feature Release is needed, increment the last `1` by calling it `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-FR-<FEATURE-NAME>-beta.2` etc.

# Close-out

- [ ] Validate with the actual end user that this Feature Release delivers a quantifiable improvement.  If yes, plan on adding the feature to the next minor release by creating a new ticket to merge the code to `master`.  If no, we leave the code dead in this branch, never to be merged to `master`, but still loved all the same.
- [ ] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Ability to replace a CHW user without any connectivity
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
When a CHW is going to leave a deployment, they return their phone to their supervisor.  In some deployments where there is no connectivity, the supervisor and the replacement CHW then need to travel to where there is connectivity.  They can then ask an admin to provision a new user and contact, get the credentials and log in.  This takes time away from when the new CHW could be visiting patients (we're ignoring the fact that the new CHW needs training)

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
We'd like a way for the supervisor to authorize and provision the new CHW to use the existing device, but in a way that doesn't require any connectivity. Further, we want a way that all records created by the new and old CHW have the correct parents for reporting purposes by the supervisor and dashboards.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Either of these happen in the field:
* the new CHW can not work and needs to wait to get connectivity and new credentials 
* the new CHW simply starts using the existing device while logged in as the old CHW. it is unclear to the supervisor and dashboards which CHW did what work when

**Additional context**
We have a deployment actively asking for this. 


**Outstanding items on this ticket:**
* [x] Allow for configuring which forms should trigger the `user_replace` transition (and, at the same time, rename the `replace_user` form  ->  `user_replace` )
* [x] @m5r - Update default replace form to support replacing any offline user (supervisor, OCA or CHW), no matter their level. Should also enable locking it down so it is only accessible to CHW & OCA users.
    * ~~As a part of this, we should update the client-side transitions to also run for online users (or else online users cannot be replaced...)~~
* [x] @jkuester - Remove need for re-syncing for old user to get logged out.  Need to trigger logout from the client when replication is complete.
    * Account for what happens if more docs are added while actively replicating
* [x] @jkuester - Handle what to do if multiple `replace_user` reports are added (while the user is offline) before any get synced.
* [x] @jkuester - Make sure user is finished replicating before re-parenting the original user's reports during the transition
* [x] @m5r - Resolve conflicts with `master`

**Fixed items on this ticket (were outstanding before):**
* [x] ~~Do we need to handle cases where the name for the new contact does not contain any chars that are `[a-z]|[A-Z]`?  (See the current behavior in [this test](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/ec42aa83be08fb03d0ce2ff48ade62997d4b460e/shared-libs/transitions/test/unit/transitions/user_replace.js#L324) where a contact with all unicode chars in their name will not have any name to append the random numbers to...~~ Won't fix - works as documented - will fix in a later ticket
* [x] Usernames with `;)` (and likely others) as derived from "contact full name", cause replace to fail: no 2nd user created, no SMS sent, current user not logged out

* [x] Ensure "Add person" can be used as it was  before when not replacing a CHW . currently no way to add a 2nd person to hierarchy. Likely means something like adding an optional field of "replace CHW?" which then shows the previously hidden "Secret Code" field

---

### Setup Steps

- Install the [latest feature release](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/feature_releases/#initial-fr-installation) by using `3.16.0-FR-offline-user-replace-beta.4` in your `horti` call. Note you may see errors in the command line - the upgrade should still proceed. Here is a sample call to a dev instance: `COUCH_URL=https://medic:password@192-168-68-26.my.local-ip.co:8443/medic horti --local --install=3.16.0-FR-offline-user-replace-beta.4`
- Check out this `7703-offline-user-replace` branch in your `cht-core` repo (needed for next step)
- Use `cht-conf` to upload the app form [`replace_user`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/7703-offline-user-replace/config/default/forms/app/replace_user.xml). Here is a sample call to a dev instance: `cht --url=https://medic:password@192-168-68-26.my.local-ip.co:8443 convert-app-forms upload-app-forms -- replace_user`
- Enable [login by SMS](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/api/#login-by-sms)) on your CHT instance:
    - Enable token login by [adding these 4 lines](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/token_login/) to your `app_settings.json` file and upload it via cht-conf
    - Ensure you have set the [`app_url`](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/#app_settingsjson) settings value
- Enable the new `user_replace` [Sentinel transition](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/transitions/) enabled in your `app_settings.json` file and upload it via cht-conf

### To trigger the Offline Replace behavior

- Log into the CHT with an offline CHW account. Ensure both the user and contact have valid phone numbers.
- Go offline either via [browser](https://www.wikihow.com/Work-Offline-in-Mozilla-Firefox) or [airplane mode](https://www.lifewire.com/turn-airplane-mode-on-or-off-on-android-5212172)
- From the current user's contact page, submit the `replace_user` form 
    - For the Admin Code field, input any value
- Submit any number of reports (for example new pregnancy or death report)
- Go online and sync
    - This will trigger the Sentinel transition to create a new user and re-parent any documents submitted by the original user after the `replace_user` form was submitted
- A token login message for the new user should be visible in the Admin console on the Outgoing messages page
- Original user should be logged out

title: Support replacing offline users from offline device
body:
# Description

The main goal of this PR is to provide the ability to do an in-place replacement of an offline user (without them being connected to the internet).  The scenario would look something like this:

1. An existing CHW is leaving the program and returns their device to their supervisor
    1. The supervisor wants to transfer the device to a new CHW immediately (without having to be connected to the internet)
1. While the device is still offline the supervisor submits a configured replace user form (e.g. the new `replace_user` form we have added to the default config).  This triggers a new client-side transition.
    1. On the device, a new contact is added for the new user and the doc for the old contact has the `user_for_contact.replaced` property set by the client-side transition
    1. Any subsequent forms that are submitted on the device will be automatically re-parented by the client-side transition so they are associated with the new contact
 1. Eventually, once the device is connected to the internet and successfully syncs, the current user on the device will be automatically logged out
 1. A new Sentinel transition will be triggered which creates the new user and sends a token login link to the new CHW so they can login as their proper user

Docs changes: https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/pull/805

Closes #7703

**Describe the bug**
I'm the kind of person that looooves to have multiple tabs open for any project I'm working. For some time now when working on the CHT with online users I would notice some time the app would just stop responding. I couldn't quite figure out why until today.  When I open 3 tabs, the third one becomes unresponsive for specific AJAX requests.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. launch the cht docker helper 
2.  upgrade to 3.16 Beta 2

A list of users load

NA

**Screenshots**
Here's a video of the basic block. Note that as soon as the interstitial tab is closed, the admin tab becomes unblocked an immediately proceeds to finish downloading users:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8253488/183219097-a37f0120-66d9-43eb-aeec-7a714a8d18cb.mp4

Oddly, if you navigate back and forth the problem persists, but if you reload you get a brief error "Error Fetching Users" but then the users load:

title: Target shouldn't send instance object with reference
body:
**Describe the bug**
The ["Vaccines given" target](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/c7a5c03b18497b8bea8324b74d8070f0ce57a37b/config/standard/targets.js#L367) should count 1 per every different instance (`inst` in the code), however it's not counting the quantity of vaccines a patient got during a visit. 

In my tests the instance was `37bfee59-c6b7-44f1-9742-9f539587299f~imm-vaccines-given-this-month01234567891011121314151617181920212223242526272829303132333435363738`
Where `37bfee59-c6b7-44f1-9742-9f539587299f` is my patient id
While `01234567891011121314151617181920212223242526272829303132333435363738` is a concatenation from 0 to the quantity of vaccines applied.

The reason could be that the same instance object is being modify because of its reference. We can try creating a new object of the instance (`inst` in the code) inside the [emit()](https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/blob/6cbf16b9f345c0123a7a0ce52c5f3eb7ba80427d/src/nools/target-emitter.js#L72) and see if the target starts counting every instance it emits. 

Also  the [emitCustom](https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/blob/6cbf16b9f345c0123a7a0ce52c5f3eb7ba80427d/src/nools/target-emitter.js#L87) function isn't described in this [documentation about targets](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/targets/). We need to add it there.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. upload standar config
2. create an immunisation report and select 5 vaccines. 
3. go to target and see how it just count 1 instead of 5

**Expected behavior**
The instance object reference shouldn't be modified when executing `emitCustom` and target should count every single vaccine applied to the patient during the current month. Also the target configuration should be fixed to be more readable. 

It's better to fix this in cht-core side than just in the config, it's an easy mistake that anyone can do without noticing, and we can help to prevent.

**Environment**
- Instance: local / standard config
- Browser: Chrome
- Client platform: MacOS
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.15 but it looks like a very old issue.

title: Icon labels on action buttons are not showing at the default dp for commonly used mobile devices
body:
Labels for icons on action buttons do not render their text if your device's horizontal resolution is 400px or less.  

A number of commonly used phones have a horizontal resolution of 720 with a default dp of 360.  With this default setting, the icon labels are not showing. If you change the dp to something higher, the labels become visible; however, changing this on every phone is onerous and it also makes the rest of the app text much smaller.  At a minimum, we should show the icon labels for the default resolution on these phones. 

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6394 addressed the same issue with **_action labels_** but [intentionally did not address](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6394) _**action button icon labels**_.  

Additional context in https://github.com/medic/config-ug-vht/issues/568 (private repo).

title: Release 3.17.0
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [X] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [x] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`.
- [ ] Raise a new issue called `Update dependencies for <version>` with a description that links to [the documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/guides/update-dependencies/). This should be done early in the release cycle so find a volunteer to take this on and assign it to them.
- [x] Write an update in the weekly [Medic Product Team call agenda](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AuJ7SerLuOPESBjQlJqpBtzwSAoVf5ykTT7fjyJBT0/edit) summarising development and acceptance testing progress and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` release testing can begin.

- [x] Create a new release branch from `3.16.0` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`, cherry pick in all commits from issues in milestone (**NB - different than normal release process!!**). Post a message to #development using this template:
```
@core_devs I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing.
- [ ] Announce the start of release testing on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*Release testing has started for {{version}} of {{product}}*

To get a sneak peak at this upcoming release, you can install `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` on your testing environment. We suggest you test your forms and workflows with this release candidate version and raise any issues that you experience. This helps to to discover any potential regressions that wouldn't otherwise be caught during release testing.

Keep an eye on the forum for the release announcement in the next couple of weeks!
```
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, that they're correctly labelled (in particular: they have the right Type, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate), and have human readable descriptions.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes) to export the issues into our release note format.

title: Update `today` XPath function to not return current time
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently we have a [custom implementation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/3d00f5ffc34510ce43dae26190ef41f57ea01154/webapp/src/js/enketo/medic-xpath-extensions.js#L86) of the `today` functionality that is identical to what is returned by the `now` function (the current date and time in the current timezone).  

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
As noted in this OpenRosa issue (https://github.com/enketo/enketo/issues/901), this behavior does not seem to follow the [ODK Spec](https://getodk.github.io/xforms-spec/#fn:today).  Unfortunately, the wording in the spec is a little confusing (to me at least) with regards to how it is actually supposed to behave.  However, both [openrosa](https://github.com/enketo/openrosa-xpath-evaluator/blob/01648be20c638f773467e299a9b65a050a409a97/src/openrosa-extensions.js#L302) and [javarosa](https://github.com/getodk/javarosa/blob/b72e0d48947c7f2b5c2d05ab9783ea9b8a259b04/src/main/java/org/javarosa/xpath/expr/XPathFuncExpr.java#L333) have coalesced on a single interpretation of the spec where `now` returns the current date and time while `today` returns the current date with the time set to midnight of the current timezone.  I think we should remove our custom implementation of `today` and just use the one provided by OpenRosa.

As things stand today, we have a bunch of forms that are doing things like `date(floor(decimal-date-time(today())))` to get the start of today.  All this extra logic could be eliminated with the new implementation of `today`.  Any logic that relies on the current time being included in `today` can just update to the spec-compliant `now` function.  

As discussed in places like [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6345#issuecomment-1152800834), [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6345#issuecomment-1155647161), and [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6345#issuecomment-1201489355) the [Enketo uplift](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/7256) is already going to cause subtle behavior changes in the behavior of `format-date` and `decimal-date` (both frequently used along with `today`). Changing `today` at the same time as these other changes would allow projects to implement proper fixes to their date handling once and for all instead of breaking some things now with the Enketo uplift and again later if we decide to switch to a spec-compliant version of `today`.  

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
One alternative would be to leave `today` alone and add a new custom function (e.g. `today-date`) that would return today's date without a time value.  This would be more passive and backwards compatible, but less spec-compliant.

**Additional context**
This has been an ongoing saga in CHT code for years:

- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/1340
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/1878
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5768

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/5831 was the PR that added the current custom functionality for `today` to cht-core.

The big difference now is that both openrosa and javarosa seem to have agreed on an implementation (that is different from what we have).

title: Update default/standard config forms so they pass validation

title: Update default/standard config forms to pass validation
body:
# Description

Updates the default/standard config forms so that they pass the new cht-conf validation checks.  The two main issues that were fixed are:

- Invalid XPaths. The explicit XPaths in form expressions are now checked to be sure they point to an actual field in the form. There were a number of forms that had invalid XPaths caused by things like:
    - Typos in the field name
    - References to input fields that were not actually listed in the form
    - References to fields at the wrong point in the hierarchy
- Using the, now deprecated, `horizontal` appearance. This now triggers a warning that you should use `columns`. There are drop-in `column` replacement values for the `horizontal` appearances we were using, so I have just updated the forms to use those.

Where it was possible, I have tried to include tests that covered the fields with updated expressions. Existing tests for the `standard` config tasks/targets depend on a crazy old version of `medic-conf-test-harness` and there does not appear to be a clean upgrade path without significantly refactoring these tests.  I have logged https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7744 to solve this later.  In the meantime, I did not want to contribute to the problem by adding more tests dependent on the old util.  So, I have also included the latest version of `cht-conf-test-harness` and written my new tests against that util.

Closes #7738

body:
**Description** Taken from the [forum post](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/updates-to-the-search-feature/2107): As a follow up to our work on [filters](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/feature-testing-filters/1917) ([ticket](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7653)), the Search feature is next on our [UI evolution](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/updates-to-the-cht-ui-ux/1998). We are moving to an expandable search to free up real estate in the top bar, collapsing the current search bar into an icon that opens when tapped. Current functionality will remain the same, with users being able to both search and filter results simultaneously.
The old version can be seen here

By default, users will see the new version. You can have users continue to see the old version by giving them the `can_view_old_filter_and_search` [permission](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/user-permissions/) but... the old version will be removed in a future release so it is important to have a plan to get users onto the new version ASAP.

body:
Add the e2e automated test for the pregnancy workflow on Standard config. To run it use the command npm run standard-wdio-local

This test is divided into three different files:

#### Pregnancy
* Before the tests are executed:
  *  Creates two women, one using the webapp and one using SMS.
* Then this test:
   * Submit a new pregnancy using webapp
   * Verify the report created.
   * Submit a new pregnancy using SMS.
   * Verify the report created.
   * Verify the targets page.

#### Pregnancy Visit
* Before the tests are executed:
  * Submit a new pregnancy, for a woman generated using the personFactory file, using SMS.
* Then this test:
   * Submit a new pregnancy visit using webapp.
   * Verify the report created.
   * Submit a new pregnancy visit using SMS.
   * Verify the report created.

#### Delivery
* Before the tests are executed:
  * Creates two women using SMS.
  * Creates new pregnancies for the women created using SMS.
  * Creates pregnancy visits for the two pregnant women (four for the first woman and one for the second woman).
* Then this test:
   * Submit a delivery using webapp.
   * Verify the report created.
   * Submit a delivery using SMS.
   * Verify the report created.
   * Verify the targets page.

title: Allow supervisors to create health workers
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Right now there is no way to for an offline user, like a supervisor, to create another user, like a CHW.  Instead they need to reach out to an CHT admin, an online user, to create the account for them.  This can often take a while and leaves the supervisor with a device and a CHW that are prevented from giving care to the area's patients. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
It would be great if supervisors, using an authentication code, were allowed to create a CHW user in an area.  This would cut out a lot of the delay in the current flow. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
NA

**Additional context**
This is similar to the offline replace feature #7703, but differs in that the supervisor would use their own device and the new CHW would get a new device provisioned for them.

Private docs:
* [Figma](https://www.figma.com/proto/igJBl04RYEsHiUMEehNyUy/User-management?node-id=1095%3A1876&scaling=scale-down&page-id=1026%3A961&starting-point-node-id=1031%3A1938)
* [Story Map](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1SsfNbuqPEVJhN-HGDEWOpA90yTPjYVA62q7vbVxr8MI/edit#slide=id.g1451dc5f7a9_0_0)
* [Discussion](https://docs.google.com/document/d/18l9175kuNlFsCiIhg2Rz7AMHrixfs6SBZWxkTut-ZGE/edit)

## Usage

Enabling this feature is similar to the existing [user-replace](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/transitions/#create_user_for_contacts) functionality.  

- Load the updated code by either:
  - Checking out the [`7753-supervisor-chw-create`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/7753-supervisor-chw-create) branch and building it locally
  - Upgrading your instance to the latest feature release  `4.1.0-4.1.0-FR-supervisor-chw-create-beta.4` ([see below](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7753#issuecomment-1373024792))
- Update app_settings:
  - Enable token login:   `"token_login": {  "enabled": true }`
  - Set app url to your host (`192.168.1.249` in this case): `"app_url": "https://192-168-1-249.my.local-ip.co/",`
  - Enable create user for contacts transition: `"transitions": { "create_user_for_contacts": true }`
- Upload `default` config forms from the [`7753-supervisor-chw-create`](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/7753-supervisor-chw-create) branch 
- Open the webapp and add a new person contact
  - Set a valid phone number
  - Choose `CHW` or `CHW Supervisor` as the "Role"
- Save the contact and sync
- Sentinel should process the new contact and automatically create a new user
  - From the "App Management" console you should be able to see the new user in the `Users` tab
  - The login link for the new user should be visible on the `Outgoing messages` tab

## Technical design

### default config

- Update contact forms that support adding persons to set the `user_for_contact.create.add = true` on the new contact doc when the user has selected `chw` or `chw_supervisor` as the role 
- [X] Should we support triggering a new user for a person from the edit contact form (or from app forms)?
    - We are only going to support adding users for new contacts.  However, we should support adding a new users for all the different ways that we can add a new person contact (e.g. any contact/app form can add a new person).  As described below, our Sentinel logic should not be dependent on which form was used to add the contact, but should work in all cases.
  - For the `default` config specifically, we should update the following forms to set `user_for_contact.create.add = true` for new persons when `chw` or `chw_supervisor` is selected for the role:
    - `district_hospital-create`
    - `health_center-create`
    - `clinic-create`
    - `person-create`

### ~~webapp~~

- ~~Add support for running client-side transitions for offline users~~
  - ~~Add boolean function (`isEnabled`) to each transition where the transition can determine if it should run for online/offline users~~  ~~After looking at this some more, I think we might be able to avoid adding a whole new function and instead just return `false` from the existing `init` function when we do not want to run the transition....~~
    - ~~The `muting.transition` should return `false` when the user is online~~
    - ~~The `create-user-for-contact.transition` should always return `true`~~
  - ~~The `transitions.service` will check `isEnabled` when loading transitions~~
- ~~Update `create-user-for-contact.transition` client-side transition to mark contacts for adding a new user~~
  - ~~When the transition sees a contact added/edited with `create_user_for_contact = true`:~~
    - ~~Set `user_for_contact.create = { status: 'READY' }` on the contact doc~~
      - ~~Can use the `create-user-for-contacts.service` to do this~~
    - ~~Delete the `create_user_for_contact` flag from the contact doc (so it doesn't run again the next time the contact is edited)~~
      -  [X] ~~should we support adding users when editing persons (or just when adding)?~~
          - ~~We are only going to support adding users for new persons~~

### transitions shared-lib

- Update `create-user-for-contacts` transition to support adding new users
  - When the transition sees a person contact with ~~`user_for_contact.create.status = 'READY'`~~ `user_for_contact.create.add = true` and the contact does not have an existing infodoc in `medic-sentinel` (meaning it is a new contact):
    - Create a new user with the contact's phone number and role
      - Load the role data from the contact doc's `roles` or `role` field. 
    - ~~Set `user_for_contact.create.status = 'DONE'` on the contact doc~~ Delete the `user_for_contact.create.add` field
    -  [X] Should we support adding and replacing users on the same contact at the same time?  Seems possible to run into this case when syncing data for an offline user.
        -  It should not be possible to hit this case since we do not support adding users on existing contacts (and so the contact should not have any existing users to replace...)
- As with the user-replace logic, the `create-user-for-contacts` transition can only be enabled when token login is also enabled. The new users will have a generated username and a login link will be sent to the contact's phone number.

## To do
- [ ] Clean up backup branch `7753-supervisor-chw-create-backup` once this feature gets merged to `master`

title: Timeouts for view requests when syncing can leave changes requests hanging forever
body:
**Describe the bug**
When an offline user requests `_changes`, two view requests are required to determine which documents the user has access to. 
If one of the view requests times out because the view is not indexed, the initiating `_changes` request hangs on forever. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Start with a hefty database, indexing the `medic` ddoc view should take over 5 minutes. 
2. Login as an offline user. 
3. Edit `docs_by_replication_key` view in the `medic` ddoc. The change should be inconsequential, even editing or adding a comment.
4. Start indexing. 
5. Sync with your offline user. 
6. Watching the api logs, you should see something like: 
```
2022-09-01 07:54:58 ERROR: Server error: {
  error: 'timeout',
  reason: 'The request could not be processed in a reasonable amount of time.',
  status: 500,
  name: 'timeout',
  message: 'The request could not be processed in a reasonable amount of time.'
} 
```
This is where your request should have been interrupted. However your client will still show that sync-ing is ongoing.

**Expected behavior**
You should get an error that syncing was not possible. Or, at least, the request should not hang forever. 

**Environment**
- App: api
- Version: 3.10+

**Additional information:**
This is a tricky situation, because of our heartbeat. 
We start sending a heartbeat immediately after we receive the request (before we start setting up required view requests). Sending a heartbeat through means that we've already sent headers and a 200 status. So if the error occurs after the first heartbeat, we can no longer properly communicate the error to the client, through a status. 

Regression after this was fixed in: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6084

body:
## transitions
- Updates the error handling for the transition so that the transitions framework will save any errors to the `replace_user` report, itself, if they occur during the transition (by setting `err.changed = true` before throwing it).
- Adds init logic to fail during Sentinel initialization if the `user_replace` transition is enabled, but token logic is not (since without token login, the new user would not be able to login...)

## api
- Adds some additional error checking to validate the new contact has `name` and `phone` fields
- Updates the re-parenting logic to only change forms with `reported_date` that is `>` the `replace_user` form (instead of `>=`).  This will prevent the `replace_user` form, itself, from getting re-parented, which causes it to re-trigger the transition again

## config/default
- Make the `user_replace` transition `false` by default in the default app_settings.  With the new init validation in the transition, we need to either enable `token_login` by default or we need the `user_replace`transition disabled by default.

title: Implement a increasing minimum test coverage
body:
**Describe the issue**
We want to increase test coverage but we don't want to stop development while we all work to get the number up to some minimum. The ideal solution is every contribution improved the test coverage % so we gradually improve coverage.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Every build publishes its coverage number to some repository. When a PR is submitted check the latest published number from the repo and ensure the PR increases the number. Include a reasonable upper limit so it doesn't keep going up to 100%. Ideally there would be some off the shelf component to do this but I haven't managed to find any.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Manually tweak a hardcoded minimum coverage as we improve but this requires frequent manual intervention.

**Similar other metrics**
If we make this a generic process then we can expand this to cover things like code complexity and other gradual code improvements.

title: Bulk delete of reports redesign
body:
**Description** [Related forum post.](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/experience-with-bulk-deleting-reports/2142) The bulk delete of Reports tab is redesigned to improve the user experience. Extra considerations: - No actions (create, verify reports, etc) are allowed when there's at least 1 item selected. Just bulk delete. - The checkboxes are always visible as long as `can_bulk_delete_reports` permission is enabled. - The Search and filter are hidden when there is at least 1 item selected. - All unselected checkboxes have gray border, including the "Select all" checkbox. - One telemetry entry is added to count every time a user bulk delete reports. - We decided that we would NOT use a feature flag for the bulk delete redesign: 1. It's not a feature that CHWs use frequently (they rarely even have the reports tab) 2. The purpose of Feature Flagging these UI changes is to give projects a way to roll out significant changes to large numbers of users over time rather than all at once. This is not likely a feature that falls into this category (see # 1). 3. While the way we do bulk delete may change over time, we are definitely moving forward with our material design changes so we would not consider reverting back to the old (well, current) way of doing bulk delete. 4. It adds complexity to the codebase 5. It gets even trickier since there are other UI feature flags - While in mobile view: if a user clicks outside the checkbox, then the reports open. If the user clicks "back", then the selection from before appears. - While in desktop view: if a user already has one item selected and then clicks outside the checkbox on a second item, this one will select (it won't open the report). If the user wants to see more details about the report, the user still have the option to expand the selected reports located on the right side. - We won't fully support responsive ui when user logins in a browser using the phone (no medic android app). See [this comment](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7778#issuecomment-1292995038) for more details. Some additional clarification about this feature behaviour are: - When the select all checkbox has a minus, and the user clicks on it - it should select all (up to 500 reports). - When that checkbox is blue and checked, and the user clicks on it - it should deselect all. - If the user has too many reports (+500) then select all - it will only select up to 500 same as in master, - and the select all checkbox is blue and checked, and the "clear selection" is available. - If the user scrolls more than +500 in the LHS, and "selects all" and then selects some more (for example 505 selected) then that's okay _for now_, same as master. (https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7883)

title: Don't hard code COUCHDB_SECRET in docker compose files
body:
**Describe the issue**
We hard code the secret for CouchDB in the [Arch v3 docker setup](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/search?q=2528396f2f58) as shown here:

```
"COUCHDB_SECRET=${COUCHDB_SECRET:-6c1953b6-e64d-4b0c-9268-2528396f2f58}"
```

This is insecure as it is public and will be used by default unless users override it.
