NA

title: Use local log driver in all Docker containers
body:
**Describe the issue**
When reviewing the new [cht-core](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds/medic%3Amedic%3Aarchv3/docker-compose%2Fcht-core.yml) and [cht-couchdb](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds/medic%3Amedic%3Aarchv3/docker-compose%2Fcht-couchdb.yml) docker-compose files for archv3 currently published to staging.dev.medicmobile.org, I suggest we use `local` instead of `json-file` for `logging:driver:`.  the JSON one is [deprecated and does not have compression](https://docs.docker.com/config/containers/logging/configure/).  As is, this means the in the worst case we could have 50MB x 20 files x 6 containers = 6GB of uncompressed logs.  local uses compression by default.

As well, `cht-nginx` and `couchdb` containers don't have a `logging:` stanza. They should have one added to them, presumably mirroring what is on the other 4 containers.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
oops - kinda spoiled it above - use `local` instead  and uniformly declare the `logging:` section for all containers ;)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
There may have been intentional design decisions that I don't appreciate that mandate sticking with uncompressed  `json-file` driver.

title: Allow for dynamically setting container and network names
body:
**Describe the issue**
When reviewing the new [cht-core](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds/medic%3Amedic%3Aarchv3/docker-compose%2Fcht-core.yml) and [cht-couchdb](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds/medic%3Amedic%3Aarchv3/docker-compose%2Fcht-couchdb.yml) docker-compose files for archv3 currently published to staging.dev.medicmobile.org, I'd prefer not to use an explicit name for the networks and the volumes. These can be [dynamically set within a project](https://www.google.com/url?q=https://docs.docker.com/engine/reference/commandline/compose/%23use--p-to-specify-a-project-name&sa=D&source=calendar&ust=1663791886590864&usg=AOvVaw2VGhCwB747h1fvOXGxdOaX) when using `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` but only if they're not explicitly set in the compose file. This is a huge win for both multi-tenant and developer setups (which are often multi-tenant ; ) 

IE go from:
```yaml
   networks: 
      cht-net: 
         name: cht-net 
```

 to this 

```yaml
   networks: 
      cht-net: 
```

Which ever way we go with, declaring networks and volumes they should be uniform.  The CouchDB container and the cht-core containers differ. (note extra - and lacking :).  My vote is the former!

CouchDB:

```yaml
   networks: 
      cht-net: 
```

CHT Core:

```yaml
   networks: 
      - cht-net
```

While we consider using `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`, I recommend _not_ using `container_name` for each container.  They will already get named after the outer most stanza value (the service) and in every case the `container_name` matches the service (eg: `container_name: cht-nginx` == `cht-nginx:` ).  Intra-container lookups will [not be affected](https://www.google.com/url?q=https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55522620/docker-compose-yml-container-name-and-hostname&sa=D&source=calendar&ust=1663791886590864&usg=AOvVaw1QRbFqBX0Cf4GwSEcseprF).

Further, implicit nomenclature will simplify scenarios where we have service name <-> container name mismatches.  For example, `haproxy` service defaults to using the docker DNS of `couchdb `as seen here - `"COUCHDB_SERVERS=${COUCHDB_SERVERS:-couchdb}` but the container is actually called something different (`container_name: cht-couchdb`).  The reason this is currently working is that DNS works with both service name and container name.


**Describe alternatives you've considered**
There may have been intentional design decisions that I don't appreciate that mandate sticking with the current nomenclature

title: Release 4.0.0
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [x] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`.
- [x] Raise a new issue called `Update dependencies for <version>` with a description that links to [the documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/guides/update-dependencies/). This should be done early in the release cycle so find a volunteer to take this on and assign it to them.
- [x] Write an update in the weekly [Medic Product Team call agenda](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AuJ7SerLuOPESBjQlJqpBtzwSAoVf5ykTT7fjyJBT0/edit) summarising development and acceptance testing progress and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` release testing can begin.

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development using this template:
```
@core_devs I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing.
- [x] Announce the start of release testing on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*Release testing has started for {{version}} of {{product}}*

To get a sneak peak at this upcoming release, you can install `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` on your testing environment. We suggest you test your forms and workflows with this release candidate version and raise any issues that you experience. This helps to to discover any potential regressions that wouldn't otherwise be caught during release testing.

Keep an eye on the forum for the release announcement in the next couple of weeks!
```
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, that they're correctly labelled (in particular: they have the right Type, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate), and have human readable descriptions.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
  - [x] Provide description, screenshots, videos, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions) and update the EOL date and status of previous releases. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.
  - [x] Assign the PR to:
    - The Director of Technology
    - An SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient
- [x] Until release testing passes, make sure regressions are fixed in `master`, cherry-pick them into the release branch, and release another beta.
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [ ] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Execute the scalability testing suite on the final build and download the scalability results on S3 at medic-e2e/scalability/$TAG_NAME. Add the release `.jtl` file to `cht-core/tests/scalability/previous_results`. More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [x] Upgrade the `demo-cht.dev` instance to this version.
- [ ] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*We're excited to announce the release of {{version}} of {{product}}*

New features include {{key_features}}. We've also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

Read the [release notes]({{url}}) for full details.

Following our support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read our [software support documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions).

Check out our [roadmap](https://github.com/orgs/medic/projects/112) to see what we're working on next.
```
- [ ] Add one last update to the [Medic Product Team call agenda](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AuJ7SerLuOPESBjQlJqpBtzwSAoVf5ykTT7fjyJBT0/edit) and use this meeting to lead an internal release retrospective covering what went well and areas to improve for next time.
- [ ] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

The following `_all_docs` is aborted by CouchDb (2.3.1):
```
[diana@doina ~]$ curl "http://admin:pass@127.0.0.1:6984/medic/_all_docs?keys=[\"e0e46c7bbae044b7eb4507c6badcb70c\",\"ea449934dcd5e506dcede2803a47fc31\"]&include_docs=true&conflicts=true" --globoff -v

< 
{"total_rows":913370,"offset":null,"rows":[

curl: (18) transfer closed with outstanding read data remaining
```

The request fails because the 2nd document produces a read failure:
```
[emergency] 2022-09-21T09:57:05.570102Z nonode@nohost <0.20174.644> -------- File corruption in <0.16669.2> at position 51824286
[error] 2022-09-21T09:57:05.570235Z nonode@nohost <0.20174.644> -------- rexi_server: from: nonode@nohost(<0.27025.642>) mfa: fabric_rpc:open_doc/3 exit:{file_corruption,<<"file corruption">>} [{couch_file,pread_iolist,2,[{file,"src/couch_file.erl"},{line,184}]},{couch_file,pread_binary,2,[{file,"src/couch_file.erl"},{line,169}]},{couch_file,pread_term,2,[{file,"src/couch_file.erl"},{line,157}]},{couch_bt_engine,read_doc_body,2,[{file,"src/couch_bt_engine.erl"},{line,343}]},{couch_db,make_doc,5,[{file,"src/couch_db.erl"},{line,1699}]},{couch_db,open_doc_int,3,[{file,"src/couch_db.erl"},{line,1637}]},{couch_db,open_doc,3,[{file,"src/couch_db.erl"},{line,281}]},{fabric_rpc,with_db,3,[{file,"src/fabric_rpc.erl"},{line,334}]}]
[error] 2022-09-21T09:57:05.570359Z nonode@nohost <0.27025.642> -------- _all_docs open error: medic ea449934dcd5e506dcede2803a47fc31 :: {error,{case_clause,{error,read_failure}}} [{fabric_view_all_docs,open_doc_int,4,[{file,[115,114,99,47,102,97,98,114,105,99,95,118,105,101,119,95,97,108,108,95,100,111,99,115,46,101,114,108]},{line,269}]},{fabric_view_all_docs,open_doc,4,[{file,[115,114,99,47,102,97,98,114,105,99,95,118,105,101,119,95,97,108,108,95,100,111,99,115,46,101,114,108]},{line,258}]}]
[notice] 2022-09-21T09:57:05.570444Z nonode@nohost <0.25226.634> 65e73c8702 127.0.0.1:6984 172.17.0.1 admin GET /medic/_all_docs?keys=["e0e46c7bbae044b7eb4507c6badcb70c","ea449934dcd5e506dcede2803a47fc31"]&include_docs=true&conflicts=true 200 aborted 1
[error] 2022-09-21T09:57:05.570496Z nonode@nohost <0.25226.634> 65e73c8702 Response abnormally terminated: {<<"ea449934dcd5e506dcede2803a47fc31">>,{case_clause,{error,read_failure}}}
```

If I request the same docs with PouchDb http adapter, the request just hangs. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Corrupt a db file (steps to do that in a controlled way is TBD)
2. Login with a user that wants to download a corrupted document
3. Login hangs forever, with no indication that an error was produced

**Expected behavior**
Corrupted database errors should be handled gracefully.

**Environment**
- Version: 4.0

**Additional context**
This seems to be an issue deep in how `node-fetch@2` (which is the peer dependency of PouchDb) handles incomplete requests using Node 16. `node-fetch@3` seems to handle the failed request correctly. 
This points to PouchDb and `node-fetch@2` peer dependency not correctly supporting Node 16.

title: Add client-side transition for offline user replace
body:
# Description

Overview of logic flow:

- CLIENT (in `webapp`)
	- `replace_user` form submitted  
	- Triggers _client-side_ `user-replace.transition` to set `replaced` properties on user's _current_ contact
	    - `replaced.by` = `_id` of new contact
	    - `replaced.status` = "PENDING"
	- Any additional reports submitted after the user is replaced (but before the client syncs) will be automatically re-parented by the client-side transition
	- Client syncs.
		- When syncing completes successfully, the `syncStatusChanged` function in the `user-replace.service` is triggered
		    - If the user has been replaced, and the status is set to "PENDING", then we know everything has now synced successfully (since that is what triggered `syncStatusChanged` in the first place
		    - Set the status on the original contact to "READY" and sync again
		    - When the next sync completes, automatically log out the user
- SERVER  
	- Server's `user_replace` transition  is triggered by updated contact with `replaced.status=READY`  
		- Creates new user  
		- Deletes existing user  
		- Sets original contact `replaced.status=COMPLETE`

title: Remove custom today XPath function
body:
# Description

This PR removes our custom `today` XPath function (allowing us to inherit the default functionality from the OpenRosa `today` function.  The difference is that our custom implementation of `today` would include the _current time value_ while OpenRosa's default implementation (which matches JavaRosa) is that `today` only returns today's date at _midnight in the current timezone_.  

## Form changes: 

In places where we were using `today`, If we do not actually care about the time value, I just let it be. If it seemed like the time value _might_ be relevant, I switched to use `now`.  When today was being wrapped with a `floor` call, I just removed the `floor` since it should no longer be necessary (see the discussion on the issue for more details about this).  Finally, I also tried to remove unnecessary calls to `decimal-date-time` as I went. We were using these a lot when comparing date values, but this is unnecessary. (Enketo supports comparing date values with `<>=`. They do not have to be converted to numbers.)

Closes https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7731

title: CERTIFICATE_MODE=OWN_CERT fails with "cannot load certificate"
body:
**Describe the bug**
In Arch v3 you can specify you're bringing your own TLS cert by setting `CERTIFICATE_MODE` to `OWN_CERT`.  This will pass our test for [files being present](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/69b478371091c0fa3cac00003e04af052050346d/nginx/ssl-install.sh#L97), but because we [hard code the path to the certs](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/69b478371091c0fa3cac00003e04af052050346d/nginx/nginx.conf#L42), nginx fails to start.


**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior assuming no existing docker containers, volumes or networks:
1. Download the current `master` [docker compose file for core](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds/medic%3Amedic%3Amaster/docker-compose%2Fcht-core.yml): `curl -o docker-compose_cht-core.yml https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds/medic%3Amedic%3Amaster/docker-compose%2Fcht-core.yml`
2. Download the current `master` [docker compose file for couch](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds/medic%3Amedic%3Amaster/docker-compose%2Fcht-couchdb.yml): `curl -o docker-compose_cht-couchdb.yml https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds/medic%3Amedic%3Amaster/docker-compose%2Fcht-couchdb.yml`
3. Create an empty `cht-ssl` volume `docker volume create cht-ssl`
4. Populate the volume with valid local-host.ip certs:
   	```
	docker run --rm -d -v cht-ssl:/root --name deleteme alpine sleep 3600
	docker exec -it deleteme sh -c "wget -P /root/  http://local-ip.co/cert/server.pem"
	docker exec -it deleteme sh -c "wget -P /root/ http://local-ip.co/cert/chain.pem"
	docker exec -it deleteme sh -c "cat  /root/server.pem /root/chain.pem > /root/cert.pem"
	docker exec -it deleteme sh -c "wget -P /root/ http://local-ip.co/cert/server.key"
	docker exec -it deleteme sh -c "mv /root/server.key /root/key.pem"
	docker stop deleteme
   	```
5. Run `up` for compose, specifying your cert paths and `OWN_CERT` like so: `SSL_CERT_FILE_PATH=/etc/nginx/private/server.pem SSL_KEY_FILE_PATH=/etc/nginx/private/key.pem CERTIFICATE_MODE=OWN_CERT  COUCHDB_PASSWORD=password COUCHDB_USER=medic docker-compose -f docker-compose_cht-core.yml -f docker-compose_cht-couchdb.yml up`

**Expected behavior**
`cht-nginx` container start with a valid TLS cert

**Logs**
here's the output of `docker logs --follow cht-nginx`. Note that we see the script validation passes with `SSL certificate exists.` but then `nginx` internal checks faile with `cannot load certificate`

title: Reports from `case_id` based workflows don't count as target emissions
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
When defining a target to apply to a specific form, and this form is a case based form that doesn't have a patient contact, target counts will never increase. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Update target emissions code to support case based workflows. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Leave it as it is. 

**Additional context**
Forum post: https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/targets-not-being-updated/2218/12

I did a bit of code exploring, and in order to get a `case_id` report to be counted for targets I had to change: 
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/275e5adc647f0e5c8cce7feaa2d496697b956622/shared-libs/rules-engine/src/rules-emitter.js#L177 - change this to not be undefined when there is no contact_id 
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/74208dbc89cb7fb0d7313fa30936b8e44e22b782/shared-libs/rules-engine/src/target-state.js#L79-L80 - the emission won't have a contact, I changed it to always get emissions for all contacts
- https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/6514ce2fc8f5d19b2a680a1aa53355ee737129a8/shared-libs/rules-engine/src/provider-wireup.js#L260 - again, the emission won't have a contact, so I changed the condition to not require it. 

cht-conf also will skip all reports that don't have a contact: https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/blob/c250f6b9a1152fdd7a6bae1a89fea9b2a57d4175/src/nools/target-emitter.js#L59

I think the best approach would be to treat the case like it were a contact in rules engine somehow.

title: Make sure sync status reflects current state of the local database
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
We set webapp sync status to success after a successful replication. However, this doesn't account for [`denied` document retries](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/db-sync.service.ts#L91). 
We [also set the `currentSeq` as last replicated seq](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/db-sync.service.ts#L196), although this might not reflect the truth, if there were database writes in the meantime (race conditions). 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Successful sync status should be displayed when the local (pouch) checkpointer `last_seq` is the same as the local database `update_seq`. 
The biggest issue with this approach is that PouchDb doesn't expose the  API to get the checkpointer document id, and it may be too fragile to just iterate over _local docs to find it. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Leave it as it is. 
- only for denied retries, add a flag that a denial happened during sync and not show success in those cases, everything else remaining unchanged. 

**Additional context**
With offline user replace, but also with move contacts, it becomes important to trust the sync status completely.

title: Add support for app developers easily starting local CHT 4 instances
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Right now, it's easy for app developers to start one or more local instances of the CHT with [CHT Docker Helper](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/app-developer/#cht-docker-helper). There is no way for them to do this with CHT 4

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
An easy way for app developers to start one or more CHT 4.0 instance.  Ideally it would include the same feature set of the current helper:
* be based off env files to store key values for each local instance 
* install (and possibly renew!) [local-ip.co](http://local-ip.co/) certs 
* show the URL of the local instance, including Fauxton URL
* given it will be the normal way to do things, leverage the new [CHT upgrader](https://github.com/medic/cht-upgrade-service/)
* _optional:_ consider moving to node instead of bash and allowing folks to install it with `npm` like we do with `cht-conf` 

**NB -** All of the above is up to the engineer to decide how to implement. Ideally as simple as possible, with as little code from the old helper to KISS, be it bash or node. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Manually launch developer instances via something like:
1. fetch the two compose files: `curl -s -o docker-compose_cht-core.yml https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds/medic%3Amedic%3Amaster/docker-compose%2Fcht-core.yml && curl -s -o docker-compose_cht-couchdb.yml https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds/medic%3Amedic%3Amaster/docker-compose%2Fcht-couchdb.yml`
1. Run this docker-compose command to start everything up: `COUCHDB_PASSWORD=password COUCHDB_USER=medic docker-compose -f docker-compose_cht-core.yml -f docker-compose_cht-couchdb.yml up`


**Additional context**
There's a [forum post](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/cht-4-0-0-preperation-for-partners-alpha-docker-demo/2233) that talks about, and has a video demo, how to start the CHT without using env files or the CHT upgrade service.

A lot of the problems for how to do this are already solved:
* **Adding Local IP Co certs:** A prototype script was written to do this already.  It overwrites the self signed certs. Private slack thread [here](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C024KTGRW/p1665694500957199?thread_ts=1665435520.618599&cid=C024KTGRW), raw script [here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/mrjones-hack-local-ip-easy-add-script/scripts/add-local-ip-certs-to-docker-4.x.sh). We could set `CERTIFICATE_MODE=OWN_CERT` and the populate the certs [like this](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/7834#issuecomment-1268710481).
* **detecting IP/URL for CHT:** We already do this in the current CHT Docker Helper by first [getting the host IP](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/docker-helper/cht-docker-compose.sh#L24),  then [building up](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/docker-helper/cht-docker-compose.sh#L45) the `*.my.local-ip.co` URL.
* **Env files:** Docker supports this natively, so if we have an env file like this:
   ```bash
   NGINX_HTTP_PORT=8080
   NGINX_HTTPS_PORT=8443
   CHT_COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=test-4.0.0
   DOCKER_CONFIG_PATH=/home/mrjones/Documents/MedicMobile/test-400
   COUCHDB_SECRET=foo-bar-bash-smang
   COUCHDB_DATA=/home/mrjones/Documents/MedicMobile/test-400/couch-test-400
   CHT_COMPOSE_PATH=/home/mrjones/Documents/MedicMobile/test-400
   COUCHDB_USER=medic
   COUCHDB_PASSWORD=password
   ```
   Assuming we have core and couch compose files in `/home/mrjones/Documents/MedicMobile/test-400` and we're in the the root directory of the [cht upgrader project](https://github.com/medic/cht-upgrade-service/) with the `docker-compose.yml` [file](https://github.com/medic/cht-upgrade-service/blob/main/docker-compose.yml) , we can just call: `docker-compose --env-file ~/Documents/MedicMobile/test-400 up`  and this just works.  We can make as many projects as we want that are peers to `test-400` directory to scale out running multiple instances locally.

title: When using self signed certs, upgrade page will report "Error when fetching progress" after upgrade was successful
body:
**Describe the bug**
When using `CERTIFICATE_MODE=SELF_SIGNED` or not setting `CERTIFICATE_MODE` (`SELF_SIGNED` is default) and not also changing `SSL_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH`, the upgrade page remains stuck reporting "Error fetching upgrading progress". 
This is a limitation of how the browser requires manual action to accept self signed certificates. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Save [cht-core.yml](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds/medic%3Amedic%3Amaster/docker-compose%2Fcht-core.yml) and [cht-couchdb.yml](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds/medic%3Amedic%3Amaster/docker-compose%2Fcht-couchdb.yml) in a folder on your PC. (use these names for the files to make upgrades possible)
2. Save [cht-upgrade service compose file](https://github.com/medic/cht-upgrade-service/blob/main/docker-compose.yml) in a different folder. 
3. Start `cht-upgrade-service` with the these env variables: COUCHDB_PASSWORD, CHT_COMPOSE_PATH, DOCKER_CONFIG_PATH. 
4. After the CHT starts up, go to the upgrade page and try to upgrade to another 4.x branch. 
5. Check the upgrade service logs to see that there are no errors and containers were recreated. 
6. Back on the upgrade page, you're still seeing "Error fetching upgrading progress". 

Further: 

8. Doing `curl -k https://localhost` works, and you get HTML back. 
9. In a new tab, open `https://localhost`. Page loads correctly. 
10. Navigate back to the upgrade page and notice that it reports that upgrade was complete. 

**Expected behavior**
Upgrade should work without needing to re-accept the cert. 

**Logs**
```
main.js:3 Error fetching upgrading progress {data: null, status: -1, config: {…}, statusText: '', headers: ƒ, …}
main.js:3 GET https://localhost/api/v2/upgrade net::ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID
```

**Screenshots**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/196898428-30756370-b7eb-4419-a366-9fd049594d82.png)

**Environment**
- Browser: any
- Client platform: (eg: Windows, MacOS, Linux)
- App: (eg: webapp, admin, sentinel, api, couch2pg, cht-conf, etc)
- Version: (eg: 2.15.0, 3.0.0, etc)

**Additional context**
This is caused by nginx creating a new certificate, because we don't save the "self_signed" location as a volume by default. 
Changing `SSL_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH` to `/etc/nginx/private` (the location where the self signed certificates are stored) fixes the issue.

title: Replication depth to get only person contacts at each level
body:
# Description
For a hierarchy branch -> chw_area -> HHs
In order for a supervisor a the branch level to view target aggregates they would need to have a replication depth of 2 (in order to replicate chw contacts in the chw_area). 
This has a down side where the supervisor replicates even the HH contacts which maybe unnecessary especially for aggregating targets in large deployments. The doc count of the supervisor can grow rapidly.
This has caused challenges in https://github.com/medic/config-brac/issues/458 where supervisors are failing to log in. 

## Changes
- Introduce a mid level for replication depth at levels 1 and above. 
This can be used to replicate person contacts in a place without getting the places under it.
This way, using the supervisor example above, a 1.5 replication depth can get the chw_area person contacts necessary for target aggregates without fetching HH places.

title: Improve admin upgrade page UX when upgrade service fails to update containers
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
If an upgrade goes well, we expect API to be down for a couple of seconds, while the new container boots up. This means that the admin upgrade page expects to receive http errors while requesting upgrade progress. 

At the same time, when we call the upgrade endpoint to finalize the upgrade, and the request succeeds, we check whether our currently installed version is the version that we requested via the upgrade. If it is not, we display an error: 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/197211475-37c29a49-38a9-42c5-8469-560ab3976b99.png)

title: Expose CouchDb port 5986 to the docker network
body:
**Describe the issue**
In order to migrate data in the CouchDb cluster, we need access to the CouchDb Cluster APIs, exposed through 5986. 
However, right now this port is bound to `127.0.0.1`, which makes it only accessible from within the CouchDb container. 
Because the API can require POSTs with large payloads, it's impractical to manage the operations manually. This means that, in order to make any cluster changes, you'd need to run a script _inside_ the CouchDb container. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Bind port 5986 to 0.0.0.0 so it's accessible via docker network. 
This would enable us to publish a separate container that only contained the necessary scripts that perform operations across the cluster. This container would share the same network with the cht core installation. 

NB. 5986 was removed in Couch 3.x and all endpoints were moved to 5984: https://github.com/apache/couchdb/issues/1523

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The alternative is to create a separate CouchDb image which bakes in the cluster-move scripts. 
To perform cluster operations, user would need to take their couchdb cluster down, bring up a separate cluster using the image that contains the scripts. This implies we'd need to maintain two CouchDb docker images.

title: Move non-additive actions from Action Bar to "More Options" menu "⋮"
body:
# Overview As a part of our[ longer term goal ](https://github.com/medic/cht-roadmap/issues/61)to align with material design standards, the "Action Bar" at the bottom of the app (left hand side AND right hand side) will be removed. The actions currently in the Action Bar will move to other locations in the app: - **Primary actions** (submitting a report, creating a new person, etc...) will move to a "[Floating Action Button](https://m3.material.io/components/floating-action-button/overview)" - **Supplemental actions** (Edit, Delete, Export, etc...) will move to a "[More Options](https://m3.material.io/components/menus/guidelines#f7434719-f2f5-47e0-a5fe-61309ee37985)" style menu "`⋮`" **This step of the evolution addresses moving some of the supplemental actions to a "More Options" menu.** **NOTE:** 1. [#7778](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7778) updated the way Bulk Delete works, which included moving Bulk Delete related actions out of the Action Bar. That work was included in [4.1.0](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/milestone/105?closed=1). 2. The Action Bar will be temporarily available as [feature flag](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/updates/feature-flags/) by enabling the `can_view_old_action_bar` permission, and it should work the same as before this work. 3. When "More Options" is displayed and the user is looking at a record (report or contact) using a mobile device, the title should still display an ellipsis when the text is too long. 4. No new capabilities are being _added_ as a part of this issue, but one existing capability is being _removed_. We are removing the capability to "Export" from the mobile (single pane) view of the Messages, Reports, and Contacts tabs. # Reports Tab **Summary:** Export, Edit, and Delete will be moved from their current location (LHS and RHS action bars in desktop) to the more options menu. If the user has the right permissions and user type (online vs. offline), the action will be shown in the menu. The action may show up in a disabled state if it is not applicable in the current view. "Export" will no longer be available in mobile view. ### Desktop view
Scenarios and expected behaviors Num | Scenario | Expected behavior -- | -- | -- 1 | - 1 or more reports are selected | The "`⋮`" icon is not shown 2 | - No reports selected

title: Switch staging server to a different URL due to breaking change
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Right now we're using the same staging server for 3.x and 4.x which means the 4.0.0 upgrade is shown to everyone on 3.x, but clicking on the upgrade button will probably brick your server.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
If we instead publish builds of 4.0.0 and later to a completely separate staging database, then they won't be shown to anyone currently running 3.x so users can't upgrade without doing manual steps.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Modifying the 3.x admin app to show some warning, but that requires everyone to upgrade to the latest 3.x release, which is unlikely.
Leaving it as is and communicating directly, but there are cases where people upgrade by accident without reading docs first.

title: Improve experience of "select all" when there are +500 reports
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently the report's "select all" is used to bulk delete reports. Maximum number of reports that "select all" can select [is 500](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/31cbe9dab8c7a7c2d2a5d4558f8112e4d8d9f872/webapp/src/ts/effects/reports.effects.ts#L229), however the user can keep scrolling in the left hand side list and pass over those 500 reports, because the list has infinit scroll. So the user can load 600 reports but only 500 are selected by "select all" (see video below). Selecting all those reports get the system slow, the user actually needs to wait some seconds to see the reports selected.

Because the user can select up to 500, the system attempts to retrieve all those summary documents, so when a report expands then it can show its content, however since there are too many selected, it gets slow and most of them shows "unknown sender" instead of the contact name (I've opened a separate [ticket](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7868) for that race condition). 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Improve the system performance by processing smaller batch of reports and clarify what is "select all" since having infinit scroll makes it confusing. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Many other systems (like gmail) has implemented regular pagination, then when the user clicks on the "select all" it will select all the items of the current page, a page can have 50 records. If they want to see the next page, then the all items from page 1 are deselected, and items from page 2 load and appear deselected as well. The user can select all from one page only.
 
This approach would help selected reports to load faster (instead of selecting 500, now is 50), it won't stress the devices, it won't stress the system by attempting to delete too many docs, and it's more understandable since the user will know the meaning of "select all" scope, a current page of 50 - instead of infinit scroll and let them guess the maximum number (500).

**Additional context**
This topic came up as part of the bulk delete redesign ([comment](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/7846#issuecomment-1301024693))

Video: Current behaviour in v3.17

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/66472237/199640498-acf25dbc-dfb5-48b0-b36a-4aee8560976c.mp4

title: Ensure all services are set up to automatically restart
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently if api crashes it needs manual intervention to start up again.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Add a [restart policy](https://docs.docker.com/compose/compose-file/compose-file-v3/#restart_policy) so all services attempt to restart with appropriate settings. One thing to keep in mind is using an appropriate delay so that the log doesn't fill up the disk and so we don't overload other services.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Not having api crash as much, but bugs happen and we should gracefully recover when possible.

title: API and Sentinel crash in CHT 4 when HAProxy returns HTML
body:
**Describe the bug**

When Sentinel and API services query HAProxy for data and HAProxy returns HTML instead of JSON, they both crash.  

**To Reproduce**
1. get your two docker compose files:
   ```
   wget https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds/medic:medic:master/docker-compose/cht-core.yml
   wget https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds/medic:medic:master/docker-compose/cht-couchdb-clustered.yml
   ```
3. Start a cluster

   ```
   COUCHDB_SERVERS="couchdb.1,couchdb.2,couchdb.3" CHT_COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=test5 COUCHDB_SECRET=test5 DOCKER_CONFIG_PATH=./ COUCHDB_DATA=./couchdb CHT_COMPOSE_PATH=./ COUCHDB_USER=medic COUCHDB_PASSWORD=password docker-compose -f cht-core.yml -f cht-couchdb-clustered.yml up
   ```
1. ensure CHT is up in browser and with `curl`
   1.  browse to https://localhost/
   2. find IP of haproxy with `docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} - {{range.NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' $(docker ps -q)` and run the command and see JSON of healthy medic DB: `curl -s http://medic:password@172.27.0.3:5984/medic | jq` 
1. check for a container names with `docker ps --format '{{.Names}}'|grep couchdb` and then stop a couch node: `docker stop deleteme_couchdb.2_1`
1. ensure CHT is DOWN in browser and with `curl`
   1.  browse to https://localhost/
   2. find IP of haproxy (`172.27.0.3` in this case) and run the command and see JSON of SAD medic DB: `curl -s http://medic:password@172.27.0.3:5984/medic | jq` 
1. start couch node again: `docker start deleteme_couchdb.2_1`
1. note that API and Sentinel have not restarted and will not restart. Online users see a full page spinner

**Expected behavior**
API and Sentinel stay do not crash when given HTML

**Logs**
[See AT ticket with extensive logs](https://github.com/medic/cht-release-testing/issues/208#issuecomment-1301449855).

**Screenshots**
NA

**Environment**
- Instance: local
- Browser: NA
- Client platform: NA
- App: sentinel, api, haproxy
- Version: 4.0.0 as of da1e1d8581392b8e9755019e3a814c85bc20a9df

**Additional context**
Solutions might be to be more defensive and not crash when getting HTML or [have HAProxy never return HTML](https://github.com/medic/cht-release-testing/issues/208#issuecomment-1301490674). 

Also related is this earlier [bug about the full page spinner](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7356).

title: Enketo selected option highlight color changes incorrectly on drag
body:
**Describe the bug**

When filling in an Enketo form on mobile the CHT shows a bright orange background behind selected options. This should always highlight the selected option, but it's quite easy to get the selected and highlighted option to be different options.

This was observed multiple times in a recent CMMB site visit. Users appeared to be coping with this by increased scrolling and re-selecting options.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Using a mobile phone go to a form which has radio button options
2. Select an option - notice the radio icon shows selected, and the background is bright orange
3. On a different option, press and hold for around 1 second before dragging down
4. Note how the second option has been highlighted, but not selected

**Expected behavior**
The highlight should always indicate the selected option.

**Logs**
N/A

**Screenshots**
![Screenshot from 2022-11-07 11-49-49](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2064938/200199614-728c2798-42dc-419c-aef5-8191aaaee29b.png)

**Environment**
- Instance: local
- Browser: Chrome, but _not_ Firefox.
- Client platform: Android and Linux
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.10.0 and 4.0.0

**Additional context**

- The highlight was added in [1630](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/1630)
- The colour is also ["quite horrible"](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/1630#issuecomment-159145207), and the text colour is difficult to read because white on orange is low contrast. Work with @n-orlowski to figure out how this should look, or if the highlighting is even still needed.

title: Release 4.1.0
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [x] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`.
- [x] Raise a new issue called `Update dependencies for <version>` with a description that links to [the documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/guides/update-dependencies/). This should be done early in the release cycle so find a volunteer to take this on and assign it to them.
- [x] Write an update in the weekly [Medic Product Team call agenda](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AuJ7SerLuOPESBjQlJqpBtzwSAoVf5ykTT7fjyJBT0/edit) summarising development and acceptance testing progress and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` release testing can begin.

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development using this template:
```
@core_devs I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing.
- [x] Announce the start of release testing on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*Release testing has started for {{version}} of {{product}}*

To get a sneak peak at this upcoming release, you can install `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` on your testing environment. We suggest you test your forms and workflows with this release candidate version and raise any issues that you experience. This helps to to discover any potential regressions that wouldn't otherwise be caught during release testing.

Keep an eye on the forum for the release announcement in the next couple of weeks!
```
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, that they're correctly labelled (in particular: they have the right Type, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate), and have human readable descriptions.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
  - [x] Provide description, screenshots, videos, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions) and update the EOL date and status of previous releases. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.
  - [x] Assign the PR to:
    - The Director of Technology
    - An SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient
- [x] Until release testing passes, make sure regressions are fixed in `master`, cherry-pick them into the release branch, and release another beta.
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds_4/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [ ] Execute the scalability testing suite on the final build and download the scalability results on S3 at medic-e2e/scalability/$TAG_NAME. Add the release `.jtl` file to `cht-core/tests/scalability/previous_results`. More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [ ] Upgrade the `demo-cht.dev` instance to this version.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*We're excited to announce the release of {{version}} of {{product}}*

New features include {{key_features}}. We've also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

Read the [release notes]({{url}}) for full details.

Following our support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read our [software support documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions).

Check out our [roadmap](https://github.com/orgs/medic/projects/112) to see what we're working on next.
```
- [ ] Add one last update to the [Medic Product Team call agenda](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AuJ7SerLuOPESBjQlJqpBtzwSAoVf5ykTT7fjyJBT0/edit) and use this meeting to lead an internal release retrospective covering what went well and areas to improve for next time.
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Update dependencies for 4.2.0
body:
Follow [the documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/guides/update-dependencies/).

Due to the 4.0.0 release we can update more dependencies without a breaking change, specifically dependencies in docker images. Bump these dependencies (eg: Node 18) and update the docs with the additional steps.

Update `node-sass` -> `sass` to resolve this deprecation warning:

```
'node-sass' usage is deprecated and will be removed in a future major version. To opt-out of the deprecated behaviour and start using 'sass' uninstall 'node-sass'.
```

Update messageformat to resolve this deprecation warning:

```
WARN deprecated messageformat@2.3.0: Package renamed as '@messageformat/core', see messageformat.github.io for more details. 'messageformat' will eventually provide a polyfill for Intl.MessageFormat, once it's been defined by Unicode & ECMA.
```

title: Confirmation prompt for "Cancel" button in forms
body:
**Problem Statement**
A recent implementation of CHT has yielded a lot of feedback and one of the most popular among them is accidental cancellation of forms. When filling the forms, particularly long ones, users have noted that due to accidental presses they get exited out of a partially filled form quite often. This has resulted in considerable delays during form submissions and extreme inconvenience for the people being surveyed.

**Solution**
A prompt requesting confirmation whether the user really intends to exit out of the form or not. A simple popup with "yes" or "no" option could save a lot of time for both the users and the patients.

title: CHT Application developer survey
Calling `/api/v1/settings/deprecated-transitions` prevents any future transitions to run over new records in API
body:
**Describe the bug**
The call to `/api/v1/settings/deprecated-transitions` will cause the settings object in the transitions lib to be unset, preventing all calls that pass documents to transitions to resolve. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Enable `death_reporting`. This doesn't just affect this transition, but this transition's code will be effective in triggering the error. Also make sure that you have no other transitions config errors, transitions must be working in order to trigger the bug. 
2. Create an SMS form. Any form will do, I just copied the ["DR" form from standard config](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/config/standard/app_settings.json#L3916). 
3. Submit a DR form through `api/v2/records` to check that the call works. 
4. Call `/api/v1/settings/deprecated-transitions` . You can even do it from your browser. 
5. Submit a DR form through `api/v2/records`. Notice that the request hangs. Also if you check api logs you'll see something like 
```
2022-11-17 09:31:19 ERROR: UNHANDLED REJECTION! 
2022-11-17 09:31:19 ERROR:   Reason: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'death_reporting')
    at Object.get (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/src/config.js:10:21)
    at getConfig (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/death_reporting.js:13:32)
    at getConfirmFormCodes (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/death_reporting.js:14:35)
    at isConfirmForm (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/death_reporting.js:17:31)
    at Object.filter (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/death_reporting.js:52:8)
    at canRun (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/index.js:220:16)
    at applyTransition (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/index.js:270:18)
    at wrapper (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/node_modules/lodash/lodash.js:5213:19)
    at /home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/node_modules/async/dist/async.js:3674:28
    at replenish (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/node_modules/async/dist/async.js:446:21) {
  [stack]: "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'death_reporting')\n" +
    '    at Object.get (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/src/config.js:10:21)\n' +
    '    at getConfig (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/death_reporting.js:13:32)\n' +
    '    at getConfirmFormCodes (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/death_reporting.js:14:35)\n' +
    '    at isConfirmForm (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/death_reporting.js:17:31)\n' +
    '    at Object.filter (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/death_reporting.js:52:8)\n' +
    '    at canRun (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/index.js:220:16)\n' +
    '    at applyTransition (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/index.js:270:18)\n' +
    '    at wrapper (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/node_modules/lodash/lodash.js:5213:19)\n' +
    '    at /home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/node_modules/async/dist/async.js:3674:28\n' +
    '    at replenish (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/transitions/node_modules/async/dist/async.js:446:21)',
  [message]: "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'death_reporting')"
} 
```

**Expected behavior**
API should be able to process transitions. 

**Logs**
Included above. 

**Environment**
- Instance: Production instance
- App: api
- Version: 3.11+

**Additional context**
I randomly noticed the error logs in a production instance, reporting that their integration calls are failing. 
This bug was introduced a long time ago, but we got away with it. Currently only `cht-conf` calls that endpoint. If there are no deprecated transitions in the config, the `settings` endpoint is called immediately afterwards, which resolves the issue by resetting the transitions lib (it gets reset when settings are updated).
However, if the config contains deprecated transitions, and the `settings` call is made, API is stuck in an invalid transitions state. 

**For projects that are affected by this**
- updating settings will fix the problem
- updating translations will fix the problem

The change can be insignificant, it only serves the purpose to trigger the code that runs in API when settings and translations are changed.

title: Error loading forms containing countdown-widget
body:
**Describe the bug**
Forms using the [`countdown-widget` timer](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/814ed5cd488d783784959e60c4066a665319accb/webapp/src/js/enketo/widgets/countdown-widget.js) fail to load in `4.x`.  

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Use a `4.x` version of cht-core
2. Upload a form that contains a countdown timer. (e.g. [this one](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/blob/master/forms/countdown-timer.xml))
3. Try to open the form 
4. See error

**Expected behavior**
The form and the timer widget should function without issue.

**Details**
This issue was unintentionally caused by [eslint refactoring changes](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/7728/files#diff-9a33bc7a9218eeeda86158feb834f8987bec3945173989f44aa87e447f580970).  Basically, `loadSound` was changed from a `function` to a `const`. The problem is that `loadSound()` is being called on line `67` which is _before_ it is actually declared on line `70`.  Thanks to the "magic" of [function hoisting](http://www.adequatelygood.com/JavaScript-Scoping-and-Hoisting.html) in JS, you can apparently reference functions before they are declared but you cannot do the same for `const`....

The fix there should be simple, though.  Just need to move the declaration of `loadSound` up before it is used.  We should also add some kind of automated e2e test that will verify the behavior of this widget so this does not happen again!

**Logs**
Browser console logs:

```
feedback.service.ts:77 TypeError: loadSound is not a function
    at countdown-widget.js:67:16
    at new TimerAnimation (countdown-widget.js:60:18)
    at Timerwidget._init (countdown-widget.js:41:5)
    at new Widget (widget.js:21:21)
    at Timerwidget._createSuperInternal (createSuper.js:15:1)
    at new Timerwidget (countdown-widget.js:30:7)
    at Collection._instantiateSingleWidget (widgets-controller.js:203:19)
    at widgets-controller.js:227:43
    at Array.forEach (<anonymous>)
    at Collection.instantiate (widgets-controller.js:227:23)
```

**Environment**
- Instance: local
- Browser: Chromium
- Client platform: Linux
- App: webapp
- Version: 4.x (master)

**Additional context**
First noticed by @lorerod!

title: Show a more useful error message when decrypting using a different secret
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The Credentials service uses a configurable key to do the encryption/decryption.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Right now if you set a credential, then change the key, then try to decrypt the credential you get a cryptic (no pun intended) error message.

```
REQ 7ed1d44f-c54a-4ea8-bcb3-5e72258e81ca 172.21.0.1 - POST /api/v2/sms/rapidpro/incoming-messages HTTP/1.0
2022-11-24 09:01:32 WARN: Non-numeric error code: ERR_OSSL_EVP_BAD_DECRYPT 
2022-11-24 09:01:32 ERROR: Server error: Error: error:06065064:digital envelope routines:EVP_DecryptFinal_ex:bad decrypt
    at Decipheriv.final (node:internal/crypto/cipher:193:29)
    at /shared-libs/settings/src/index.js:67:30
    at processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:96:5) {
  [stack]: 'Error: error:06065064:digital envelope routines:EVP_DecryptFinal_ex:bad decrypt\n' +
    '    at Decipheriv.final (node:internal/crypto/cipher:193:29)\n' +
    '    at /shared-libs/settings/src/index.js:67:30\n' +
    '    at processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:96:5)',
  [message]: 'error:06065064:digital envelope routines:EVP_DecryptFinal_ex:bad decrypt',
  library: 'digital envelope routines',
  function: 'EVP_DecryptFinal_ex',
  reason: 'bad decrypt',
  code: 'ERR_OSSL_EVP_BAD_DECRYPT'
} 
```

The fix is to set the credential again which uses the new encryption key, but it's hard to tell that from the error message. Replace this error message with a more useful one which lets you know how to fix it.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None...

**Additional context**
[Initially reported here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7472#issuecomment-1326153603).

title: Error 500 when processing SMS message missing year from Bikram Sambat aggregate
body:
**Describe the bug**
If a form definition contains a bikram sambat aggregate field, but the receiving SMS is missing this field, API will throw an error and not process the record. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a form with a `bsAggregate` field (added with issue: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/4613) 
2. Create a record that is missing this field.
3. See error

**Expected behavior**
We should be able to gracefully handle missing fields in SMS forms. 

**Logs**
```
ERROR: Can not aggregate bsAggreDate without bsYear 
   [stack]: 'TypeError: Cannot read property \'patient_id\' of undefined\n    at Object.exports.merge (/srv/software/medic-api/md5-IaUJW7p4rpaMwbWhKl5C1A==/src/services/report/smsparser.js:373:35)\n    at getDataRecord (/srv/software/medic-api/md5-IaUJW7p4rpaMwbWhKl5C1A==/src/services/records.js:129:17)\n    at Object.createByForm (/srv/software/medic-api/md5-IaUJW7p4rpaMwbWhKl5C1A==/src/services/records.js:190:10)\n    at messages.map.message (/srv/software/medic-api/md5-IaUJW7p4rpaMwbWhKl5C1A==/src/services/messaging.js:174:48)\n    at Array.map (<anonymous>)\n    at createDocs (/srv/software/medic-api/md5-IaUJW7p4rpaMwbWhKl5C1A==/src/services/messaging.js:174:25)\n    at validateIncomingMessages.then.messages (/srv/software/medic-api/md5-IaUJW7p4rpaMwbWhKl5C1A==/src/services/messaging.js:233:25)\n    at <anonymous>\n    at process._tickCallback (internal/process/next_tick.js:188:7)',
RES POST /api/sms HTTP/1.1 500 35 134.816 ms
ERROR: Server error: { TypeError: Cannot read property 'patient_id' of undefined
```

- App: api
- Version: 3.15+

title: Release 4.2.0
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [ ] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`.
- [x] Raise a new issue called `Update dependencies for <version>` with a description that links to [the documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/guides/update-dependencies/). This should be done early in the release cycle so find a volunteer to take this on and assign it to them.
- [x] Write an update in the weekly [Medic Product Team call agenda](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AuJ7SerLuOPESBjQlJqpBtzwSAoVf5ykTT7fjyJBT0/edit) summarising development and acceptance testing progress and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have passed acceptance testing and have been merged into `master` release testing can begin.

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development using this template:
```
@core_devs I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a git tag and when CI completes successfully notify the QA team that it's ready for release testing.
- [x] Announce the start of release testing on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*Release testing has started for {{version}} of {{product}}*

To get a sneak peak at this upcoming release, you can install `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` on your testing environment. We suggest you test your forms and workflows with this release candidate version and raise any issues that you experience. This helps to to discover any potential regressions that wouldn't otherwise be caught during release testing.

Keep an eye on the forum for the release announcement in the next couple of weeks!
```
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, that they're correctly labelled (in particular: they have the right Type, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate), and have human readable descriptions.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
  - [x] Provide description, screenshots, videos, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions) and update the EOL date and status of previous releases. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.
  - [x] Assign the PR to:
    - The Director of Technology
    - An SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient
- [x] Until release testing passes, make sure regressions are fixed in `master`, cherry-pick them into the release branch, and release another beta.
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds_4/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Execute the scalability testing suite on the final build and download the scalability results on S3 at medic-e2e/scalability/$TAG_NAME. Add the release `.jtl` file to `cht-core/tests/scalability/previous_results`. More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [ ] Upgrade the `demo-cht.dev` instance to this version.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*We're excited to announce the release of {{version}} of {{product}}*

New features include {{key_features}}. We've also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

Read the [release notes]({{url}}) for full details.

Following our support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read our [software support documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions).

Check out our [roadmap](https://github.com/orgs/medic/projects/112) to see what we're working on next.
```
- [x] Add one last update to the [Medic Product Team call agenda](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AuJ7SerLuOPESBjQlJqpBtzwSAoVf5ykTT7fjyJBT0/edit) and use this meeting to lead an internal release retrospective covering what went well and areas to improve for next time.
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Use _all_docs to get forms documents in API
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
If installation is interrupted before view indexing is finished, API will start up immediately, without waiting for indexes to be up to date. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
I think this warrants a discussion. 

Some context: 
- this case can present when: 
  - CHT 4.x is being installed on an existing data-set - for example when upgrading from 3.x without pre-indexing views
  - an upgrade is staged, but finalized at a later date (and after a significant number of changes have been pushed to the database) 
- in this scenario, API has already started on the correct version, so we are passed the point of upgrade. where the old version of API would still be running
- we are facing potential downtime while views are not up to date, regardless of choice

The options are to:
1. Wait for all views to be indexed before starting API
- this means that the API startup page will be displayed for the duration of this process
- API will not respond to any requests 

2. Start API anyway
- depending on which views require indexing, API could be working partially, responding to some requests that don't require querying  these views, and timing out for others
- startup could be blocked because some views are required in startup steps: for example `medic-client/doc_by_type` is queried when getting forms: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/services/forms.js#L23

One thing to note is that most projects will not actively use all views. For example, some webapp projects might never use SMS views and vice versa. When installing or upgrading, **all views** will be indexed.

Manually set the `editStatus` of an Enketo form to `false` before rendering the form. During the form initialization, the re-evaluation of some `calculate`s can cause the form to be marked as edited before receiving any input from the user.
