title: Move additive actions from the Action Bar to Floating Action Button
body: # Overview As a part of our [longer term goal](https://github.com/medic/cht-roadmap/issues/61) to align with material design standards, the "Action Bar" at the bottom of the app (left hand side AND right hand side) is being removed. This issue will **remove the Action Bar** (_see Notes below_), **introduce a [Floating Action Button (FAB)](https://m3.material.io/components/floating-action-button/overview)**, and **move additive actions** (creating reports, places, people, etc...) from the Action Bar to the FAB. This will affect single pane (mobile) and dual pane views (desktop) on the [Messages](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/features/messaging/), [Reports](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/features/reports/), and [People](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/features/contacts/) tabs. The Figma mockups can be found [here](https://www.figma.com/file/3wFzMcNEGxV6se1QWftckk/UX-Stages?node-id=230%3A9424&t=BsHuimIOqnExyorI-0). #### NOTES 1. The Action Bar will be temporarily available through a [feature flag](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/updates/feature-flags/) by enabling the `can_view_old_action_bar` [permission](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/user-permissions/). Be aware that [#7778](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7778) **_uses the same permission_**. 2. Issue [#5962](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5962) will be worked on separately, _after_ the FAB update is released. This FAB issue will define a default order when multiple actions are in the FAB. # FAB Contents This table illustrates which actions are **currently** available based on what is selected and which device is being used. This is not changing. There are [permissions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/user-permissions/) to control the visibility of the Call and Message actions on the Contacts tab. ![Screenshot 2023-01-19 at 2 47 50 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10096985/213544955-8e0ee7f1-08f9-419a-8f5e-f31bd4fca2e3.png) _In all cases, only show relevant actions based on `context`._ ## Mobile View The FAB options will show up as a drawer from the bottom with rows of actions, much like it looks today for Forms, but with the other options (Call, Message, Contact Forms) in this list as well. ![Screenshot 2023-01-19 at 2 39 49 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10096985/213543673-52da4e12-fe2e-4f5f-9925-78b5854bb92d.png) ## Desktop View There are two trigger buttons, one is located in the list's footer which only has a label (no icon), and the other one is located on the top right side and only has an icon (no label). ![Screenshot 2023-03-07 at 6 02 22 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/66472237/224626072-1881959a-2c4d-4b56-9e36-2afd343b8db7.png) The FAB options will show up as a modal window in the middle of the screen. The options will be in a list just like the mobile drawer mentioned above. If the option name is too long, then display it in two lines and use the ellipsis to trim the text. If the user clicks outside the modal or presses "Esc" from the keyboard, also if the user navigates to another page, then the modal should close. ## Trigger button The old action bar will be removed and tapping on the list footer's button (desktop) or in the FAB (mobile) will bring up the action list. FAB button: - No label - If there is more than one action: plus sign icon - If there is only one action, but the action's icon isn't Font Awesome: plus sign icon. - If there is only one action, and the action is a Font Awesome: action's icon. List footer's button: - No icon - Show label ## Order of items in the list Issue https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5962 will allow a custom order by for actions in the list, but the default will be as below. Reference the colorful table above to understand what is shown when. For example, you'll notice that there are never more than 3 "types" of things shown at once. 1. Call 2. Message 3. "Place" Contact Forms, in alphabetical 4. "Person" Contact Forms, alphabetical 5. App Forms, alphabetical # Messages Tab The only action available on this tab is `Send message`. The old action bar will be removed and tapping on the list footer's button (desktop) or in the FAB (mobile) will bring up the `Send Message` modal. # Contacts Tab The Contacts Tab has five possible actions: `Call`, `Send message`, `New place`, `New person`, and `New action` (report). ## Mobile View #### Left Hand Side (Top Level) - The only option available is `New place`. Move it to the FAB. When the search input has the focus and the soft-keyboard appears, then hide the FAB. #### Right Hand Side (Place) - There are three options: `New place`, 'New person', and `New action`. Move all these to the FAB. - Never skip the drawer if the one thing is a Form. #### Right Hand Side (Person) - There are three* options: `Call`, `Send message`, and `New action`. Move all these to the FAB. - Never skip the drawer if the one thing is a Form. _* `Call` only shows up if you are on a mobile device._ ## Desktop View #### Left Hand Side The action will be moved to the list footer's bottom. #### Right Hand Side Same as in mobile # Reports Tab The Reports tab has four main Actions: `Submit report`, `Send message`, `Update facility` and `Review`. ## Review action - This action is moved to the More Options menu. - When a user taps on it, shows a modal (desktop) or a bottom drawer (mobile) with two options: "Has errors" and "Correct". Show in one row, with "Has errors" on the left and "Correct" on the right. - The review badge is moved next to the form's name. ![Screenshot 2023-03-13 at 4 00 43 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/66472237/224654728-9bd83add-5aa0-408f-b6fc-c4fa0e774bae.png) ## Mobile View #### Left Hand Side The only option available is `Submit report`. Move it to the FAB. - Icon should always be a `+` - Always show the drawer, even if there is only one thing on the list - The FAB is hidden behind the Filter panel when it's open. - When the search input has the focus and the soft-keyboard appears, then hide the FAB if possible. - While in multiselect (bulk delete), hide the FAB #### Right Hand Side - There are two options: `Send message` and `Update facility`. Move it to the FAB - While in multiselect (bulk delete), hide the FAB ## Desktop View #### Left Hand Side - The only option is `Submit report`. Move it to the list footer's button. - While in multiselect (bulk delete), hide the FAB #### Right Hand Side - There are two options: `Send message` and `Update facility`. Move it to the FAB - While in multiselect (bulk delete), hide the FAB

title: Upgrade webapp's angular to v15
body:
# Description

Upgrading from v12 to v13:
- All @angular/XX libraries were upgraded to v13
- [Typescript was upgraded to v4.4.2](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-4-4.html) which is the minimum required by Angular 13
- Angular 13 now creates a `.angular/cache` directory [to improve build speed](https://blog.angular.io/angular-v13-is-now-available-cce66f7bc296#05df). This was added to the gitignore file.
- The ` MethodCall` from angular compiler [was deprecated here](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/42882/files#diff-1002bdc266028e1c303492a63ed5990124b8fd29a8f87098d07f86c0519d47f0R319), I've replaced it with `Call`
- Now there's an error when trying to build the app and when there's a `window.location.reload(true|false)` [this parameter isn't standard](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Location/reload), I've removed it.

Upgrading from v13 to v14:
- [Typescript was upgraded to 4.6](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-4-6/#breaking-changes) which is the minimum required for Angular 14.
- The typescript eslint libs were upgraded to support the new version of typescript.
- I fixed the unit tests, and now we need to reset the store in the `beforeEach`.
- Also, the new version of ngrx changed a bit how [tests are done](https://ngrx.io/guide/store/testing#testing-selectors) in selectors, that’s something I fixed.
- The [parser provider](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/providers/parse.provider.ts) was fixed, something changed in the [angular compiler classes](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/50f95f831e7da84e2b879dd4b9b7764ca07ef0e7/packages/compiler/src/expression_parser/parser.ts).
- At this point I can see an improvement in speed, when running `grunt unit-webapp` on `master branch` (angular v12) it takes 3m 31.3s to complete, while on my branch (angular v14) it takes 2m 7s
- Removed `polyfills-es5.js`, since angular **drop support for IE11**, see [End of IE11 support](https://blog.angular.io/angular-v13-is-now-available-cce66f7bc296)

Upgrading from v14 to v15:
- Removed `relativeLinkResolution` from app router module, [depracation](https://angular.io/guide/update-to-version-15#relativelinkresolution-is-not-configurable-in-the-router).
- Upgraded typescript to 4.8 min supported by Angular v15
- Upgraded typescript eslint libs to match the new version of typescript. (@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin: 5.43, @typescript-eslint/parser: 5.43)
- Upgraded NgRx libraries and the Ngx Translate Core lib to support Angular v15 (@ngrx/effects, @ngrx/store, @ngx-translate/core)
- Set the `tsconfig.base.json`'s target to ES2020 to support latest typescript, and fix the error: `Class constructor cannot be invoked without 'new'`
- Fixed unit test configuration to match how angular finds specs files. That's in angular.json and test.ts
- Fixed angular material styles and classes selectors, more in [mdc v15](https://material.angular.io/guide/mdc-migration).

**NOTE:**
Whenever we have the error below, it's likely that `@angular/compiler`, `@angular-devkit/build-angular`  or `@angular-builders/custom-webpack` aren't resolved properly in the `package-lock.json`. So, uninstall these 3, then install them again in that order.

![Screen Shot 2022-12-22 at 12 36 21 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/66472237/209088049-aaf33272-dd0c-4640-9917-a309c5782eea.png)

title: Error deleting documents on slow connection
body:
**Describe the bug**
Users get an error when bulk deleting documents. The message they see says "Error deleting document". 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Log in as an online user with the ability to bulk delete reports
2. Make your browser window small enough so that it is showing mobile view (single pane)
3. Go to the reports tab
4. Throttle your connection to "Slow 3G" or "Low-end mobile"
5. Go into "Select" mode
6. Select several (I did 4) reports 
7. Immediately tap on "Delete All"
8. Tap on "Delete" on the confirmation page
9. See the error

**Expected behavior**
The documents I have selected should be deleted without error OR don't give me the option to delete until you are actually ready to delete them. 

**Logs**

[127-0-0-1.my.local-ip.co.har.txt](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/files/10288574/127-0-0-1.my.local-ip.co.har.txt)


**Screenshots/Videos**

**3.17.0**

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10096985/209172384-ec306878-60f0-4872-9c4f-62a396afb0a9.mov

</details>

**4.1.0**

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10096985/209172437-9d5ff491-13a3-43be-a376-adcc9a95a240.mov




**Environment**
- Instance: demo-cht.dev (3.17.0) and local docker instance (4.1.0)
- Browser: Chrome
- Client platform: MacOS
- App: WebApp
- Version: I've verified it is an issue on 3.17.0 and 4.1.0. [Another user is experiencing it on 3.16.1](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/experience-with-bulk-deleting-reports/2142/3?u=michael).

**Additional context**
For me, this wasn't an issue on desktop in 3.17.0 because the "Delete All" action bar doesn't show up until everything it needs is loaded. On 4.1.0, the "Delete All" option shows up immediately so it is still an issue even on desktop. 

At time of writing this, there have already been a few other issues identified related to bulk delete: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7300 , https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7868 , https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7883

title: CI build fails for external contributors
body:
**Describe the issue**
The CI build steps for internal contributors are: 
1) build and test all services code (webapp, api, sentinel, etc)
2) build services docker images 
3) publish services docker images to private amazon ECR

For external contributors, step 3 would fail, since they do not have access to the private amazon ECR credentials (saved as a GH environment variable). Instead of publishing to amazon ECR, the images should be saved as artefacts and attached to the GH build. 
However, this path is not taken at the moment, and the CI is trying to push service images to ECR, and fails: 

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/runs/3888134996/jobs/6635149994

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Fix the build for external contributors.

title: Allow users to report client-side crashes via screenshots
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently when a CHT application causes a crash, the user sees a basic error message with no actionable in distinguishable details.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9014751/213537506-df9be9ad-f1f4-4ae0-847e-391802b4478c.png)

Although the details of the crash are recorded via feedback documents - it would sometimes be useful for users to report their users via screenshot. 

Example: an app developer in an offline context is working beside a user who experiences a crash.
Example: a user experiences a crash which cannot be found in feedback docs
Example: an app developer is asked to help fix crashes in an app where they don't have access.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
It'd be great if the crashing stack was hidden by default but the user could choose to view it. 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9014751/213540367-aa73ea68-90c0-49b1-b267-3b600fcd2e16.png)

Clicking details could show some details would would allow an app developer to fix the problem:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9014751/213541514-511f9aab-f998-419f-ae01-647a07f1108c.png)

I'm not sure what will realistically fit in a screenshot - but it might also be valuable to include:

* top of crash stack
* instance url
* username
* current date time
* last successful sync time

title: API Crashes on malformed translation docs
body:
**Describe the bug**
API fails to start when any of the translation docs `messages-xx` is missing some properties that are expected. 
This can happen for a number of reasons, and has been the case for many releases. 
Since 4.0, this can be triggered very easily when deleting languages. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Make sure Sentinel is up and up to date with the queue.
2. Create a new language (can do from admin app)
3. Delete this new language. (can do from admin app)
4. Wait for Sentinel to process this deletion. 
5. Restart API. 
6. See error. 

**Expected behavior**
API should not crash when languages are deleted. 

**Logs**
```
2023-01-23 15:31:19 ERROR: Fatal error initialising medic-api 
2023-01-23 15:31:19 ERROR: TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object
    at Function.keys (<anonymous>)
    at Object.loadTranslations (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/translation-utils/src/translation-utils.js:5:12)
    at /home/diana/projects/medic/api/src/services/config-watcher.js:32:55
    at Array.forEach (<anonymous>)
    at /home/diana/projects/medic/api/src/services/config-watcher.js:27:23
    at processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:96:5)
    at async /home/diana/projects/medic/api/server.js:38:5 {
  [stack]: 'TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object\n' +
    '    at Function.keys (<anonymous>)\n' +
    '    at Object.loadTranslations (/home/diana/projects/medic/shared-libs/translation-utils/src/translation-utils.js:5:12)\n' +
    '    at /home/diana/projects/medic/api/src/services/config-watcher.js:32:55\n' +
    '    at Array.forEach (<anonymous>)\n' +
    '    at /home/diana/projects/medic/api/src/services/config-watcher.js:27:23\n' +
    '    at processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:96:5)\n' +
    '    at async /home/diana/projects/medic/api/server.js:38:5',
  [message]: 'Cannot convert undefined or null to object'
} 
```

**Environment**
- Instance: local
- App: api
- Version: 3.4.0+ would crash on malformed translation docs, but after 4.0 api will crash when languages are deleted because that will produce the "malformed" docs (tombstones of deleted translation docs) and serve them to translations utils. 

The workaround for 4.x projects encountering this is to delete all `messages-xx` tombstones and restart API.

title: CHT 4.x Docker services fail to communicate in multi-nodes setup
body:
**Describe the bug**
Often, when I start my multi-node clustered CHT 4.x instance, I get errors in my API container and nginx containers and the CHT fails to start

**To Reproduce**
1. Set up 4 computers as a [multi-node clustered CHT 4.x instance](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/4.x/self-hosting-multiple-nodes/)
2. run `docker compose up -d` on the CHT Core node
3. Go to the browser and try and load the CHT

**Expected behavior**
The CHT shows a login  page and loads correctly

**Logs**

The API container has this error repeatedly:

```
RequestError: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.1.7:5984
    at new RequestError (/api/node_modules/request-promise-core/lib/errors.js:14:15)
    at Request.plumbing.callback (/api/node_modules/request-promise-core/lib/plumbing.js:87:29)
    at Request.RP$callback [as _callback] (/api/node_modules/request-promise-core/lib/plumbing.js:46:31)
    at self.callback (/api/node_modules/request/request.js:185:22)
    at Request.emit (node:events:513:28)
    at Request.onRequestError (/api/node_modules/request/request.js:877:8)
    at ClientRequest.emit (node:events:513:28)
    at Socket.socketErrorListener (node:_http_client:481:9)
    at Socket.emit (node:events:513:28)
    at emitErrorNT (node:internal/streams/destroy:157:8) {
  cause: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.1.7:5984
      at TCPConnectWrap.afterConnect [as oncomplete] (node:net:1247:16) {
    errno: -111,
    code: 'ECONNREFUSED',
    syscall: 'connect',
    address: '10.0.1.7',
    port: 5984
  },
  error: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.1.7:5984
      at TCPConnectWrap.afterConnect [as oncomplete] (node:net:1247:16) {
    errno: -111,
    code: 'ECONNREFUSED',
    syscall: 'connect',
    address: '10.0.1.7',
    port: 5984
  }
}
```

This, in turn, causes the the webserver (nginx) to fail to talk to API, so the browser to my instance gives a `502` error:

```
502 Bad Gateway
nginx/1.19.6
```

The nginx container of course has errors too, because API can't talk to HA Proxy:

```
CERTIFICATE MODE = SELF_SIGNED
Running SSL certificate checks
self signed SSL cert already exists.
Launching Nginx
/docker-entrypoint.sh: Configuration complete; ready for start up
10.131.161.1 - - [26/Jan/2023:23:33:51 +0000] "GET /medic/login?redirect=https%3A%2F%2F10-131-161-147.my.local-ip.co%2F HTTP/1.1" 502 157 "-" "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Ubuntu; Linux x86_64; rv:109.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/109.0"
2023/01/26 23:33:51 [error] 29#29: *1 connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream, client: 10.131.161.1, server: , request: "GET /medic/login?redirect=https%3A%2F%2F10-131-161-147.my.local-ip.co%2F HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.0.1.4:5988/medic/login?redirect=https%3A%2F%2F10-131-161-147.my.local-ip.co%2F", host: "10-131-161-147.my.local-ip.co"
```

**Screenshots**

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8253488/214974738-882076a9-d8b6-41e2-a503-0179fcd8e725.png)

**Environment**
- Instance: local dev
- Browser: all
- Client platform: ubuntu
- App: docker
- Version: any multi-node clustered 4.x instance

**Additional context**

When testing this, everything may work on the first try.  If that's the case try and run this 5 or 6 times on the CHT core node and check in a browser if it succeeds each time:

```
docker kill $(docker ps --quiet)
cd /home/ubuntu/cht/upgrade-service/
docker compose up -d
```

The semi-functional work around is to aggressively restart containers, with out changing anything and then some how it starts working again.  

There was [some speculation](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C02F2TAME90/p1674756143835159?thread_ts=1674694330.228769&cid=C02F2TAME90) (private slack thread) that the fix to this was:
* change all CouchDB names from `couchdb.1` -> `couchdb-1.local`
* in the CouchDB compose files (1 on each node), add an explicit name: `container_name: couchdb-1.local`

This is not the case.  I still get high occurrences of this error when I set my CouchDB servers in my CHT Core `.env` file to have the correct name: `COUCHDB_SERVERS=couchdb-1.local,couchdb-2.local,couchdb-3.local` and then set each of CouchDB compose file look like this node 1 in this example (below).  

```yaml
version: '3.9'
services:
  couchdb-1.local:
    container_name: couchdb-1.local
    image: public.ecr.aws/s5s3h4s7/cht-couchdb:4.0.1-4.0.1
    volumes:
      - ./srv:/opt/couchdb/data
      - cht-credentials:/opt/couchdb/etc/local.d/
    environment:
      - "COUCHDB_USER=${COUCHDB_USER:-admin}"
      - "COUCHDB_PASSWORD=${COUCHDB_PASSWORD:?COUCHDB_PASSWORD must be set}"
      - "COUCHDB_SECRET=${COUCHDB_SECRET}"
      - "COUCHDB_UUID=${COUCHDB_UUID}"
      - "SVC_NAME=${SVC1_NAME:-couchdb-1.local}"
      - "CLUSTER_PEER_IPS=couchdb-2.local,couchdb-3.local"
      - "COUCHDB_LOG_LEVEL=${COUCHDB_LOG_LEVEL:-error}"
    logging:
      driver: "local"
      options:
        max-size: "${LOG_MAX_SIZE:-50m}"
        max-file: "${LOG_MAX_FILES:-20}"
    restart: always
    networks:
      - cht-net
      - cht-overlay
volumes:
  cht-credentials:
networks:
  cht-net:
     name: ${CHT_NETWORK:-cht-net}
  cht-overlay:
     driver: overlay
     external: true
```

# Description

There was a [discussion on Slack](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C02F2TAME90/p1674141851263569) recently about having a script we could encourage folks to run who were having troubles running CHT 4.x's docker containers. title: Support for running Tasks.js and Targets.js without Nools
body:
### Description

This is a proposed change which allows CHT Application code to run without the Nools library.

- This provides a workaround for https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6506 and https://github.com/medic/cht-conf/issues/225
- Step in the direction of https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5906. When ready we can remove the nools.emitter
- Probable minor performance gains since nools is a weird box of mysteries. May improve https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/5515 if that issue is correct about Nools holding target instances in memory.

### User Details
This proposes to introduce a new optional variable in `app_settings.json` at [tasks.disableNools](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/compare/noNools?expand=1#diff-ad9f410e750994f008b5e63e2b5587375a03000a3b3f5d004fe6f69930e48c4bR223). When this value is set to `true` then the nools library is not used to process tasks.js and targets.js application code.

### Code Details
- I've proposed to move `rules-emitter.js` into a folder which contains `index` and `emitter.nools` and `emitter.metal` (better name available?)
- The value from appSettings is piped down and the appropriate emitter is chosen and used by index.
- I've updated relevant unit tests to run for both emitters - their behaviors should be nearly identical for projects using declarative configuration
- There are some more significant changes in `shared-libs/rules-engine/test/integration.spec.js` because nools breaks how `sinon.useFakeTimers` works. Since this is no longer broken when nools is disabled, I've updated those tests so the test time is equal to the time in which the rules engine is initialized.

title: Add a way to easily access CouchDb when API is down
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
This is the lifecycle of a request that needs to reach CouchDb in the CHT: 
1. client creates the request
2. nginx receives, and forwards to API
3. API receives, filters and forwards to CouchDb
4. CouchDb responds
5. API forwards response
6. Nginx forwards response

Out of the 3 services above, only Nginx exposes ports to the outside web, so reaching API or CouchDb directly is not possible.

When API is down due to a configuration error or any other malfunction, CouchDb is only reachable from within the container / network, which is cumbersome and error prone, when having to debug and fix issues only by using curl (or other basic commands). 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Think of a way to short-circuit access to CouchDb thought Nginx when API is down, while maintaining security. 

**Additional context**
It was cumbersome and slow to debug a production CouchDb problem using curl only to make complex requests (that require headers, payloads and authentication).

title: Add wdio retries
body:
**Describe the issue**
Our e2e tests are flaky, to the point where it's more likely for a build to fail than pass. This means engineers continually have to retry builds in order to get a green tick and be allowed to merge. Our policy is to keep on top of these issues and resolve them as they come up but history has shown we never find the time to do it.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Investigate turning on WDIO retries so individual tests are tried again and the build is only failed if they repeatedly fail. In addition we need better test reporting so we can see if the retries are making the build slower, or obscuring other issues.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Turn off the requirement for a green build. That will reduce confidence in the testing and it's likely regressions will be committed by people who assume the failures are flakes.
- Deal with flaky tests with extreme prejudice. If a test flakes it should be immediately skipped, and if we get around to fixing it in the future it can be re-enabled. The problem is flakiness is very common so possibly too many tests would get skipped. This may be worth looking into if retries don't work for any reason.

title: Implement a way of restricting which users are allowed to replicate
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Be it for performance reasons (for example: needing to prioritize certain users for replicating quickly) or for data integrity reasons (for example users that have orphaned contacts after a move contacts or a rollback), restricting replication to only some users has been a go-to solution for CHT projects a few times in cht history. 

A few of the ways this has been implemented:
- socially, by instructing some users to stop using their devices
- hot-patching the instance to add custom code which will produce the same result
- IP blocking at load balancer level 

None of the solutions above are easy or guarantee results: the social solution becomes inefficient very quickly for large projects, hot-patching with custom code is very risky, ip blocking requires that the target users have "stable" IPs and technical knowledge and accessibility to change the config of the load balancer. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Find way to:
- stop specific users from replicating (have an exclusions "list")
- allow only specific users from replicating (have an inclusions "list")

The user selection should be flexible, some example of criteria for selecting users can be: role, permission, username, facility_id (or facility ancestor). 
When a user is denied replication, their replication endpoint calls should respond with a status and error message that will stop the client from progressing replication (no "denied" errors for example, which do not stop replication progression). 
Changing the list of users should be easy, but be restricted to certain users (maybe only admins?). 

**Additional context**
Restricting replication, implemented socially, was the solution chosen by a partner when mitigating effects of moving most of the contacts in a large deployment.

title: Extract form's instance code out from the Enketo Service in webapp
body:
**Describe the issue**

Currently, `webapp` can only display one Enketo form at a time; the enketo service is doing form's instance jobs like [unloading a form](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/ee964cba74e63c5263c703d7b715dd634153ddb1/webapp/src/ts/services/enketo.service.ts#L811), [setup form's buttons](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/ee964cba74e63c5263c703d7b715dd634153ddb1/webapp/src/ts/services/enketo.service.ts#L708), [force a form recalculation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/ee964cba74e63c5263c703d7b715dd634153ddb1/webapp/src/ts/services/enketo.service.ts#L699), etc. 

There is a risk of race condition between form instances; for example, the webapp loads a pregnancy form, then loads a pregnancy follow-up form (by changing the URL); the pregnancy form may have a delay and ends up calling the service to unload after the pregnancy follow up was loaded. The [unload](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/ee964cba74e63c5263c703d7b715dd634153ddb1/webapp/src/ts/services/enketo.service.ts#L811) function has code that affected the pregnancy follow up form. 

These race conditions are rare but can still happen. If we fix this, then maintenance and extensibility will be easier. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
- Extract the form's instance-specific code out of the Enketo Service. The service receives the form instance and executes support operations like extracting data for saving, fetching and setting attachments, etc. 
- Operations over a form instance shouldn't affect another form instance. 
- A form instance has a clear life cycle that the implementing page can control.

title: Prevent data loss through re-sync when restoring data from backup
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Data loss when restoring from backups is most likely unavoidable. 
However there is one mitigation we can deploy, with relatively little cost. 

First, follow these steps to reproduce how data loss happens now: 
1. Launch CHT (4.x is easiest, but this applies to every release since 2017) and create an offline user
2. Login as the offline user. 
3. Create a data backup. 
4. As the offline user, create some documents and sync. 
5. As the admin, check that the documents created on step 4 exist on the server. 
6. Overwrite live data with the backup (simulate a restoration from backup). 
7. Check that the documents created on step 4 don't exist on the server (this is expected, those docs were created AFTER the backup). 
8. Sync as the offline user. 
9. Check that the documents created on step 4 don't exist on the server. 

What happens on step 9 is caused by the way we save the replication checkpointer in Pouchdb: [at replication source](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/webapp/src/ts/services/db-sync.service.ts#L88). This means that the document that holds the replication sequence for client uploads exists only on the client. The client doesn't know the server was restored from a backup, so it will keep uploading docs based on the locally stored sequence. This sequence is _after_ the docs created on step 4. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
PouchDb supports multiple settings for the `checkpoint`, and by default will save the checkpointer on both `source` and `target`. 
If the checkpointer is also saved on the target, when reaching step 9, PouchDb will check replication history on both checkpointers and choose the latest common seq. Because the server will have an older seq, the documents created on 4 will be re-uploaded. No data loss. 

With this approach, in case the server checkpointer becomes corrupted, is deleted, etc, the client will start replication from 0. This means that the local database is iterated over in batches and, for each batch, it will query a server endpoint (_revs_diff) to check whether the docs already exist. This endpoint is unfiltered, and requests are forwarded directly to CouchDb.  Only missing docs will be uploaded.
We should assess the performance impact of a client resetting replication, both for the client and for the server. 

When implementing this, we should also make sure that we somehow "start" by writing the server-side checkpointer, if possible, so we avoid all clients going through the process described above. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Don't change anything. 

**Additional context**
We recently restored a production  deployment from a backup due to server-side data corruption.

title: Deprecate use of  `SSL_CERT_FILE_*` , `CERTIFICATE_MODE` & `SSL_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH` for nginx image
body:
**Describe the issue**
Infrastructure team has decided that `CERTIFICATE_MODE` and `SSL_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH` should be deprecated (see below). Additionally, after research, we decided we should also deprecate  `SSL_CERT_FILE_PATH` and `SSL_KEY_FILE_PATH`  per #7949.

* It's confusing and complicated
* It works fine just use `cht-ssl` volume for persistence and have CHT admins follow steps to copy in their cert.
* Default can safely be to always create a self signed cert on boot which can easily be overwritten
* For Let's Encrypt, we use another container which mounts `cht-ssl` volume - [recommend official certbot docker image
](https://eff-certbot.readthedocs.io/en/stable/install.html#id5)


**Describe the improvement you'd like**
* remove all code, docs and test for the `CERTIFICATE_MODE`  and `SSL_VOLUME_MOUNT_PATH`  environment variables

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
*  do nothing - it mostly works as is
* double down and try and get everything easier and less error prone by enhancing existing functionality.

title: Enable easy integration with certbot and nginx container
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Right now we're working on [deprecating the built in functionality](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8098) of our Let's Encrypt integration.  

After this, we should add in easy integration with an external to the CHT core  way to generate TLS certificates using Let's Encrpyt.  This will enable partners to easily set up TLS for self hosted deployments. 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Using the [published certbot image](https://eff-certbot.readthedocs.io/en/stable/install.html#id5) we should:
* Make it easy for certbot to publish ` /.well-known/acme-challenge/*` by exposing this path  in `nginx` config and accessible via the `cht-ssl` volume 
* use `--deploy-hook` as needed to copy config/certs to where they need to after certificate is created

title: DNS queries for *.my.local-ip.com fail causing development instances to be unreachable
body:
**Describe the issue**
We have 3 projects that heavily rely on the *.my.local-ip.com TLS certs:
* [NGINX Local IP](https://github.com/medic/nginx-local-ip/)
* [CHT Docker Helper for 3.x](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/3.x/app-developer/#cht-docker-helper)
* [CHT Docker Helper for 4.x](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/4.x/app-developer/#cht-docker-helper-for-4x)

Because TLS requires DNS and because the DNS server for my.local-ip.com often fails, it feels like a developers instances is broken, when in fact DNS is failing to resolve for their my.local-ip.com IP.  

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Provide a new solution that offers the same conveniences as my.local-ip.com but has stable DNS. Either a commercial offering or a self hosted option based on open source

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
* Hope that my.local-ip.com resolves their DNS issue
* Stop offering a valid TLS cert from a real CA and revert back to only https://localhost self signed certs

The Release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

title: Add hooks in nginx container for certbot
body:
# Description

* `enable_certbot_compatability()` function in [ssl-install.sh](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/8099-nginx-certbot/nginx/ssl-install.sh#L110) -  Creates  the directories to serve `certbot` validation HTTP GET requests
*  `enable_certbot_compatability()` function in [ssl-install.sh](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/8099-nginx-certbot/nginx/ssl-install.sh#L110) - Creates a `/etc/nginx/private/deploy.sh` script to run after `certbot` creates the certs to move them to the right location for `nginx` to see them.
* Note - this PR overrides the use of `AUTO_GENERATE`, as a preemptive re-use of it instead of deprecating it, as we're planning to do.  It also removes `generate_certificate_auto()` from [ssl-install.sh](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/8122/files#diff-1d142cadb0d352501f8ba0fa27b775e113f561125f67e52099cd8414d84cfe4fL67). This seemed less invasive, but I'm open to input!

medic/cht-core#8099

## To test

Assumes FQDN of `deleteme2-certbot-nginx-cht.plip.com` and a CHT SSL docker volume of `cht_cht-ssl`. Both are configurable in the `.env` file for certbot service. Use your own FQDN and verify volume name in `.env`.

Steps 7-11 will be the basis of the new documentation to [be added here.](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/4.x/adding-tls-certificates/)

1. provision Ubuntu 22.04 w/ Public IP and FQDN
   *NOTE* - you can not use auto created AWS EC2 names (eg `ec2-35-180-117-38.eu-west-3.compute.amazonaws.com`). You must create a FQDN outside of the  `*.amazonaws.com` domain.
3. install docker
    ```
    curl -fsSL get.docker.com -o get-docker.sh && sh get-docker.sh
    ```
4. Install CHT using compose files from this PR (per `curl` call), create dirs, env file, compose files per [the single node self hosted steps](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/4.x/self-hosting-single-node/). Note we set `CERTIFICATE_MODE=AUTO_GENERATE`:
    ```
    sudo apt-get install wamerican
    mkdir -p /home/ubuntu/cht/{compose,certs,upgrade-service,couchdb}
    couchdb_secret=$(shuf -n7 /usr/share/dict/words --random-source=/dev/random | tr '\n' '-' | tr -d "'" | cut -d'-' -f1,2,3,4,5,6,7)
    couchdb_password=$(shuf -n7 /usr/share/dict/words --random-source=/dev/random | tr '\n' '-' | tr -d "'" | cut -d'-' -f1,2,3,4,5,6,7)
    cat > /home/ubuntu/cht/upgrade-service/.env << EOF
    CHT_COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=cht
    COUCHDB_SECRET=${couchdb_secret}
    DOCKER_CONFIG_PATH=/home/ubuntu/cht/upgrade-service
    COUCHDB_DATA=/home/ubuntu/cht/couchdb
    CHT_COMPOSE_PATH=/home/ubuntu/cht/compose
    COUCHDB_USER=medic
    COUCHDB_PASSWORD=${couchdb_password}
    COUCHDB_UUID=${uuid}
   CERTIFICATE_MODE=AUTO_GENERATE
    EOF
    cd /home/ubuntu/cht/
    curl -s -o ./compose/cht-core.yml https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/medic:medic:8099-nginx-certbot/docker-compose/cht-core.yml
    curl -s -o ./compose/cht-couchdb.yml https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/_couch/builds_4/medic:medic:8099-nginx-certbot/docker-compose/cht-couchdb.yml
    curl -s -o ./upgrade-service/docker-compose.yml https://raw.githubusercontent.com/medic/cht-upgrade-service/main/docker-compose.yml
    ```

5. start CHT services:
    ```
    cd /home/ubuntu/cht/upgrade-service
    docker compose up --detach
    ```

7. test `.well-known`  works inside the container CHT nginx container:
   ```shell
   echo "should show 'CERTIFICATE_MODE AUTO_GENERATE':"
   curl http://deleteme2-certbot-nginx-cht.plip.com/.well-known/acme-challenge/index.html
   ```
   
   **NOTE** If this fails, see note below. Do not proceed - it won't work!
   
8. create certbot compose and env file
   ```shell
   mkdir -p /home/ubuntu/cht/certbot
   cd /home/ubuntu/cht/certbot
   cat > docker-compose.yml << EOF
   version: '3.9'
   services:
     certbot:
         container_name: certbot
         hostname: certbot
         image: certbot/certbot
         volumes:
           - ssl-storage:/etc/nginx/private/
           - ssl-storage:/var/log/letsencrypt/
         command: certonly --debug --deploy-hook /etc/nginx/private/deploy.sh --webroot -w /etc/nginx/private/certbot/ --domain \$DOMAIN --non-interactive --key-type rsa --agree-tos --register-unsafely-without-email \$STAGING
   volumes:
     ssl-storage:
         name: \${CHT_SSL_VOLUME}
         external: true
   EOF
   
   cat > .env << EOF
   DOMAIN=deleteme2-certbot-nginx-cht.plip.com
   STAGING=
   CHT_SSL_VOLUME=cht_cht-ssl
   TZ=America/Whitehorse
   EOF
   ```
   
9. generate certs
   ```shell
   cd /home/ubuntu/cht/certbot
   docker compose up
   ```
   
10. reload `nginx`
    ```shell
    docker exec -it cht_nginx_1 nginx -s reload
    ```

11. confirm you have valid certs on domain

12. For a production instance, create a cronjob for once a week to renew certs:
    ```
    #!/bin/sh
    cd /home/ubuntu/cht/certbot
    docker compose up
    ```

### well-known/acme-challenge/index.html failing to show "CERTIFICATE_MODE AUTO_GENERATE"

This is likely because the CI build is not passing so the images on AWS aren't up to date :( The fix is to manually build the `nginx` container and update the image used in the compose file.  Follow these steps

1. stop all services 
   ```
   docker kill $(docker ps --quiet)
   ```
2. checkout cht-core, cd into it, build `nginx` image: 
   ```
   cd
   git clone https://github.com/medic/cht-core.git
   cd cht-core/nginx
   docker build -t nginx-8099 .
   ```
3. replace the image in the compose file with the one you just built:
   ```
   sed -i "s/image:\ public.ecr.aws\/medic\/cht-nginx:4.1.0-8099-nginx-certbot/image: nginx-8099/g" /home/ubuntu/cht/compose/cht-core.yml
   ```
4. go back to step `#5` above and start again ensuring the `curl` call succeeds.

title: Expose Prometheus-style metrics from API endpoint
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

As a part of https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8114 we are specifying Prometheus as the recommended time series database for real-time CHT metrics.  Unfortunately, Prometheus cannot directly consume our existing [`/monitoring` API endpoint](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/api/#get-apiv2monitoring) because the returned data is not in a format that Prometheus can ingest.

Our current solution is to run an extra service, [the `json-exporter`](https://github.com/prometheus-community/json_exporter), that handles taking data from our `/monitoring` API and maps it to a format that Prometheus can ingest.  The downside of this (besides just having the extra effort/complexity of an additional service) is that when new data is added to `/monitoring` and we want to record that data in Prometheus, the `json-exporter` config must be updated.  (And _every deployment_ of the monitoring stack will have to update their copy of the config.)

**Describe the solution you'd like**
[Many third-party software](https://prometheus.io/docs/instrumenting/exporters/#software-exposing-prometheus-metrics) expose metrics in a format that Prometheus can directly ingest (typically on the `/metrics` endpoint).  We could do the same in the CHT and allow Prometheus to directly pull the metrics.  This would eliminate the need for config changes when adding new metric values (since Prometheus can just discover the new metrics as the CHT server is updated).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could write our own exporter (instead of using `json_exporter`) which could be pre-configured to fetch metrics for a particular version of the CHT.  Then partners would only need to keep their version of the exporter in sync with their CHT version (and not worry about updating config files...).

title: Expose CHT API to extension libs at runtime
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The [Extension Libs](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7824) feature introduced in 4.2.0.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
The Extension Libs are available via CHT API so they can be invoked from tasks, targets, contact summary, and enketo forms (and maybe others?). This is a big win for reuse, of business logic like determining if someone is high risk, _but_ you cannot currently call one extension lib from another.

Provide some way for an extension lib to access the CHT API and potentially call another extension lib for maximum reuse.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- have cht-conf bundle everything together, but then if a dev changes a single character in a lib then the user has to download all the js again not just the file that changed.
- expose common functions from cht-core, but it's impossible to predict all possible functions

title: When unmuting parent do not cascade to contacts that were already muted before the parent
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently when muting/unmuting a parent contact (e.g. a household), the muting/unmuting will cascade down to the children of the contact (and so the household members will also be muted).  

However, consider the scenario where a CHW area contains a household, `H` that contains members: `A` and `B`.

- The CHW mutes `A` because they have temporarily left the area
- The CHW retires and so the CHW Supervisor mutes the whole CHW Area 
  - The muting cascades down to `H` and `B` (and technically `A`, but it is already muted)
- A new CHW is onboarded and so the supervisor unmutes the CHW Area.
  - The unmute cascades down to `H`, `A`, and `B` 
 
The undesirable behavior is that `A` is unmuted because the CHW Area was unmuted when, in fact, `A` has not yet returned to the area and should still be muted.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
From a behavior perspective, I think it would be preferable for unmuting to not cascade to contacts that were previously already muted.  The only thing that should unmute those contacts would be submitting an unmute form for them specifically.

**Additional context**
Originally raised in a conversation [on the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/new-documentation-available-re-muting/2476/3).

title: Refactor initial replication to not use PouchDb replicate
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
When performing initial replication, the user needs to download and save all documents from the server. 
Right now, initial replication uses the standard Pouch/Couch APIs and sequence of calls: 
- call _changes
- check local revs for existence of docs
- call _bulk_get or _all_docs to download missing docs
- repeat until _changes returns no results

The _changes feed request is expensive, because it requires calls to: 
- get all allowed doc ids, which is an expensive multi-key view request 
- get a batch of changes for these doc ids

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

title: Method for linking feedback docs to relevant telemetry docs
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
When analyzing feedback documents, I want to know what device the user is running, their doc_count, their available disk space. It'd be great to have all the telemetry stuff that we know about a user.

Currently, when doing this analysis there is no way to link a feedback doc and telemetry doc except for username and datetime. If a user has telemetry documents from multiple devices on the same day then we cannot know which device the error happened on and the analysis loses accuracy.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Telemetry documents have a [deviceId](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/performance/telemetry/#metadata) and a wealth of information about the user.  If the feedback document had the same `deviceId` then we can link the documents during in analysis.  

Very useful for Global Database Failures and other intermittent problems which happen project-wide.

title: PouchDb `Failed to execute 'transaction' on 'IDBDatabase'` due to device inactivity
body:
**Describe the bug**
This issue was reported numerous times, but became prominent more recently, after a big project upgraded to a newer version of the CHT, and started writing tasks to disk. 
Upon inspecting feedback documents generated by users reporting this problem, we've noticed that when a "global failure" was reported, the log list frequently also contained errors about IndexedDb timeouts.  
An example: 
```
\"Error getting tasks for all contacts\",{\"status\":500,\"name\":\"indexed_db_went_bad\",\"message\":\"unknown\",\"error\":true,\"reason\":\"TimeoutError\"}]"}
```

We followed this lead and found several Chromium bug reports about people seeing similar errors when laptops went to sleep while IndexedDB connections were open: 
https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=855624
https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=955470

@kennsippell 's excellent data analysis showed that:
- this is happening when users have a large number of documents
- issue is more frequent for older versions of Chrome but there are cases for newer versions as well. 

I managed to replicate this multiple times on my own device (Pixel 6a), on CHT-Core ~4.2.0, with a user with 26000 documents. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Replicate a user with a large number of documents (according to data, above 25000 docs)
2. Open the task page.
3.1. Put the phone to sleep for a few minutes
3.2. Switch to another activity for a few minutes (I had a whatsapp call which probably took a lot of device resources). 
4. Open CHT App again and see error. 

**Expected behavior**
Tasks should be displayed. 

**Logs**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/227868362-d7722875-bec7-4cdd-81a5-cf85eb23f3d9.png)

The last error seems to repeat ad-infinitum. I kept the tab opened for 30 minutes, and the console reports that 36.000 have been logged: 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/227868610-a07a0684-869e-4b44-83a1-a575117d8411.png)

This is a sample feedback document that was generated during one of these events: 

https://gist.github.com/dianabarsan/82c01f0c3331f7c85427151816c9cc3c

**Screenshots**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/227868161-65bf8401-ba3f-4e29-959f-949c9d00cfaa.png)

If I ignore the error and stay on the tasks page I see: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/227966337-6f44996f-3990-4d10-b6ec-a15dae60a60a.png)


**Environment**
- Browser: Chrome
- App: webapp
- Version: TBD based on data analysis

**Additional context**
This is definitely a race condition, so repro steps will most likely not trigger the error every time. 
Refreshing the app and keeping the screen on and the app in the foreground fixes the issue.

title: Race condition during sentinel startup
PouchDb `indexed_db_went_bad` due to device inactivity
body:
**Describe the bug**
This is similar to https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8149
Except the error is different. It is also triggered differently, as it happens when an attempt to write times out, compared to the other error that happens on a read. 

Please insert statistics @kennsippell 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Replicate a user with a large number of documents (according to data, above 25000 docs)
2. Create a script that takes 100 documents that the user should see, deletes all doc attachments and adds lots of keys to the docs. I added ~5000 uuid keys and values. The purpose is to make the bulkDocs payload large enough that there is enough of a time span to put the phone to sleep. 
3. Connect phone to desktop and use `chrome://inspect` in order to track network requests on the device. 
4. Run the script that updates/creates 100 ultra large docs.
5. Sync. Watching the network tab, put the phone to sleep immediately after you see the outgoing `_bulk_get` request finish. 
6. Put the phone to sleep immediately. Wait for a few minutes. 

**Logs**

The logs will be riddled with `Failed to execute 'transaction' on 'IDBDatabase` errors, most likely. Scroll through the errors until you see the `indexed_db_went_bad` error. 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/228361807-a28a6310-b78a-4531-8708-b6af2e9f558f.png)

Example feedback doc created during event: https://gist.github.com/dianabarsan/8d4ca724f5833df8c602d89d045468a6

**Screenshots**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/228361734-6d704c2e-1471-4e11-ab61-73302233b8b0.png)

**Environment**
- Instance: local
- Browser: Chrome
- App: webapp
- Version: 4.2.0

**Additional context**
This was a lot trickier to replicate than https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8149. I think I only saw these errors in the 5th or 6th try, after I had reduced CPU performance on the phone by 4x. 
Just as with the other issue, reloading the app and keeping the phone screen on fixes the issue.

title: Duplicate outbound requests are sent when a document matches multiple config options
body:
**Describe the bug**
Described very aptly on the forum: https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/outbound-destination-property/2485/5 and https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/outbound-destination-property/2485/3

> However, we are seeing one object outbound being executed twice for the same form. Never the first one and it works if it’s only one outbound object, but if we have two outbound objects, the second one is executed twice. If there are three the second and the third one are executed twice as well.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create two identical outbound configs (they need different names, but everything else should be identical)
2. Submit a document that matches the relevancy condition
3. Wait for the document to be processed and for the outbound queue to clear (could take up to 10 minutes)
4. Check outbound recipient requests and notice there were three calls, instead of 2. 

**Expected behavior**
Only two requests should be executed. 

**Logs**
No errors in the logs

**Environment**
- App: sentinel
- Version: 3.9+ 

**Additional context**
In order to figure out what was going on, I had to add debug messages all over the outbound code, and I ended up with logging the error that we received here: 
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/mark_for_outbound.js#L47

and it is: 
```
{
  error: 'conflict',
  reason: 'Document update conflict.',
  status: 409,
  name: 'conflict',
  message: 'Document update conflict.',
  stack: 'Error\n' +
    '    at Object.generateErrorFromResponse (/sentinel/node_modules/pouchdb-errors/lib/index.js:104:18)\n' +
    '    at /sentinel/node_modules/pouchdb-adapter-http/lib/index.js:254:33\n' +
    '    at runMicrotasks (<anonymous>)\n' +
    '    at processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:96:5)',
  docId: '41ac853d-9e76-479b-ac6a-1dd2dea52969-info'
}
```
This is because the same infodoc gets updated when outbound succeeds, but we don't bother updating the rev to allow successive edits. https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/shared-libs/transitions/src/transitions/mark_for_outbound.js#L44

This causes every following outbound "block" to throw an error and generate a task - that would trigger another outbound request on a schedule - even if the initial request was actually successful.

title: fix(#8166): Update tune.bufsize and remove rsyslog from haproxy image
body:
# Description

According to documentation, when increasing `tune.bufsize`, `maxconn` should be decreased by the same factor, otherwise there is a risk of OOM. 
> values larger than default size will increase memory usage, possibly causing the system to run out of memory. 

https://www.haproxy.com/documentation/hapee/latest/onepage/#3.2-tune.bufsize

In our config, we both increased maxconn and tune.bufsize by x 100. This caused the haproxy memory footprint to increase to up to 18GB. This memory is not released when connections are dropped and crashed instances that had a lower amount of available memory than this. 

Additionally, this PR removes `rsyslog` from haproxy image. It was no longer needed, since docker logs are already enough for funnelling haproxy logs, and having the service running prevented the container from restarting when the main haproxy process ran out of memory. 
The container automatically restarts now, so setting a default resource limit to the container becomes an option. 

medic/cht-core#8166

title: API Changes watcher skips changes - or becomes blocked
body:
**Describe the bug**
I believe this is a race condition, as it has been only reported twice, as far as we know. 
Once was [on the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/404-error-on-model-xml/2455/11) and once on [slack](https://medic.slack.com/archives/C024KTGRW/p1680869810577819). 
On slack, I was able to log into the instance and personally checked this was happening. I updated a form document and saw nothing appear in the api logs about receiving a change. 
Restarting API fixed the issue. 

I believe this is a race condition. I'll examine the instance logs for clues and update with findings. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Load CHT 4.1.0
1. Wait 10 seconds. 
1. `docker restart <your haproxy container>` or `docker restart <your couchdb container>`
1. Upload a new form
1. Load the new form in webapp and see error. When checking the console, you'll see a request to get `model.xml` and `form.html`, and both would fail with a 404. 

**Expected behavior**
Form attachments should be generated by changes watcher on the fly. 

**Logs**
No logs. no errors.

title: Upgrade Webapp to use Bootstrap 4 or 5
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
We use a very old version of `ngx-bootstrap@^7`, which can no longer be installed without passing `legacy-peer-deps`, because it lists an older Angular version as a peer dependency - it supports up to Angular 12.

At the same time, we use [Bootstrap 3 in webapp](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/a30c1649e129cca54a42cc4e60976ce73a314af9/webapp/src/ts/app.component.ts#L146).  
[Support for `bootstrap3` was dropped in `ngx-bootstrap@10`](https://github.com/valor-software/ngx-bootstrap/blob/development/CHANGELOG.md#breaking-changes). 
The latest version of `ngx-bootstrap` still supports bs3 is `9.0.0`, which supports up to Angular 14.  

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Update webapp to use a newer version of Bootstrap. Bootstrap 4 might be the easiest migration, with minimal changes required. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Drop `ngx-bootstrap`?
- We're fine with installing with `legacy-peer-deps` and ignore compatibility mismatches

**Additional context**
I wanted to remove the need for installing with `legacy-peer-deps`, this was the only true blocker.

title: nginx and haproxy should respect `Accept` headers when responding with error templates
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?** Both nginx and haproxy use the default error templates for 4xx and 5xx responses. These templates are html. Respecting the `Accept` header would standardize the behavior of the CHT, and this is important since we expect third party software to call CHT APIs. To reproduce: - start CHT 4.x - stop your api container `docker stop ` - request a JSON response from API: ```shell curl -k https://localhost -H 'Accept: application/json' ``` ``` 502 Bad Gateway

502 Bad Gateway

nginx/1.19.6
``` If you are logged into webapp, you will see a JSON parse error spammed in the console: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35681649/232050203-f0b152b0-fe75-4156-bece-2765155dc3b0.png) **Describe the improvement you'd like** We should change nginx and haproxy configs to respond with JSON when the `Accept: application/json` header is passed. **Describe alternatives you've considered** Leave it as it is. **Additional context** I had a script that passed the result of an API call to `jq`. Because the response was html, my `jq` call failed. Similarly, we've seen reports of feedback docs being generated that feedback docs get generated in webapp when with `Unexpected token < in JSON at position 0`: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6412 https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7782

body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
It's a good time to remove the Guided Tour, since we now have the [Training Cards](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/training/training-cards/) ([ticket](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6598)), which projects can customize and deliver remote short trainings to their CHWs. 

The CHT now has a place where projects can get templates of trainings cards that explains features from the CHT Framework, these can be adapted to specific scenarios. 

Also, most projects do their initial trainings with CHWs on-site, and users might not get to see the Guided Tour popping up on their first login.

title: Remove configuration wizard
body: **Describe the issue** Related [forum post](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/configuration-wizard/2670). The configuration wizard will be displayed the first time a user logs in if the user has the `can_configure` permission and the `setup_complete` property in `app_settings` is `false`. Closing this screen (even without setting anything) updates `setup_complete` to `true` and the screen does not show up again (but is still accessible from the hamburger menu). **Step 1** The modem setup, is only needed if you’ll be sending SMS which isn’t the first concern for most projects anymore. **Step 3** The language preference, is mostly useful for translating SMS messages, now users on smartphones pick their own language when they log in. **Step 2** ( Identify Care Coordinators) and **Step 4** (Registration form) aren't being used anywhere. it was probably useful in the DIY days, but less so today. **Describe the improvement you'd like** Remove the configuration wizard from webapp **Describe alternatives you've considered** Leave it there and fix the UI to explain better the steps and make it more friendly.

title: Add a way to know whether an offline user successfully synced
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Knowing whether a user has successfully managed to upload all of their pending documents is important in many situations. To list a few: 
- before changing hierarchies
- before moving contacts
- before an upgrade
- before disabling an account

This is a temporary knowing, of course, because once the user is offline, they could make as many edits as they desire, while the server gets no information about this. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We already store the upwards replication checkpointer on the serverside. This checkpointer document contains the local sequence of the last document that was uploaded. 
If we could store the generic `update_seq` of the local database along with this seq, we could compare the two to determine whether sync-ing is in progress or was interrupted before all documents were uploaded. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The checkpointer document is right now a byproduct if PouchDb replication, which PouchDb doesn't provide direct access to. 
We could either choose the direction of gaining access to it or build our own structure to store this information. 

**Additional context**

title: Nginx can't connect to API after container restarts because of dynamic IP allocation
body:
**Describe the bug**
Docker allocates dynamic IPs within a network. When a container restarts, there's a chance the IP changes. However nginx caches DNS queries to backend servers and never tries them again. 
As a result, after an API restart and IP change, nginx fails to connect. 

This is a known issue: 
https://github.com/docker/compose/issues/3314
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/27912917/how-to-configure-docker-port-mapping-to-use-nginx-as-an-upstream-proxy
https://serverfault.com/questions/722438/nginx-refresh-upstream-server-ip
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/63154521/connect-failed-113-host-is-unreachable-while-connecting-to-upstream-nginx-f

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Start CHT 4.
1. Run `docker network inspect <your network name>` and check API's IP
1. Restart some containers to get IPs to swap. I used: 
```docker stop <haproxy> -t 0 && docker stop <api> -t 0 && docker start <haproxy> && docker start <api>```. 
For some reason, when restarting a single container, I never got an IP change, but did get it quite consistently when restarting two. 
1. Wait for one minute - or make sure everything is up and running by checking container logs. Make a request to the server. 
1. Get 502. 


**Expected behavior**
nginx should be able to remap backends ips. 

**Logs**
```
2023/04/27 21:19:33 [error] 41#41: *8603 connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream, 
client: 172.30.0.1, server: , request: "GET /api/info HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://172.30.0.7:5988/api/info", 
host: "localhost"
172.30.0.1 - admin [27/Apr/2023:21:19:33 +0000] "GET /api/info HTTP/1.1" 502 157 "-" "-"
```

The IP of api was `172.30.0.6` at this point. 

**Environment**
- App: nginx
- Version: 4+

**Additional context**
I discovered this when working on https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8173, after adding an e2e test that restarted haproxy, which resulted in an expected API restart as well. Once API was up, nginx could not connect. 
Restarting nginx fixes this issue.

title: Contact and Messages Tab:  footer button scrolls with content, not staying pinned
body:
## Describe the bug

_Originally reported on the forum [here](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/change-of-button-position-after-a-given-number-of-entries/2708)._

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7998 Introduced a Floating Action Button and a list footer button (on desktop). The list footer button on desktop is supposed to stay pinned to the bottom of the list at all times. On the Contacts tab, when there are many rows in the list (basically once a scrollbar shows up), it becomes "unpinned" and scrolls with the content. It seems to work fine on the Reports tab, I didn't test the Messages tab, and it's not applicable to the Tasks tab (there is no button on the LHS on Tasks tab).

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Go to the Contacts tab on desktop
2. Make sure you have more places than can fit on the screen by creating a bunch of test places. 
3. Scroll down
4. Notice that the list footer button scrolls with the content

**NB** - the same thing happens on messages tab too

## Expected behavior
List footer button should stay pinned in all circumstances.

## Screenshots

Animated GIF (say "Jiff!!!") showing reports tab working, but people tab not working
![bottom button](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10096985/236032562-872f0b43-2ffa-4195-a361-26a2f181ccfe.gif)

Video showing people tab fixed #8219, but messages tab is broken:

title: Align nginx and ALB timeout values
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
In k8s medic-hosted deployments, we use AWS ALB as a proxy to API. 
In 4.x deployments, we use nginx. 

ALB has a configured timeout on 1h, however our nginx configured timeout is 10 minutes: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/nginx/nginx.conf#L14

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
I think should align these values. 
We should evaluate: 
- which requests we expect to be lengthy
- how long we expect them to be

**Additional context**
CouchDb has an internal default timeout of 5 minutes. We have seen this timeout get set with large requests to get purged docs.

title: Upgrade Message in Clustered Mode Should Include CouchDB containers (couchdb.1, couchdb.2, etc) - for use by kubernetes upgrade service
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**

When using the CHT in a cluster, the upgrade message should include a list of the couchdb containers to be upgraded by the upgrade service. This is important when dealing with the [kubernetes upgrade service](https://github.com/medic/upgrade-service-kubernetes) since it can upgrade couchdb even in a cluster on different nodes.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**

The upgrade message includes a list of all couchdb containers (couchdb.1, couchdb.2, couchdb.3, etc) - possibly by querying couchdb for the cluster nodes.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Alternative is that the upgrade has to be done manually by editing the deployment manifest. This is not ideal. Especially, since the Kubernetes upgrade service already supports this.

title: Support collapsible form groups
body:
Currently there is no way to show/hide sections of a form except via `relevant` logic.  This does not work for all use-cases since values in the non-relevant part of the form will not be saved at the end. ([Forum conversation](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/collapsible-form-section/2713/7?u=michael))

The default Enekto webapp supports being able to just collapse groups (that do not have the `field-list` appearance).  

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8441903/236499737-6fc095b4-d9c1-422f-9333-23528346360e.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8441903/236499821-dc413d6a-0a13-4dc4-be52-992158ab1640.png)

We could support similar functionality in the CHT, though we may want to make it opt-in. So if you added the `collapsible` appearance to a group it would make this happen.  (Also would be good to consider some way of making the group collapsed by default, when desired, so the content is initially hidden until the user expands the group....)

title: Figure out a different way to use purged docs cache
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Right now, purged docs are cached for a very short interval (5 minutes) - for considerations of memory management. 
Recent research has shown that: 
- users end up having a very large number of documents before purging - with 40k being common, growing up to 100k docs
- cache is used in 40% of requests

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Experiment with increasing TTL, and only bust cache when purging has run again. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
If experiments show that the memory footprint of the cache for a large project (suppose 4000 users each with 60k pre-purge docs, cached), investigate whether cache can be saved on disk.

**Additional context**
@kennsippell has been analyzing production logs and observing request behavior. Querying for purged docs in this project, which has  very aggressive purging and high number of pre-purge docs, the purging requests take up to 40% of server time.

title: Can't turn off permissions for `national_admin` role in admin app
body:
**Describe the bug**
A user with the `role` of national admin will always have all permissions enabled in webapp. 
[This was reserved solely for db admins](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blame/1edc93a9555737e2734fb37f4d7883a2fe3c400d/webapp/src/ts/services/auth.service.ts#L33) (user with the reserved couchdb role `_admin`) but was changed when adding the [CHT script API](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/commit/869fd7103723730f9f7a7a990c058687c8c3cbf5).

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Disable UHC (delete the `uhc` property in `settings` and uncheck the permission `can_view_last_visited_date` for all roles)
2. Create an online user. Give them the `national_admin` role. You can either configure this role or just leave it unconfigured and just add it manually to the `user` doc in `_users` db. Assign this user to a contact that would see places that have [`count_visits` enabled](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/config/default/app_settings.json#L335).
3. Login with this user and load the contacts tab.
4. See that the contacts list shows UHC last visited dates. 

**Expected behavior**
It should be possible to not display `last_visited` for `national_admin` role, but currently we only exclude that for `_admin`. 

**Logs**
Not applicable. 

**Screenshots**
![image](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/35681649/851e1bef-8a41-4156-bd83-2f4ed5d5e415)


**Environment**
- App: webapp
- Version: 3.12+

**Additional context**
Reported [on the forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/seeking-clarity-on-the-national-admin-role-and-mm-online-role/2746/3?u=diana) after logs for a live instance were analyzed and observing very long view queries made by `national_admin`s loading the contact page, even though they did not have permissions to view last visited dates.
