title: Updating contact information through the API
body:
This is a request for an update in relation to the feature request below:
Organization: International Training and Education Center for Health (I-TECH)
Organization Type: Technical
What Other Organizations Would Benefit From This Feature: All

**Describe the Feature:** As an engineer working with the API, I would like to be able to update contact information so that I can easily update certain bits of information about the contact.

**What “Pain Point” Does The Proposed Feature Address:** Currently there is no way to update contact information through the API. For instance, if I need to update a client’s phone number from another platform then I’d need to directly write to CouchDB. As far as I can tell, CouchDB does not support partial updates to documents as well. The current solution creates implementation leaks and room for error.

**Proposed Solution**: Open up a route under the contacts/people resource that allows one to supply some data points about the contact they’d like changed. For example a PUT request to /contacts/:id that accepts a JSON payload with the data points to update. This given that contact’s identifier is supplied.

Links To Supporting Information / Uploads: (https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/updating-contact-information-throught-the-api/2692)
Link to previous GH ticket: [Updating contact information through the API](https://github.com/medic/config-itech/issues/1501)

title: Working with messages between RapidPro and CHT using code: making automated messages from Rapidpro to CHT and clients visible on the message tab
body:
[Working with messages between RapidPro and CHT contacts using code](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/working-with-messages-between-contacts-using-code/2691)
Your Organization: Medic/University of Washington – CHV-NEO
Organization Type: Technical
What Other Organizations Would Benefit From This Feature: interventions with an interactive messaging component
Describe the Feature: CHV-NEO is an app that integrates the CHT (eCHIS) with RapidPro to provide direct to client communication between community Health volunteers (CHVs) and their clients (specifically peri-partum women). Part of this intervention includes sending automated messages to clients, and clients sending back unstructured conversational responses, which CHVs respond to manually. We would like the automated messages sent from RapidPro to clients to also appear in the Messages tab. We want them to appear as being sent from the community health volunteer (CHV) to the client. This so that the CHV is able to make sense out of the messaging history and respond to their clients appropriately and on time.
What “Pain Point” Does The Proposed Feature Address:  Currently on CHT, only manual interactive messages between the CHV and the client are visible on the message tab chat thread. Clients are also receiving daily/weekly automated messages – visit reminders and educational messages – most of which end with a question, but these are not visible in the messages tab. When clients send messages in response to automated messages, the client messages’ meaning cannot be easily understood without the automated message as context. We would like CHVs to be able to see the automated messages so they can follow the conversation, but have automated messages appear as read so that CHVs can prioritize interactive messages from the client that need a prompt response. This feature is essential for launch of the CHV-NEO program June 1.
Proposed Solution: 
We explored the following ways of doing this through RapidPro webhooks:
POSTing to /api/sms and specifying “from” and “to” properties in the payload. This did not seem to work.
Creating an sms_message data record for the contact directly in CouchDB. This worked. However, we noted that since these automated messages will show up as new messages for the CHV, it would create spam and make it difficult to discern these automated messages from actual client interactions.
Directly write the message to the database (should not trigger unread message notification)
Where we need help:
Alternatives to achieving this that may be easier and less complicated
How to mark the sms_message data record as already read so that we avoid spamming the CHV. This in the case that there are no better ways of achieving what we need.
Do you have funding to cover external developers? Yes with technical support from the product team
Do You Have Resources (Designers, Developers, PMs) Available: we have a designer, PM and developer
Links To Supporting Information / Uploads: forum post is here [Working with messages between RapidPro and CHT contacts using code](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/t/working-with-messages-between-contacts-using-code/2691) additional information on MobileWACh is in the description below
The messaging strategy used in CHV-NEO is adapted from a previous intervention named Mobile WACh (Publications can be found [here, ](https://bmjopen.bmj.com/content/11/12/e056062.long)[here](https://dl.acm.org/doi/epdf/10.1145/2702123.2702124) and [here](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29924912/)). In this strategy, clients receive automated messages grounded in behavioral theory and covering a range of health education topics. Automated messages end with a question to promote engagement and behavior change. Clients are encouraged to respond to messages with unstructured messages, which CHVs then respond to in an ongoing conversation. Note that unlike previous 2-way texting projects using the CHT, in our messaging strategy we are not expecting structured responses (eg 1/0) and we are not asking the same question in every message (eg do you need help). In our previous implementations of Mobile WACh across 7 studies in Kenya we have seen that clients message conversationally, including responses that cannot be understood without reading the prior system message (eg. “Yes”, “No”, “A little”). It is therefore necessary for CHVs to be able to read the automated messages when reading client messages. It is also necessary for the messaging tab of CHT to only indicate unread messages when there are unread client messages for the CHV to respond to (not automated messages that do not need the CHV’s attention). See the screenshots below for examples of the types of messages clients send and how the desired functionality was facilitated in a different messaging system.

title: Replace local-ip.co in CHT 3.x Docker Helper, ensure certs get installed.
body:
**Describe the issue**
We did a lot of work around #8100 to improve DNS and TLS for app developers.  This work was not back-ported to [Docker Helper for CHT 3.x](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/guides/hosting/3.x/app-developer/#cht-docker-helper) so it still uses the problematic `local-ip.co`.  As well, it looks like the cert isn't actually installed and users need to run the [add-local-ip-certs-to-docker.sh](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/add-local-ip-certs-to-docker.sh) script and specify the name of their container.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Have CHT 3.x Docker Helper default to using `local-ip.medicmobile.org` and ensure cert installs correctly.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
leave as is

title: Medic-api-log indicating empty responses during periods of high load
body:
I'm analysing production medic-api-logs to monitor a CHT production instance. I'm seeing intermittent drops in [yield](https://sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives/) where large numbers of requests are "unsuccessful" for sustained periods (1% of total requests are unsuccessful, and the worst minutes have ~35% of requests unsuccessful).

Looking at request logs during these periods of low yield, some are due to 500 errors due to overload at CouchDB. But it is 10x more common to see logged response events which look like this:

```
[2023-04-17 11:45:42] RES 0a90537d-6101-4510-ace7-42714ce05b0b 197.155.150.209 - GET /medic/form%3Atb_followup_weekly/form.html HTTP/1.1 - - - ms
[2023-04-17 11:45:42] RES 0dfa85c6-2559-4c7c-b639-5032b4257ecd 197.155.150.209 - GET /medic/form%3Acontact%3Ac30_supervisor_area%3Acreate/model.xml HTTP/1.1 - - - ms
[2023-04-17 11:45:42] RES 11c38315-f93d-4fbf-ba4e-e6ca0335b866 197.155.150.209 - GET /medic/form%3Aanc_followup/form.html HTTP/1.1 - - - ms
```

The `- - -` is indicating that the response from Medic-API has no status code, no response time, etc. We use morgan for these logs, and according to [this morgan issue](https://github.com/expressjs/morgan/issues/121) the cause of logging events like this is:

> This happens when you do not write a response and allow the app to just hang. The reason you get the dashes is because since you didn't write a response, there is no response code, there is no response time, there is no response size, etc. Basically you are seeing all the properties of the response as dashes (i.e. unknown) and the properties of the request populated in that log.

During a period of ~20 days, this affected >1% of all responses. These drops in yield usually coincide with periods of high load. This happened multiple times every day with the worst day having ~5000 responses like this. This affects many different url paths (list below).  The majority of these responses are logged within 10 minutes of the request, but many (~10%) are after 10-20 minutes, and many (~10%) are after 60-70 minutes. 

url_bucket | count
-- | --
medic/form%3.* | 2400
/medic/_changes w/o longpoll | 2161
/medic/_design/medic-client | 2009
/purging/changes | 1992
/medic/_bulk_docs | 1128
/_session | 625
/dbinfo | 426
/medic/_revs_diff | 210
/medic/_all_docs | 170
medic-user-.*-meta/_local.* | 138
/medic/[a-zA-Z0-9\-]{36} | 130
/medic/login | 125
medic-user-.*-meta | 104
/api/v2/monitoring | 104
/medic/_design/medic-client/_view/doc_by_type | 103
/api/v1/users-info | 91
/api/info | 84

title: Refactor downwards continuous replication following the Nairobi protocol
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
The continuous replication algorithm currently uses a mix between a custom filtered replication (via two view requests + one changes request) and standard CouchDb endpoints. 

This means that: 
- we can't use multiple replicas, because we can't reliably use sticky sessions for the view requests + the changes request
- we require 2 potentially very expensive queries (one view request + changes request with many doc ids)
- the need for tombstones

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
The Nairobi protocol replaces downwards continuous replication, and instead uses an API endpoint that was added as part of the [initial replication improvement](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8134).  

Rough steps:
- Client uploads all their locally changed docs; this will still use the existing PouchDb replication. 
- Client makes a request for all doc ids and revs they should have
- Client compares with ids and revs in the pouchdb
 - Download and store all docs that don't exist in pouch or have been updated
- For docs that exist in pouch but not couch, query the server to find out if they have been deleted or purged, and if so remove from pouch

The advantages are:
- potentially no longer requires tombstones to exist
- allows for shard replicas because no more changes feed requests
- lots of complex code removed

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
[Alternatives have been described here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Jz6QDYDJiICz5lLEeFB3odh-YoI_0c_AKHJvoVE-Exo/edit#).

title: Release 4.2.1
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create an GH Milestone and add this issue to it.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.
- [x] Ensure that all issues are labelled correctly, particularly ensure that "Regressions" are labelled with "Affects: <version>" labels. The "Affects" label is used in a link in the Known Issues section of the release notes of that version so it has to match exactly. To make sure the label is correct go to the [release notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) and ensure the issue is listed.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR to the release branch. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version patch`.
- [x] Ensure that issues from merged commits are closed and mapped to a milestone.
- [x] Write an update in the #product-team Slack channel summarising development and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The Release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have been merged into `master` then the release process can start:

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`).
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #product-team Slack channel:
```
@product_team, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag. 
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make. 
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
    - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
    - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, that they're correctly labelled (in particular: they have the right Type, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate), and have human readable descriptions.
    - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes) to export the issues into our release note format.
    - [x] Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
    - [x] Add a link to the new release page in the [Release Notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) section.
    - [x] Assign the PR to:
        - The Director of Technology or a developer
        - An SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Ensure the release notes PR above is merged. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds_4/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*Announcing the release of {{version}}*

This release fixes {{number of bugs}}. Read the [release notes]({{url}}) for full details.
```
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: "Sync Now" reports success even if the replication fails due to timeout
body:
**Describe the bug**
When user clicks "Sync Now," a request is sent to API which times out if it takes >10 minutes. If this request fails due to timeout, no files are moved and the replication is not successful. Despite the timeout, the user sees a success message: "All reports synced".

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Login as a heavy user on a congested server. Alternatively, prepare a custom build of cht-core which reduces the timeout from 10minutes to something short (eg. <1 second).
2. Fill some forms on the device which should replicate up. Create some forms on the server which should replicate down.
3. Click "sync now".  
4. The _changes request needs to take longer than the timeout value to reproduce this issue. You can test if the timeout happened because the files you created will not have synced.
5. Observe the sync status in the hamburger menu - you will see "All reports synced" in green.

**Expected behavior**
Users should be see a failure message for syncronizations which timeout.
It is good these timeouts are not retrying on failure - we likely shouldn't change that

**Logs**
`/medic/_changes` requests which fail in this manner return a mostly empty result with `200` status code

**Environment**
- Instance: dev
- Browser: Chrome
- App: webapp
- Version: main (4.3)

**Additional context**
Based on recent analysis, ~10% of requests to `/medic/_changes` timeout in production for Muso-Mali over a period of 23 days.

title: feat(#8296): the Nairobi replication protocol
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

|     |      |

|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: chore, feat, fix, perf.

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

Refactors continuous downwards replication to: 
- not use PouchDb replication
- use same design as initial replication, downloading a list of all doc ids, and comparing them with existent data set
- if a doc is updated or new, it gets downloaded
- if a doc is missing, we check whether it should be deleted. This leverages a new endpoint that, provided a list of docs ids, returns a list of ids that are deleted or purged. The client deletes the documents that this endpoint returns.
- purging for the client is no longer necessary, deleting purged docs occurs when calling the endpoint above, this PR removes all purging endpoints
- tombstones are no longer necessary, Sentinel no longer generates tombstones. Existent tombstones will not be removed. 
- when contacts are deleted, their associated reports are orphaned
- restricted _changes requests and _all_docs requests always return "default" changes and docs (ddoc, settings, user-settings and serviceworker) to allow for restricted users to receive upgrades after this change

title: Split up the ci-webdriver-default action
body:
**Describe the issue**
Now that we've converted e2e tests from protractor to wdio the run takes about 50 minutes to complete. This is too long.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Break up the suite into smaller test suites that can run in parallel. These suites should be broken up into functional groups, eg: all the enketo tests, all the contacts tests, all the admin tests, etc.

It doesn't matter terribly much how many suites we end up with but there will be a sweet (no pun intended) spot - if broken down too far then the build will take a long time to complete because there's a limit on how many runners we can have in parallel and there is a one-off cost for starting the suite. Use your judgement about where this limit should be but somewhere between 4-10 suites should work.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Reducing test coverage (obviously bad).
Finding other ways to speed tests up (bigger effort).

title: Verify PWA installation option

title: Release 4.1.2
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create an GH Milestone and add this issue to it.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.
- [x] Ensure that all issues are labelled correctly, particularly ensure that "Regressions" are labelled with "Affects: <version>" labels. The "Affects" label is used in a link in the Known Issues section of the release notes of that version so it has to match exactly. To make sure the label is correct go to the [release notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) and ensure the issue is listed.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR to the release branch. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version patch`.
- [x] Ensure that issues from merged commits are closed and mapped to a milestone.
- [x] Write an update in the #product-team Slack channel summarising development and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The Release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have been merged into `master` then the release process can start:

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`).
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #product-team Slack channel:
```
@product_team, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag. 
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make. 
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
    - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
    - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, that they're correctly labelled (in particular: they have the right Type, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate), and have human readable descriptions.
    - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes) to export the issues into our release note format.
    - [x] Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
    - [x] Add a link to the new release page in the [Release Notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) section.
    - [x] Assign the PR to:
        - The Director of Technology or a developer
        - An SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Ensure the release notes PR above is merged. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds_4/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*Announcing the release of {{version}}*

This release fixes {{number of bugs}}. Read the [release notes]({{url}}) for full details.
```
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Show reports of online user's associated place and below
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Part of this other [issue](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7496).
The scope of this work is only for online users. The users will be associated with a specific facility, and they (ideally) only can see data for that facility and below. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We have good data proving that they are currently interacting with the filter/search quite a bit, and in particular, the facility filter on the reports tab. @michaelkohn please fill in here if appropriate. 

So, we can add new permission (`can_default_facility_filter`) to default filters of the report's tab to the user's associated facility. A less complex and less intrusive solution ([POC](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/7496-add-default-place-filter)) is the following:
- Go get the user’s contact from DB, to get the facility
- Wait for the facility filter to finish getting the list of facilities from DB
- Go through the list and find the user’s facility
- Mark the facility and child facilities as selected and trigger the search

Other considerations:
- The user can still remove the filter and see reports from other facilities at the same level. 
- If the user reloads the page, or navigates to another tab and then comes back to the Reports tab, then the default filters will be applied.
- This feature isn't available for offline-users and db admin users.
- We won't add a visual indicator in the parent place when the child place is selected as part of this work. There's a separate [ticket](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7727) for that, and it will be scheduled later. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Create new CouchDB views and point the filter functionality to those views to retrieve data.
- Do nothing and expect users can do the filter by themselves.

title: Inconsistent user roles/permissions when user doc and users-settings are not consistent
body:
**Describe the bug**

> Essentially cht-core should consistently use the [roles and permissions] in user-settings because that's the only one that's downloaded for offline use. However I suspect couchdb db level permissions will use the one in the _users db because that's the only one it knows about. The CHT has code to keep these in sync but obviously it's not working correctly.

https://github.com/medic/cht-couch2pg/issues/137#issuecomment-1603301412

Just a quick example:

* [Here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/0c7399770fdcb94dbbc1764f25e3141e6b79b5b9/sentinel/src/lib/purging.js#L69) sentinel pull roles from the `_users` db
* [Here](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/0c7399770fdcb94dbbc1764f25e3141e6b79b5b9/admin/src/js/controllers/users.js#L25) admin app pulls from `user-settings`
* [Here](https://github.com/medic/config-muso/issues/987#issuecomment-1587832887) a system admin alters one doc through Fauxton but not the other (this is common)

These two security docs stay in alignment when edited through the CHT UI, but when edited through scripts or Fauxton they are frequently not in sync. CHT currently expects these documents to be identical -- when they are not, it can cause inconsistent roles and permissions for users.

Labeling as bug because of this statement "The CHT has code to keep these in sync but obviously it's not working correctly".

**Describe the bug**
Instead of loading the next batch of 50 contacts when the user scrolls down the LHS list, nothing happens. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create 100 `district_hospitals`. Name them `district 1` -> `district 100` for easy spotting.
2. Login as an admin. 
3. Load the contacts page. Scroll down the list of contacts and notice that you don't get the 2nd page of district hospitals to load. 

**Expected behavior**
Infinite scrolling should work. 

**Logs**
No errors in logs.

**Environment**
- Instance: any 4.2 prod instance 
- App: webapp
- Version: 4.2

title: Release 4.2.2
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create an GH Milestone and add this issue to it.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.
- [x] Ensure that all issues are labelled correctly, particularly ensure that "Regressions" are labelled with "Affects: <version>" labels. The "Affects" label is used in a link in the Known Issues section of the release notes of that version so it has to match exactly. To make sure the label is correct go to the [release notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) and ensure the issue is listed.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR to the release branch. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version patch`.
- [x] Ensure that issues from merged commits are closed and mapped to a milestone.
- [x] Write an update in the #product-team Slack channel summarising development and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The Release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have been merged into `master` then the release process can start:

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`).
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #product-team Slack channel:
```
@product_team, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag. 
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make. 
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
    - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
    - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, that they're correctly labelled (in particular: they have the right Type, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate), and have human readable descriptions.
    - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes) to export the issues into our release note format.
    - [x] Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
    - [x] Add a link to the new release page in the [Release Notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) section.
    - [x] Assign the PR to:
        - The Director of Technology or a developer
        - An SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Ensure the release notes PR above is merged. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds_4/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*Announcing the release of {{version}}*

This release fixes {{number of bugs}}. Read the [release notes]({{url}}) for full details.
```
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Upgrade cannot be initiated when there are no past `upgrade_log` entries
body:
**Describe the bug**
Installing and upgrading the CHT should each create an `upgrade_log` doc entry in `medic-logs`. 
If, for any reason, all upgrade logs are deleted, the admin app will display an error that the current upgrade was interrupted. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Launch CHT 4.x
2. In the `medic-logs` database, locate a document that looks like `upgrade_log:<timestamp>:<version>`. Delete this doc.
3. Go to admin upgrade page.
4. See error

**Expected behavior**
Upgrading through the UI should be possible. 

**Screenshots**
![image](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/35681649/d3c483c8-23a9-4e9b-aa65-5df43d6a077c)

**Environment**
- Instance: any 4.x
- App: api
- Version: 4.0.0

**Additional context**
Creating a "dummy" upgrade log fixes this issue:
```
{
  "_id": "upgrade_log:1687793528101",
  "state": "finalized"
}
```
These logs are not used for any logic outside of upgrading (or analytics). Once the upgrade is initiated, the dummy log can be deleted safely.

title: 0.6% of Muso production requests spending >60 minutes in API.  1.4% of total API workload
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Based on recent analysis of Muso production traffic (23 days of traffic with 1.2M requests), >9.5% of all requests spend >90 minutes being processed by API. We know that the ELB terminates these connections after 60 minutes, so this leaves API spinning without any value to users.

Hours at API | % of requests
-- | --
2 | 8.5%
4 | 6.9%
8 | 5.1%

Top 10 request patterns taking > 8 hours

url pattern | hi
-- | --
/medic/_changes (offline user) |
/medic/_changes (longpoll) |
/purging/changes |
medic/form%3.*
/medic/_bulk_docs
medic-user-.*-meta/_changes.*
/medic/_revs_diff
/medic/_design/medic-client/_view/data_records_by_type
/medic/[a-zA-Z0-9\-]{36}
/api/v1/users-info
/medic/_design/medic-client/_view/doc_by_type
medic/resources/.*

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Timeout for requests at API? I won't stop CouchDB from continuing to process the query which is already in the pipe, but it could stop additional useless heavy requests from coming through.

title: Userspace configuration options
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
I want to make the CHT Core repo extensible so that downstream consumers have a structured way of building their own versions while keeping patches and changes distinct enough that they're easy to understand and potentially contribute upstream.

We're building for Azure so need (will need) to patch in things like application insights and blob storage connections, as well as B2C for authorisation.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
I have a somewhat working solution which merges a source (git module) repo with a patch folder into a build folder, which is what we actually test against/deploy. I've set up a meta package.json for all the scripting and have extended the gruntfile the `--tasks` flag.

Honestly would just like a chance to show someone how it all works? I'd like to do less work anyway, and a userspace config zone would help. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I mean I've built an approach. It could do with work, but it's got a lot going for it.

**Additional context**
So, just a methodology that made @dianabarsan ask me to raise an issue, though honestly not sure how to present it. It's just a technique for altering ini files with another file (echo could echo a file).

```sh
echo "
[daemons]
httpsd = {couch_httpd, start_link, [https]}
[admins]
admin = ${COUCHDB_PASSWORD}
[ssl]
port = 6984
enable = true
cert_file = /opt/couchdb/etc/certs/cert.pem
key_file = /opt/couchdb/etc/certs/privkey.pem
cacert_file = /opt/couchdb/etc/certs/chain.pem" |

sudo crudini --merge /opt/couchdb/etc/local.ini
```

Having a default and a stipulated location a script might look for a merge file would be one way of giving userspace control.

title: feat(#8328): show reports of online user's place
body:
# Description

- Adds feature to default the place filter to the user's associated place. 
- Adds permission to enable the feature.

Knowns of this feature:
- The user can still remove the filter and see reports from other facilities at the same level.
- If the user reloads the page, or navigates to another tab and then comes back to the Reports tab, then the default filters will be applied.
- This feature isn't available for offline-users and db admin users.
- We won't add a visual indicator in the parent place when the child place is selected as part of this work. There's a separate [ticket](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7727) for that, and it will be scheduled later. 

medic/cht-core#8328

[PR CHT-Docs ](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/pull/1142)

<details>
  <summary>Special scenario when a user can see reports from another place, and when a user cannot see reports from their place and below the hierarchy</summary>


There is an edge case scenario where a user (from `Place-A`) submits a report for another place (`Place-B`) in the same hierarchy level. 
When the default filter is applied to show reports from `"Place-A"`, the user will be able to see this report. While if users from `"Place-B"` apply the filter to show reports from `Place-B`, they won't see this report.

This is because CHT takes the report’s contact -- the user’s contact that submitted the report. Then CHT gets the parent place and places below it in the hierarchy, to associate the report with those places and put them in a CouchDB's view (`reports_by_place`). This is where we get the reports from when the place filter is applied. 

https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/66472237/58e54e56-9e92-4f2d-9efd-ed138678c2ee

</details>

title: chore: enable strictNullChecks for webapp
body:
<!--
Please use semantic PR titles that respect this format:

<type>(#<issue number>): <subject>

Quick example:

feat(#1234): add hat wobble
^--^(#^--^): ^------------^
|     |      |
|     |      + - > subject
|     |
|     + -------- > issue number
|
+ -------------- > type: chore, feat, fix, perf.

https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/contribute/code/workflow/#commit-message-format
-->

# Description

Basically all this PR does is set the [`strictNullChecks` TS config option](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig#strictNullChecks) in our webapp TS config (and also updates the types in the existing TS code to allow the app to still build...).

(Note that `strictNullChecks` is a _subset_ of what you get by enabling the [`strict` flag](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig#strict). So, this is a good step in that direction.)

Implementation code changes have been kept to an absolute minimum. Besides updates to _typing_ (which technically have no effect on the actual behavior of the code) there were a few places where I had to change a value from `undefined` to `null` (or vice versa) to remain compatible with inherited type definitions.  Other than these changes, the actual logic of the implementation code should be completely unchanged!

## Benefits of `strictNullChecks`

- Prevents the need for unnecessary and redundant null-checking throughout the code since types can be used to guarantee something is valued
- TS can indicate where optional chaining (or other null checking) is required since it knows what _could be_ `null`

## Methodology for this PR

- The majority of the changes involved code that was creating empty Array literals (`[]`) that were populated later.  With `strictNullChecks`, TS was interpreting the type of those arrays as `never[]` if they were created with no type specified.  The fix here is just to specify the type of thing the array will hold when instantiating the variable.
- Another common problem was when default values were provided for function parameters. Often if `null` was provided (and no type was specified for the parameter, then TS was concluding that the _type_ for those variables was just `null`.  The fix here was just to specify the type for parameters that had default values.
- I have put a modest amount of effort into using _more specific_ types and not just slapping `any` on everything.  Where I was absolutely certain of a type (typically local variables), I used that specific type.  Otherwise, I did not dig too deep. If I did not know the exact type, but I did know that it was an _actual object_ (and not just primitive/null/undefined), I would use `Record<string, any>`.
- The main goal was to change as little as possible while still being able to successfully build the project. This is why I have not tried to consistently apply types across the changed files or anything. I have only updated the minimum places necessary to allow for building the project.
- There are a ton of places where minor logic changes could have "improved" the typing for a particular function/variable. I have resisted the urge to make these logic changes here and instead focused on updating the types to reflect _the current state of the code_.
    - The result of this is some objectively bad types being used (e.g. `object | null`) but I think it is preferable to leave these bad types as beacons for future refactors instead of trying to fix everything now and run the risk of causing a subtle defect that is missed because of the scope of these changes...

title: Release 4.3.0
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create a GH Milestone for the release. We use [semver](http://semver.org) so if there are breaking changes increment the major, otherwise if there are new features increment the minor, otherwise increment the service pack. Breaking changes in our case relate to updated software requirements (egs: CouchDB, node, minimum browser versions), broken backwards compatibility in an api, or a major visual update that requires user retraining.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone. Ideally each minor release will have one or two features, a handful of improvements, and plenty of bug fixes.
- [x] Identify any features and improvements in the release that need end-user documentation (beyond eng team documentation improvements) and create corresponding issues in the cht-docs repo
- [x] Assign an engineer as Release Engineer for this release.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version <major|minor>`.
- [x] Raise a new issue called `Update dependencies for <version>` with a description that links to [the documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/guides/update-dependencies/). This should be done early in the release cycle so find a volunteer to take this on and assign it to them.
- [x] Ensure that issues from merged commits are closed and mapped to a milestone.
- [x] Write an update in the #product-team Slack channel summarising development and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The Release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have been merged into `master` then the release process can start:

- [x] Create a new release branch from `master` named `<major>.<minor>.x` in `cht-core`. Post a message to #development Slack channel using this template:
```
@core_devs I've just created the `<major>.<minor>.x` release branch. Please be aware that any further changes intended for this release will have to be merged to `master` then backported. Thanks!
```
- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`).
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #product-team Slack channel:
```
@product_team, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag. 
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make. 
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
  - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
  - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, that they're correctly labelled (in particular: they have the right Type, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate), and have human readable descriptions.
  - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes) to export the issues into our release note format.
  - [x] Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
  - [x] Provide description, screenshots, videos, and anything else to help communicate particularly important changes.
  - [x] Document any required or recommended upgrades to our other products (eg: cht-conf, cht-gateway, cht-android).
  - [x] Add the release to the [Supported versions](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions) and update the EOL date and status of previous releases. Also add a link in the `Release Notes` section to the new release page.
  - [x] Assign the PR to:
    - The Director of Technology or a developer
    - An SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Ensure the release notes PR above is merged. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds_4/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Execute the scalability testing suite on the final build and download the scalability results on S3 at medic-e2e/scalability/$TAG_NAME. Add the release `.json` file to `cht-core/tests/scalability/previous_results`. More info in the  [scalability documentation](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/tests/scalability/README.md).
- [ ] Upgrade the `demo-cht.dev` instance to this version.
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/c/product/releases/26), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*We're excited to announce the release of {{version}} of {{product}}*

New features include {{key_features}}. We've also implemented loads of other improvements and fixed a heap of bugs.

Read the [release notes]({{url}}) for full details.

Following our support policy, versions {{versions}} are no longer supported. Projects running these versions should start planning to upgrade in the near future. For more details read our [software support documentation](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#supported-versions).

Check out our [roadmap](https://github.com/orgs/medic/projects/112) to see what we're working on next.
```
- [x] Add one last update to the #product-team Slack channel and use the thread to lead an internal release retrospective covering what went well and areas to improve for next time.
- [x] Add any open "known issues" from the prior release that were not fixed in this release. Done by adding the correct `Affects: 4.x.x` label.  
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Evaluate experience of filter by case_id
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
This feature didn't get considered when we redesigned the experience of the search bar and the selection of multiple reports. 
When a report is selected by clicking the checkbox, the search bar is hidden, so the user can't search. If a report has a `case_id` link, and they click on it, the filter won't apply because it's in select mode. 

The mobile experience is also weird because the filter is in the report's detail page, so the user might not know that the filter can't apply if in select mode. 

The intention of this ticket is to reevaluate the user experience with the Care Team trio and determine the best feasible design. 

Related to https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8401

**Additional context**
When a report has a case_id field, this field is highlighted as a link in the report details page, and the link is meant to apply a filter that shows all other reports with the same case_id. The interaction should be described here: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/6291

title: Feature flag to limit filters for online users
body:
**Describe the issue**
A default facility filter was added as part of this [work](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8328).

Make a performance analysis with big data to see the performance impact of applying multiple filters. Some questions we want to answer when having big data: 
- Is it more expensive to load reports with a default place filter? 
- What is the performance of applying more than one filter? 
    - They start with one and then add another one. How efficiently the app finds the intersection of the two sets of results and pages them?

It would also be interesting to compare the performance improvements when using CouchDB v3.x

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
If the performance is bad, then we can consider these options:
 - All filters can be used, and limit the filter to apply just one at a time. The downside is that the default filter will be lost. 
 - Just one filter can be used; the other ones are disabled or removed. Based on permissions. For example, users can use only the facility filter or just the search bar.
 - Allow default filter, but prevent a user from applying more filters.

title: Enable http/2 in nginx config
body:
**Describe the performance issue**
Self hosters right now have to either live with slower http/1 or either implement http/2 themselves. This does not apply to Medic hosted projects who get http/2 implemented on the load balancer in AWS.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Make a minor update to the nginx config file to turn http/2 on and then test the change.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Documentation and additional setup steps.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to record the performance metrics:
1. Set up a representative offline user with a decent number of docs (~5000 should do)
2. Because this is testing network latency do not set up the CHT on the same machine. Also this can't use our standard AWS setup which already has h2 enabled. You will however need TLS otherwise http/2 will not be available.
3. Throttle your connection to represent real world conditions.
4. Time loading the login page for the first time. This is testing downloading the static resources into the service worker, and it won't be obvious in the UI when it completes, so you'll need to watch the network tab.
5. Log in and time initial replication.

**Measurements**
Above...

**Additional context**
- http/3 is out and should be another improvement but not currently supported by nginx. Cross that bridge later.
- @mrjones-plip did a small scale test and commented here: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/pull/8278#issuecomment-1569444978

title: Add support for HTTP/2 in nginx
body:
**Describe the issue**
In our [nginx config](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/nginx/nginx.conf), we only support HTTP/1 

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
By adding support for HTTP/2, we can improve performance for self hosted deployments who have nginx facing CHWs

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
currently AWS hosted (including Medic hosted) CHT deployments use [ELB](https://aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/) which [already supports HTTP/2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/userguide/how-elastic-load-balancing-works.html#load-balancer-scheme), so we could do nothing and leverage this.  As well, other self hosted partners could use [traefik](https://traefik.io/traefik/) or [caddy](https://caddyserver.com/).

title: chore(#7462): bifurcate EnektoService into FormService
body:
# Description

The goal of this PR is to separate out the logic in the `EnketoService` that is directly related to rendering Enekto forms and recording the report from the extra logic that is specific to the CHT domain.  A new `EnektoFormService` has been created to contain the form-related logic. This is what the coming cht-form web component can depend on (instead of the web component having to worry about stubbing out a large amount of services that are not actually necessary for just displaying the form and recording the result.  

Whereas before, the cht-form web component would need to stub out behavior for `9` different services (and these stubs would have to be maintained whenever the api for those services changed), after this PR, the cht-form web component will only need to stub behavior for the `DbService`. 

<details>
<summary>Original dependency tree</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR

subgraph "Direct EnketoService Depenencies"
	attachment
    cht-script-api([cht-script-api])
    contact-summary([contact-summary])
    db([db])
    enekto-prepopulation-data
    enketo-translation
    extract-lineage
    feedback([feedback])
    file-reader
    get-report-content
    language([language])
    lineage-model-generator
    search([search])
    submit-form-by-sms([submit-form-by-sms])
    training-cards([training-cards])
    transitions([transitions])
    translate
    translate-from
    user-contact
    xml-forms([xml-forms])
    z-score([z-score])
    
    get-report-content --> db & file-reader
    lineage-model-generator --> db
end

subgraph "Transitive Dependencies"
auth
changes
contact-types
debug
feedback
form2sms
format-date
get-data-records
location
pipes
route-snapshot
session
settings
telemetry
uhc-settings
uhc-stats
user-settings([user-settings])
validation
version
xml-forms-context-utils
end

db -.-> session & location
enekto-prepopulation-data --> language & enketo-translation & user-settings
language -.-> settings & format-date & telemetry
search -.-> db & session & get-data-records & telemetry
submit-form-by-sms -.-> form2sms & settings
user-contact --> user-settings & lineage-model-generator & db
xml-forms -.-> auth & changes & contact-types & db & file-reader & user-contact & xml-forms-context-utils & feedback
z-score -.-> changes & db
contact-summary -.-> settings & pipes & feedback & uhc-settings & uhc-stats & cht-script-api
transitions -.-> settings & validation
feedback -.-> db & session & version & debug & language & telemetry
cht-script-api -.-> settings & changes & session
training-cards -.-> xml-forms & db & session & route-snapshot & feedback

```

</details>

<details>
<summary>New dependency tree</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR

subgraph "Direct EnketoFormService Dependencies"
	attachment
    db([db])
    enekto-prepopulation-data
    enketo-translation
    extract-lineage
    translate
    translate-from
	enekto-prepopulation-data --> enketo-translation
end
```


</details>

## Details:

I have gone to great lengths to resist the urge of doing any unnecessary low-level refactoring. Instead, whenever possible I have just copied functions in their entirety without touching the contacts. 

- Extracted logic specific to displaying forms from `EneketoService` into a new `EnketoFormService`
    - Basically all the data needed for rendering the form (user settings, contact-summary, etc) can be passed in from the EnektoService to the `EnektoFormService.renderForm` function
- Extracted `UserSettingsService` and `LanguageService` from the `EnketoPrepopulationDataService`
    - I needed to do this in order to keep the EnketoPrepopulationDataService as a part of EnketoFormService, but not have to stub out behavior for UserSettingsService and LanguageService in the web compoent
- Update `UserSettings` service to include a function that returns the user's settings with the `language` pre-populated
    - Convenience method for use by the `EnketoService` and the `Forms2SmsService` (basically just recreating the tiny but of code removed from EnketoPrepopulationDataService)
- The EnketoService and EnketoFormService unit tests represent the majority of the code changes, but I have tried to approach these changes in a way that is both safest and easiest to review:
    - Prior to the final commit in this PR, I only made minor changes to the EnektoService tests as necessary to keep the tests running during the refactoring process.  
    - So, after all of the refactoring changes to the implementation code, the EnektoService unit tests still pass with only minor changes (to account for certain functions being moved to the EnektoFormService).
    - In the final commit of the PR, I have bifurcated the unit tests to separate the tests specific to the EnketoFormService from the ones that pertain to the EnektoService
        - When separating these tests, I have tried, as much as possible, to not edit the contents of the tests, but instead to just change the minimum necessary for the test to call the new EnektoFormService APIs.
        - Due to time constraints, I have not updated the remaining EnektoService unit tests to mock out the behavior of the EnektoFormService. Instead, I have left the logic of these tests intact so that they still call through to the EnektoFormService code.  This means that these tests are unnecessarily complex, but it seems an acceptable tradeoff at this point to avoid a huge re-write of the tests at this time.

title: Loading the webapp fails on with WebView version 74
body:
**Describe the bug** Starting at CHT 4.2.0, when a self hosted CHT instance uses `nginx` as it's front end, certain Android devices fail with a console error `Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token ? main.js:1` **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Install CHT Core 4.2.0 in docker helper. Do not use AWS ELB 2. Using CHT Android 1.0.1 with webview 74 or lower, connect to CHT Core 4. See error in console `Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token ? main.js:1` and see full screen spinner. **Expected behavior** You should be prompted to log in to the CHT with no errors in console **Screenshots**
Console tab
Network tab
Security tab
**Environment** - Instance: local dev - Browser: CHT Android 1.0.1 WebView 74 or 68 - Client platform: See above - App: webapp - Version: 4.2.0 and above **Additional context** This was discovered while testing #8278. It's assumed that this wasn't caught earlier because we test on Gamma which uses AWS ELB to terminate TLS. Indeed, testing CHT COre 4.2.0 on Gamma with the exact same handset as above works. Testing on 4.1.0 and 4.0.0 on the same handset also work. Also, testing the same 4.2.0 instance with WebView 111 worked fine. All desktop browsers worked as well.

title: API fails to start because of large form attachments exceed POST allowed payload
body:
**Describe the bug**
A [step] in our API startup sequence is to re-generate all forms attachments: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/api/src/services/generate-xform.js#L258
The code attempts to update all forms at one, in one big `_bulk_docs` request. The payload for this request will include all form attachments and form docs. This includes images and any other media elements that the forms require. 
This request can fail with a `413 Content Too Large`.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create some forms that have very large media attachments. Upload these forms individually to the server. An alternative would be to create many forms. 
2. Restart API
3. See error

![image](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/35681649/eb6e184b-e413-42a8-a836-9d8873021908)

**Expected behavior**
API should not fail to start when there are too many forms to upload. 

**Environment**
- Instance: any
- App: api
- Version: Code was not changed since 3.7.0, it's possible this only affects 4.0.0+ due to architecture changes, but I have not tested. 

**Additional context**
Originally reported on the forum.

title: Offline users stuck on spinner on load until certain views are indexed
body:
**Describe the bug**
Because of a recent change in webapp, offline users' UI (tabs, header, logo) won't load until all of the initialization is done. 
Depending on how many documents they have, this can take a long time after initial sync, because some of those initializations require view calls. 
The UI that the user sees is a spinner without an indication of what is happening. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a user with 10.000 docs. 
2. Login. Wait for initial replication. 
3. See spinner for _a while_ (minutes)

**Expected behavior**
Before the webapp change, the UI would load immediately after initial replication, even if many actions required their corresponding views to get indexed.

**Logs**
No logs on the device

**Video**
https://github.com/medic/cht-core/assets/35681649/ae80ada9-6dcd-47f6-bf5a-37a81e940d1c

This video is recorded on my desktop computer, using Chrome incognito. I have not throttled the browser in any capacity. 
It takes 30 seconds to download all docs and then 2 minutes (!) to get to see the UI. 

**Environment**
- Instance: local
- Browser: Chrome
- App: webapp
- Version: 4.3.0

**Additional context**
Introduced in `4.3.0` by https://github.com/medic/cht-core/commit/5be8ea494ab63ab2825d6b727f3a7e97e508dc93

title: Invalid phone for patient still running triggers
body:
**Describe the bug** CHT-Core 4.3 recently added a feature where we can register patient by passing patient phone number. Though phone number validation is done internally, since **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Prepare a patient registration form with schedule and phone number field on patient.
Click for config ### Sample config ```json { "form": "N", "events": [ { "name": "on_create", "trigger": "add_patient_id", "params": "", "bool_expr": "doc.patient_name" }, { "name": "on_create", "trigger": "assign_schedule", "params": "Registration Reminders", "bool_expr": "doc.patient_name" } ], "validations": { "join_responses": false, "list": [ { "property": "patient_phone", "translation_key": "messages.n_na.duplicate_phone", "rule": "uniquePhone('patient_phone')" }, { "property": "patient_age", "rule": "(integer && min(0) && max(125))", "translation_key": "messages.n.invalid_format" }, { "property": "patient_name", "rule": "(string && lenMin(1) && lenMax(30))", "translation_key": "messages.n.invalid_format" } ] }, "messages": [ { "translation_key": "messages.n_na.registered", "recipient": "", "event_type": "report_accepted", "bool_expr": "doc.errors.length===0" }, { "translation_key": "messages.n_na.duplicate_phone", "recipient": "", "event_type": "provided_phone_not_unique" } ] } ```
2. Submit this form with some invalid phone number **Expected behavior** 1. First trigger `add_patient_id` shouldn't run and patient id shouldn't be assigned. 2. Second trigger `assign_schedule` should not be created. **Screenshots** Look at Invalid message, generated medic id, and reminder schedules created. **Environment** - Instance: (eg: jajarkot-ne dev instance) - Browser: Any - Client platform: Any - App: webapp, api - Version: (eg: 4.3) **Proposed solution:** Expose a method to validate phone in app_settings in [rules](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/apps/reference/app-settings/#rules), such that we can call phone validation and give message, and stop transition.

title: fix(#8478): Added validPhone validation so that triggers are not fired for patients with invalid phone.
body:
Bug Fix (#8478 ): Invalid phone for patient still running triggers

# Description
Added validPhone validation so that phone validation is done before registration triggers are run. So now if validPhone validation fails for a patient none of the registration triggers configured for the forms are run similar to how Age validation of 0 to 125 failure causes none of the triggers to run if age is above 125 or negative.

Why this was necessary? 
We had a form to add patient with phone number but although patient wasn't added due to invalid phone assign_schedules trigger for the supplied doc was still running so schedules were created for a patient that was invalid. 

Fork Branch: [valid_phone_8478](https://github.com/PrjShrestha/cht-core/tree/valid_phone_8478)

title: Prioritise Outbound Push Requests
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When processing outbound push requests it is possible to have requests triggered by a form associated to a contact be processed before the request triggered by the contact's creation which can lead to errors in the system being called.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A way to prioritise outbound push requests in a queue

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
This is currently handled outside the CHT by retrying the requests once they are sure the new contact has been registered.

**Additional context**
None

none really

title: API crashes when CouchDB is overloaded
body:

When CouchDB is overloaded it gets unresponsive and ends up responding with 5xx errors that make the API crash.  
It was seen on a training instance backed by a single couch node with 30 cores and 32 GB of RAM dealing with a spike of thousands of users. More info in https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8324

title: Release 4.3.1
body:
# Planning - Product Manager

- [x] Create an GH Milestone and add this issue to it.
- [x] Add all the issues to be worked on to the Milestone.
- [x] Ensure that all issues are labelled correctly, particularly ensure that "Regressions" are labelled with "Affects: <version>" labels. The "Affects" label is used in a link in the Known Issues section of the release notes of that version so it has to match exactly. To make sure the label is correct go to the [release notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) and ensure the issue is listed.

# Development - Release Engineer

When development is ready to begin one of the engineers should be nominated as a Release Engineer. They will be responsible for making sure the following tasks are completed though not necessarily completing them.

- [x] Set the version number in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` and submit a PR to the release branch. The easiest way to do this is to use `npm --no-git-tag-version version patch`.
- [x] Ensure that issues from merged commits are closed and mapped to a milestone.
- [x] Write an update in the #product-team Slack channel summarising development and identifying any blockers (the [milestone-status](https://github.com/medic/support-scripts/tree/master/milestone-status) script can be used to get a breakdown of the issues). The Release Engineer is to update this every week until the version is released.

# Releasing - Release Engineer

Once all issues have been merged into `master` then the release process can start:

- [x] Build a beta named `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` by pushing a lightweight git tag (e.g. `git tag <major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1`).
- [x] Once the CI completes successfully notify the team by writing a message in the #product-team Slack channel:
```
@product_team, I’ve just created the `<major>.<minor>.<patch>-beta.1` tag. 
Please let me know if there’s any final update we need to make. 
If all is good, then in 24h, I will start the release. Thanks!
```
- [x] Add release notes to the [Core Framework Releases](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/) page:
    - [x] Create a new document for the release in the [releases folder](https://github.com/medic/cht-docs/tree/main/content/en/core/releases).
    - [x] Ensure all issues are in the GH Milestone, that they're correctly labelled (in particular: they have the right Type, "UI/UX" if they change the UI, and "Breaking change" if appropriate), and have human readable descriptions.
    - [x] Use [this script](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/master/scripts/release-notes) to export the issues into our release note format.
    - [x] Manually document any known migration steps and known issues.
    - [x] Add a link to the new release page in the [Release Notes](https://docs.communityhealthtoolkit.org/core/releases/#release-notes) section.
    - [x] Assign the PR to:
        - The Director of Technology or a developer
        - An SRE to review and confirm the documentation on upgrade instructions and breaking changes is sufficient
- [x] Create a release in GitHub from the release branch so it shows up under the [Releases tab](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/releases) with the naming convention `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. This will create the git tag automatically. Ensure the release notes PR above is merged. Link to the release notes in the description of the release.
- [x] Confirm the release build completes successfully and the new release is available on the [market](https://staging.dev.medicmobile.org/builds_4/releases). Make sure that the document has new entry with `id: medic:medic:<major>.<minor>.<patch>`
- [x] Announce the release on the [CHT forum](https://forum.communityhealthtoolkit.org/), under the "Product - Releases" category using this template:
```
*Announcing the release of {{version}}*

This release fixes {{number of bugs}}. Read the [release notes]({{url}}) for full details.
```
- [x] Mark this issue "done" and close the Milestone.

title: Update lodash
body:
**Describe the issue**
We're a couple of patch releases behind lodash latest and the version we're on has a known vulnerability. Unfortunately updating is blocked by https://github.com/lodash/lodash/issues/5563 and a naive update fails a unit test (and presumably prod) with debouncing contact searching in the add/edit user screen.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Find a workaround to unblock updating lodash.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Living with the old version.
- Not using lodash, at least in this one place.
- Removing debouncing in the admin search function.

title: Update configuration deployment action to use latest cht-conf
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
We have a [GH Action](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/tree/master/.github/actions/deploy-with-medic-conf) published which is used in Continuous Deployment so apps can be updated easily but it's based on `medic-conf` which is years out of date.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Create a new action which uses cht-conf with a new name. If possible mark the old one as deprecated so GH warns anyone using it.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Keeping the name the same but because it explicitly says "medic-conf" it'd be good to have a clean break.

# Description

- Upgrades webapp's angular to v16
- Upgrades Typescript, rxjs, tslibs, ngxbootstrap versions in order to support Angular 16.
- Replaces Bootstrap's accordion with Angular Material's. This fixes this [issue](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8471).

- Removes `defaultProject` from angular.json, this property is deprecated.
- Because the new version of ngx-bootstrap drop support to Bootstrap v3, we started to use Bootstrap v4.
- Overrides styles of Bootstrap 4, patching, so app looks the same as before in the new design and old design (action bar and filters). We are working on removing Bootstrap gradually from Webapp. 
- Overrides Angular Material's fonts to use the Noto fonts, this fixes [this issue ](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/8520)

body:
**Describe the issue**
When we moved away from Grunt a lot of the commands just ended up getting inlined into the package.json. Many of these are never intended to be called by devs or CI - they are only executed as part of another command. As such they are not needed in the package.json. Worse still, the package.json is very restrictive in how the commands can be formatted (no new lines, for example) so it's difficult to read and diff.

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
Remove all the sub-scripts from the package.json by extracting them into bash or node scripts.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Other build tools, but then we end up back where we started...

title: Support deploying with Podman
body:
**What feature do you want to improve?**
Currently the official supported deployment of the CHT is restricted to a Docker environment.  It would be nice to also support [Podman](https://podman.io/) which is an _almost_ drop-in replacement for Docker maintained by RedHat + community (and the creators of the [Container Commandos coloring book](https://developers.redhat.com/e-books/container-commandos-coloring-book)...).  

Reasons someone might prefer Podman over Docker include:

- More FLOSS ecosystem/community - Everything is Apache 2, without proprietary code getting Trojaned in via "Desktop" applications....
- Better security model - Podman's architecture is inherently more secure than Docker's.
- Closer to Kubernetes - Podman pods are more k8s-style
 
Describe the improvement you'd like**
I tried running the CHT containers via Podman (using the `podman-docker` compatibility layer + normal `docker-compose`).  The two main issues I uncovered were:

1. The [`local` log driver](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/issues/7801) is [not supported in Podman](https://docs.podman.io/en/latest/markdown/podman-run.1.html#log-driver-driver).  Only `k8s-file`, `journald`, `none`, `passthrough`, and `json-file`. (Default `journald`).
2. Podman's DNS seems to work a bit differently and critically [does not listen at `127.0.0.11`](https://github.com/containers/dnsname/issues/81) which is [hard-coded in our nginx config](https://github.com/medic/cht-core/blob/58f23a8db0651faeb8c9fdeb7a00a288e05950cf/nginx/templates/server.conf.template#L1).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We can just live and die according to the whims of Docker Inc.

**Additional context**
I do not know of anything being blocked by this lack of Podman support. The main point of this issue is just to record the results of my investigation for future reference if it ever comes up....

title: Sentinel stuck in infinite loop when 100 sequential deletions fail to generate tombstones
body:
**Describe the bug**
Sentinel only advances its `transitions-seq` sequence if a successful change is processed. 
Sentinel also only loads 100 docs at a time, to prevent an OOM error when there are millions of changes to process. 

If all of the 100 sequential changes fail to be processed by transitions, sentinel will keep requesting the same 100 docs over and over and be stuck in this loop forever. 

**To Reproduce**
This is easiest to reproduce in 4.2.2 and lower, because we can use tombstones to trigger this. Transitions alone will only error when writes fail, but tombstones can fail for a variety of reasons.
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Launch CHT v 4.2.2. 
2. Stop sentinel. 
3. With a script, create 1000 documents. Then delete those 100 documents, making sure you only save 3 keys in your delete, `_id`, `_rev` and `_deleted`. 
4. Run compaction. 
5. Start Sentinel. 
6. Leave sentinel running for a while and observe that the number of docs to process stays the same - you can use the monitoring endpoint for this. 
If you check the logs, you will see that sections like: 
```
2023-09-12 14:43:05 ERROR: Tombstone: could not process doc id: <doc_id> seq: <SEQ> {
  error: 'not_found',
  reason: 'missing',
  status: 404,
  name: 'not_found',
  message: 'missing',
  docId: <doc_id>
} 
```
If you search the log for the same doc id, you will find multiple appearances for the same doc. 

**Expected behavior**
For tombstones specifically, we could advance the seq even if the tombstone could not be created (?). For other failures, I'm not sure.

**Environment**
- Instance: live training instance
- App: sentinel
- Version: 3.9+, tombstones no longer trigger this in 4.3+. 

**Additional context**
This was affecting a live training instance. 
As a workaround, the sentinel seq can be advanced manually to skip the problematic batches.

title: The upgrade test fails when releasing a final
body:
**Describe the issue**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. -->
When a final release is published the upgrade test fails because it installs the latest version (the one that was just released) then tries to upgrade to it.

Example build: https://github.com/medic/cht-core/actions/runs/6255863600/job/16986706159

```
[0-0] RUNNING in chrome - file:///tests/e2e/upgrade/upgrade.wdio-spec.js
[0-0] Error in "Performing an upgrade.should upgrade to current branch"
Error: Can't call parentElement on element with selector "span=4.4.0" because element wasn't found
    at async Object.getInstallButton (/home/runner/work/cht-core/cht-core/tests/page-objects/upgrade/upgrade.wdio.page.js:14:25)
    at async Context.<anonymous> (/home/runner/work/cht-core/cht-core/tests/e2e/upgrade/upgrade.wdio-spec.js:104:27)
```

**Describe the improvement you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to change. -->
Skip the test. Everything else works but it's confusing and concerning to have a red build after releasing.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could fix it so it installs the "latest - 1" but the release has already happened so there's no point failing anyway.
